Nu'aym ibn 'Amr and al-Harith ibn Zayd said to him: "What religion are you upon, O Muhammad?" He said: "Upon the religion of Ibrahim." They said: "Ibrahim was a Jew." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then bring the Torah; it is between us and you." But they refused him, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.[[Narrated by al-Tabari in his *Tafsir* from Ibn 'Abbas: 6/228–229; and Ibn Shihab in *al-Sirah*: 2/201. Al-Suyuti also attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim. See *al-Durr al-Manthur*: 2/170; *Asbab al-Nuzul*, p. 131.]]

Al-Kalbi narrated from Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a man and a woman from the people of Khaybar committed adultery, and in their book the punishment was stoning. They disliked stoning them because of their nobility among them, so they referred their matter to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), hoping that he would have a concession. He ruled that they be stoned. Al-Nu'man ibn Awfa and Bahri ibn 'Amr said to him: "You have been unjust toward them, O Muhammad; stoning is not due for them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Between me and you is the Torah." They said: "You have been fair to us." He said: "Who is the most knowledgeable of you in the Torah?" They said: "A one-eyed man who lives in Fadak, called Ibn Suriya." So they sent for him, and he came to Madinah. Jibril had described him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Are you Ibn Suriya?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Are you the most knowledgeable of the Jews?" He said: "That is what they claim." He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called for a portion of the Torah, in which the stoning was written, and said to him: "Read." When he came to the verse of stoning, he placed his palm over it and read what came after it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). 'Abdullah ibn Salam said: "O Messenger of Allah, he has passed over it." So he stood up, lifted his palm from it, and then read to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to the Jews: that the married man and the married woman, if they commit adultery and the evidence is established against them, shall be stoned; and if the woman is pregnant, she shall be made to wait until she delivers what is in her womb. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then ordered the two Jews to be stoned, and they were stoned. The Jews were angered by this and departed, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, who are called to the Book of God﴾[[The story is from the narration of al-Kalbi from Ibn 'Abbas. This al-Kalbi is Abu al-Nadr Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kalbi, who is accused of lying. When he fell ill, he said to his companions in his illness: "Everything I have narrated to you from Abu Salih is a lie." See *Tahdhib al-Tahdhib*: 9/157–159; *al-Isra'iliyyat wa al-Mawdu'at fi al-Tafsir* by Shaykh Muhammad Abu Shahbah. It is, however, established that the two Jews who committed adultery were stoned in the six canonical books. See *Nasb al-Rayah* by al-Zayla'i: 3/326–327.]] ﴿so that He may judge between them; then a faction of them turns away, while they are averse.﴾

That is because they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days," and what they used to fabricate deceived them in their religion. Al-Ghurur (deception) is enticing someone with what will bring them no benefit at all. ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾. Al-Iftira' (fabrication) is inventing lies.

٥٥/ب The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So how will it be when We gather them﴾, meaning, how will their state be, or how will they act, when We gather them ﴿for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾ [and it is the Day of Resurrection] [[Omitted from "B".]] ﴿and every soul will be paid in full [were given in full] what it earned﴾, meaning the recompense for what it earned of good or evil, ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾, meaning their good deeds will not be diminished, and no additional evil deeds will be added to their evil deeds.

That is because they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for a few numbered days," and what they used to fabricate deceived them in their religion. Al-Ghurur (deception) is enticing someone with what will bring them no benefit at all. ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾. Al-Iftira' (fabrication) is inventing lies.

٥٥/ب The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So how will it be when We gather them﴾, meaning, how will their state be, or how will they act, when We gather them ﴿for a Day about which there is no doubt﴾ [and it is the Day of Resurrection] [[Omitted from "B".]] ﴿and every soul will be paid in full [were given in full] what it earned﴾, meaning the recompense for what it earned of good or evil, ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾, meaning their good deeds will not be diminished, and no additional evil deeds will be added to their evil deeds.

His saying, Most High: ﴿Say, "O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty"﴾. Qatadah said: It is mentioned that the Prophet (ﷺ) asked his Lord to give the kingdom of Persia and Byzantium to his community, so Allah, Most High, revealed this verse. Ibn 'Abbas and Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, he promised his community the kingdom of Persia and Byzantium. The hypocrites and the Jews said: "Far-fetched, far-fetched! How could Muhammad (ﷺ) obtain the kingdom of Persia and Byzantium? They are mightier and more secure than that. Were Makkah and Madinah not enough for Muhammad, that he covets the kingdom of Persia and Byzantium?" So Allah revealed this verse: ﴿Say, "O Allah"﴾.[[Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shafi, p. 25: al-Wahidi mentioned it in his Asbab (Occasions of Revelation), p. 131, from Ibn 'Abbas and Anas, may Allah be pleased with them. I did not find a chain of transmission for it.]] It has been said: its meaning is "O Allah," and when the vocative particle was omitted, the letter "meem" was added at its end. Others said: the "meem" in it has a meaning of its own, and its meaning is "O Allah, direct us to good" (ummana bi-khayr), i.e., "aim at us" (iqsud-na). The vocative particle was omitted from it, as in their saying "halumma ilayna" (come to us); its original form was "hal umma ilayna," and then it became common in speech, so the hamzah was dropped for ease. Sometimes they also lightened it and said "la humma."

His saying, ﴿Owner of Sovereignty﴾ [meaning, "O Owner of Sovereignty"], i.e., Owner of the servants and of what they possess. It has also been said: "O Owner of the heavens and the earth." Allah, Most High, said in some of the Books: "I am Allah, King of kings, Owner of kings. The hearts of kings and their forelocks are in My hand. If the servants obey Me, I will make them a mercy upon them; and if they disobey Me, I will make them a punishment upon them. So do not occupy yourselves with cursing the kings; rather, turn in repentance to Me, and I will incline them toward you."[[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat. al-Haythami said: in its chain is Ibrahim ibn Rashid, who is abandoned (matruk), Majma' al-Zawa'id 5/249. al-Albani said: very weak, Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Da'ifah 1/68.]]

His saying, Most High: ﴿You give sovereignty to whom You will﴾. Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it means the sovereignty of prophethood. Al-Kalbi said: ﴿You give sovereignty to whom You will﴾, namely Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions, ﴿and You take sovereignty away from whom You will﴾, namely Abu Jahl and the chiefs of Quraysh. It has also been said: ﴿You give sovereignty to whom You will﴾ refers to the Arabs, and ﴿You take sovereignty away from whom You will﴾ refers to Persia and Byzantium. As-Suddi said: ﴿You give sovereignty to whom You will﴾: Allah gave it to the prophets, peace be upon them, and commanded the servants to obey them; ﴿and You take sovereignty away from whom You will﴾: He removed it from the tyrants and commanded the servants to oppose them. It has also been said: ﴿You give sovereignty to whom You will﴾ refers to Adam and his offspring, and ﴿You take sovereignty away from whom You will﴾ refers to Iblis and his soldiers.

His saying, Most High: ﴿You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will﴾. 'Ata' said: ﴿You honor whom You will﴾ refers to the Muhajirun (Emigrants) and the Ansar (Helpers), and ﴿You humble whom You will﴾ refers to Persia and Byzantium. It has also been said: ﴿You honor whom You will﴾ refers to Muhammad (ﷺ) and his companions, until they entered Makkah with ten thousand men, prevailing over it; and ﴿You humble whom You will﴾ refers to Abu Jahl and his companions, until their heads were cut off and they were thrown into the well (al-qalib). It has also been said: ﴿You honor whom You will﴾ through faith and guidance, and ﴿You humble whom You will﴾ through disbelief and misguidance. It has also been said: ﴿You honor whom You will﴾ through obedience, and ﴿You humble whom You will﴾ through disobedience. It has also been said: ﴿You honor whom You will﴾ through victory, and ﴿You humble whom You will﴾ through subjugation. It has also been said: ﴿You honor whom You will﴾ through wealth, and ﴿You humble whom You will﴾ through poverty. It has also been said: ﴿You honor whom You will﴾ through contentment and satisfaction, and ﴿You humble whom You will﴾ through greed and covetousness.

﴿In Your hand is the good﴾, i.e., in Your hand is the good and the evil, but He mentioned only one of them. Allah, Most High, said: ﴿garments that protect you from the heat﴾ (16:81, al-Nahl), i.e., from the heat and the cold, but He mentioned only one of them. ﴿Indeed, You are over all things Competent.﴾

He, the Exalted, said: ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day﴾, meaning He makes the night enter into the day, until the day becomes fifteen hours and the night nine hours. ﴿And He causes the day to enter into the night﴾, until the night becomes fifteen hours and the day nine hours. Whatever is lost from one of them is added to the other. ﴿And He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living﴾. The people of Madinah, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Hafs, on the authority of 'Asim, read al-mayyit (the dead) with a shaddah on the yaa' here, and in al-An'am, Yunus, and al-Rum, and in al-A'raf (﴿for a dead land﴾) and in Fatir (﴿to a dead land﴾). Nafi' added (﴿Or one who was dead and We gave him life﴾, 6:122), (﴿the flesh of his dead brother﴾, 49:12), and (﴿a dead land which We have revived﴾, 36:33), and he doubled the shaddah in them. The others read them without the shaddah. Ya'qub read ﴿brings forth the living from the dead﴾ with a shaddah on the yaa' of mayyit.

Ibn Mas'ud, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: the meaning of the verse is that He brings forth the animal from the sperm-drop, which is dead, and brings forth the sperm-drop from the animal.

'Ikrimah and al-Kalbi said: He brings forth the living from the dead, that is, the chick from the egg, and brings forth the egg from the bird. Al-Hasan and 'Ata' said: He brings forth the believer from the disbeliever, and brings forth the disbeliever from the believer. The believer is living of heart, and the disbeliever is dead of heart. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Or one who was dead and We gave him life﴾ (6:122). Al-Zajjaj said: He brings forth tender, fresh vegetation from the dry seed, and brings forth the dry seed from living, growing vegetation.

﴿And You provide for whom You will without account﴾, without restriction [and without stinginess] [[In manuscript B: "and without hardship."]].

We were informed by Abu al-Qasim 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi, who said: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us, who said: Abu Ja'far 'Abd Allah ibn Isma'il ibn Ibrahim al-Hashimi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Zayd al-Sa'igh informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Azhar informed us, who said: al-Harith ibn 'Umayr informed us, who said: Ja'far ibn Muhammad informed us, from his father, from his grandfather, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the Opening of the Book (al-Fatihah), the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi), and the two verses of Al 'Imran (from ﴿Allah bears witness﴾ to His saying ﴿Indeed, the religion with Allah is Islam﴾, and ﴿Say: O Allah, Owner of sovereignty﴾ to His saying ﴿without account﴾) are suspended, and between them and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, there is a veil. They said: O Lord, will You send us down to Your earth and to one who disobeys You? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: By My might, I swear that none of My servants will recite you after every prayer except that I will make Paradise his abode, regardless of what he has done, and I will house him in the enclosure of holiness, and I will look upon him with My hidden Eye every day seventy times, and I will fulfill for him every day seventy needs, the least of which is forgiveness, and I will protect him from every enemy and envious one, and I will help him against them." [[We have not found this hadith in the books of Sunnah available to us. The author attributed it to al-Harith in his Musnad and weakened it.]] It was narrated by al-Harith from 'Amr, and it is weak.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 28:

His statement, exalted and majestic is He: ﴿Let not the believers take the disbelievers as allies rather than the believers﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Al-Hajjaj ibn ʿAmr ibn Abi al-Huqayq and Qays ibn Zayd were [[in B: "yuzannu" (they were suspecting) ... In al-Wahidi's Asbab al-Nuzul: "yubatinuna nafaran" (they were keeping secret ties with a group)]] (they were keeping secret ties) with a group of the Ansar, seeking to lead them astray from their religion. Rifa'ah ibn al-Mundhir, ʿAbd Allah ibn Jubayr and Saʿid ibn Khaythamah said to those men: "Avoid these Jews, lest they lead you astray from your religion." But those men refused, except to maintain their secret friendship with them, so Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah and others, who used to show affection to the disbelievers of Makkah.

Al-Kalbi said, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them): It was revealed concerning the hypocrites, ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions. They used to take the Jews and the polytheists as allies, bring them news, and hope that they would gain victory over the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed this verse and forbade the believers from the like of their conduct.

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever does that﴾, that is, allying with the disbelievers by conveying news to them and disclosing the weaknesses of the Muslims to them, ﴿then he has nothing to do with Allah in anything﴾ [i.e., he has nothing to do with the religion of Allah in anything]. [[Omitted from A.]] Then He made an exception, saying: ﴿except when you fear a danger from them﴾, meaning: except when you fear them with a real fear. Mujahid and Yaʿqub read "taqiyyah" (تَقِيَّةً) on the pattern of baqiyyah, because they wrote it with a yā' and not with an alif, like ḥaṣāh and nawāh. It is a verbal noun: one says taqaytuhu (تقيته) taqatan (تُقَاةً), and taqa taqiyyatan and taqwan (تَقًى تَقِيَّةً وَتَقْوًى). When you say ittaqaytu, the verbal noun is al-ittiqa' (الِاتِّقَاء). He said "tattaqu" from ittiqa' and then said "tuqatan" and did not say "ittiqa'an," because when the meanings of two words are one, it is permissible to derive the verbal noun of one of them in the form of the other, as in His statement: ﴿And devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾ (73:8).

The meaning of the verse is that Allah, exalted is He, forbade the believers from allying with the disbelievers, flattering them and keeping secret friendship with them, except when the disbelievers are dominant and prevailing, or when the believer is among a disbelieving people whom he fears, so he placates them with his tongue while his heart is at rest in faith, to defend himself, provided he does not make lawful a forbidden blood or forbidden property, or disclose to the disbelievers the weaknesses of the Muslims. Taqiyyah is only permitted with fear of being killed and with the soundness of intention. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿except one who is forced while his heart remains firm in faith﴾ (16:106). This is a concession; so if he endures until he is killed, he has a great reward. Some people denied taqiyyah today [[in A: "to them"]]. Mu'adh ibn Jabal and Mujahid said: Taqiyyah existed at the beginning of Islam, before the religion was firmly established and the Muslims were strong. But today Allah has honoured Islam, so it is not fitting for the people of Islam to take precaution against their enemy. Yahya al-Bakka' said: I said to Saʿid ibn Jubayr during the days of al-Hajjaj: "Al-Hasan used to say to you that taqiyyah is with the tongue while the heart is at rest in faith?" Saʿid said: "There is no taqiyyah in Islam; taqiyyah is only with the people of war."

﴿And Allah warns you of Himself﴾, that is, Allah frightens you with His punishment for allying with the disbelievers, committing what is forbidden, and opposing what is commanded. ﴿And to Allah is the final return.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 29–30:

﴿Say: Whether you conceal what is in your breasts﴾ that is, your hearts, of love for the disbelievers ﴿or reveal it﴾, their allegiance, in word and deed, ﴿Allah knows it﴾. Al-Kalbi said: whether you keep secret what is in your hearts toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of denial, or you manifest it, by warring against him and fighting him, Allah knows it and preserves it against you until He requites you for it. Then He said: ﴿And He knows﴾, it is in the nominative case, as a resumption (al-isti'naf, a new independent clause) ﴿what is in the heavens and what is in the earth﴾, meaning: if nothing is hidden from Him in the heavens or in the earth, then how could your allegiance to the disbelievers and your inclination toward them in the heart be hidden from Him? ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent﴾.

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day every soul will find﴾. Yawm (day) is in the accusative case by removing the preposition of the relation, that is, "on the day"; it was also said: by supposing a verb, that is, "Remember and fear the Day every soul will find" ﴿what it has done of good present﴾, nothing of it will be diminished, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they will find what they did present﴾ (18:49). ﴿And what it has done of evil﴾: some of them made it a predicate in the place of the accusative, meaning: it will find present what it did of good [and evil, so it will be gladdened by what it did of good] [[Omitted from B.]]. Others made it a new independent clause, and the evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them both: "And what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that there were a far distance."

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿It wishes that between it﴾, that is, between the soul, ﴿and between it﴾, meaning, and between the evil, ﴿a far distance﴾. Al-Suddi said: a far place. Muqatil said: as far as between the east and the west. Al-amad is the term and the limit to which one arrives. Al-Hasan said: it pleases one of them that he never encounters his deed. It was also said: it wishes that it had not done it. ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to the servants﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 29–30:

﴿Say: Whether you conceal what is in your breasts﴾ that is, your hearts, of love for the disbelievers ﴿or reveal it﴾, their allegiance, in word and deed, ﴿Allah knows it﴾. Al-Kalbi said: whether you keep secret what is in your hearts toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of denial, or you manifest it, by warring against him and fighting him, Allah knows it and preserves it against you until He requites you for it. Then He said: ﴿And He knows﴾, it is in the nominative case, as a resumption (al-isti'naf, a new independent clause) ﴿what is in the heavens and what is in the earth﴾, meaning: if nothing is hidden from Him in the heavens or in the earth, then how could your allegiance to the disbelievers and your inclination toward them in the heart be hidden from Him? ﴿And Allah is over all things Competent﴾.

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day every soul will find﴾. Yawm (day) is in the accusative case by removing the preposition of the relation, that is, "on the day"; it was also said: by supposing a verb, that is, "Remember and fear the Day every soul will find" ﴿what it has done of good present﴾, nothing of it will be diminished, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they will find what they did present﴾ (18:49). ﴿And what it has done of evil﴾: some of them made it a predicate in the place of the accusative, meaning: it will find present what it did of good [and evil, so it will be gladdened by what it did of good] [[Omitted from B.]]. Others made it a new independent clause, and the evidence for this interpretation is the reading of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them both: "And what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that there were a far distance."

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿It wishes that between it﴾, that is, between the soul, ﴿and between it﴾, meaning, and between the evil, ﴿a far distance﴾. Al-Suddi said: a far place. Muqatil said: as far as between the east and the west. Al-amad is the term and the limit to which one arrives. Al-Hasan said: it pleases one of them that he never encounters his deed. It was also said: it wishes that it had not done it. ﴿And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to the servants﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 3, verses 31–32:**

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: If you love Allah, then follow me; Allah will love you﴾. It was revealed concerning the Jews and the Christians, when they said: "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved ones" [[Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi: p. 135.]].

Al-Dahhak related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: The Prophet ﷺ stood over the Quraysh while they were in the Masjid al-Haram, having set up their idols, hung ostrich eggs on them, and put earrings (al-shunuf) [[Earrings.]] in their ears, while they prostrated to them. He said: "O assembly of Quraysh! By Allah, you have opposed the religion (millah) of your father Ibrahim and Isma'il!" [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit, 2/431. In the narration of al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas there is some obscurity; see also Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 135.]] Then the Quraysh said to him: "We only worship them out of love for Allah, so that they may bring us closer to Allah in nearness (zulfa)." So Allah the Exalted said: "Say, O Muhammad: If you love Allah and worship the idols so that they bring you near to Him, then follow me, and Allah will love you. I am His messenger to you and His proof against you." That is, follow my law (shari'ah) and my way (sunnah), and Allah will love you. The love of the believers for Allah is their following of His command, their preference for His obedience, and their seeking His pleasure. The love of Allah for the believers is His praise of them, His reward for them, and His pardon of them. This is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And will forgive you your sins; and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

It was also said that when this verse was revealed, 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy said to his companions: "Muhammad makes his obedience like the obedience of Allah, and he commands us to love him as the Christians loved 'Isa ibn Maryam." Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and the Messenger; but if they turn away﴾, meaning they turn away from obeying them both, ﴿then indeed Allah does not love the disbelievers﴾, meaning He does not approve their deed and does not forgive them.

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Muhammad ibn Sinan informed us: Fulayh informed us: Hilal ibn 'Ali informed us, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "All of my nation will enter Paradise except the one who refuses." They said: "And who would refuse?" He said: "Whoever obeys me enters Paradise, and whoever disobeys me has refused." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-I'tisam, Chapter: Following the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, 13/249. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 1/192–193.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Ubadah informed us: Yazid informed us: Sulaym ibn Hayyan [and he praised him] [[Omitted from manuscript B.]] informed us: Sa'id ibn Mina' said: "He narrated to us, or I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: Angels came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was asleep. Some of them said: 'He is asleep.' Others said: 'The eyes are asleep but the heart is awake.' Then they said: 'Indeed, there is a parable for your companion here, so strike a parable for him.' They said: 'His likeness is that of a man who built a house, placed in it a feast, and sent a summoner. Whoever answers the summoner enters the house and eats from the feast, and whoever does not answer the summoner does not enter the house and does not eat from the feast.' Then they said: 'Explain it to him so that he may understand.' They said: 'As for the house, it is Paradise; the summoner is Muhammad ﷺ. Whoever obeys Muhammad has obeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys Muhammad has disobeyed Allah. And Muhammad ﷺ is the one who distinguishes between people.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-I'tisam, Chapter: Following the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, 13/249. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah, 1/192–193.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 33–34:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah﴾ [Qur'an 3:33], to the end of the verse. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: The Jews said, "We are from the descendants of Ibrahim (Abraham), Ishaq (Isaac) and Ya'qub (Jacob), and we are upon their religion." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. That is, Allah chose these people for Islam, while you are upon other than the religion of Islam. ﴿Chose (isţafā)﴾ means selected; it is of the form ifta'ala, derived from ṣafwa (ṣafwah), which is the pure essence of everything. ﴿Adam﴾ is the father of mankind; ﴿and Noah, and the family of Ibrahim, and the family of 'Imran﴾. It has been said: by "the family of Ibrahim and the family of 'Imran" He meant Ibrahim and 'Imran themselves, as in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And a remnant of what the family of Musa and the family of Harun left behind﴾ [Qur'an 2:248], meaning Musa and Harun.

And others said: The family of Ibrahim are Isma'il, Ishaq, Ya'qub and the Tribes (al-Asbat), and Muhammad ﷺ was from the family of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. As for the family of 'Imran, Muqatil said: he is 'Imran ibn Yashhar ibn Qahath ibn Lawi ibn Ya'qub, peace be upon him, the father of Musa and Harun. Al-Hasan and Wahb said: he is 'Imran ibn Ashham ibn Amun, from the descendants of Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon them both, the father of Maryam and 'Isa. It has also been said: 'Imran ibn Mathan. He specified these people for mention because all the prophets and messengers are from their offspring. ﴿Descendants, one of another﴾ [Qur'an 3:34]. Its derivation is from dhara'a, meaning he created. It has also been said: it is from dharr, because He brought them forth from the loins of Adam like tiny particles (dharr), and offspring and fathers are both called dhurriyyah. So the sons are dhurriyyah because He created them, and the fathers are dhurriyyah because He created the sons from them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And a sign for them is that We carried their dhurriyyah﴾ [Qur'an 36:41], meaning their fathers.

﴿Dhurriyyah﴾ is in the accusative on the meaning of "and He chose descendants." ﴿Some of them from others﴾, that is, some of them are from the offspring of others. It has been said: some of them are from others in support (al-tanasur); it has also been said: some of them are upon the religion of others. ﴿And Allah is Hearing, Knowing﴾.

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 35:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When the wife of Imran said﴾. She was Hannah bint Faqudha, the mother of Maryam (Mary). Imran was Imran ibn Mathan, not Imran the father of Musa (Moses), peace be upon him. Between them there were eighty-one hundred years [1080 years]. The sons of Mathan were the leaders of the Children of Israel, their rabbis and their kings. It is also said: Imran ibn Ashham.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿My Lord, I have vowed to You what is in my womb, dedicated [to Your service]﴾, meaning: I have made what is in my womb dedicated, a vow from me to You. ﴿So accept it from me. Indeed You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾. The nadhr (vow) is what a person makes obligatory upon himself. ﴿Muharraran﴾ means freed, purely devoted to God, set apart for the worship of God and the service of the church (kanisah), so that I will not occupy him with anything of this world. Everything that is made pure is muharrar; it is said: I freed (harrartu) the slave when I manumitted him and released him from bondage.

Al-Kalbi, Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others said: When the muharrar was freed, he was placed in the church, where he would attend to it, sweep it and serve it, and he would not leave it until he reached puberty. Then he was given a choice: if he wished, he would remain, and if he wished, he could go wherever he liked. But if he wanted to leave after being given the choice, that was not permitted for him. Every one of the prophets and scholars had among his descendants someone dedicated to Bayt al-Maqdis (the Holy House, Jerusalem). Only boys were dedicated, and a girl was not suitable for this because of the menstruation and harm that befalls her. So the mother of Maryam dedicated what was in her womb.

The account behind this is that Zakariyya and Imran had married two sisters. Ashya' bint Faqudha, the mother of Yahya, was married to Zakariyya, and Hannah bint Faqudha, the mother of Maryam, was married to Imran. Hannah had been without a child until she grew old, and they were a family held in high regard with God. While she was sitting in the shade of a tree, she saw a bird feeding its young, and her soul was stirred with longing for a child. So she prayed to God to grant her a child and said: O God, I vow to You that if You provide me with a child, I will give him in charity to Bayt al-Maqdis so that he will be among its custodians and servants. She then conceived Maryam and dedicated what was in her womb, not knowing what it was. Her husband said to her: Woe to you, what have you done? Do you not consider that if what is in your womb is a female, she is not fit for this? The two of them then fell into anxiety over this, and Imran died while Hannah was pregnant with Maryam.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on surah 3, verse 36:

﴿When she gave birth to her﴾, that is, she bore her, and behold, it was a female. The pronoun in His saying "waḍaʿat-hā" (she gave birth to her) refers to the *al-nadhīr* (the vowed offering), not to what was born; for this reason it was made feminine. ﴿She said﴾, Hannah, and she had hoped it would be a boy. ﴿My Lord, I have given birth to a female﴾, as an apology to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And Allah knows best what she gave birth to﴾, with the *tā'* of *waḍaʿat* given a *jazm* (sukun), as a report from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is the reading of the majority. Ibn ʿĀmir, Abu Bakr and Yaʿqub read *waḍaʿtu* with a *raf'* (damma) on the *tā'*, making it part of the speech of Maryam's mother. ﴿And the male is not like the female﴾ in serving the church and the worshippers in it, because of her *ʿawrah* (nakedness, i.e. her vulnerability), her weakness, and what befalls her of menstruation and postpartum bleeding. ﴿And I have named her Maryam﴾. *Maryam* in their language means "the worshipper" and "the servant." Maryam was the most beautiful of the women of her time and the best of them. ﴿And I seek refuge for her﴾, I protect her and grant her safe keeping, ﴿in You, and for her offspring﴾, her children, ﴿from the accursed Satan﴾. *Al-shayṭān* is the expelled, cursed one, and *al-rajīm* is the one pelted with shooting stars.

Akhbaranā ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Mulayḥī, who said: Anā Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Nuʿaymī, who said: Anā Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf, who said: Anā Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, who said: Anā Abu al-Yamān, who said: Anā Shuʿayb, from al-Zuhrī, who said: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me, and he said: Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There is no child of Adam born but that Satan touches him when he is born, so the infant cries out loudly from the touch of Satan, except Maryam and her son." Then Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) recited: "And I seek refuge for her in You, and for her offspring, from the accursed Satan." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in *al-Tafsir*, *Tafsir Surat Āl ʿImrān*, chapter: "And I seek refuge for her…", 8/212. Also narrated by Muslim in *al-Faḍāʾil*, chapter on the virtues of ʿĪsā, no. (2366), 4/1838. And the author in *Sharḥ al-Sunnah*: 14/406.]]

Akhbaranā ʿAbd al-Wāḥid al-Mulayḥī, who said: Anā Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Nuʿaymī, who said: Anā Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf, who said: Anā Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, who said: Anā Abu al-Yamān, who said: Anā Shuʿayb, from Abu al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every child of Adam, Satan pokes him in his side with his finger when he is born, except ʿĪsā son of Maryam. He went to poke him, but he poked the veil." [[Narrated by Imam Aḥmad in *al-Musnad* from Abu Hurayra, 2/523. And al-Ṭabarī in *al-Tafsir*: 6/342. Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in *al-Bidāya wa-l-Nihāya* from Imam Aḥmad, 2/57, and said: "This is on the condition of the two *Ṣaḥīḥs*, though they did not record it by this route." And see the note of Shaykh Maḥmūd Shākir on al-Ṭabarī's *Tafsīr*, 6/342.]]

The commentary of Allah's words ﴿So her Lord accepted her with a goodly acceptance﴾ means: Allah accepted Maryam from Hannah in place of the one dedicated. "Tqabbala" means the same as "qabila" and "radiya" (to accept and be pleased). "Al-qabul" is the verbal noun (masdar) of "qabila, yaqbalu, qabulan," like "al-wuluʿ," "al-wuzuʿ," and no other form beyond these three has come. It was also said: the meaning of "tqabbul" is taking responsibility for her upbringing and attending to her affairs. ﴿And He made her grow a goodly growth﴾: its meaning is, "He made her grow, and she grew a goodly growth." It was also said that this is a verbal noun (masdar) not from the same root as the verb (ʿala ghayr al-lafz) [[In B: al-masdar.]]. The same applies to His words ﴿So her Lord accepted her with a goodly acceptance﴾ [and its like is common, as when you say "takallamtu kalaman" (I spoke a speech). Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: ﴿So her Lord accepted her with a goodly acceptance﴾] [[Omitted in A.]], meaning: He placed her on the path of the fortunate. ﴿And He made her grow a goodly growth﴾: that is, He made her physical form balanced, without excess or deficiency, so that she would grow in a day what a newborn grows in a year. ﴿And Zakariyya took charge of her﴾. The people of narratives (ahl al-akhbar) said: When Hannah gave birth to Maryam, she wrapped her in a cloth and carried her to the mosque, and placed her with the rabbis (al-ahbar), the sons of Harun. At that time they were in charge of Bayt al-Maqdis in the same way that the keepers (al-hijaba) were in charge of the Kaʿba. She said to them, "Take this offering (al-nadhira)." The rabbis competed for her, because she was the daughter of their imam and the one who offered their sacrifices. Zakariyya said to them, "I have the most right to her, for her maternal aunt is with me." The rabbis said, "We will not do that. If she were left with the person most entitled to her, she would be left with her mother who bore her. Rather, we will draw lots over her, and she will be with whoever's lot comes out." So they went, and they were twenty-nine [[In B: twenty-seven.]] men, to a flowing river. Al-Suddi said: it was the river Jordan. They cast their pens into the water, on the condition that whoever's pen remained in the water and rose up would be most entitled to her.

It was also said: each pen bore the name of one of them.

It was also said: they used to write the Torah, so they cast into the water the pens that were in their hands, and Zakariyya's pen [was stuck in the water] [[In B: it was stuck in it firmly.]] and rose above the water, while their pens sank and went down into the river. This was related by Muhammad ibn Ishaq and a group.

It was also said: Zakariyya's pen flowed upward against the water, and their pens flowed with the current.

Al-Suddi and a group said: rather, Zakariyya's pen remained fixed and stood above the water as if it were in mud, while their pens flowed with the current of the water, so the water carried them away. Thus it determined the lot against them, and Zakariyya drew the lot. Zakariyya was the head of the rabbis and their prophet. This is the meaning of His words, exalted is He, ﴿And Zakariyya took charge of her﴾. Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Asim read it with a doubled fa' (wa-kaffalaha), so Zakariyya is in the accusative position, meaning: Allah entrusted her to Zakariyya and assigned her to him by lot. The others read it with a single fa' (wa-kafalaha), so Zakariyya is in the nominative position, meaning: Zakariyya took her into his own care and attended to her affairs. He is Zakariyya ibn Adhan ibn Muslim ibn Sadduq, one of the descendants of Sulayman ibn Dawud, peace be upon them both.

Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Hafs, from Asim, read "Zakariyya" with a short vowel (maqsur), while the others read it with a long vowel (mamdud).

When Zakariyya took Maryam into his own care, he built a chamber (bayt) for her and arranged for her to be nursed. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: he placed her with her maternal aunt, Umm Yahya, until she grew up and reached the age of women. Then he built her a mihrab in the mosque, its door placed in the middle of it, which could only be reached by a ladder, like the door of the Kaʿba, so that no one else could climb to it. He used to bring her food, drink and oil every day. ﴿Whenever Zakariyya entered upon her in the mihrab﴾. By "mihrab" is meant the upper room. The mihrab is the most honoured place of a gathering and its front, and likewise it is part of the mosque. The mosque is also called a mihrab. Al-Mubarrad said: a mihrab is not so called unless one ascends to it by steps. Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas said: when Zakariyya went out he would lock seven doors on her, and when he entered upon her in her upper room ﴿he found with her provision﴾, that is, fruit out of its season: summer fruit in winter, and winter fruit in summer. ﴿He said, "O Maryam, from where is this for you?"﴾ Abu ʿUbayda said: its meaning is "min ayna laki hadha?" (from where is this for you?). Some of them objected to him and said: its meaning is "min ayya jihatin laki hadha?" (from which direction is this for you?), because "anna" is used to ask about the direction, and "ayna" is used to ask about the place. ﴿She said, "It is from Allah."﴾ That is, from the fruit of Paradise. Al-Hasan said: when Maryam was born she never took a breast, and her provision came to her from Paradise. Zakariyya would say to her, "From where is this for you?" and she would say, "It is from Allah." She spoke while she was still a child. ﴿Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning.﴾

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: then Bani Isra'il were struck by a famine, while she remained in her condition, until Zakariyya was too weak to carry her. He went out to the Bani Isra'il and said, "O Bani Isra'il, you know, by Allah, that my age has grown great and I have become too weak to bear Maryam bint ʿImran. Which of you will take charge of her after me?" They said, "By Allah, we have struggled and the drought has struck us as you see." So they pushed her onto one another, but then they found no way other than carrying her, so they drew lots over her with the pens. The lot came out upon a carpenter from the Bani Isra'il called Yusuf ibn Yaʿqub, who was a cousin of Maryam. So he carried her. Maryam perceived in his face the severity of this burden upon him, and she said to him, "O Yusuf, think well of Allah, for Allah will provide for us." Then Yusuf began to be provided for on account of her presence with him. Every day he would bring her from his earnings what would suffice her, and when he brought it in to her in the church, Allah made it grow. Then Zakariyya would enter upon her and see with her a surplus of provision, not in proportion to what Yusuf brought her, and he would say, "O Maryam, from where is this for you?" She would say, "It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without reckoning." [[See Sirat Ibn Hisham: 2/49, which mentions the story in abridged form from Ibn Ishaq without an isnad, and in which the lot is said to have come out upon Jurayj the monk.]]

The people of narratives said: When Zakariyya saw that, he said, "Indeed, He who is able to bring Maryam fruit out of its season, without any cause, is able to set right my wife and grant me a child out of its time, despite my old age." So he hoped for a child. This was because the members of his household had died out, and Zakariyya had grown old and despaired of having a child.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 38–39:

God Most High said: ﴿There, Zachariah called upon his Lord﴾, that is, at that moment. ﴿He said, "My Lord"﴾, that is, "O my Lord, ﴿grant me﴾, that is, give me, ﴿from Yourself﴾, that is, from Your presence, ﴿a good offspring﴾, that is, a blessed, pious, righteous and pleasing child." The word dhurriyyah (offspring) may be singular or plural, masculine or feminine, and here it is singular, as shown by His saying: ﴿So grant me from Yourself a guardian﴾ (Maryam 19:5). He said "good" (tayyibah) in the feminine because of the feminine form of the word dhurriyyah. ﴿Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication﴾, that is, the one who hears it. It is also said that it means the one who answers it, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me﴾ (Ya-Sin 36:25), that is, respond to me.

﴿Then the angels called to him﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read fa-nadahu (with the ya', "he called him"), while the others read fa-nadathu (with the ta', "she called him"). Whoever reads with the ta' does so because the word "angels" (al-mala'ikah) is feminine in form, and also because when the verb of a group of males comes first, the feminine form is better, as in His saying: ﴿The bedouins say﴾ (al-Hujurat 49:14).

It is reported from Ibrahim that he said: "Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, used to make the word for angels masculine in the Qur'an." Abu Ubaydah said: "We see that Abdullah chose this in opposition to the polytheists who said that the angels are the daughters of Allah, Exalted." It is also narrated that al-Sha'bi reported that Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "If you differ regarding the ta' and the ya', then make it ya' and make the Qur'an masculine."

By "the angels" here he means Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him, alone, as in His saying in Surat al-Nahl: ﴿He sends down the angels﴾ (16:2), meaning Jibril, ﴿with the Spirit﴾, that is, with the revelation. In Arabic it is permissible to refer to a single person with a plural expression, as when people say: "I heard this report from the people," though he heard it from one person. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿Those to whom the people said﴾ (Ali 'Imran 3:173), meaning Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud, and "the people" meaning Abu Sufyan ibn Harb. Al-Mufaddal ibn Salamah said: "When the speaker is a leader, it is permissible to refer to him with a plural, because his companions are with him. Jibril, peace be upon him, was the chief of the angels, and he was rarely sent except with a group, so this usage followed that pattern."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿while he was standing in prayer in the mihrab﴾ (the prayer niche, a place of worship, here the inner sanctuary of the mosque), that is, in the mosque. Zachariah was the great rabbi who offered the sacrifices. He would open the door of the altar, and they would not enter until he gave them permission to enter. So while he was standing in prayer in the mihrab, that is, in the mosque, near the altar, praying, the people were waiting for him to permit them to enter. Then he saw a young man wearing white garments, and he was frightened by him, so he called to him. This was Jibril, peace be upon him, saying: "O Zachariah, ﴿indeed Allah gives you good news﴾." Ibn 'Amir and Hamzah read inna (with a kasrah on the alif), by implying a verb of saying, the meaning being: "the angels called to him and said, 'Indeed Allah gives you good news.'" The others read it with a fatha, by making the calling govern it, as if he said: "the angels called to him that Allah gives you good news." Hamzah read yubshuruka and its like throughout the Qur'an with light pronunciation (yubshiruka, without doubling), except for His saying: ﴿So with what do you give good news?﴾ (al-Hijr 15:54), where they agreed on doubling it. al-Kisa'i agreed with him here in both places, and in Surat Subhan, al-Kahf and 'Asq. Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr agreed with him in 'Asq. The rest read it with doubling. Whoever reads with doubling, it is from bashshara, yubashshiru, tabshiran, and this is the most eloquent and clearest of the dialects. The evidence for doubling is His saying: ﴿So give good news to My servants﴾ (al-Zumar 39:17), ﴿And We gave him good news of Isaac﴾ (al-Saffat 37:112), ﴿They said, "We have given you good news of the truth"﴾ (al-Hijr 15:55), and other verses. Whoever reads with light pronunciation, it is from basara, yabsuru, which is the dialect of Tihamah. Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, read it as ﴿Yahya﴾. It is a name that is not declined, because of its definiteness and the extra letter at its beginning, like Yazid and Ya'mur. Its plural is yahyawun, like Musawun and 'Isawun.

They differed about why he was named Yahya. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Because Allah brought life through him to the barren womb of his mother." Qatadah said: "Because Allah gave life to his heart with faith." It is also said: "Because Allah gave him life through obedience, so that he never disobeyed and never intended a sin."

﴿Confirming﴾ is in the accusative as a state (hal). ﴿A word from Allah﴾, meaning 'Isa, peace be upon him. 'Isa was called "the word of Allah" because Allah Most High said to him: "Be," without a father, and he was. So the name "the word" was applied to him, because by it he came into being. It is also said that he was called "word" because he is guided by it, just as one is guided by the speech of Allah Most High. It is also said that it is the good news from Allah Most High to Maryam about 'Isa, peace be upon him, through His speech by the tongue of Jibril, peace be upon him. And it is said: because Allah Most High informed the prophets, in His books, of His word that He would create a prophet without a father, and so He called him a "word" because he came into being through that promise. Yahya, peace be upon him, was the first to believe in 'Isa, peace be upon him, and confirm him. Yahya, peace be upon him, was six months older than 'Isa, and they were maternal cousins. Then Yahya was killed before 'Isa, peace be upon him, was raised up.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: ﴿a word from Allah﴾ means "a book from Allah and His signs." The Arabs say: "Recite to me the word of so-and-so," meaning his poem.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and a master﴾ is an intensive form (fa'il) from sada, yasudu, and it means the leader who is followed and to whose word people turn. Al-Mufaddal said: "He meant a master in religion." Al-Dahhak said: "The master is the one of good character." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The master is the one who obeys his Lord, Mighty and Majestic." Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "The master is the jurist, the scholar." Qatadah said: "A master in knowledge, worship and scrupulousness." It is also said: "the forbearing one whom nothing angers." Mujahid said: "the noble one before Allah Most High." Al-Dahhak said: "The master is the pious one." Sufyan al-Thawri said: "The one who does not envy." It is also said: "The one who surpasses his people in all the qualities of goodness." It is also said: "He is the one content with what Allah has apportioned to him." It is also said: "the generous one." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Who is your master, O Banu Salamah?" They said: "Jadd ibn Qays, though we consider him stingy." He said: "What disease is worse than stinginess? Rather, your master is 'Amr ibn al-Jamuh." [This hadith has been narrated through several chains from Jabir, Abu Hurayrah and Anas, marfu' (traced to the Prophet), and it has been narrated mursal (with a missing companion) from Habib ibn Abi Thabit from the Prophet (ﷺ). It was recorded by al-Bukhari in al-Adab al-Mufrad, p. 90, published by Maktabat al-Adab; by Abu al-Shaykh al-Isbahani in Kitab al-Amthal, no. 89–95, pp. 56–59; by Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah, 7/317; and by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak, 3/219, from Abu Hurayrah, with the wording: "Rather, your master is al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur," and he said: "Sahih according to the condition of Muslim." Al-Haythami said: "It was narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except the teacher of al-Tabarani" (Majma' al-Zawa'id, 3/315). See also: al-Isabah of Ibn Hajar, 4/615–616; Usd al-Ghabah of Ibn al-Athir, 4/206–207; Majma' al-Zawa'id, 9/314–315.]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and chaste, and a prophet from among the righteous﴾. Al-hasur (chaste) is originally from al-hasr, which means confinement. According to the saying of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, Ibn 'Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Qatadah, 'Ata' and al-Hasan, may Allah be pleased with them, al-hasur is the one who does not come to women nor approach them. On this view it is the form fa'ul in the sense of fa'il, meaning that he restrains himself from desires. [It is also said: he is the poor man who has no wealth.] Thus al-hasur would mean "the one who is restrained (mahsur)," that is, prevented from women. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: "He had something like the fringe of a garment, and he married nonetheless, so that he would lower his gaze more." There is another view: that al-hasur is the one who refrains from intercourse while being able to do it. A group chose this view for two reasons. The first: the statement came in the form of praise, and this is closer to deserving praise. The second: it keeps a defect further away from the prophets.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 40:

His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿My Lord﴾, meaning: O my master. He said this to Jibril (peace be upon him). This is the saying of al-Kalbi and a group, and it was said: he said it to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. ﴿How can there be for me a boy﴾, meaning: where (ana) can there be for me a son, ﴿and I have already reached old age﴾. This is from the inverted usage (al-maqlub), meaning: I have already reached old age and become decrepit, just as one says "al-jahd balaghani" (hardship has reached me), meaning: I am in hardship. And it was said: its meaning is "and old age has reached me," and it overtook me and weakened me. Al-Kalbi said: Zakariyya, on the day he was given the good news of a child, was ninety-two years old. It was also said: ninety-nine years old. Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he was one hundred and twenty years old, and his wife was ninety-eight years old. This is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿and my wife is barren﴾, meaning: unable to bear children. It is said: "rajul 'aqir" and "imra'ah 'aqir" (a barren man and a barren woman), and "qad 'aqura" with the qaf vowelled with a damma, "ya'quru 'uqran" and "'uqarah" (she became barren). ﴿He said: Thus Allah does what He wills﴾.

If it is asked: why did Zakariyya say, after Allah had promised him, ﴿How can there be for me a boy?﴾ Was he doubting Allah's promise and His power? It is answered: when Zakariyya heard the call of the angels, Satan came to him and said: "O Zakariyya, the voice you heard is not from Allah; it is from Satan. Had it been from Allah, He would have revealed it to you as He reveals to you in all other matters." So he said that to repel the whispering. This was reported by Ikrimah and al-Suddi. Another answer: he did not doubt Allah's promise; he only questioned its manner, i.e., how would that be?

**The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 3, verses 41–42:**

Allah's words, ﴿He said: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign."﴾ means: a sign by which I may know the time of my wife's conception, so that I may increase in worship in gratitude to You.

﴿He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people"﴾ means you will refrain from speech ﴿for three days,﴾ and you will devote yourself wholly to My worship. It does not mean that his tongue was restrained from speech. Rather, it was a prohibition against speaking, while he remained sound and well, as He said in Surah Maryam, verse 10: ﴿that you will not speak to the people for three nights while being sound.﴾ This is supported by Allah's words, ﴿And glorify [Him] in the evening and the morning,﴾ so He commanded him to remember Him and forbade him from speaking to people.

Most of the exegetes (mufassirun) said: his tongue was restrained from speaking with people for three days. Qatadah said: He held back his tongue from speech as a punishment for asking for the sign after the angels had spoken to him directly, so he was unable to speak for three days. As for Allah's words, ﴿except by gesture (ramzan)﴾, ramz means a signal. A signal may be made with the tongue, the eye, or the hand, and his signal was with the index finger. Al-Farra' said: ramz may be made with the tongue without clear articulation, being a hidden sound resembling a whisper. Ata' said: by it He meant fasting for three days, because when they fasted they would not speak except by gesture.

﴿And remember your Lord much and glorify [Him] in the evening and the morning.﴾ It has been said that the glorification (tasbih) here means prayer. Al-'Ashiyy is the period between the decline of the sun and its setting, and from this the midday (Zuhr) and afternoon ('Asr) prayers are called the two prayers of the 'ashiyy. Al-Ibkar is the period from the Fajr prayer until the forenoon (duha).

Allah's words: ﴿And when the angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you"﴾, meaning, He has selected you, ﴿and purified you,﴾ it has been said from being touched by men. It has also been said from menstruation and postnatal bleeding. Al-Suddi said: Mary did not menstruate. It has also been said: from sins. ﴿And has chosen you above the women of the worlds.﴾ It has been said: above the women of her own time. It has also been said: above all the women of the worlds in that she bore a child without a father, which was not granted to any other woman. And it has been said: in being dedicated (tahrir) in the mosque, and no female had been dedicated before her.

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi related to us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, Ahmad ibn Raja' related to us, al-Nadr related to us, from Hisham, who said: my father related to me, who said: I heard Abd Allah ibn Ja'far say: I heard Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The best of its women is Maryam bint 'Imran, and the best of its women is Khadijah" (may Allah be pleased with both of them).

**The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 3, verses 41–42:**

Allah's words, ﴿He said: "My Lord, appoint for me a sign."﴾ means: a sign by which I may know the time of my wife's conception, so that I may increase in worship in gratitude to You.

﴿He said: "Your sign is that you will not speak to the people"﴾ means you will refrain from speech ﴿for three days,﴾ and you will devote yourself wholly to My worship. It does not mean that his tongue was restrained from speech. Rather, it was a prohibition against speaking, while he remained sound and well, as He said in Surah Maryam, verse 10: ﴿that you will not speak to the people for three nights while being sound.﴾ This is supported by Allah's words, ﴿And glorify [Him] in the evening and the morning,﴾ so He commanded him to remember Him and forbade him from speaking to people.

Most of the exegetes (mufassirun) said: his tongue was restrained from speaking with people for three days. Qatadah said: He held back his tongue from speech as a punishment for asking for the sign after the angels had spoken to him directly, so he was unable to speak for three days. As for Allah's words, ﴿except by gesture (ramzan)﴾, ramz means a signal. A signal may be made with the tongue, the eye, or the hand, and his signal was with the index finger. Al-Farra' said: ramz may be made with the tongue without clear articulation, being a hidden sound resembling a whisper. Ata' said: by it He meant fasting for three days, because when they fasted they would not speak except by gesture.

﴿And remember your Lord much and glorify [Him] in the evening and the morning.﴾ It has been said that the glorification (tasbih) here means prayer. Al-'Ashiyy is the period between the decline of the sun and its setting, and from this the midday (Zuhr) and afternoon ('Asr) prayers are called the two prayers of the 'ashiyy. Al-Ibkar is the period from the Fajr prayer until the forenoon (duha).

Allah's words: ﴿And when the angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you"﴾, meaning, He has selected you, ﴿and purified you,﴾ it has been said from being touched by men. It has also been said from menstruation and postnatal bleeding. Al-Suddi said: Mary did not menstruate. It has also been said: from sins. ﴿And has chosen you above the women of the worlds.﴾ It has been said: above the women of her own time. It has also been said: above all the women of the worlds in that she bore a child without a father, which was not granted to any other woman. And it has been said: in being dedicated (tahrir) in the mosque, and no female had been dedicated before her.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 43:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord﴾. The angels spoke to her directly (shifahan), meaning: obey your Lord. Mujahid said: prolong the standing in prayer for your Lord. [And qunut means obedience.] [[Omitted from B.]] It was also said: qunut means prolonged standing. Al-Awza'i said: when the angels said that to her, she stood in prayer until her feet swelled and she secreted blood and pus. ﴿And prostrate yourself and bow down﴾. It was said: he mentioned prostration before bowing only because that was the order in their law (shari'ah). It was also said: rather, bowing came before prostration in all the laws, and the waw here does not denote sequence but mere combination, just as a man may say: "I saw Zayd and 'Amr," even if he saw 'Amr before Zayd. ﴿With those who bow down﴾. He did not say "with the female bowers" (ma'a al-raki'at), so that the expression would be more general and comprehensive, for it includes both men and women. It was also said: its meaning is "with those who pray in congregation."

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 3, verses 44–46:**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿That is among the tidings of the unseen. We reveal it to you.﴾ He says to Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿That﴾ which I have mentioned of the story of Zakariyya, Yahya, Maryam, and Isa, ﴿is among the tidings of the unseen,﴾ i.e., among the reports of the unseen. ﴿We reveal it to you.﴾ He returned the pronoun (al-kināya) to ﴿that,﴾ and so He mentioned it in this way. ﴿And you were not with them﴾ O Muhammad ﴿when they cast their pens﴾, meaning their arrows, into the water for the drawing of lots, ﴿to see which of them would take charge of Maryam,﴾ i.e., nurse her and raise her. ﴿And you were not with them when they disputed﴾ about her guardianship.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When the angels said, "O Maryam, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name is the Messiah, Isa, son of Maryam."﴾ He said "whose name" only to return the pronoun to Isa. They differed over why he was called "Masih" (the Messiah). Some said: it is fa'il in the sense of maf'ul (passive), meaning that he was wiped (masuh) of impurities and purified of sins. It was also said: because he was wiped with blessing. It was said: because he came out of his mother's womb anointed with oil. It was said: Jibril wiped him with his wing so that Satan had no path to him. It was said: because he had no arch to his foot (masih al-qadam, i.e., flat-footed, without a hollow sole). The Dajjal (the Antichrist) was called "Masih" because one of his eyes was wiped (blind). Others said it is fa'il in the sense of fa'il (active), like ʿALIM and ʿĀLIM (both meaning "knowing"). Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: he was called Masih because he did not wipe anyone afflicted with a disease except that he was healed. It was also said: he was named thus because he used to travel (yasih) across the earth and did not stay in one place; according to this view, the letter mim in it is extra. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: al-Masih means "the truthful." And "al-masih" can also mean "the liar," and by this sense the Dajjal was named; the word is among the words with opposite meanings (al-adḍād). ﴿Honoured﴾, i.e., noble, exalted, possessing rank and standing, ﴿in this world and the Hereafter, and among those brought near﴾ to Allah.

﴿And he will speak to people in the cradle﴾ as a child before the time of speech, as He mentioned in Surah Maryam, where he said: "Indeed, I am the servant of Allah; He has given me the Scripture" [19:30]. It is narrated from Mujahid, who said: Maryam said: "When I was alone with Isa, he would speak to me and I would speak to him; but when a person occupied me away from him, he would glorify Allah within my womb while I listened." [Note: This statement does not fit the text of the noble verse, and no one other than Mujahid held it; the author has related it in the form of weak reporting (bi-ṣīghat al-taḍʿīf).] As for His saying ﴿and in maturity﴾, Muqatil said: meaning when he reaches maturity before he is raised to the heaven. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: ﴿and in maturity﴾ refers to after his descent from the heaven. It was also said: He informed her that he would live until he reached middle age, and his speech after maturity is his reporting of miraculous matters. It was also said: ﴿and in maturity﴾ refers to his being a prophet, and He gave her the good news of the prophethood of Isa, peace be upon him; his speech in the cradle is a miracle, and his speech in maturity is a call (to faith). Mujahid said: ﴿and in maturity﴾ means forbearing (ḥalīm). The Arabs praise maturity because it is the middle state of age, the soundness of intellect, the soundness of judgment, and experience (ʿal-iḥtināk, i.e., the full development of age). ﴿And among the righteous.﴾

Meaning: he is among the righteous servants.

**"She said, 'My Lord!'"** (﴿قَالَتْ رَبِّ﴾): "My lord" (yā sayyidī), addressed to Jibril. It is also said that she was addressing Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. **"How can I have a son when no man has touched me?"** (﴿أَنَّى يَكُونُ لِي وَلَدٌ وَلَمْ يَمْسَسْنِي بَشَرٌ﴾): no man has come near me. She said this in wonder, since it had not been the custom for a child to be born without a father. **"He said, 'So it is. Allah creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.'"** (﴿قَالَ كَذَلِكِ اللَّهُ يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَاءُ إِذَا قَضَى أَمْرًا * فَإِنَّمَا يَقُولُ لَهُ كُنْ فَيَكُونُ﴾): that is, the coming-into-being of a thing, as He wills.

**His words, "And He will teach him the Book"** (﴿وَيُعَلِّمُهُ الْكِتَابَ﴾): The people of Madina, ʿĀṣim and Yaʿqūb read it with the *yāʾ* (third person, "He will teach him"), in keeping with the verse "So Allah creates what He wills." It is also said that it refers back to His words "Allah gives you good news" (﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُبَشِّرُكِ﴾), so that "He will teach him" follows from that. The others read it with the *nūn* (first person plural, "We will teach him"), as an expression of majesty, like His words "That is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you" (﴿ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَنْبَاءِ الْغَيْبِ نُوحِيهِ إِلَيْكَ﴾).

**"The Book"** (al-kitāb) means the writing and the script. **"And wisdom"** (al-ḥikmah) means knowledge and understanding (fiqh). **"And the Torah and the Gospel"**: Allah taught him the Torah and the Gospel.

**"And a messenger to the Children of Israel"** (﴿وَرَسُولًا إِلَى بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ﴾): that is, We will make him a messenger to the Children of Israel. It is said that he was a messenger while still a child, and it is also said that he became a messenger only after reaching maturity. The first of the prophets of the Children of Israel was Yūsuf (Joseph), and the last of them was ʿĪsā (Jesus), peace be upon them both. When he was sent, he said, **"That I..."** (﴿أَنِّي﴾). Al-Kisāʾī said: it is read with a *fatḥah* because the message fell upon him (i.e., the *anna* is governed by the verb of the message). It is also said that its meaning is "bi-anni" (with the fact that I). **"I have come to you with a sign"** (﴿قَدْ جِئْتُكُمْ بِآيَةٍ﴾), an indication, **"from your Lord"** (﴿مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ﴾), which confirms what I say. He said "a sign" (*āyah*) in the singular, although he brought several signs, because they all pointed to one thing, which is the truth of his message.

When ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, said this to the Children of Israel, they asked, "And what is it?" He said, **"That I..."** (﴿أَنِّي﴾). Nāfiʿ read it with a *kasrah* on the *alif* (*inni*), as a resumption (*istiʾnāf*, a new sentence). The rest read it with a *fatḥah*, in the sense of "bi-anni" (with the fact that I). **"Create"** (﴿أَخْلُقُ﴾): that is, I shape and determine. **"For you out of clay something like the form of a bird"** (﴿لَكُمْ مِنَ الطِّينِ كَهَيْئَةِ الطَّيْرِ﴾). He said: "On condition that Allah protects me from the agonies of death." So he called upon Allah, and it was done.

**His words, "And I tell you"** (﴿وَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾): and I inform you **"of what you eat"** (﴿بِمَا تَأْكُلُونَ﴾), of what I have not witnessed, **"and what you store up"** (﴿وَمَا تَدَّخِرُونَ﴾), what you keep **"in your houses"** (﴿فِي بُيُوتِكُمْ﴾), until you eat it. It is also said that he would tell a man what he had eaten the previous night, what he would eat that day, and what he had stored for supper.

Al-Suddī said: ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, was in the kuttāb (Qur'anic school), telling the boys what their fathers were doing. He would say to a boy: "Go, for your family has eaten such-and-such, and they have set aside such-and-such for you." The boy would go to his family, weeping for them, until they gave him that thing. They would say: "Who told you this?" He would say: "ʿĪsā." So they kept their children away from him and said: "Do not play with this sorcerer." They gathered them into a house. ʿĪsā, peace be upon him, came looking for them, and they said: "They are not here." He said: "What is in this house?" They said: "Pigs." ʿĪsā said: "So they shall be." They opened it, and there were pigs. This spread among the Children of Israel, and the Children of Israel resolved to kill him. When his mother feared for him, she carried him on her she-donkey and fled with him from them to the people of Egypt.

Qatādah said: this (story) is in al-Mā'idah, where there was a table (khiwān) that came down upon them wherever they were, like the manna and the quails. They were commanded not to betray it and not to store any of it for the next day, but they betrayed and stored. ʿĪsā would tell them what they had eaten from the table and what they had kept from it, and Allah transformed them into pigs.

**His words, "Indeed, in that"** (﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ﴾), which I have mentioned, **"is a sign for you, if you are believers"** (﴿لَآيَةً لَكُمْ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ﴾).

Abu 'Ubayda said: by "some" he meant "all", i.e., all that was forbidden to you. The word "some" may be used to mean "all", as in the verse of Labid:

*"A leaver of dwellings when I do not like them,
or some of the souls, their pigeons (death) seize."*

That is, "all souls."

[[Ibn Sida did not accept this, saying: "This is not, in my view, as the lexicographers claim, that 'some' means 'all'. This is a refutation, and there is no proof in this verse, because he only meant by 'some of the souls' his own soul." See: Lisan al-'Arab 7/119; Sharh al-Mu'allaqat al-Sab' by al-Anbari, p. 573.]]

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord﴾, meaning the signs that were mentioned. He used the singular because they are all one kind in indicating his prophethood. ﴿So fear Allah and obey me.﴾

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿When Jesus perceived disbelief from them﴾, i.e., found it. This is what al-Farra' said. Abu 'Ubayda said: he recognized it. Muqatil said: he saw it. ﴿From them, disbelief,﴾ and they intended to kill him, he sought help against them, and ﴿said: "Who are my helpers toward Allah?"﴾

Al-Suddi said: The reason for this was that when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Jesus, peace be upon him, to the Children of Israel and commanded him to call them, the Children of Israel rejected him and expelled him. So he went out with his mother, traveling through the land. He stopped in a town at the house of a man, who hosted them and treated them kindly. In that city there was a tyrannical, oppressive ruler. One day that man came, anxious and grieved, and entered his house, while Mary was with his wife. Mary said to her: "What is the matter with your husband? I see him dejected." She said: "Do not ask me." Mary said: "Tell me; perhaps Allah will relieve his distress." She said: "We have a king who imposes upon each man of us a day on which he must feed him and his soldiers and give them wine to drink; if he does not do so, he punishes him. Today is our turn, and we have no means for this." She said: "Then tell him not to be distressed, for I will command my son, and he will pray for him, and that will suffice." So Mary spoke to Jesus, peace be upon him, about this. Jesus said: "If I do that, evil will befall." She said: "Do not worry, for he has treated us well and honored us." Jesus, peace be upon him, said: "Then tell him, when that time draws near, to fill his cooking pots and jars with water, and then inform me." He did so, and Jesus, peace be upon him, prayed to Allah, and the water in the pots turned into broth and meat, and the water in the jars turned into wine, the like of which people had never seen. When the king came, he ate, and when he drank the wine he said: "From where is this wine?" He said: "From such-and-such a land." The king said: "My wine is from that land, and it is not like this." He said: "It is from another land." When the king was confused and pressed, he said: "I will inform you. With me is a youth who never asks Allah for anything without Him giving it to him, and he prayed to Allah, so He turned the water into wine." The king had a son whom he wished to make his successor, but he died a few days before that, and he was the most beloved of creation to him. So he said: "A man prayed to Allah until He turned the water into wine; let him be brought to me so that he may revive my son." So Jesus was called and spoke to him about that. Jesus said: "Do not do it, for if he lives, evil will befall." The king said: "I do not care. Do I not see him?" Jesus said: "If I revive him, will you leave me and my mother to go wherever we wish?" He said: "Yes." So he prayed to Allah, and the boy lived. When the people of his kingdom saw that he had come back to life, they rushed at them with weapons and said: "He ate us all this time, and now when his death approached he wants to make his son our ruler, so that he may eat us as his father did!" They fought, and Jesus and his mother departed. He passed by the disciples (al-hawariyyun, the close companions of Jesus), who were fishing. He said: "What are you doing?" They said: "We are fishing." He said: "Will you not come with me so that I may make you fishers of men?" They said: "Who are you?" He said: "I am Jesus son of Mary, the servant of Allah and His messenger. Who are my helpers toward Allah?" They believed in him and set off with him.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Who are my helpers toward Allah?﴾ Al-Suddi and Ibn Jurayj said: "with Allah," meaning "along with Allah." The Arabs say: "al-dawd ila al-dawd ibil," meaning "a group together with a group are camels." And as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And do not consume their property with your property﴾ (4:2), meaning "along with your property." Al-Hasan and Abu 'Ubayda said: "ila" here means "fi," i.e., "who are my helpers in Allah," that is, "in the cause of Allah and His path." It was also said: "ila" retains its own meaning, and the sense is: "who will add his support to the support of Allah for me?"

They differed concerning the disciples (al-hawariyyun). Mujahid and al-Suddi said: they were fishermen who fished for fish, and they were called hawariyyun because of the whiteness of their garments. It was also said: they were boatmen. Al-Hasan said: they were launderers, and they were named so because they used to whiten clothes (yuhawwirun al-thiyab), i.e., they made them white. 'Ata' said: Mary handed Jesus, peace be upon him, over to various trades, and the last one she gave him to was the disciples, who were launderers and dyers. She gave him to their chief so that he might learn from him. Clothes gathered with him, and a journey came up for the chief. He said to Jesus: "You have learned this craft. I am leaving on a journey and will not return for ten days. These are people's clothes of various colors, and I have marked each one with a thread indicating the color it is to be dyed. You must be free of them by the time I return." He went out. Jesus boiled a single vat of one color and put all the clothes into it, and said: "Be, by Allah's permission, as I want you to be." The disciple returned, and all the clothes were in the vat. He said: "What have you done?" He said: "I have finished with them." He said: "Where are they?" He said: "In the vat." He said: "All of them?" He said: "Yes." He said: "You have ruined those clothes!" He said: "Get up and look." Jesus took out a red garment, a yellow garment, and a green garment, until he had brought them out in the colors that were intended. The disciple began to marvel, and he knew that this was from Allah. He said to the people: "Come and see." He and his companions believed in him, and they are the disciples.

Al-Dahhak said: they were named hawariyyun for the purity of their hearts. Ibn al-Mubarak said: they were named so for the trace of worship and its light upon them. The original meaning of "hawar" among the Arabs is intense whiteness. It is said: "a man who is ahwar" and "a woman who is hawra'," meaning one with intense whiteness of the eye. Al-Kalbi and 'Ikrima said: the hawariyyun are the chosen ones, and they were the chosen ones of Jesus, peace be upon him, and there were twelve men. Rawh ibn al-Qasim said: I asked Qatada about the hawariyyun, and he said: "They are those fit for the caliphate." He also reported from him that he said: "The hawariyyun are the ministers." Al-Hasan said: "The hawariyyun are the helpers, and the hawari is the supporter." In the language of the Arabs specifically, the hawari is the man whom one seeks help from in matters that befall him.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Muliħi informed us; Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us; al-Humaydi informed us; Sufyan informed us; Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir informed us, saying: I heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called the people on the day of the Trench, and al-Zubayr volunteered. Then he called them again, and al-Zubayr volunteered. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Every prophet has a hawari, and my hawari is al-Zubayr.'"

[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Fada'il al-Sahaba, chapter: Virtues of al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam: 7/79–80, and in al-Jihad and al-Maghazi. Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahaba, chapter: On the virtues of Talha and al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them both, no. 2415, 4/1879. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunna: 14/122.]]

Sufyan said: al-hawari is the helper. Ma'mar said: Qatada said: "The hawariyyun were all from Quraysh: Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Hamza, Ja'far, Abu 'Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah, 'Uthman ibn Maz'un, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Talha ibn 'Ubayd Allah, and al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, may Allah be pleased with them all."

﴿The disciples said: "We are the helpers of Allah"﴾, the supporters of the religion of Allah and His messenger, ﴿We believed in Allah, and bear witness﴾, O Jesus, ﴿that we are Muslims.﴾
