The disciple returned, and all the clothes were in the vat. He said: "What have you done?" He said: "I have finished with them." He said: "Where are they?" He said: "In the vat." He said: "All of them?" He said: "Yes." He said: "You have ruined those clothes!" He said: "Get up and look." Jesus took out a red garment, a yellow garment, and a green garment, until he had brought them out in the colors that were intended. The disciple began to marvel, and he knew that this was from Allah. He said to the people: "Come and see." He and his companions believed in him, and they are the disciples.

Al-Dahhak said: they were named hawariyyun for the purity of their hearts. Ibn al-Mubarak said: they were named so for the trace of worship and its light upon them. The original meaning of "hawar" among the Arabs is intense whiteness. It is said: "a man who is ahwar" and "a woman who is hawra'," meaning one with intense whiteness of the eye. Al-Kalbi and 'Ikrima said: the hawariyyun are the chosen ones, and they were the chosen ones of Jesus, peace be upon him, and there were twelve men. Rawh ibn al-Qasim said: I asked Qatada about the hawariyyun, and he said: "They are those fit for the caliphate." He also reported from him that he said: "The hawariyyun are the ministers." Al-Hasan said: "The hawariyyun are the helpers, and the hawari is the supporter." In the language of the Arabs specifically, the hawari is the man whom one seeks help from in matters that befall him.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Muliħi informed us; Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us; Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us; al-Humaydi informed us; Sufyan informed us; Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir informed us, saying: I heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called the people on the day of the Trench, and al-Zubayr volunteered. Then he called them again, and al-Zubayr volunteered. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Every prophet has a hawari, and my hawari is al-Zubayr.'"

[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Fada'il al-Sahaba, chapter: Virtues of al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam: 7/79–80, and in al-Jihad and al-Maghazi. Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahaba, chapter: On the virtues of Talha and al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them both, no. 2415, 4/1879. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunna: 14/122.]]

Sufyan said: al-hawari is the helper. Ma'mar said: Qatada said: "The hawariyyun were all from Quraysh: Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Hamza, Ja'far, Abu 'Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah, 'Uthman ibn Maz'un, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Talha ibn 'Ubayd Allah, and al-Zubayr ibn al-'Awwam, may Allah be pleased with them all."

﴿The disciples said: "We are the helpers of Allah"﴾, the supporters of the religion of Allah and His messenger, ﴿We believed in Allah, and bear witness﴾, O Jesus, ﴿that we are Muslims.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 53:

﴿Our Lord, we have believed in what You have sent down﴾ from Your Book, ﴿and we have followed the Messenger﴾ (Jesus), ﴿so register us among the witnesses﴾ who bear witness to Your prophets with truth. And ʿAtaʾ said: "among the prophets," because every prophet is a witness over his nation.

Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "with Muhammad (ﷺ) and his nation, because they bear witness for the messengers that they conveyed the message."

And they schemed, and Allah schemed; and Allah is the best of schemers (﴿وَمَكَرُوا وَمَكَرَ اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ﴾).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَمَكَرُوا﴾ means the disbelievers among the Children of Israel, the one whom Jesus sensed to be disbelieving among them, and they set about killing Jesus, peace be upon him. This was because, after his people had expelled him and his mother, Jesus, peace be upon him, returned to them with the Disciples (al-Hawariyyun), and he called them to the religion. They resolved to kill him and conspired together to assassinate him. That is their scheming.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَمَكَرَ اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ﴾. Scheming from the created beings is wickedness, deception and trickery. Scheming from Allah is the gradual leading of the servant (istidraj) and seizing him suddenly from where he does not know, as He said: "We will lead them step by step from where they do not know" (7:182). Al-Zajjaj said: the scheming of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is His recompense for their scheming, so He named the recompense by the name of the initial act because it is in response to it, as in His saying: ﴿اللَّهُ يَسْتَهْزِئُ بِهِمْ﴾ (2:15) and "He is the one who deceives them" (4:142). The scheming of Allah, the Exalted, in this verse is specifically directed at them, and it is His casting the likeness (shabah) upon their companion who intended to kill Jesus, peace be upon him, until he himself was killed.

Al-Kalbi said, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: Jesus encountered a group of Jews, and when they saw him they said: "The sorcerer, the son of the sorceress, has come," and "the fornicator, the son of the fornicator," and they slandered him and his mother. When Jesus, peace be upon him, heard that, he invoked against them and cursed them, and Allah transformed them into pigs. When Judas (Yahudha), the head and leader of the Jews, saw that, he was terrified and feared his supplication. The Jews united their word to kill Jesus, peace be upon him, and they rushed at him to kill him. Allah sent Gabriel (Jibril) to him, and he brought him into a small room (khawkha) which had an opening (rawzana) in its roof, and Allah raised him up to the heavens through that opening. Judas, the head of the Jews, ordered a man from among his companions called Tatyanus to enter the room and kill him. When he entered, he did not see Jesus, and he delayed coming out to them, so they assumed he was fighting him inside. Allah cast the likeness of Jesus, peace be upon him, upon him, and when he came out they thought he was Jesus, peace be upon him, so they killed him and crucified him.

Wahb said: They came upon Jesus during part of the night and set up a wooden cross to crucify him, but the earth grew dark, so Allah sent the angels, and they came between them and him. Jesus gathered the Disciples that night and gave them his counsel, then said: "One of you will disbelieve in me before the rooster crows, and will sell me for a small sum of money." So they went out and dispersed. The Jews were searching for him, and one of the Disciples came to the Jews and said to them: "What will you give me if I show you the Messiah?" So they gave him thirty dirhams, he took them, and he showed them where he was. When he entered the house, Allah cast upon him the likeness of Jesus, and Jesus was raised up. They seized the one who had shown them the way and he said: "I am the one who showed you to him." But they did not pay attention to his words, and they killed him and crucified him, thinking that he was Jesus. When the likeness of Jesus was crucified, Mary, the mother of Jesus, and a woman whom Jesus had prayed for and whom Allah had cured of madness came, weeping beside the crucified one. Jesus, peace be upon him, came to them and said to them: "Why are you weeping? Allah the Exalted has raised me up, and nothing but good has befallen me, and this is a matter that was made to appear to them as such." Then, after seven days, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to Jesus, peace be upon him: "Descend upon Mary al-Majdaliyya" (a place-name, on its mountain), "for no one has wept over you as she has wept, nor grieved as she has grieved. Then let the Disciples gather to you, so that you may disperse them across the earth as callers to Allah, Mighty and Majestic." So Allah caused him to descend upon her, and the mountain blazed with light when he descended. The Disciples gathered to him, and he dispersed them across the earth as callers. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, raised him up to Himself. That night is the one in which the Christians celebrate Tashann (the night of the Christian observance). When the Disciples woke in the morning, each one of them spoke in the language of the people to whom Jesus had sent him. This is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَمَكَرُوا وَمَكَرَ اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ خَيْرُ الْمَاكِرِينَ﴾.

Al-Suddi said: The Jews imprisoned Jesus in a house along with ten of the Disciples, and a man from among them entered upon them, and Allah cast Jesus' likeness upon him. Qatada said: It was reported to us that the Prophet of Allah, Jesus, peace be upon him, said to his companions: "Which of you will have my likeness cast upon him, and he will be killed?" A man from the people said: "I, O Prophet of Allah." So that man was killed, Allah protected Jesus, peace be upon him, raised him up to Himself, clothed him with feathers (al-rish), dressed him in light, cut off from him the pleasure of food and drink, and he flew with the angels, so he is with them around the Throne. He was a human being, an angelic being, a heavenly being and an earthly being.

The historians said: Mary conceived Jesus when she was thirteen years old, and she gave birth to Jesus in Bethlehem (Bayt Lahm) in the land of Urishalim (Jerusalem), sixty-five years after Alexander's conquest of the land of Babylon. Allah revealed to him at the age of thirty, and Allah raised him from Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) on the Night of Power (Laylat al-Qadr) in the month of Ramadan, when he was thirty-three years old. So his prophethood lasted three years. His mother Mary lived six years after his ascension.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 55:

﴿When God said: "O Jesus, I will take you and raise you up to Me"﴾. They differed concerning the meaning of "tawaffi" (taking in full, causing to die, or putting to sleep) here. Al-Hasan, al-Kalbi and Ibn Juraij said: "I will take you (qabid) and raise you up to Me in this world, without death." This is supported by the words of the Exalted: ﴿So when You took me (tawaffaytani)﴾ (5:117), meaning: You took me up to the heavens while I was alive, because his people only became Christians after his being raised to heaven, not after his death. According to this view, "tawaffi" has two interpretations. The first: "I will raise you to Me complete, and they will not have harmed you in any way," from the expression "tawaffaytu kadha wa-istawfaytuhu," meaning, when you take something in full. The second: "I will receive you (mustalimuka)" [in manuscript A: mustaslimuka], from the expression "tawaffaytu minhu kadha," meaning, I received it from him. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: the intended meaning of "tawaffi" is sleep, and every one with eyes sleeps. Jesus had fallen asleep, and God raised him up to the heavens while he was asleep. The meaning is: "I will put you to sleep and raise you up to Me," as the Exalted said: ﴿And it is He who takes you (yatawaffakum) by night﴾ (6:60), meaning: He puts you to sleep.

Some of them said: the intended meaning of "tawaffi" is death. It is narrated from Ali ibn Talha, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that its meaning is: "I will cause you to die." This is supported by the words of the Exalted: ﴿Say: The angel of death who is charged with you will take you (yatawaffakum)﴾ (32:11). According to this view there are two interpretations. The first is what Wahb said: God caused Jesus to die for three hours of the day, then God raised him to Himself. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: the Christians claim that God caused him to die for seven hours of the day, then gave him life and raised him. The second is what al-Dahhak and a group said: in this verse there is inversion (taqdim and ta'khir); its meaning is: "I will raise you to Me and purify you from those who disbelieved, and cause you to die after I bring you down from the heaven."

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us, Abu al-Qasim Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Baghawi informed us, Ali ibn al-Ja'd informed us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Salama al-Majishun informed us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayra, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the son of Mary will surely descend among you as a just judge; he will break the cross, kill the swine, abolish the jizya, and wealth will overflow until no one accepts it." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Anbiya', chapter: The descent of Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon them both: 6/490. And Muslim in al-Iman, chapter: The descent of Jesus son of Mary as a judge by the law of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), no. (155), 1/135-136. And the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 15/80-81.]

It is also narrated from Abu Hurayra, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning the descent of Jesus, peace be upon him, that he said: "In his time all religions will perish except Islam, and the Dajjal will perish, and he will remain on earth for forty years, then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him." [Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Malahim, chapter: The emergence of the Dajjal: 6/177, and al-Mundhiri remained silent about it. And Ahmad in al-Musnad from Abu Hurayra: 2/406, 437, at length.]

It was said to al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl: "Do you find the descent of Jesus in the Qur'an?" He said: "Yes: ﴿and as an adult (kahlan)﴾, and he did not reach middle age in this world; rather the meaning is: and as an adult after his descent from the heaven."

The words of the Exalted: ﴿and purify you from those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: I will bring you out from among them and save you from them. ﴿And I will place those who follow you above those who disbelieve until the Day of Resurrection﴾. Qatadah, al-Rabi', al-Sha'bi, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: they are the people of Islam who believed him and followed his religion in monotheism from the community of Muhammad (ﷺ); so they are above those who disbelieve, dominant and victorious through power, protection and proof. Al-Dahhak said: it means the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) are above those who disbelieved. It was also said: they are the people of Rome. And it was said: he meant by them the Christians, who are above the Jews until the Day of Resurrection, since the kingdom of the Jews has gone, while the kingdom of the Christians lasts until near the Hour. According to this, "following" (ittiba') means claiming and affection, not following the religion.

﴿Then to Me is your return﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿and I will judge between you concerning that wherein you used to differ﴾ regarding the matter of religion and the matter of Jesus.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 56–60:

﴿As for those who disbelieve, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world﴾ by killing, captivity, the jizya (poll-tax) and humiliation, ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾, that is, and in the Hereafter, by the Fire, ﴿and they will have no helpers﴾.

﴿As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them their rewards in full﴾. Al-Hasan and Hafs read it with the yā' (fa-yuwaffīhim), and the rest read it with the nūn (nuwaffī), meaning: We will give in full the rewards of their deeds. ﴿And Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾, that is, He does not show mercy to the disbelievers nor praise them with goodness.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That﴾, that is, this which I have related to you of the report concerning ʿIsā, Maryam and the disciples (al-Ḥawāriyyūn), ﴿We recite it to you﴾ [we inform you of it through the recitation of Jibrīl to you] [[Omitted from manuscript A.]] ﴿from the Signs and the Wise Reminder﴾. It means the Qur'an, and the Reminder full of wisdom. Muqatil said: "The Wise Reminder" means the muḥkam (firmly established), protected from falsehood. It was also said: "The Wise Reminder" is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Maḥfūz), which is suspended from the Throne, made of white pearl. It was also said: "from the Signs" means the indications that point to your prophethood, because they are reports that no one knows except a reader of a scripture or one to whom revelation is sent, and you are unlettered (ummī) and do not read.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of ʿIsā with Allah is like the likeness of Ādam﴾, the verse was revealed concerning the delegation of Najrān. They said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Why do you revile our companion?" He said: "What do I say?" They said: "You say that he is the servant of Allah." He said: "Yes, he is the servant of Allah, His messenger, and His word which He cast to Maryam the virgin, the chaste." They became angry and said: "Have you ever seen a human being without a father?" So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of ʿIsā with Allah﴾ [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 136.]] in that He created him without a father is like the likeness of Ādam, for he was created without a father or a mother. ﴿He created him from dust; then He said to him﴾, meaning to ʿIsā, peace be upon him, ﴿"Be," and he was﴾, meaning, so he came to be. If it is asked: what is the meaning of His saying, ﴿He created him from dust, then He said to him, "Be," and he was,﴾ when there is no "bringing into being" after the creation? It is answered: its meaning is: then He created him, then He informed you that I said to him "Be," and he was, without sequence in the creation, as occurs in birth. This is like a man's saying: "I gave you a dirham today, then I gave you a dirham yesterday," meaning: then I inform you that I gave you a dirham yesterday. In the preceding comparison there is evidence for the permissibility of analogical reasoning (qiyās), because qiyās is the returning of a derivative case (far') to a basis (aṣl) by a kind of resemblance, and Allah, exalted is He, returned the creation of ʿIsā to Ādam, peace be upon them both, by a kind of resemblance.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The truth is from your Lord﴾, that is, it is the truth. It was also said: the truth has come to you from your Lord. ﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾, those who are in doubt. The address is to the Prophet ﷺ, and what is meant is his community (ummah).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 61:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Whoever argues with you concerning it﴾, that is, disputes with you concerning Jesus or concerning the truth, ﴿after the knowledge has come to you﴾ that Jesus is the servant of Allah and His messenger. ﴿Then say: "Come, let us call"﴾. Its origin is taʿālawū (تَعَالَوُا), a form of tafāʿalū (تَفَاعَلُوا) from al-ʿulūw (the height/elevation), and the damma was burdensome on the yāʾ, so it was dropped. Al-Farrāʾ (the grammarian) said: it means taʿālā (come), as if he were saying: "Rise up." His saying ﴿nadʿu﴾ (let us call) is in the jussive because it is the answer to the imperative, and the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the wāw. ﴿Our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves﴾. It was said: "our sons" refers to al-Hasan and al-Husayn, and "our women" to Fatimah, and "ourselves" means himself and ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him. The Arabs call a man's cousin his own self, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And do not defame one another﴾ (49:11), meaning your brothers. It was also said that it is general, meaning the community of the people of the religion. ﴿Then let us earnestly invoke﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: that is, we humbly supplicate in prayer. al-Kalbi said: we strive and exert ourselves in supplication. al-Kisai and Abu ʿUbayda said: we curse one another; al-ibtihal (the mutual invocation) is al-iltiʿan (mutual cursing), and it is said: "upon him is the bahlat of Allah," that is, His curse. ﴿Then we will invoke the curse of Allah upon the liars﴾, from us and from you, concerning the matter of Jesus.

When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse to the delegation of Najran and invited them to mubahalah (mutual imprecation), they said: "Until we return and consider our affair, then we will come to you tomorrow." So some of them withdrew privately with one another, and they said to al-ʿAqib, who was their man of judgment: "O ʿAbd al-Masih, what do you think?" He said: "By Allah, you have known, O assembly of Christians, that Muhammad is a prophet sent by God. By Allah, no people have ever invoked a curse upon a prophet and then their elders survived or their young grew up. If you do that, you will surely perish. So if you refuse except to remain upon what you hold concerning your companion, then make peace with the man and return to your lands." They came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had gone out in the morning embracing al-Husayn and holding the hand of al-Hasan, with Fatimah walking behind him and ʿAli behind her, and he was saying to them: "When I supplicate, say ʿAmin." The bishop of Najran said: "O assembly of Christians, I see faces which, if they asked Allah to remove a mountain from its place, He would remove it. So do not invoke a curse, lest you perish and not one Christian remains upon the face of the earth until the Day of Resurrection." They said: "O Abu al-Qasim, we have decided not to curse you, and to leave you upon your religion and remain upon our religion." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then if you refuse the mubahalah, embrace Islam, and you will have what the Muslims have and you will bear what they bear." They refused, so he said: "Then I shall declare war upon you." They said: "We have no strength to fight the Arabs, but we will make a treaty with you on condition that you do not attack us, do not frighten us, and do not turn us back from our religion, on condition that we pay you every year two thousand garments: a thousand in Safar and a thousand in Rajab." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concluded the treaty with them on that basis and said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the punishment had already hung over the people of Najran. Had they invoked a curse, they would have been transformed into monkeys and swine, and the valley would have blazed with fire upon them, and Allah would have uprooted Najran and its people, even the birds upon the trees, and within a year all the Christians would have perished."

[[Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf: Abu Nuʿaym narrated it in Dala'il al-Nubuwwah through the route of Muhammad ibn Marwan al-Suddi, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas, at length; and Ibn Marwan is abandoned (matruk) and accused of lying. Then Abu Nuʿaym narrated something similar from al-Shaʿbi as a mursal report, and in it: "If you refuse the mubahalah, then embrace Islam..." See al-Kafi al-Shaf p. 26. Al-Tabari also narrated it in his Tafsir 6/479–480 through the route of Ibn Ishaq from Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr concerning the verse ﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative﴾, mentioning it as a mursal report. See also: al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti 2/229–233 and Ibn Kathir 1/371–372.]].

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, this is the true narrative.﴾ *Al-naba' al-haqq* (the true report). ﴿And there is no god except Allah.﴾ The word *min* (مِنْ) in ﴿وَمَا مِنْ إِلَهٍ﴾ is a *ṣilah* (a superfluous particle that adds emphasis without changing the meaning), so the sense is: "and there is no god but Allah." ﴿And indeed Allah is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾

﴿But if they turn away﴾ from faith, ﴿then indeed Allah is All-Knowing of the corrupters﴾, meaning those who worship other than Allah and call people to worship other than Allah.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you﴾, and the verse continues. The exegetes said: The delegation of Najran came to Medina and met the Jews, and they disputed about Abraham (peace be upon him). The Christians claimed that he was a Christian and that they were upon his religion and were the people most worthy of him. The Jews said: Rather, he was a Jew, and they were upon his religion and were the people most worthy of him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Both groups are free of Abraham and his religion. Rather, Abraham was a *ḥanīf* (upright, devoted to monotheism), a Muslim, and I am upon his religion. So follow his religion, the religion of Islam." The Jews said: "O Muhammad, you want nothing more than that we take you as a lord, just as the Christians took Jesus as a lord." The Christians said: "O Muhammad, you want nothing more than that we say about you what the Jews said about Ezra." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, come to a word...﴾ [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/235.]]

The Arabs call every account that has an explanation a *kalimah* (word), and from this usage the *qaṣīdah* (ode) was called a *kalimah*. ﴿Sawā'﴾ means equitable, just between us and you, even. It is said: "Such-and-such called to *al-sawā'*," meaning to fairness. The *sawā'* of everything is its middle. From this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So he saw him in the midst of the Blazing Fire﴾ (37:55). The half is called *sawā'* because the most just and best of matters is its middle.

*Sawā'* is an adjective (*na't*) describing *kalimah*, except that it is a *maṣdar* (verbal noun), and verbal nouns are not made dual, plural, or feminine. When the *sīn* is vowelled with a fatḥa, the word is read with a long vowel (*mamdūd*, sawā'). When the *sīn* is vowelled with a kasra or ḍamma, it is read short (*maqṣūr*, sawa or suwa), as in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿a place equal﴾ (20:58), *makānan suwā*.

Then he explained the word, saying: ﴿that we worship none but Allah﴾. The grammatical position (*maḥall*) of *an* (أَنْ) here is nominative (*raf'*), with an implied *hiya* (it is). Al-Zajjaj said it is nominative as the subject of an inceptive sentence (*mubtada'*). It was also said that its position is accusative (*naṣb*) by removing the preposition (*naz' ḥarf al-ṣifah*), meaning *bi-an lā na'bud illā Allāh* (that we do not worship except Allah). It was also said that its position is genitive (*khafḍ*) as an apposition (*badal*) for *kalimah*, meaning: "Come to the matter that we do not worship except Allah."

﴿And that we do not associate anything with Him, and that some of us do not take others as lords besides Allah﴾, as the Jews and Christians did. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ (9:31). Ikrimah said: this refers to some of them prostrating to others, meaning: do not prostrate to other than Allah. It was also said: its meaning is that we do not obey anyone in disobedience to Allah.

﴿But if they turn away, then say: Bear witness that we are Muslims﴾, meaning, you say to them: "Bear witness" ﴿that we are Muslims﴾, sincere in monotheism.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi related to us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi' related to us: Shu'ayb related to us, from al-Zuhri: Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud related to us that Abd Allah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) informed him that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb informed him that Heraclius sent for him in a caravan of Quraysh, who were merchants in Syria during the truce that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had made with Abu Sufyan and the disbelieving Quraysh. They came to him while he was in Iliya, and he summoned them to his assembly, with the great men of the Romans around him. He called for the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which he had sent with Dihyah ibn Khalifah al-Kalbi to the governor of Busra, and he gave it to Heraclius, who read it, and it said:

"In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. From Muhammad, the servant of Allah and His Messenger, to Heraclius, the great one of the Romans. Peace be upon whoever follows guidance. To proceed: I invite you with the call of Islam. Embrace Islam and you will be safe; embrace Islam and Allah will give you your reward twice. But if they turn away, then say: Bear witness that we are Muslims.﴾" [[Al-Bukhari, Tafsir, Surat Al 'Imran, chapter: "Say: O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you...", 8/214.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi related to us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us: Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi' related to us: Shu'ayb related to us, from al-Zuhri: Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud related to us that Abd Allah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) informed him that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb informed him that Heraclius sent for him in a caravan of Quraysh, who were merchants in Syria during the truce that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had made with Abu Sufyan and the disbelieving Quraysh. They came to him while he was in Iliya, and he summoned them to his assembly, with the great men of the Romans around him. He called for the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which he had sent with Dihyah ibn Khalifah al-Kalbi to the governor of Busra, and he gave it to Heraclius, who read it, and it said:

"In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. From Muhammad, the servant of Allah and His Messenger, to Heraclius, the great one of the Romans. Peace be upon whoever follows guidance. To proceed: I invite you with the call of Islam. Embrace Islam and you will be safe; embrace Islam and Allah will give you your reward twice. But if you turn away, the sin of the peasants (*al-Ariseen*) will be upon you. ﴿O People of the Scripture, come to a word that is equitable between us and you: that we worship none but Allah, and that we associate nothing with Him, and that some of us do not take others as lords besides Allah. The Torah and the Gospel were revealed long after Abraham: there was a thousand years between Abraham and Moses, and two thousand years between Moses and Jesus. ﴿Will you not then use your reason?﴾ [i.e., to see] the falsehood of your claim?

﴿Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a ḥanīf (one who turns away from all religions to the upright religion), a Muslim, and he was not one of the polytheists.﴾

It is said: the ḥanīf is one who turns away from all religions toward the upright religion. It is also said: the ḥanīf is one who affirms the oneness of God, performs the pilgrimage, offers sacrifice, is circumcised, and faces the Kaaba. It is the easiest of the religions and the most beloved of them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe.﴾ That is, those who followed him in his time, ﴿and this Prophet﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿and those who believe﴾ with him, meaning from this community. ﴿And Allah is the Protector of the believers.﴾

Al-Kalbī narrated from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, and Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated from Ibn Shihāb with its chain, the ḥadīth of the migration to Abyssinia, when Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) migrated to Abyssinia and settled there, and the Prophet (ﷺ) migrated to Medina, and what happened at Badr happened. [60/b] The Quraysh gathered in Dār al-Nadwa (the council house of Quraysh) and said: "We have a claim against those among the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) who are with the Negus, in revenge for those of you who were killed at Badr. So gather wealth and send it as a gift to the Negus, perhaps he will hand over to you those of your people who are with him. Let two men of your opinion be dispatched for this." So they sent ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ and ʿUmāra ibn al-Walīd with gifts of leather and other things. They boarded the sea and came to Abyssinia. When they entered upon the Negus, they prostrated to him and greeted him, and said to him: "Our people are sincere advisers to you, grateful to you, and desirous of your well-being. They have sent us to you to warn you about these people who have come to you, for they are the people of a lying man who has emerged among us, claiming that he is the Messenger of Allah. No one among us has followed him except the foolish. We had made life difficult for them and forced them into a valley in our land where no one could enter upon them and none of them could leave, and hunger and thirst were killing them. When the matter became severe for them, he sent his cousin to you to corrupt your religion, your kingdom, and your subjects. So beware of them, and hand them over to us, and we will deal with them for you." They also said: "A sign of this is that when they enter upon you, they will not prostrate to you, nor greet you with the greeting by which people greet you, out of aversion to your religion and your custom."

He said: The Negus summoned them, and when they came, Jaʿfar shouted at the door: "The party of Allah seeks permission to enter upon you." The Negus said: "Tell this shouter to repeat his words." Jaʿfar did so. The Negus said: "Yes, let them enter under the protection of Allah and His covenant." ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ looked at his companion and said: "Do you not hear how they speak of the party of Allah?" and what the Negus had replied to them. This displeased them both. Then they entered upon him, and they did not prostrate to him. ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said: "Do you not see that they are too proud to prostrate to you?" The Negus said to them: "What prevents you from prostrating to me and greeting me with the greeting by which those who come to me from the regions greet me?" They said: "We prostrate to Allah, who created you and your kingdom. That greeting was for us, and we were worshippers of idols. Then Allah sent among us a truthful Prophet, who commanded us with the greeting that Allah approves, which is peace, the greeting of the people of Paradise." The Negus recognized that this was true, and that it is in the Torah and the Gospel. He said: "Which of you is the one who called out: 'The party of Allah seeks permission to enter upon you'?" Jaʿfar said: "I am." He said: "Speak." He said: "You are a king among the kings of the earth, and one of the People of the Book, and excessive speech and injustice are not fitting in your presence. I would like to answer on behalf of my companions. So order these two men, let one of them speak and the other be silent, so that you may hear our discourse." ʿAmr said to Jaʿfar: "Speak." Jaʿfar said to the Negus: "Ask these two men: are we slaves or free? If we are slaves who have run away from our masters, then return us to them." The Negus said: "Are they slaves or free?" ʿAmr said: "No, they are free and noble." The Negus said: "They have been saved from slavery." Then Jaʿfar said: "Ask them whether we have shed blood unjustly so that retaliation is required from us?" The Negus said: "If it is a qinṭār (a large measure of gold), then I will pay it." ʿAmr said: "No, not even a qīrāṭ (a small measure)." The Negus said: "Then what do you want from them?" ʿAmr said: "We and they were on one religion and one affair, the religion of our fathers. Then they abandoned that and sought something else. So their people sent us to you to hand them over to us." The Negus said: "What is this religion you were upon, and the religion you have followed? Tell me the truth." Jaʿfar said: "As for the religion we were upon, we have abandoned it; it is the religion of Satan. We used to disbelieve in Allah and worship stones. As for the religion to which we have turned, it is the religion of Allah, Islam. A messenger came to us with it from Allah, and a book like the Book of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam (Jesus son of Mary), confirming it." The Negus said: "O Jaʿfar, you have spoken of a great matter, so take your time." Then the Negus ordered that the nāqūs (a wooden or metal clapper used to call to prayer) be struck, and every qissīs (priest) and monk gathered before him. When they had gathered before him, the Negus said: "I beseech you by Allah, who sent down the Gospel to ʿĪsā, do you find between ʿĪsā and the Day of Resurrection a sent Prophet?" They said: "Yes, by Allah. ʿĪsā gave us good news of him, and said: 'Whoever believes in him has believed in me, and whoever disbelieves in him has disbelieved in me.'" The Negus said to Jaʿfar: "What does this man say to you, and what does he command you and forbid you?" He said: "He recites to us the Book of Allah, commands what is good, forbids what is evil, commands good neighborliness, the maintenance of kinship ties, and kindness to orphans, and commands us to worship Allah alone, without partner." He said: "Recite to me some of what he recites to you." So he recited to them Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt and al-Rūm. The eyes of the Negus and his companions overflowed with tears, and they said: "Increase for us, O Jaʿfar, of this good speech." So he recited to them Sūrat al-Kahf. ʿAmr wanted to anger the Negus, so he said: "They revile ʿĪsā and his mother." The Negus said: "What do you say about ʿĪsā and his mother?" Jaʿfar recited to them Sūrat Maryam. When Jaʿfar reached the mention of Maryam and ʿĪsā, peace be upon them both, the Negus lifted a little spit from his siwāk (tooth-stick), about the amount that an eye is irritated by, and said: "By Allah, the Messiah did not exceed what you say, this much." Then he turned to Jaʿfar and his companions and said: "Go, for you are secure (sayyūm) in my land. Whoever reviles you or harms you will be fined." Then he said: "Rejoice and do not fear, for there is no dahwara (gathering and casting into a pit) today against the party of Abraham." ʿAmr said: "O Negus, who is the party of Abraham?" He said: "These men and their companion from whom they came, and whoever follows them." The polytheists denied this and claimed to be upon the religion of Abraham. Then the Negus returned to ʿAmr and his companion the wealth they had brought, and said: "Your gift to me is a bribe, so take it back, for Allah has given me dominion and did not take a bribe from me." Jaʿfar said: "So we departed, and we were in the best of homes and the most honorable of neighbors." On that day, while he was in Medina, Allah, the Exalted, revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), concerning their dispute about Abraham, the words: ﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Abraham are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe. And Allah is the Protector of the believers.﴾ [Recorded by Ibn Isḥāq in al-Sīrah from Umm Salama, 1/211–215, and from his route Imam Aḥmad in al-Musnad, 1/201–203, from Umm Salama. Al-Haythamī said in al-Majmaʿ (6/27): "Aḥmad narrated it, and its narrators are the narrators of the authentic (ṣaḥīḥ)." Al-Wāḥidī mentioned it in Asbāb al-Nuzūl, pp. 138–141.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 69–72:

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿A party of the People of the Book wish[ed]﴾. It was revealed concerning Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman and 'Ammar ibn Yasir, when the Jews invited them to their religion, and so it was revealed: ﴿A party wished﴾ [[Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 142.]] [a group of the People of the Book wished], [[Omitted from B.]] meaning the Jews, ﴿that they might mislead you﴾ away from your religion and return you to disbelief, ﴿but they mislead none except themselves, and they do not perceive﴾.

﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah﴾, meaning the Qur'an and the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿while you are witnesses﴾ that his description is mentioned in the Torah and the Gospel.

﴿O People of the Scripture, why do you mix the truth with falsehood﴾: you mix Islam with Judaism and Christianity. It was also said: why do you mix belief in 'Isa (peace be upon him), which is the truth, with disbelief in Muhammad (ﷺ), which is falsehood? It was also said: [it means] the Torah that was revealed to Musa, mixed with the falsehood that you altered and wrote with your own hands. ﴿And conceal the truth while you know﴾ that Muhammad (ﷺ) and his religion are true.

His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And a party of the People of the Scripture said, "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day"﴾, the verse. Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: Twelve rabbis of the Jews of Khaybar and the villages of 'Uyayna conspired together, and some of them said to others: "Enter the religion of Muhammad at the beginning of the day with the tongue only, without conviction, then disbelieve at the end of the day, and say: 'We examined our books and consulted our scholars, and we found that Muhammad is not that, and his falsehood has become clear to us.'" When you do that, his companions will doubt their religion and accuse him, and they will say: "They are People of the Book and they know more about it than us," and so they will turn back from their religion.

Mujahid, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: This was concerning the qiblah. When the qiblah was turned to the Ka'bah, it grieved the Jews, and Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf said to his companions: "Believe in what has been revealed to Muhammad concerning the Ka'bah, and pray towards it at the beginning of the day, then disbelieve and return to your qiblah at the end of the day. Perhaps they will say, 'These are People of the Book, and they are more knowledgeable,' and they will return to our qiblah." So Allah the Exalted informed His Messenger of their secret, and revealed: ﴿And a party of the People of the Scripture said, "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day"﴾ ﴿and disbelieve at its end, perhaps they will return﴾. "Its beginning" is called "face" (wajh) because it is its best part and the first thing that confronts the viewer and that he sees; ﴿perhaps they will return﴾, so that they doubt and turn back from their religion.

It was also said: [it means] the Torah that was revealed to Musa, mixed with the falsehood that you altered and wrote with your own hands. ﴿And conceal the truth while you know﴾ that Muhammad (ﷺ) and his religion are true.

His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿And a party of the People of the Scripture said, "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day"﴾, the verse. Al-Hasan and al-Suddi said: Twelve rabbis of the Jews of Khaybar and the villages of 'Uyayna conspired together, and some of them said to others: "Enter the religion of Muhammad at the beginning of the day with the tongue only, without conviction, then disbelieve at the end of the day, and say: 'We examined our books and consulted our scholars, and we found that Muhammad is not that, and his falsehood has become clear to us.'" When you do that, his companions will doubt their religion and accuse him, and they will say: "They are People of the Book and they know more about it than us," and so they will turn back from their religion.

Mujahid, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: This was concerning the qiblah. When the qiblah was turned to the Ka'bah, it grieved the Jews, and Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf said to his companions: "Believe in what has been revealed to Muhammad concerning the Ka'bah, and pray towards it at the beginning of the day, then disbelieve and return to your qiblah at the end of the day. Perhaps they will say, 'These are People of the Book, and they are more knowledgeable,' and they will return to our qiblah." So Allah the Exalted informed His Messenger of their secret, and revealed: ﴿And a party of the People of the Scripture said, "Believe in what has been revealed to those who believed at the beginning of the day"﴾ ﴿and disbelieve at its end, perhaps they will return﴾. "Its beginning" is called "face" (wajh) because it is its best part and the first thing that confronts the viewer and that he sees; ﴿perhaps they will return﴾, so that they doubt and turn back from their religion.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 73:

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And do not believe except in one who follows your religion﴾: this is connected to the first part of the speech of the Jews, some of them to others. ﴿And do not believe﴾, that is, do not affirm, ﴿except one who follows your religion﴾, that is, agrees with your creed. The lam in "li-man" is a supplementary particle (silah), meaning: do not affirm except one who follows your religion, Judaism, like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say, "Perhaps there has drawn near for you [some] of what you seek to hasten"﴾ (16:72), meaning: radafa lakum, that is, radfakum (what follows you).

﴿Say, "Indeed, guidance is the guidance of Allah"﴾: this is a report from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that the clarification is His clarification. Then they differed. Some of them said: it is a parenthetical statement between two statements, and what follows is connected to the first statement, reporting the saying of the Jews, some to others, and its meaning is: "And do not believe except in one who follows your religion, and do not believe that anyone will be given the like of what you have been given of knowledge, the Book, wisdom, the signs such as manna and quail, the splitting of the sea, and other miracles (karamat). And do not believe that they will argue with you before your Lord, because you are more correct in religion than they are." This is the meaning of the saying of Mujahid.

It was also said: the Jews said to their followers, ﴿And do not believe except in one who follows your religion﴾ ﴿that anyone be given the like of what you have been given﴾ of knowledge, meaning: lest anyone be given it. The "la" (not) is implied here, like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ (4:176), meaning: lest you go astray. They say: do not believe them, lest they know the like of what you know, so that you would have superiority over them in knowledge, and lest they argue with you before your Lord, so that they say: "You have come to know that our religion is true." This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn Juraij.

Al-Hasan and al-A'mash read ﴿in yu'ta﴾ with a kasra on the alif, so the speech of the Jews is complete at His saying: ﴿except one who follows your religion﴾, and what follows is from the speech of Allah, the Exalted, who says: Say, O Muhammad, ﴿Indeed, guidance is the guidance of Allah, [that] anyone be given﴾, where "an" carries the sense of negation, meaning: no one is given the like of what you have been given, O community of Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿or that they will argue with you before your Lord﴾, meaning: unless the Jews argue with you falsely, saying, "We are better than you." His saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿before your Lord﴾ means: before the favour of your Lord toward you in that. This is the meaning of the saying of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, al-Kalbi and Muqatil. Al-Farra' said: it is permissible for "aw" to carry the sense of "until," as one says: "Cling to him until he gives you your right" (aw yu'tiyaka haqqaka), meaning: until he gives you your right. The meaning of the verse is: no one has been given the like of what you, O community of Muhammad, have been given of religion and proof, until they argue with you before your Lord.

Ibn Kathir read ﴿a-an yu'ta﴾ with a madd, as an interrogative, and in that case there is an ellipsis; its estimate is: "Will anyone be given the like of what you have been given, O company of Jews, of the Book and wisdom, which you envy and do not believe in?" This is the saying of Qatadah and al-Rabi', and they both said: this is from the speech of Allah, who says: Say to them, O Muhammad, ﴿Indeed, guidance is the guidance of Allah﴾, [by] that He sent down a Book like your Book and sent a Prophet, whom you envied and disbelieved in.

﴿Say, "Indeed, bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing"﴾. His saying, "or they will argue with you," according to this reading, is a return to addressing the believers, and "aw" is in the sense of "anna," since both are particles of condition and consequence, one of which is placed in the position of the other. That is: "And if they argue with you, O company of believers, before your Lord, then say, O Muhammad: Indeed, guidance is the guidance of Allah, and we are upon it." It is also permissible that the whole is addressed to the believers, and the structure of the verse would be: "[Lest] anyone be given the like of what you have been given, O company of believers, [for] they envy you. So say: ﴿Indeed, bounty is in the hand of Allah﴾, and if they argue with you, say: ﴿Indeed, guidance is the guidance of Allah﴾."

It is also permissible that the report about the Jews is complete at His saying ﴿so that they may return﴾, and His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And do not believe﴾ is the speech of Allah by which He strengthens the hearts of the believers, lest they doubt at the Jews' confusion and their falsification of their religion. He says: do not affirm, O company of believers, except one who follows your religion, and do not affirm that anyone will be given the like of what you have been given of religion and virtue, and do not affirm that they will argue with you in your religion before your Lord, or that they will be able to do so, for indeed guidance is the guidance of Allah. And ﴿Indeed, bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾. Thus the whole verse is an address from Allah to the believers at the Jews' confusion, lest they doubt.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿He singles out for His mercy﴾, i.e., for His prophethood, ﴿whom He wills. And God is the Possessor of great bounty﴾.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you﴾, the verse. It was revealed concerning the Jews. God the Exalted informed that among them there is trustworthiness and treachery. The qintar is an expression for a large amount of wealth, and the dinar is an expression for a small amount of wealth. The meaning is: among them is one who renders the trust even if it is large, and among them is one who does not render it even if it is small. Muqatil said: ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you﴾ refers to the believers among the People of the Book, such as 'Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions. ﴿And among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you﴾ refers to the disbelieving Jews, such as Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and his companions.

Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding the Mighty and Majestic's saying ﴿And among the People of the Book is one who, if you entrust him with a qintar, will return it to you﴾, that it refers to 'Abdullah ibn Salam: a man deposited with him one thousand two hundred ounces of gold, and he returned it to him. ﴿And among them is one who, if you entrust him with a dinar, will not return it to you﴾ refers to Finhas ibn 'Azura: a man of Quraysh deposited a dinar with him, and he betrayed him.

As for the Almighty's saying ﴿will return it to you﴾, Abu 'Amr, Abu Bakr and Hamzah recited ﴿yu'addih﴾ and ﴿la yu'addih﴾, and likewise ﴿nuslih﴾, ﴿nu'tih﴾ and ﴿nuwallih﴾, with the ha' (h) pronounced with a sukun (silent). Abu Ja'far, Qalun and Ya'qub recited with ikhtilas (a brief, truncated vowel) of the kasrah, and the rest recited with ishba' (full vowel) of the kasrah. Whoever pronounces the ha' with a sukun says it is because it was placed in the position of jazm (apocopation), which is the omitted ya'. Whoever uses ikhtilas suffices with the kasrah in place of the ya'. Whoever uses ishba' follows the original form, since the original for the ha' is full vocalization.

﴿Except while you keep standing over him﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "mulihhan" (persistently), meaning he stands over him, demanding it from him insistently. Al-Dahhak said: "muwaziban" (persevering), meaning you persevere over him in demanding it. It was also said: he meant that you deposited it with him, then you reclaimed it while you were standing over his head and did not leave him; then he returns it to you. But if you leave him and delay, he denies it and does not return it.

﴿That﴾, i.e., that permissibility and that betrayal, ﴿is because they say: "There is no blame upon us regarding the common people"﴾, i.e., there is no sin or wrongdoing upon us regarding the wealth of the Arabs, like the Almighty's saying: ﴿There is no cause for blame against the good-doers﴾. The reason is that the Jews said: "The wealth of the Arabs is lawful for us, because they are not upon our religion and have no sanctity in our Book." They used to consider it permissible to wrong those who differed with them in their religion.

Al-Kalbi said: The Jews said, "All wealth was originally ours, so whatever is in the hands of the Arabs of it belongs to us. They only wronged us and usurped it from us, so there is no blame upon us in taking it from them."

Al-Hasan, Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil said: In the pre-Islamic period, the Jews made transactions with men from among the Muslims. When those men embraced Islam, the Jews demanded from them the remainder of their wealth. They said, "You have no right over us, and we have no obligation to repay you, because you have abandoned your religion, and the covenant between us and you has ended." They claimed that they had found this in their books. So God the Mighty and Majestic refuted them, and the Mighty Speaker said: ﴿And they speak falsehood against God while they know it﴾. Then He said, refuting them:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 76:

﴿Yes [indeed]﴾ means: it is not as they say; rather, "upon them there is no way [of blame regarding the unlettered]." Then he began and said, ﴿whoever fulfils﴾, meaning: but rather, whoever fulfils ﴿his covenant﴾, meaning: the covenant of Allah which He made with him in the Torah concerning belief in Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an, and the fulfilment of trusts. It has also been said: the pronoun in "his covenant" refers back to the one who fulfils. ﴿And fears [Allah]﴾ from disbelief, treachery and breaking the covenant, ﴿then indeed Allah loves those who are mindful [of Him]﴾.

Abdul-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Qabisah ibn Uqbah informed us: Sufyan narrated to us from al-A'mash, from Abdullah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Umar, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There are four qualities whoever has them is a pure hypocrite, and whoever has one of them has a quality of hypocrisy until he gives it up: when he is entrusted, he betrays; when he speaks, he lies; when he makes a covenant, he breaks it; and when he disputes, he acts wickedly." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Iman, chapter "The sign of the hypocrite" (1/89), and in al-Mazalim, chapter "And when he disputes, he acts wickedly" (5/107); and by Muslim in al-Iman, chapter "Explanation of the qualities of the hypocrite," no. (106) (1/78). The author also cited it in Sharh al-Sunnah (1/74).]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 3, verse 77:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price﴾. ʿIkrimah said: It was revealed concerning the chiefs of the Jews, who concealed what Allah had enjoined upon them in the Torah concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ). They altered it and wrote something else with their own hands, and they swore that it was from Allah, so that the food and bribes that they received from their followers would not be lost to them.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, that Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, that Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, that Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, that Musa ibn Isma'il informed us, that Abu ʿAwanah informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Wail, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever swears an oath of perjury (yamin sabr) by which he seizes the property of a Muslim man will meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection while He is angry with him." Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed, confirming that: ﴿Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price﴾ to the end of the verse. Then al-Ashʿath ibn Qays entered and said: "What is Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman telling you?" They said: "Such and such." He said: "It was revealed concerning me. I had a well in the land of a cousin of mine, so I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spoke to him. He said: 'Bring your proof, or his oath.' I said: 'In that case he will swear by it, O Messenger of Allah.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Whoever swears an oath of perjury, while he is a wrongdoer in it, by which he seizes the property of a Muslim man, will meet Allah on the Day of Resurrection while He is angry with him.'"

Abu Muhammad al-Baghawi (the author) reports, from Ismaʿil ibn Abd al-Qahir, that Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad al-Farisi informed us, that Muhammad ibn ʿIsa al-Juludi informed us, that Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us, that Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us, that Qutaybah ibn Saʿid informed us, that Abu al-Ahwas informed us, from Simak ibn Harb, from ʿAlqamah ibn Wail ibn Hujr, from his father, who said: A man from Hadramawt and a man from Kindah came to the Prophet (ﷺ). The Hadrami said: "O Messenger of Allah, this man has seized a land of mine that was my father's." The Kindi said: "It is land in my possession that I cultivate; he has no right in it." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to the Hadrami: "Do you have a proof?" He said: "No." He said: "Then his oath is due from him." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, this man is a wrongdoer and does not care what he swears to." He said: "You have no right over him except that." So he set off to swear to him. When he turned away, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, if he swears regarding his property in order to consume it unjustly, he will meet Allah while He is turned away from him."

ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr narrated it from ʿAlqamah and said that the man was Imru al-Qays ibn ʿAbis al-Kindi, and his opponent was Rabiʿah ibn ʿAbdan.

It is also narrated that when he (Imru al-Qays) intended to swear, this verse was revealed, so Imru al-Qays refrained from swearing, acknowledged his opponent's right, and handed it over to him.

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us, that Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Sarakhsi informed us, that Abu Musʿab informed us, from Malik, from al-ʿAlaʾ ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Saʿid ibn Kaʿb, from his brother Abd Allah ibn Kaʿb ibn Malik, from Abu Umamah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever seizes the right of a Muslim man by his oath, Allah forbids Paradise to him and makes the Fire obligatory for him." They said: "Even if it is a small thing, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Even if it is a twig of arak wood." He said it three times.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, that Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, that Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, that Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, that ʿAmr ibn Muhammad informed us, that Hushaym ibn Muhammad informed us, that al-ʿAwwam ibn Hawshab informed us, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa, that a man displayed merchandise in the market and swore by Allah that he had been offered for it what he had not been offered, in order to deceive a Muslim man into it. So this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price﴾.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who exchange﴾, that is, who substitute, ﴿the covenant of Allah﴾, and He meant the trust, ﴿and their oaths﴾, the false ones, ﴿for a small price﴾, that is, a small amount of the worldly goods. ﴿Those have no share﴾, meaning no portion, ﴿in the Hereafter﴾ or its bounties. ﴿Allah will not speak to them﴾ with speech that benefits them or gladdens them. It was said: this means anger, just as a man says: "I will not speak to so-and-so," when he is angry with him. ﴿Nor will He look at them on the Day of Resurrection﴾, that is, He will not show mercy to them, nor do good to them, nor bestow any goodness upon them. ﴿Nor will He purify them﴾, that is, He will not praise them with good words, nor cleanse them of sins. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment﴾.

Ismaʿil ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us, that Abd al-Ghaffar ibn Muhammad al-Farisi informed us, that Muhammad ibn ʿIsa al-Juludi informed us, that Ibrahim ibn Muhammad informed us, that Sufyan informed us, that Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us, that Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar informed us, from Shuʿbah, from ʿAli ibn Mudrik, from Abu Zurʿah, from Kharashah ibn al-Hurr, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Three people, Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor look at them, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it three times. Abu Dharr said: "They have failed and lost. Who are they, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The one who lets his garment hang down, the one who reminds of his favours (by giving), and the one who promotes his merchandise with a false oath." [Muslim, Iman, chapter on the severity of the prohibition of letting the garment hang down and reminding of gifts, no. 171.] In another narration: "The one who lets his garment hang down."

Imam Abu ʿAli al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us, that Usayd Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-ʿAlawi informed us, that Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Hamdawayh al-Marwazi informed us, that Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Dinar, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Three people, Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor look at them, nor purify them, and for them is a painful punishment: a man who swore an oath regarding the property of a Muslim in order to seize it; a man who swore a false oath after the afternoon prayer that he had been offered more for his merchandise than he had been offered, while he was lying; and a man who withheld the surplus of his water, and Allah, exalted is He, says: 'Today I withhold from you My surplus, just as you withheld the surplus of what your hands did not produce.'"

They were Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, Malik ibn al-Sayf, Huyayy ibn Akhtab, Abu Yasir, and Shu'bah ibn Umar the poet. ﴿who distort their tongues with the Book﴾ meaning: they twist their tongues with distortion and alteration, and this is what they changed of the description of the Prophet ﷺ and the verse of stoning, and other things. It is said: "lawa lisanahu 'ala kadha" (he twisted his tongue regarding such-and-such), meaning he altered it. ﴿That you may think it is from the Book﴾ meaning: that you may suppose what they distorted to be ﴿from the Book﴾ which Allah, exalted is He, revealed. ﴿But it is not from the Book. And they say, "It is from Allah," but it is not from Allah. And they speak falsehood about Allah while they know﴾ deliberately, ﴿while they know﴾ that they are liars. Al-Dahhak reported from Ibn Abbas that the verse was revealed concerning both the Jews and the Christians together, because they distorted the Torah and the Gospel and added to the Book of Allah what was not part of it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is not for a human being that Allah should give him the Book﴾ — the verse. Muqatil and al-Dahhak said: "It is not for a human being" refers to Jesus, peace be upon him. This is because the Christians of Najran used to say that Jesus commanded them to take him as a lord, so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿It is not for a human being﴾, meaning Jesus, ﴿that Allah should give him the Book﴾, meaning the Gospel [[Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 146.]].

Ibn Abbas and Ata said: ﴿It is not for a human being﴾ meaning Muhammad, ﴿that Allah should give him the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an. This is because Abu Rafi' al-Qurazi from the Jews, and the chief [[In B: "laysa", which is an error. In al-Wahidi: "al-Rayis".]] of the Christians of Najran, said: "O Muhammad, do you want us to worship you and take you as a lord?" He said: "I seek refuge in Allah from commanding the worship of other than Allah; it is not for this that Allah sent me, nor for this did He command me [[In B: "ba'thani".]]." So Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse [[Narrated by Ibn Ishaq in the Sirah, and from him al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 6/539. They differed regarding it. Ali, Ibn Abbas and al-Hasan said: "Be jurists and scholars." Qatadah said: "Wise men and scholars." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The scholar who acts upon his knowledge." It is reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: "Jurists who teach."

It is also said: the rabbani is the one who trains people with the lesser knowledge before the greater. Ata said: "Scholars, wise men, and sincere advisers to Allah among His creation." Abu Ubayda said: I heard a learned man say: "The rabbani is the one knowledgeable in the lawful and the unlawful, in commanding and forbidding, knowledgeable of the news of the community, what has been and what will be." It is also said: the rabbaniyyun are above the ahbar (rabbis), and the ahbar are the scholars, while the rabbaniyyun are those who combine knowledge with insight into managing people.

Al-Mu'arrij said: "Be rabbaniyyin, submitting to your Lord," from rububiyyah (lordship). Originally it was rabbiyy, then an alif was added for emphasis, then a nun was added because of the alif's sukun, as it is said: san'ani and bahrani.

Al-Mubarrad said: they are masters of knowledge, named thus because they nurture knowledge, uphold it, and nurture those who learn it with the lesser sciences before the greater ones. Whoever takes charge of correcting and completing something has nurtured it, yarubbuhu. Its singular is "rabban," (as they said: rayyan) and 'atshan, shab'an and 'uryan; then the nisbah ya' was attached to it, as they said: lihyani and raqabani.

It is related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "It is the one who nurtures his knowledge through his action." Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said when Ibn Abbas died: "Today the rabbani of this community has died."

﴿Because you have been﴾, meaning: because you are, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?﴾ (Surah Maryam, verse 29), meaning: who is in the cradle. ﴿Teaching the Book﴾. Ibn Amir, Asim, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "tu'allimuna" with the doubled 'ayn, from ta'lim (teaching). The others read "ta'lamuna" with the single 'ayn, from 'ilm (knowledge), like His saying: ﴿and because you have been studying﴾, meaning: you have been reading.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 3, verses 80–81:**

His saying, ﴿nor would He command you﴾: Ibn 'Amir, 'Asim, Hamzah and Ya'qub read *wa-la yamurakum* with a fatha on the *ra'* (*naṣb*), coordinating it with his saying *thumma yaqula* ("then he says"). The verb is then subordinate to "human being" (*al-bashar*), meaning: "nor would that human being command." It is also said that the verb is governed by an implied *an* (the subjunctive particle), meaning: "nor that that human being would command." The rest of the readers read it with a *damma* on the *ra'* (*raf'*), as a new sentence (*isti'naf*). Its meaning is: "nor would God command you." Ibn Juraij and a group said: "nor would Muhammad command you" (ﷺ).

﴿that you take the angels and the prophets as lords﴾, like the act of the Quraysh and the Sabians, who said, "the angels are the daughters of God," and like the Jews and Christians, who said about the Messiah and 'Uzayr what they said.

﴿Would he command you to disbelief after you have submitted?﴾ He said this in the manner of astonishment and denial, meaning: he would not say this.

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿And when God took the covenant of the prophets: "Whatever I have given you of Scripture and wisdom..."﴾ Hamzah read *limā* with a kasra on the *lām*, and the others read it with a fatha. Whoever reads the *lām* with a kasra, it is the *lām* of attribution (*lām al-idafah*) that has entered upon *mā*, and its meaning is "that which" (*alladhī*), meaning: He took the covenant of the prophets for the sake of that which He gave them of the Scripture and wisdom, that is, that they are the possessors of the sacred laws (*ashāb al-sharā'i'*). Whoever reads the *lām* with a fatha, its meaning is "for that which I have given you," in the sense of a statement (*khabar*). It is also said that it is in the sense of a conditional (*jazā'*), meaning: "if I give you" or "whatever I give you," and the answer of the conditional is His saying, ﴿you shall surely believe in him﴾.

His saying: ﴿Whatever I have given you﴾: Nafi' and the people of Medina read *ātaynākum* ("We have given you") in the plural of majesty, as in: "And We gave David the Psalms" (4:163) and "And We gave him wisdom as a child" (19:12). The rest of the readers read it with a *ta'* (*ātaytukum*), to agree with the written text (*al-khatt*) and because of His saying: ﴿and I am with you﴾.

The scholars differed concerning who is meant by this verse. One group held that God took the covenant from the prophets specifically, that they should convey the Book of God and His messages to His servants, that they should confirm one another, and that He took the pledge from every prophet that he would believe in the prophets who would come after him and support him if he lived to see him; and if he did not live to see him, that he would command his people to support him if they lived to see him. Thus He took the covenant from Moses that he would believe in Jesus, and from Jesus that he would believe in Muhammad (ﷺ).

[Others said: He took the covenant from them concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ).] According to this view, they differed. Some said: He took the covenant only from the People of the Book to whom He sent the prophets. This is the view of Mujahid and al-Rabi'. Do you not see His saying: ﴿Then there will come to you a messenger confirming what is with you, you shall surely believe in him and surely support him﴾? Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent to the People of the Book, not to the prophets. What proves this is that in the reading of 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy ibn Ka'b it is: ﴿And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture﴾. As for the well-known reading, ﴿And when God took the covenant of the prophets﴾, it means: God took the covenant of the prophets that they should take the pledge from their nations, that they should believe in Muhammad (ﷺ), confirm him, and support him if they lived to see him.

Some of them said: He meant that God took the covenant from the prophets and their nations altogether concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ), so He sufficed with mentioning the prophets, because the covenant with the leader is a covenant upon the followers. This is the meaning of the saying of Ibn 'Abbas. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: God did not send any prophet, from Adam onward, without taking from him the covenant concerning the matter of Muhammad, and taking the covenant from his people that they would believe in him, and that if he were sent while they were alive, they would surely support him.

His saying: ﴿Then there will come to you a messenger confirming what is with you﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿you shall surely believe in him and surely support him﴾. God, may He be exalted, says to the prophets, when He brought forth the offspring from the loins of Adam (peace be upon him), and the prophets among them were like lamps and lights, and He took from them the covenant concerning the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿He said: "Do you acknowledge and accept My covenant on that?"﴾, meaning: "Do you accept My pledge upon that?" The *iṣr* is the heavy covenant. ﴿They said: "We acknowledge it." He said﴾, may God be exalted: ﴿"Then bear witness"﴾, meaning: "Then bear witness, you yourselves, against yourselves and against your followers," ﴿and I am with you among the witnesses﴾ against you and against them. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Then bear witness" means "then know." Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: God said to the angels, "Then bear witness against them," as an allusion to an unmentioned party.

**Surah 3 (Āl ʿImrān), verse 82, in al-Baghawi's commentary (Maʿālim al-Tanzīl):**

﴿Whoever turns away after that﴾ (i.e., after the affirmation), ﴿those are the defiant ones (al-fāsiqūn)﴾: the disobedient, those who have gone out of faith.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 83–90:

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah?﴾ The reason for this is that the People of the Book disagreed, and each one claimed that he was upon the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). They brought their dispute to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Both groups are free from the religion of Ibrahim (peace be upon him)." They became angry and said: "We will not accept your judgment, nor will we adopt your religion." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Do they seek other than the religion of Allah?﴾ [See: Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 4/127; al-Bahr al-Muhit of Abu Hayyan: 2/514; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. 146.]

Abu Ja'far, the people of Basra, and Hafs on the authority of 'Asim recited ﴿yabghun﴾ with the yā' (third-person masculine), in accordance with His saying: ﴿And those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ The others recited it with the tā' (second-person), in accordance with His saying: ﴿what I have given you﴾ and ﴿...﴾.

﴿And to Him has submitted﴾ means: submitted and yielded. ﴿whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or by compulsion﴾. So "willingly" (ṭawʿ) is yielding and following with ease, and "by compulsion" (karh) is that which is with hardship and the soul's reluctance.
