So this was revealed about them: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.﴾

﴿How will Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief?﴾ The wording is interrogative, but its meaning is negation, i.e., Allah does not guide them. It was also said its meaning is: how will Allah guide them in the Hereafter to Paradise and reward? ﴿And they had testified that the Messenger was true and that clear proofs had come to them. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

﴿Abiding therein; the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.﴾ The reason for this: when al-Harith ibn Suwayd joined the disbelievers, he regretted it, and sent to his people: "Ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Is there any repentance for me?" They did so, and Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Except for those who repent after that and reform, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

﴿Except for those who repent after that and reform, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [See: al-Tabari: 6/573; Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 147.] Because of what he had done, a man of his people brought it to him and recited it to him. Al-Harith said: "By Allah, as far as I know, you are truthful, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is more truthful than you, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is the most truthful of the three." Al-Harith returned to Madinah, embraced Islam, and his Islam was sound.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve after their belief and then increase in disbelief﴾. Qatadah and al-Hasan said: it was revealed concerning the Jews who disbelieved in 'Isa (peace be upon him) and the Injil after their belief in their prophets, then increased in disbelief by disbelieving in Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: it was revealed concerning the Jews and Christians who disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ) when they saw him, after their belief, by his description and attributes in their books; then they increased in disbelief, meaning: sins while in their state of disbelief.

Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning all disbelievers who associated partners with Allah after acknowledging that Allah is their Creator; then they increased in disbelief, meaning: they persisted in their disbelief until they died in it.

Al-Hasan said: "They increased in disbelief" means that whenever a verse was revealed, they disbelieved in it, and so they increased in disbelief. It was also said: they increased in disbelief by their saying: "We await for Muhammad the vicissitudes of time."

Al-Kalbi said: it was revealed concerning the eleven companions of al-Harith ibn Suwayd. When al-Harith returned to Islam, they remained in disbelief in Makkah and said: "We will remain in disbelief as long as we wish; whenever we want to return, what was revealed about al-Harith will be revealed about us." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, whoever of them entered Islam, his repentance was accepted, and it was revealed concerning those of them who died as disbelievers:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers﴾, to the end of the verse.

If it is said: Allah has promised to accept the repentance of whoever repents, so what is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Their repentance will never be accepted, and those are the astray﴾? It is said: their repentance will not be accepted if they turn back at the time of witnessing death, as He said: ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now"﴾ [al-Nisa': 18].

It was also said this refers to the companions of al-Harith ibn Suwayd, when they held back from Islam and said: "We will wait for Muhammad; if fortune favors him, we will return to his religion." Their repentance will not be accepted because they are waiting and not sincere in their conviction, and those are the astray.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on surah 3, verse 91:

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and die while they are disbelievers, never will be accepted from any of them the earth full of gold﴾, meaning: the amount that would fill the earth from its east to its west. ﴿Gold﴾ is in the accusative as a specification (*tafsir*, the grammatical term for *tamyīz*), like their saying: "twenty dirhams" (عِشْرُونَ دِرْهَمًا).

﴿Even if he would ransom himself with it﴾. It was said: its meaning is "even if he ransomed himself with it," and the *wāw* (وَ) is extra and inserted. ﴿For those will be a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers﴾.

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, Muhammad ibn Bashshar informed us, Ghundar informed us, Shu'bah informed us, from Abu Imran, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik narrate from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Allah will say to the least punished of the people of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection: 'If you had everything that is on the earth, would you ransom yourself with it?' He will say: 'Yes.' He will say: 'I wanted from you something easier than that while you were in the loins of Adam: that you not associate anything with Me, but you insisted on associating others with Me.'" [[Recorded by al-Bukhari in the Book of Softening of the Heart (*al-Riqaq*), chapter "Whoever Is Scrutinized in Reckoning Is Punished," 11/400, and in the chapter "Description of Paradise and Hellfire," 11/416, and in the Book of the Prophets, chapter "The Creation of Adam and His Offspring." Muslim recorded it in the Book on the Attributes of the Hypocrites and Their Rulings, chapter "The Disbeliever Seeking Ransom by Filling the Earth with Gold," no. 2805, 4/2160. Al-Musannif (al-Baghawi) also recorded it in *Sharh al-Sunnah*, 15/242.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 92:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿You will never attain righteousness﴾ means: Paradise. This is what Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and Mujahid said. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: piety (taqwa). It was also said: obedience (ta'ah). It was also said: good (khayr). Al-Hasan said: that you be righteous (abrar).

Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri told us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi told us: Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi told us, Muhammad ibn Hammad told us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah told us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, from 'Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Hold fast to truthfulness, for truthfulness leads to righteousness, and righteousness leads to Paradise. A man continues to tell the truth and strive for truthfulness until he is recorded with Allah as a siddiq (a person of great truthfulness). Beware of lying, for lying leads to wickedness, and wickedness leads to the Fire. A man continues to lie and strive for lying until he is recorded with Allah as a kadhdhab (a great liar)." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Adab, chapter on the saying of Allah, the Exalted: "O you who believe, fear Allah and be with the truthful": 10/507; and Muslim in al-Birr wa al-Silah, chapter on the ugliness of lying and the goodness of truthfulness, no. (2607), 4/2013; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/152.]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿until you spend from that which you love﴾ means: from the most beloved of your wealth to you. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that what is meant by it is the payment of zakat.

Mujahid and al-Kalbi said: this verse was abrogated (nasakha) by the verse of zakat. Al-Hasan said: every spending by which the Muslim seeks the Face of Allah, even a date, by it he attains this righteousness. 'Ata' said: ﴿You will never attain righteousness﴾ means the nobility of religion and piety, until you give charity while you are healthy and miserly.

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us, Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi told us, Abu Mus'ab told us, from Malik, from Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, that he heard Anas ibn Malik say: "Abu Talhah al-Ansari was the wealthiest of the Ansar in Madinah, and the most beloved of his property to him was Bayruha', which faced the mosque. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to enter it and drink from its pleasant water." Anas said: "When this verse was revealed, ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love﴾, Abu Talhah stood up before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, indeed Allah, exalted is He, says in His Book: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love﴾, and the most beloved of my property to me is Bayruha'. It is a charity for the sake of Allah; I hope for its righteousness and its reward with Allah. So place it, O Messenger of Allah, wherever you wish.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Bakh, bakh! That is profitable wealth' — or he said: 'That is profitable wealth, and I have heard what you said about it, and I think you should give it to your closest relatives.' Abu Talhah said: 'I will do so, O Messenger of Allah,' and Abu Talhah distributed it among his relatives and his paternal cousins." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Zakat, chapter on zakat to relatives: 3/325; in al-Wakalah, chapter on when a man says to his agent: place it where Allah shows you: 4/493; in the Tafsir, Tafsir of Surah Al 'Imran, chapter: "You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love": 8/223; and in al-Wasaya and al-Ashribah. Also narrated by Muslim in al-Zakat, chapter on the virtue of spending and charity on relatives, no. (998): 2/693; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 6/189-190.]

It is narrated from Mujahid that he said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) wrote to Abu Musa al-Ash'ari to buy for him a slave girl from the captives of Jalula' on the day it was conquered. She was brought to him and he was pleased with her, so he said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love﴾," and so 'Umar freed her. [Al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/260, attributed to 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir.]

And it is narrated from Hamzah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, who said: This verse occurred to the heart of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar: ﴿You will never attain righteousness until you spend from that which you love﴾. Ibn 'Umar said: "I considered what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had given me, and nothing was more beloved to me than a certain woman. She is free for the sake of Allah, the Exalted." He said: "Had it not been that I do not take back anything I have given for the sake of Allah, I would have married her." [Narrated by al-Tabari through the transmission of Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid: 6/588; see also al-Kafi al-Shafi by Ibn Hajar, p. 27; al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/260.]

﴿And whatever you spend, indeed Allah is Knowing of it﴾ means: He knows it and will reward it.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 93–94:**

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel, except what Israel had forbidden for himself before the Torah was sent down.﴾ The occasion of the revelation of this verse: the Jews said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, "You claim that you follow the religion (millah) of Ibrahim (Abraham)? Ibrahim did not eat the flesh of camels and their milk, but you eat them, so you are not upon his religion!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "That was lawful for Ibrahim, peace be upon him." They said, "Everything that we forbid today was forbidden to Nuh (Noah) and Ibrahim, until it reached us." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 3/2; Asbab al-Nuzul p. 148.]] ﴿All food was lawful to the Children of Israel﴾, meaning: except carrion and blood, for these were never lawful at any time.

﴿except what Israel had forbidden for himself﴾, and he is Ya'qub (Jacob), peace be upon him, ﴿before the Torah was sent down﴾. That is: the matter is not as they claimed, that the flesh and milk of camels were forbidden to Ibrahim; rather, everything was lawful for him and for the Children of Israel. Israel only forbade them for himself before the Torah was revealed, meaning: their prohibition is not in the Torah.

They differed concerning the food that Ya'qub forbade for himself and concerning its cause. Abu al-'Aliyah, 'Ata', Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: that food was the flesh of camels and their milk. It is narrated that Ya'qub fell severely ill and his sickness lasted long, so he vowed that if Allah healed him from his sickness, he would forbid the food and drink most beloved to him. The most beloved food to him was the flesh of camels, and the most beloved drink to him was their milk, so he forbade both.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, al-Suddi and al-Dahhak said: it was the veins (al-'uruq).

The cause of this was that he suffered from ʿirq al-nasa (sciatica, literally "vein of the hip"). The origin of his pain, as narrated by Juwaybir and Muqatil from al-Dahhak, was that Ya'qub had vowed that if Allah granted him twelve sons and he came to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) in good health, he would slaughter the last of them. Then an angel [from among the angels] [[Omitted from: A.]] met him and said, "O Ya'qub, you are a strong man, so do you wish to wrestle?" He grappled with him, but neither of them could throw the other. Then the angel pressed him with a single squeeze, and sciatica afflicted him because of it. Then the angel said to him, "As for me, if I had wished to throw you, I would have done so. But I squeezed you this squeeze because you had vowed that if you came to Bayt al-Maqdis in good health you would slaughter your last son. So Allah has made for you, through this squeeze, a way out of that." When Ya'qub arrived there, he intended to slaughter his son, but he forgot the angel's words. Then the angel came to him and said, "I only squeezed you to provide an escape, and your vow has been fulfilled, so there is no way for you to reach your son."

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi said: Ya'qub set out from Harran, wishing to reach Bayt al-Maqdis, when he fled from his brother 'Isaw (Esau). He was a fierce and powerful man. An angel met him, and Ya'qub thought that he was a thief, so he tried to throw him down. The angel squeezed Ya'qub's thigh, then ascended to the sky while Ya'qub, peace be upon him, watched him. Sciatica was then provoked in him, and he suffered from it great affliction and hardship. He could not sleep at night because of the pain, and he would spend the night crying out (zuqa'), that is, shrieking. So Ya'qub swore that if Allah healed him, he would not eat any vein, nor any food containing a vein, so he forbade it for himself. After that, his sons would follow the veins, removing them from the meat.

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas: When sciatica afflicted Ya'qub, the physicians prescribed that he avoid the flesh of camels, so Ya'qub forbade it for himself.

Al-Hasan said: Israel forbade for himself the flesh of the she-camel, as an act of worship to Allah the Exalted, so he asked his Lord to permit it for him, but Allah forbade it to his offspring [[See these reports in: al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/263–264.]].

Then they differed concerning the status of this forbidden food for the Children of Israel after the Torah was revealed. Al-Suddi said: Allah forbade them in the Torah what they had been forbidding before it was revealed. 'Atiyyah said: it was forbidden to them only through the prohibition of Israel, for he had said, "If Allah heals me, none of my offspring shall eat it," and it was not forbidden to them in the Torah. Al-Kalbi said: Allah did not forbid it ﴿to them﴾ [[Omitted from: A.]] in the Torah, but it was forbidden to them after the Torah because of their wrongdoing, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We forbade them good things which had been made lawful for them﴾ (Surat al-Nisa', verse 160). And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws, and of cattle and sheep We forbade them their fat, except what their backs carry or the entrails, or what is mixed with bone. That was Our recompense for their rebellion, and indeed We are truthful﴾ (Surat al-An'am, verse 146). Whenever the Children of Israel committed a great sin, Allah forbade them some good food, or sent upon them a plague (rijz), which is death.

Al-Dahhak said: none of that was forbidden to them, nor did Allah forbid it in the Torah. Rather, they forbade it upon themselves, following their father, and then they attributed its prohibition to Allah. So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, refuted them, and said: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿"Bring the Torah and recite it"﴾ until it becomes clear that it is as you have said, ﴿"if you are truthful."﴾ But they did not bring it. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said:

﴿So whoever fabricates a lie against Allah after that, those are the wrongdoers.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 95–98 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Say: "God has spoken the truth. So follow the religion of Abraham, a man of pure faith, and he was not one of the polytheists."﴾ He called them to follow the religion of Abraham because in following the religion of Abraham is following him (ﷺ).

God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds.﴾ The occasion of revelation of this verse: the Jews said to the Muslims, "Jerusalem is our qiblah (direction of prayer). It is superior to the Ka'bah and older, and it is the place of migration of the prophets." The Muslims said, "Rather, the Ka'bah is superior." So God the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds.﴾

﴿In it are clear signs: the station of Abraham. And whoever enters it is safe.﴾ None of these virtues belongs to Jerusalem.

The scholars differed concerning God the Exalted's words: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah.﴾ Some of them said: It is the first house that appeared upon the surface of the water at the creation of the heavens and the earth. God created it two thousand years before the earth, and it was a white foam upon the water, and the earth was spread out (duhiya) from beneath it. This is the view of Abdullah ibn Umar, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi.

Others said: It is the first house built on the earth. It is narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn that God the Exalted placed beneath the Throne a house, which is the Bayt al-Ma'mur (the Frequented House), and He commanded the angels to circumambulate it. Then He commanded the angels who dwell on the earth to build on the earth a house after its likeness and measure, so they built it, and its name is al-Dirah. And He commanded those on the earth to circumambulate it, just as the people of heaven circumambulate the Bayt al-Ma'mur.

It is also narrated that the angels built it two thousand years before the creation of Adam, and they used to make pilgrimage (hajj) to it. When Adam made the pilgrimage, the angels said, "Your pilgrimage is accepted, O Adam. We made pilgrimage to this House a thousand years before you." It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: He meant that it is the first house Adam built on the earth. It was also said: It is the first blessed house established on the earth as guidance for mankind. This is narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib. Al-Dahhak said: It is the first house in which blessing was placed. It was also said: It is the first house established for mankind to be visited in pilgrimage. It was also said: It is the first house made a qiblah for people. Al-Hasan and al-Kalbi said: Its meaning is: It is the first mosque and place of worship established for mankind, in which God is worshipped, as God the Exalted said: ﴿In houses which God has permitted to be raised﴾, meaning the mosques.[[See al-Tabari: 7/19–22, where this last view is preferred.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Musa ibn Isma'il informed us: Abd al-Wahid informed us: al-A'mash informed us: Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Taymi informed us, from his father, who said: I heard Abu Dharr say: I said, "O Messenger of God, which mosque was established on the earth first?" He said: "The Sacred Mosque." I said: "Then which?" He said: "The Farthest Mosque." I said: "How long was between them?" He said: "Forty years. Then wherever prayer overtakes you, pray, for the virtue is in it."[[Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Anbiya', chapter "Hadathana Musa ibn Isma'il": 6/407, and Muslim in al-Masajid wa Mawadi' al-Salah, no. (520): 1/370.]]

God the Exalted's words: ﴿at Bakkah﴾. A group said: It is Makkah itself, and this is the view of al-Dahhak. The Arabs interchange the letters ba' and mim, so they say: sabbada ra'sahu and sammadahu (he shaved his head), and darbatun lazib and lazim (a constant blow). Others said: Bakkah is the site of the House, and Makkah is the name of the whole town.

It was also said: Bakkah is the site of the House and the place of circumambulation (tawaf). It was named Bakkah because people crowd (yatabakkawna) in it, that is, they press against one another, and some pray in front of others, and some pass in front of others.

Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr said: It was named Bakkah because it breaks (tabukku) the necks of tyrants, that is, it crushes them. No tyrant intended it with evil except that God destroyed him.

As for Makkah, it was named so because of the scarcity of its water, from the saying of the Arabs: makka al-fasil dar' ummihi and amtakkahu, when the suckling camel sucks out all the milk in its mother's udder. It is also called Umm Rahm, because mercy descends upon it.

﴿Blessed﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), meaning: possessing blessing. ﴿And a guidance for the worlds﴾, because it is the qiblah of the believers. ﴿In it are clear signs﴾: Ibn Abbas recited ﴿a clear sign﴾ in the singular, and he meant the station of Abraham alone. The others recited ﴿clear signs﴾ in the plural, and so they mention among them the station of Abraham [[the stone]] on which Abraham stood, and the mark of his two feet was on it, but it was effaced from the great amount of rubbing by hands. Among those signs are: the Black Stone, al-Hatim, Zamzam, and all the places of rites. It was also said: The station of Abraham is the whole Haram. Among the signs in the House is that birds fly and do not rise above it, and that a hunting bird, when it pursues prey, if the prey enters the Haram it holds back from it. It is a land to which the prophets, the messengers, the saints and the righteous have journeyed, and the obedience and charity made in it are multiplied a hundredfold.

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Makhladi informed us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj informed us: Abu Mus'ab Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr al-Zuhri informed us: Malik ibn Anas informed us, from Zayd ibn Rabah and Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Abd Allah, from Abu Abd Allah al-Aghar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other, except the Sacred Mosque."[[Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Salah fi Masjid Makkah wa al-Madinah, chapter "Fadl al-Salah fi Masjid Makkah wa al-Madinah": 3/63, and Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter "Fadl al-Salah bi-Masjidayy Makkah wa al-Madinah," no. (1395): 2/1013, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/335.]]

God the Mighty and Majestic's words: ﴿And whoever enters it is safe﴾: this means from being attacked (in a dispute) within it. This was by the supplication of Abraham, peace be upon him, when he said: "My Lord, make this a secure land." The Arabs in the pre-Islamic era used to kill one another and raid one another, but whoever entered the Haram was safe from killing and raiding. This is the meaning of the verse according to al-Hasan, Qatadah and most of the exegetes. God the Exalted said: ﴿Do they not see that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are snatched away from around them?﴾ (Surah al-Ankabut, verse 67). It was also said: The meaning is that whoever entered it in the year of the Qada' 'Umrah with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was safe, as God the Exalted said: ﴿You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, in security﴾ (Surah al-Fath, verse 27). That is: For God there is an obligatory duty upon the people, the pilgrimage to the House. Abu Ja'far, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs recited ﴿hijj al-bayt﴾ with a kasrah on the ha' in this word only, and the others recited it with a fathah on the ha'. The latter is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. Both are eloquent dialects and their meaning is one.

Hajj is one of the pillars of Islam. Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Abd Allah ibn Musa informed us: Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan informed us, from Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, establishing the prayer, giving the zakat, the pilgrimage (hajj), and fasting in Ramadan."[[Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Iman, chapter "Du'a'ukum Iman'ukum": 1/49, and Muslim in al-Iman, chapter "Arkan al-Iman," no. **The Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi on surah 3, verses 95–98 (part 2 of 2)**

Its detail is that he finds a mount suitable for someone like him, and he has provisions for the going and the return, beyond the maintenance of his dependants and those whose maintenance is obligatory for him, for the journey there and back, and beyond any debt he owes. He also finds a travelling company that sets out at a time when it is the custom of the people of his town to set out. If they leave before him, or delay their departure until a time when they cannot arrive except by covering more than one stage (*marhalah*, a day's journey) each day, then he is not obliged to set out at that time. It is also required that the road be safe. If there is fear on it from an enemy, whether Muslim or non-Muslim, or from an ambusher (*rasadi*) who demands something he is not obliged to give, then the obligation does not apply. It is also required that the inhabited stations be populated, so that he finds provisions and water in them. If it is a time of drought (*judubah*), when its people have dispersed or its water has run dry, then he is not obliged. And if he does not find a mount but is able to walk, or does not find provisions but is able to earn them along the way, the pilgrimage (*hajj*) is not obligatory for him, though it is recommended if he does it. According to Malik, it is obligatory for him.

As for capacity through another (*al-istita'ah bil-ghayr*), it is this: the man is unable himself, either because he is disabled or because he has an illness that is not expected to go away, but he has wealth with which he can hire someone to perform the pilgrimage on his behalf. He is obliged to hire someone. Or, if he has no wealth, but his son or a stranger offers him the service of performing the pilgrimage on his behalf, then he is obliged to instruct them to do so, provided he trusts their sincerity. This is because the obligation of pilgrimage is tied to capacity. It is said in common usage: "So-and-so is able to build a house," even though he does not build it himself, but rather does so with his wealth or through his helpers.

According to Abu Hanifa, pilgrimage is not obligatory through the offer of service. According to Malik, it is not obligatory for the one who is permanently incapacitated (*al-ma'dub*) in terms of wealth.

The evidence of those who make it obligatory is what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us: Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi told us, Abu Mus'ab told us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, that he said: Al-Fadl ibn Abbas was riding behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when a woman from Khath'am came to him seeking a legal ruling. Al-Fadl began to look at her, and she looked at him, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned al-Fadl's face to the other side. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, the obligation of Allah upon His servants regarding the pilgrimage has come to my father while he is an elderly old man who cannot remain steady on the mount. May I perform the pilgrimage on his behalf?" He said: "Yes." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Pilgrimage, chapter on the obligation of pilgrimage and its virtue: 3/378; and in the chapter on performing pilgrimage on behalf of one who cannot remain steady on a mount, and the chapter on a woman performing pilgrimage on behalf of a man; and by Muslim in the Book of Pilgrimage, chapter on performing pilgrimage on behalf of one incapacitated by disability or who is in a state of ihram and the like, no. 1334: 2/973. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/25.]

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾. Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Ata said: it means he denies the obligation of pilgrimage. Mujahid said: it means whoever disbelieves in Allah and the Last Day.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: It was revealed concerning the Jews, when they said: "Pilgrimage to Makkah is not obligatory."

Al-Suddi said: It refers to one who finds what he needs for pilgrimage, then does not perform it until he dies; this is disbelief in it. Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi told us: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi told us: Abu al-Hasan al-Kalamati told us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar told us: Sahl ibn Ammar told us: Yazid ibn Harun told us: Shurayk told us, from al-Layth, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, from Abu Umamah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is not prevented by an apparent need, or a restraining illness, or an oppressive ruler, and does not perform pilgrimage, let him die, if he wishes, as a Jew, or if he wishes, as a Christian." [This hadith has been narrated with close wording from a number of the Companions through weak chains. Ibn al-Jawzi mentioned it in al-Mawdu'at (the fabricated reports), and al-Uqayli and al-Daraqutni said: nothing authentic has come concerning it. Ibn Hajar said: it has several chains. The first: al-Sa'id ibn Mansur recorded it in his Sunan, and Ahmad, Abu Ya'la and al-Bayhaqi recorded it through various routes from Shurayk, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Ibn Sabit, from Abu Umamah... Layth is weak, and Shurayk has poor memory. Sufyan opposed him and transmitted it as mursal (with a missing link). Ahmad narrated it in his Kitab al-Iman from Waki, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Ibn Sabit... as mursal, and Ibn Abi Shaybah mentioned it from Layth as mursal. Abu Ya'la cited it through another route from Shurayk from Layth, differing from the first chain. The second: from Ali, raised to the Prophet: "Whoever possesses provisions and a mount that would carry him to the House of Allah and does not perform pilgrimage, there is no harm upon him whether he dies as a Jew or a Christian." Al-Tirmidhi narrated it and said: gharib (rare), and there is criticism in its chain, and al-Harith is declared weak. Kitab al-Hajj, chapter on what has come concerning the severity regarding abandoning pilgrimage: 3/541. The third: from Abu Hurayrah, raised to the Prophet, narrated by Ibn Adi from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman al-Qatabi from Abu al-Mihzam, and both are abandoned (matruk). It has authentic routes, though they are stopped at the Companion level (mawquf), narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur and al-Bayhaqi from Umar ibn al-Khattab. Then he said: "When this mawquf report is combined with the mursal of Ibn Sabit, it is known that this hadith has a basis. Its meaning applies to one who considers abandoning it permissible, and this shows the error of one who claims it is fabricated. And Allah knows best." Talkhis al-Habir: 2/222–223; al-Kafi al-Shaf p. 28. See also: Nasb al-Raya of al-Zayla'i: 4/410–411.]

It is superior to the Ka'bah and older, and it is the place of migration of the prophets." The Muslims said, "Rather, the Ka'bah is superior." God created it two thousand years before the earth, and it was a white foam upon the water, and the earth was spread out (duhiya) from beneath it. This is the view of Abdullah ibn Umar, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi.

**The Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi on surah 3, verses 95–98 (part 2 of 2)**

Its detail is that he finds a mount suitable for someone like him, and he has provisions for the going and the return, beyond the maintenance of his dependants and those whose maintenance is obligatory for him, for the journey there and back, and beyond any debt he owes. He also finds a travelling company that sets out at a time when it is the custom of the people of his town to set out. If they leave before him, or delay their departure until a time when they cannot arrive except by covering more than one stage (*marhalah*, a day's journey) each day, then he is not obliged to set out at that time. It is also required that the road be safe. If there is fear on it from an enemy, whether Muslim or non-Muslim, or from an ambusher (*rasadi*) who demands something he is not obliged to give, then the obligation does not apply. It is also required that the inhabited stations be populated, so that he finds provisions and water in them. If it is a time of drought (*judubah*), when its people have dispersed or its water has run dry, then he is not obliged. And if he does not find a mount but is able to walk, or does not find provisions but is able to earn them along the way, the pilgrimage (*hajj*) is not obligatory for him, though it is recommended if he does it. According to Malik, it is obligatory for him.

As for capacity through another (*al-istita'ah bil-ghayr*), it is this: the man is unable himself, either because he is disabled or because he has an illness that is not expected to go away, but he has wealth with which he can hire someone to perform the pilgrimage on his behalf. He is obliged to hire someone. Or, if he has no wealth, but his son or a stranger offers him the service of performing the pilgrimage on his behalf, then he is obliged to instruct them to do so, provided he trusts their sincerity. This is because the obligation of pilgrimage is tied to capacity. It is said in common usage: "So-and-so is able to build a house," even though he does not build it himself, but rather does so with his wealth or through his helpers.

According to Abu Hanifa, pilgrimage is not obligatory through the offer of service. According to Malik, it is not obligatory for the one who is permanently incapacitated (*al-ma'dub*) in terms of wealth.

The evidence of those who make it obligatory is what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us: Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi told us, Abu Mus'ab told us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, that he said: Al-Fadl ibn Abbas was riding behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when a woman from Khath'am came to him seeking a legal ruling. Al-Fadl began to look at her, and she looked at him, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned al-Fadl's face to the other side. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, the obligation of Allah upon His servants regarding the pilgrimage has come to my father while he is an elderly old man who cannot remain steady on the mount. May I perform the pilgrimage on his behalf?" He said: "Yes." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Pilgrimage, chapter on the obligation of pilgrimage and its virtue: 3/378; and in the chapter on performing pilgrimage on behalf of one who cannot remain steady on a mount, and the chapter on a woman performing pilgrimage on behalf of a man; and by Muslim in the Book of Pilgrimage, chapter on performing pilgrimage on behalf of one incapacitated by disability or who is in a state of ihram and the like, no. 1334: 2/973. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/25.]

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾. Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Ata said: it means he denies the obligation of pilgrimage. Mujahid said: it means whoever disbelieves in Allah and the Last Day.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: It was revealed concerning the Jews, when they said: "Pilgrimage to Makkah is not obligatory."

Al-Suddi said: It refers to one who finds what he needs for pilgrimage, then does not perform it until he dies; this is disbelief in it. Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi told us: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi told us: Abu al-Hasan al-Kalamati told us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar told us: Sahl ibn Ammar told us: Yazid ibn Harun told us: Shurayk told us, from al-Layth, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, from Abu Umamah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is not prevented by an apparent need, or a restraining illness, or an oppressive ruler, and does not perform pilgrimage, let him die, if he wishes, as a Jew, or if he wishes, as a Christian." [This hadith has been narrated with close wording from a number of the Companions through weak chains. Ibn al-Jawzi mentioned it in al-Mawdu'at (the fabricated reports), and al-Uqayli and al-Daraqutni said: nothing authentic has come concerning it. Ibn Hajar said: it has several chains. The first: al-Sa'id ibn Mansur recorded it in his Sunan, and Ahmad, Abu Ya'la and al-Bayhaqi recorded it through various routes from Shurayk, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Ibn Sabit, from Abu Umamah... Layth is weak, and Shurayk has poor memory. Sufyan opposed him and transmitted it as mursal (with a missing link). Ahmad narrated it in his Kitab al-Iman from Waki, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Ibn Sabit... as mursal, and Ibn Abi Shaybah mentioned it from Layth as mursal. Abu Ya'la cited it through another route from Shurayk from Layth, differing from the first chain. The second: from Ali, raised to the Prophet: "Whoever possesses provisions and a mount that would carry him to the House of Allah and does not perform pilgrimage, there is no harm upon him whether he dies as a Jew or a Christian." Al-Tirmidhi narrated it and said: gharib (rare), and there is criticism in its chain, and al-Harith is declared weak. Kitab al-Hajj, chapter on what has come concerning the severity regarding abandoning pilgrimage: 3/541. The third: from Abu Hurayrah, raised to the Prophet, narrated by Ibn Adi from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman al-Qatabi from Abu al-Mihzam, and both are abandoned (matruk). It has authentic routes, though they are stopped at the Companion level (mawquf), narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur and al-Bayhaqi from Umar ibn al-Khattab. Then he said: "When this mawquf report is combined with the mursal of Ibn Sabit, it is known that this hadith has a basis. Its meaning applies to one who considers abandoning it permissible, and this shows the error of one who claims it is fabricated. And Allah knows best." Talkhis al-Habir: 2/222–223; al-Kafi al-Shaf p. 28. See also: Nasb al-Raya of al-Zayla'i: 4/410–411.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 95–98 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Say: "God has spoken the truth. So follow the religion of Abraham, a man of pure faith, and he was not one of the polytheists."﴾ He called them to follow the religion of Abraham because in following the religion of Abraham is following him (ﷺ).

God the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds.﴾ The occasion of revelation of this verse: the Jews said to the Muslims, "Jerusalem is our qiblah (direction of prayer). It is superior to the Ka'bah and older, and it is the place of migration of the prophets." The Muslims said, "Rather, the Ka'bah is superior." So God the Exalted revealed: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds.﴾

﴿In it are clear signs: the station of Abraham. And whoever enters it is safe.﴾ None of these virtues belongs to Jerusalem.

The scholars differed concerning God the Exalted's words: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah.﴾ Some of them said: It is the first house that appeared upon the surface of the water at the creation of the heavens and the earth. God created it two thousand years before the earth, and it was a white foam upon the water, and the earth was spread out (duhiya) from beneath it. This is the view of Abdullah ibn Umar, Mujahid, Qatadah and al-Suddi.

Others said: It is the first house built on the earth. It is narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn that God the Exalted placed beneath the Throne a house, which is the Bayt al-Ma'mur (the Frequented House), and He commanded the angels to circumambulate it. Then He commanded the angels who dwell on the earth to build on the earth a house after its likeness and measure, so they built it, and its name is al-Dirah. And He commanded those on the earth to circumambulate it, just as the people of heaven circumambulate the Bayt al-Ma'mur.

It is also narrated that the angels built it two thousand years before the creation of Adam, and they used to make pilgrimage (hajj) to it. When Adam made the pilgrimage, the angels said, "Your pilgrimage is accepted, O Adam. We made pilgrimage to this House a thousand years before you." It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: He meant that it is the first house Adam built on the earth. It was also said: It is the first blessed house established on the earth as guidance for mankind. This is narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib. Al-Dahhak said: It is the first house in which blessing was placed. It was also said: It is the first house established for mankind to be visited in pilgrimage. It was also said: It is the first house made a qiblah for people. Al-Hasan and al-Kalbi said: Its meaning is: It is the first mosque and place of worship established for mankind, in which God is worshipped, as God the Exalted said: ﴿In houses which God has permitted to be raised﴾, meaning the mosques.[[See al-Tabari: 7/19–22, where this last view is preferred.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Musa ibn Isma'il informed us: Abd al-Wahid informed us: al-A'mash informed us: Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Taymi informed us, from his father, who said: I heard Abu Dharr say: I said, "O Messenger of God, which mosque was established on the earth first?" He said: "The Sacred Mosque." I said: "Then which?" He said: "The Farthest Mosque." I said: "How long was between them?" He said: "Forty years. Then wherever prayer overtakes you, pray, for the virtue is in it."[[Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Anbiya', chapter "Hadathana Musa ibn Isma'il": 6/407, and Muslim in al-Masajid wa Mawadi' al-Salah, no. (520): 1/370.]]

God the Exalted's words: ﴿at Bakkah﴾. A group said: It is Makkah itself, and this is the view of al-Dahhak. The Arabs interchange the letters ba' and mim, so they say: sabbada ra'sahu and sammadahu (he shaved his head), and darbatun lazib and lazim (a constant blow). Others said: Bakkah is the site of the House, and Makkah is the name of the whole town.

It was also said: Bakkah is the site of the House and the place of circumambulation (tawaf). It was named Bakkah because people crowd (yatabakkawna) in it, that is, they press against one another, and some pray in front of others, and some pass in front of others.

Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr said: It was named Bakkah because it breaks (tabukku) the necks of tyrants, that is, it crushes them. No tyrant intended it with evil except that God destroyed him.

As for Makkah, it was named so because of the scarcity of its water, from the saying of the Arabs: makka al-fasil dar' ummihi and amtakkahu, when the suckling camel sucks out all the milk in its mother's udder. It is also called Umm Rahm, because mercy descends upon it.

﴿Blessed﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), meaning: possessing blessing. ﴿And a guidance for the worlds﴾, because it is the qiblah of the believers. ﴿In it are clear signs﴾: Ibn Abbas recited ﴿a clear sign﴾ in the singular, and he meant the station of Abraham alone. The others recited ﴿clear signs﴾ in the plural, and so they mention among them the station of Abraham [[the stone]] on which Abraham stood, and the mark of his two feet was on it, but it was effaced from the great amount of rubbing by hands. Among those signs are: the Black Stone, al-Hatim, Zamzam, and all the places of rites. It was also said: The station of Abraham is the whole Haram. Among the signs in the House is that birds fly and do not rise above it, and that a hunting bird, when it pursues prey, if the prey enters the Haram it holds back from it. It is a land to which the prophets, the messengers, the saints and the righteous have journeyed, and the obedience and charity made in it are multiplied a hundredfold.

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Makhladi informed us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj informed us: Abu Mus'ab Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr al-Zuhri informed us: Malik ibn Anas informed us, from Zayd ibn Rabah and Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Abd Allah, from Abu Abd Allah al-Aghar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other, except the Sacred Mosque."[[Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Salah fi Masjid Makkah wa al-Madinah, chapter "Fadl al-Salah fi Masjid Makkah wa al-Madinah": 3/63, and Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter "Fadl al-Salah bi-Masjidayy Makkah wa al-Madinah," no. (1395): 2/1013, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/335.]]

God the Mighty and Majestic's words: ﴿And whoever enters it is safe﴾: this means from being attacked (in a dispute) within it. This was by the supplication of Abraham, peace be upon him, when he said: "My Lord, make this a secure land." The Arabs in the pre-Islamic era used to kill one another and raid one another, but whoever entered the Haram was safe from killing and raiding. This is the meaning of the verse according to al-Hasan, Qatadah and most of the exegetes. God the Exalted said: ﴿Do they not see that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are snatched away from around them?﴾ (Surah al-Ankabut, verse 67). It was also said: The meaning is that whoever entered it in the year of the Qada' 'Umrah with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was safe, as God the Exalted said: ﴿You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, in security﴾ (Surah al-Fath, verse 27). It was also said: It is a report with the meaning of a command, its implied sense being: "Whoever enters it, grant him security," like His words: ﴿So there shall be no obscenity, nor wickedness, nor disputing during the pilgrimage﴾ [al-Baqarah: 197], meaning: Do not commit obscenity and do not commit wickedness. Some scholars went so far as to say that whoever is liable to be killed by retribution (qisas) or by a fixed penalty (hadd), and then takes refuge in the Haram, is not to be executed within it, but he is not to be fed, sold to, or bought from, until he leaves it and is then killed. This was said by Ibn Abbas, and Abu Hanifah held this view. Others held that the killing required by the Law is carried out within it. However, if someone commits the crime within the Haram, his punishment is carried out within it by consensus.

It was also said: Its meaning is: whoever enters it, magnifying it and seeking nearness to God the Mighty and Majestic, will be safe on the Day of Resurrection from the punishment.

God the Mighty and Majestic's words: ﴿And for God, upon the people, is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾. That is: For God there is an obligatory duty upon the people, the pilgrimage to the House. Abu Ja'far, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs recited ﴿hijj al-bayt﴾ with a kasrah on the ha' in this word only, and the others recited it with a fathah on the ha'. The latter is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. Both are eloquent dialects and their meaning is one.

Hajj is one of the pillars of Islam. Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Abd Allah ibn Musa informed us: Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan informed us, from Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, establishing the prayer, giving the zakat, the pilgrimage (hajj), and fasting in Ramadan."[[Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Iman, chapter "Du'a'ukum Iman'ukum": 1/49, and Muslim in al-Iman, chapter "Arkan al-Iman," no. (19): 1/45, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/17.]]

The scholars said: For the obligation of hajj there are five conditions: Islam, sanity, puberty, freedom, and capability (istita'ah). Thus it is not obligatory upon the disbeliever or the insane. And if they perform it themselves, it is not valid, because the disbeliever is not among those eligible for worship, and the insane person's act has no legal standing. It is not obligatory upon a child or a slave. If a discerning child performs it, or a slave, their hajj is valid as a voluntary act, but it does not discharge the obligatory duty of Islam from them. So if the child reaches puberty, or the slave is freed, after having performed hajj, and the conditions for the obligation of hajj are fulfilled in his case, it becomes obligatory upon him to perform hajj again. It is not obligatory upon one who is not capable, due to God's words: ﴿for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾. However, if he undertakes it with hardship and performs hajj, the obligatory duty of Islam is discharged from him.

Capability is of two kinds. One is being capable by his own body, and the other is being capable through another. As for capability by one's own body, it means being able to travel by oneself, and finding provision and a mount. Abd al-Wahid ibn Muhammad al-Kisa'i al-Khatib informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal narrated to us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us: al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Sa'id ibn Salim informed us, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abbad ibn Ja'far, who said: We sat with Abd Allah ibn Umar, and I heard him say: A man asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ), "What is the pilgrim (hajj)?" He said: "The dishevelled, the unkempt." Then another man stood up and said: "O Messenger of God, which hajj is best?" He said: "Raising the voice in the talbiyah and shedding blood (sacrifice)." Then another man stood up and said: "O Messenger of God, what is the way (sabil)?" He said: "Provision and a mount."[[Reported by al-Tirmidhi in al-Tafsir, Tafsir Surat Al 'Imran: 8/348, and he said: "This is a hadith we do not know except from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Khuzi al-Makki, and some scholars have spoken about Ibrahim ibn Yazid because of his memory." Al-Shafi'i in Tartib al-Musnad: 1/284. Ibn Majah reported it in al-Manasik, chapter "Ma Yujib al-Hajj," no. (2896): 2/967, al-Daraqutni in al-Sunan: 2/217, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/14. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Talkhis al-Habir: 2/221: "All its chains are weak." Abd al-Haqq said: All its chains are weak. Abu Bakr ibn al-Mundhir said: The hadith is not authentically established as a musnad report on this matter, and the sound of the narrations is the report of al-Hasan as a mursal.]]
