When Adam made the pilgrimage, the angels said, "Your pilgrimage is accepted, O Adam. We made pilgrimage to this House a thousand years before you." It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: He meant that it is the first house Adam built on the earth. It was also said: It is the first blessed house established on the earth as guidance for mankind. This is narrated from Ali ibn Abi Talib. Al-Dahhak said: It is the first house in which blessing was placed. It was also said: It is the first house established for mankind to be visited in pilgrimage. It was also said: It is the first house made a qiblah for people. Al-Hasan and al-Kalbi said: Its meaning is: It is the first mosque and place of worship established for mankind, in which God is worshipped, as God the Exalted said: ﴿In houses which God has permitted to be raised﴾, meaning the mosques.[[See al-Tabari: 7/19–22, where this last view is preferred.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Musa ibn Isma'il informed us: Abd al-Wahid informed us: al-A'mash informed us: Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Taymi informed us, from his father, who said: I heard Abu Dharr say: I said, "O Messenger of God, which mosque was established on the earth first?" He said: "The Sacred Mosque." I said: "Then which?" He said: "The Farthest Mosque." I said: "How long was between them?" He said: "Forty years. Then wherever prayer overtakes you, pray, for the virtue is in it."[[Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Anbiya', chapter "Hadathana Musa ibn Isma'il": 6/407, and Muslim in al-Masajid wa Mawadi' al-Salah, no. (520): 1/370.]]

God the Exalted's words: ﴿at Bakkah﴾. A group said: It is Makkah itself, and this is the view of al-Dahhak. The Arabs interchange the letters ba' and mim, so they say: sabbada ra'sahu and sammadahu (he shaved his head), and darbatun lazib and lazim (a constant blow). Others said: Bakkah is the site of the House, and Makkah is the name of the whole town.

It was also said: Bakkah is the site of the House and the place of circumambulation (tawaf). It was named Bakkah because people crowd (yatabakkawna) in it, that is, they press against one another, and some pray in front of others, and some pass in front of others.

Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr said: It was named Bakkah because it breaks (tabukku) the necks of tyrants, that is, it crushes them. No tyrant intended it with evil except that God destroyed him.

As for Makkah, it was named so because of the scarcity of its water, from the saying of the Arabs: makka al-fasil dar' ummihi and amtakkahu, when the suckling camel sucks out all the milk in its mother's udder. It is also called Umm Rahm, because mercy descends upon it.

﴿Blessed﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), meaning: possessing blessing. ﴿And a guidance for the worlds﴾, because it is the qiblah of the believers. ﴿In it are clear signs﴾: Ibn Abbas recited ﴿a clear sign﴾ in the singular, and he meant the station of Abraham alone. The others recited ﴿clear signs﴾ in the plural, and so they mention among them the station of Abraham [[the stone]] on which Abraham stood, and the mark of his two feet was on it, but it was effaced from the great amount of rubbing by hands. Among those signs are: the Black Stone, al-Hatim, Zamzam, and all the places of rites. It was also said: The station of Abraham is the whole Haram. Among the signs in the House is that birds fly and do not rise above it, and that a hunting bird, when it pursues prey, if the prey enters the Haram it holds back from it. It is a land to which the prophets, the messengers, the saints and the righteous have journeyed, and the obedience and charity made in it are multiplied a hundredfold.

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Makhladi informed us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sarraj informed us: Abu Mus'ab Ahmad ibn Abi Bakr al-Zuhri informed us: Malik ibn Anas informed us, from Zayd ibn Rabah and Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Abd Allah, from Abu Abd Allah al-Aghar, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers in any other, except the Sacred Mosque."[[Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Salah fi Masjid Makkah wa al-Madinah, chapter "Fadl al-Salah fi Masjid Makkah wa al-Madinah": 3/63, and Muslim in al-Hajj, chapter "Fadl al-Salah bi-Masjidayy Makkah wa al-Madinah," no. (1395): 2/1013, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 2/335.]]

God the Mighty and Majestic's words: ﴿And whoever enters it is safe﴾: this means from being attacked (in a dispute) within it. This was by the supplication of Abraham, peace be upon him, when he said: "My Lord, make this a secure land." The Arabs in the pre-Islamic era used to kill one another and raid one another, but whoever entered the Haram was safe from killing and raiding. This is the meaning of the verse according to al-Hasan, Qatadah and most of the exegetes. God the Exalted said: ﴿Do they not see that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are snatched away from around them?﴾ (Surah al-Ankabut, verse 67). It was also said: The meaning is that whoever entered it in the year of the Qada' 'Umrah with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was safe, as God the Exalted said: ﴿You will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, in security﴾ (Surah al-Fath, verse 27). It was also said: It is a report with the meaning of a command, its implied sense being: "Whoever enters it, grant him security," like His words: ﴿So there shall be no obscenity, nor wickedness, nor disputing during the pilgrimage﴾ [al-Baqarah: 197], meaning: Do not commit obscenity and do not commit wickedness. Some scholars went so far as to say that whoever is liable to be killed by retribution (qisas) or by a fixed penalty (hadd), and then takes refuge in the Haram, is not to be executed within it, but he is not to be fed, sold to, or bought from, until he leaves it and is then killed. This was said by Ibn Abbas, and Abu Hanifah held this view. Others held that the killing required by the Law is carried out within it. However, if someone commits the crime within the Haram, his punishment is carried out within it by consensus.

It was also said: Its meaning is: whoever enters it, magnifying it and seeking nearness to God the Mighty and Majestic, will be safe on the Day of Resurrection from the punishment.

God the Mighty and Majestic's words: ﴿And for God, upon the people, is the pilgrimage to the House, for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾. That is: For God there is an obligatory duty upon the people, the pilgrimage to the House. Abu Ja'far, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs recited ﴿hijj al-bayt﴾ with a kasrah on the ha' in this word only, and the others recited it with a fathah on the ha'. The latter is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. Both are eloquent dialects and their meaning is one.

Hajj is one of the pillars of Islam. Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Abd Allah ibn Musa informed us: Hanzalah ibn Abi Sufyan informed us, from Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Islam is built upon five: the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, establishing the prayer, giving the zakat, the pilgrimage (hajj), and fasting in Ramadan."[[Reported by al-Bukhari in al-Iman, chapter "Du'a'ukum Iman'ukum": 1/49, and Muslim in al-Iman, chapter "Arkan al-Iman," no. (19): 1/45, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/17.]]

The scholars said: For the obligation of hajj there are five conditions: Islam, sanity, puberty, freedom, and capability (istita'ah). Thus it is not obligatory upon the disbeliever or the insane. And if they perform it themselves, it is not valid, because the disbeliever is not among those eligible for worship, and the insane person's act has no legal standing. It is not obligatory upon a child or a slave. If a discerning child performs it, or a slave, their hajj is valid as a voluntary act, but it does not discharge the obligatory duty of Islam from them. So if the child reaches puberty, or the slave is freed, after having performed hajj, and the conditions for the obligation of hajj are fulfilled in his case, it becomes obligatory upon him to perform hajj again. It is not obligatory upon one who is not capable, due to God's words: ﴿for whoever is able to find a way to it﴾. However, if he undertakes it with hardship and performs hajj, the obligatory duty of Islam is discharged from him.

Capability is of two kinds. One is being capable by his own body, and the other is being capable through another. As for capability by one's own body, it means being able to travel by oneself, and finding provision and a mount. Abd al-Wahid ibn Muhammad al-Kisa'i al-Khatib informed us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal narrated to us: Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us: al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman informed us: al-Shafi'i informed us: Sa'id ibn Salim informed us, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abbad ibn Ja'far, who said: We sat with Abd Allah ibn Umar, and I heard him say: A man asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ), "What is the pilgrim (hajj)?" He said: "The dishevelled, the unkempt." Then another man stood up and said: "O Messenger of God, which hajj is best?" He said: "Raising the voice in the talbiyah and shedding blood (sacrifice)." Then another man stood up and said: "O Messenger of God, what is the way (sabil)?" He said: "Provision and a mount."[[Reported by al-Tirmidhi in al-Tafsir, Tafsir Surat Al 'Imran: 8/348, and he said: "This is a hadith we do not know except from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Khuzi al-Makki, and some scholars have spoken about Ibrahim ibn Yazid because of his memory." Al-Shafi'i in Tartib al-Musnad: 1/284. Ibn Majah reported it in al-Manasik, chapter "Ma Yujib al-Hajj," no. (2896): 2/967, al-Daraqutni in al-Sunan: 2/217, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/14. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Talkhis al-Habir: 2/221: "All its chains are weak." Abd al-Haqq said: All its chains are weak. Abu Bakr ibn al-Mundhir said: The hadith is not authentically established as a musnad report on this matter, and the sound of the narrations is the report of al-Hasan as a mursal.]]

**The Ma'alim al-Tanzil of al-Baghawi on surah 3, verses 95–98 (part 2 of 2)**

Its detail is that he finds a mount suitable for someone like him, and he has provisions for the going and the return, beyond the maintenance of his dependants and those whose maintenance is obligatory for him, for the journey there and back, and beyond any debt he owes. He also finds a travelling company that sets out at a time when it is the custom of the people of his town to set out. If they leave before him, or delay their departure until a time when they cannot arrive except by covering more than one stage (*marhalah*, a day's journey) each day, then he is not obliged to set out at that time. It is also required that the road be safe. If there is fear on it from an enemy, whether Muslim or non-Muslim, or from an ambusher (*rasadi*) who demands something he is not obliged to give, then the obligation does not apply. It is also required that the inhabited stations be populated, so that he finds provisions and water in them. If it is a time of drought (*judubah*), when its people have dispersed or its water has run dry, then he is not obliged. And if he does not find a mount but is able to walk, or does not find provisions but is able to earn them along the way, the pilgrimage (*hajj*) is not obligatory for him, though it is recommended if he does it. According to Malik, it is obligatory for him.

As for capacity through another (*al-istita'ah bil-ghayr*), it is this: the man is unable himself, either because he is disabled or because he has an illness that is not expected to go away, but he has wealth with which he can hire someone to perform the pilgrimage on his behalf. He is obliged to hire someone. Or, if he has no wealth, but his son or a stranger offers him the service of performing the pilgrimage on his behalf, then he is obliged to instruct them to do so, provided he trusts their sincerity. This is because the obligation of pilgrimage is tied to capacity. It is said in common usage: "So-and-so is able to build a house," even though he does not build it himself, but rather does so with his wealth or through his helpers.

According to Abu Hanifa, pilgrimage is not obligatory through the offer of service. According to Malik, it is not obligatory for the one who is permanently incapacitated (*al-ma'dub*) in terms of wealth.

The evidence of those who make it obligatory is what Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi told us: Zahir ibn Ahmad told us, Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi told us, Abu Mus'ab told us, from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, from Abdullah ibn Abbas, that he said: Al-Fadl ibn Abbas was riding behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when a woman from Khath'am came to him seeking a legal ruling. Al-Fadl began to look at her, and she looked at him, so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) turned al-Fadl's face to the other side. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, the obligation of Allah upon His servants regarding the pilgrimage has come to my father while he is an elderly old man who cannot remain steady on the mount. May I perform the pilgrimage on his behalf?" He said: "Yes." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Pilgrimage, chapter on the obligation of pilgrimage and its virtue: 3/378; and in the chapter on performing pilgrimage on behalf of one who cannot remain steady on a mount, and the chapter on a woman performing pilgrimage on behalf of a man; and by Muslim in the Book of Pilgrimage, chapter on performing pilgrimage on behalf of one incapacitated by disability or who is in a state of ihram and the like, no. 1334: 2/973. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 7/25.]

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is Free of need from the worlds﴾. Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan and Ata said: it means he denies the obligation of pilgrimage. Mujahid said: it means whoever disbelieves in Allah and the Last Day.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: It was revealed concerning the Jews, when they said: "Pilgrimage to Makkah is not obligatory."

Al-Suddi said: It refers to one who finds what he needs for pilgrimage, then does not perform it until he dies; this is disbelief in it. Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi told us: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi told us: Abu al-Hasan al-Kalamati told us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar told us: Sahl ibn Ammar told us: Yazid ibn Harun told us: Shurayk told us, from al-Layth, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Sabit, from Abu Umamah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is not prevented by an apparent need, or a restraining illness, or an oppressive ruler, and does not perform pilgrimage, let him die, if he wishes, as a Jew, or if he wishes, as a Christian." [This hadith has been narrated with close wording from a number of the Companions through weak chains. Ibn al-Jawzi mentioned it in al-Mawdu'at (the fabricated reports), and al-Uqayli and al-Daraqutni said: nothing authentic has come concerning it. Ibn Hajar said: it has several chains. The first: al-Sa'id ibn Mansur recorded it in his Sunan, and Ahmad, Abu Ya'la and al-Bayhaqi recorded it through various routes from Shurayk, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Ibn Sabit, from Abu Umamah... Layth is weak, and Shurayk has poor memory. Sufyan opposed him and transmitted it as mursal (with a missing link). Ahmad narrated it in his Kitab al-Iman from Waki, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Ibn Sabit... as mursal, and Ibn Abi Shaybah mentioned it from Layth as mursal. Abu Ya'la cited it through another route from Shurayk from Layth, differing from the first chain. The second: from Ali, raised to the Prophet: "Whoever possesses provisions and a mount that would carry him to the House of Allah and does not perform pilgrimage, there is no harm upon him whether he dies as a Jew or a Christian." Al-Tirmidhi narrated it and said: gharib (rare), and there is criticism in its chain, and al-Harith is declared weak. Kitab al-Hajj, chapter on what has come concerning the severity regarding abandoning pilgrimage: 3/541. The third: from Abu Hurayrah, raised to the Prophet, narrated by Ibn Adi from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman al-Qatabi from Abu al-Mihzam, and both are abandoned (matruk). It has authentic routes, though they are stopped at the Companion level (mawquf), narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur and al-Bayhaqi from Umar ibn al-Khattab. Then he said: "When this mawquf report is combined with the mursal of Ibn Sabit, it is known that this hadith has a basis. Its meaning applies to one who considers abandoning it permissible, and this shows the error of one who claims it is fabricated. And Allah knows best." Talkhis al-Habir: 2/222–223; al-Kafi al-Shaf p. 28. See also: Nasb al-Raya of al-Zayla'i: 4/410–411.]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 99:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah while Allah is Witness over what you do?﴾

﴿Say: O People of the Scripture, why do you avert [people] from the way of Allah⟩ — that is: why do you turn away from the religion of Allah, ﴿those who believe, seeking to make it crooked⟩ — seeking it, ﴿crooked⟩ — deviation and inclination. That is: why do you bar from the way of Allah, seeking for it crookedness? Abu 'Ubaydah said: "al-'iwaj" (with a kasrah on the ʿayn) refers to [crookedness] in religion, speech and deeds, while "al-'awaj" (with a fatha on the ʿayn) refers to a wall and every upright standing thing.

﴿While you are witnesses, and Allah is not unaware of what you do⟩ — [that in the Torah it is written] the description of Muhammad (ﷺ), and that the religion of Allah which He accepts none other than is Islam.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 100:

﴿O you who have believed, if you obey a faction of those who were given the Scripture﴾ Zayd ibn Aslam said: Shas ibn Qays, a Jewish elder of great disbelief and of severe disparagement of the Muslims, passed by a group of men from the Aws and the Khazraj who were gathered in one assembly, talking together. He was angered by what he saw of their harmony and their good relations in Islam, after the enmity that had existed between them in the pre-Islamic period (jahiliyyah). He said: "The chiefs of the Banu Qaylah have gathered in this land. By Allah, we will have no place among them once they are gathered here!" So he ordered a young Jewish man who was with him: "Go to them, sit with them, then remind them of the Day of Bu'ath and what came before it, and recite to them some of the poetry they exchanged about it." Bu'ath was a day on which the Aws fought the Khazraj, and victory in it went to the Aws over the Khazraj. The young man did so and spoke. The people then spoke in response, they disputed and boasted to one another, until two men from the two clans leapt up onto their knees: Aws ibn Qibti, of the Banu Harithah from the Aws, and Jabbar ibn Sakhr, of the Banu Salamah from the Khazraj. They quarrelled, then one of them said to his companion: "If you wish, by Allah, I will bring it back now as it was!" Both parties were enraged and said: "We accept! Weapons, weapons! Our appointment is at al-Zahirah," which was a lava field (harrah). They went out to it, and the Aws and the Khazraj joined together against one another in their claims which they had held in the pre-Islamic period. This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he went out to them with those of the Emigrants who were with him, until he came to them. Then he (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of Muslims! Is it the call of the jahiliyyah while I am among you, after Allah has honoured you with Islam, cut off from you the burden (ijr) of the jahiliyyah, and united you? Will you return to what you were upon as disbelievers? Allah, Allah!" The people then recognised that this was a prompting of Satan and a scheme of their enemy. They cast the weapons from their hands, wept, and embraced one another. Then they departed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), listening and obedient. Allah the Exalted then revealed this verse concerning them.

[Note in the edition: Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 29: "al-Tabari transmitted it from Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father. Ibn Ishaq transmitted it in al-Maghazi, and Ibn Hisham mentioned it without Ibn Ishaq's chain. al-Tha'labi and al-Wahidi mentioned it in their Asbab (occasions of revelation) from Zayd ibn Aslam without a chain." al-Suyuti also attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh. See: al-Durr al-Manthur 4/278–279; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi pp. 149–150; al-Tabari 7/55–56; Sirah of Ibn Hisham 2/556–557.]

﴿They would turn you back into disbelievers after your belief﴾ Jabir said: I never saw a day whose beginning was more evil and whose end was more good than that day. Then Allah the Exalted said, in a manner of wonder:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 101:

﴿And how can you disbelieve?﴾ That is: why do you disbelieve? ﴿While the verses of Allah are recited to you﴾ (the Qur'an), ﴿and among you is His Messenger﴾ (Muhammad ﷺ).

Qatadah said concerning this verse: "There are two clear signs: the Book of Allah and the Prophet of Allah. As for the Prophet of Allah, he has passed away. As for the Book of Allah, He has left it among you as a mercy and a blessing from Allah."

Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Abbas al-Humaydi informed us; Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz informed us; Abu al-Fadl al-Hasan ibn Ya'qub ibn Yusuf al-'Adl informed us; Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab al-'Abdi informed us; Abu Ja'far ibn 'Awf informed us; Abu Hayyan Yahya ibn Sa'id ibn Hayyan [from Yazid ibn Hayyan] [[Addition from manuscript B.]] informed us, saying: I heard Zayd ibn Arqam say: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us one day delivering a sermon. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'Amma ba'd (to proceed). O people, I am only a human being. The messenger of my Lord is about to come to me and I will answer him. I am leaving among you two weighty things. The first of them is the Book of Allah, in which is guidance and light. So hold fast to the Book of Allah and take hold of it.'" He urged them to it and encouraged them toward it. Then he said: "And my family, I remind you of Allah concerning my family." [[A fragment of a hadith narrated by Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter on the virtues of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, no. (2408): 4/1873–1874, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/117–118.]]

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever holds fast to Allah﴾, that is: whoever seeks protection in Allah and adheres to His religion and obedience, ﴿then he has been guided to a straight path﴾, a clear way. Ibn Jurayj said: "And whoever holds fast to Allah" means: whoever believes in Allah. The root of ʿiṣmah (protection, safeguarding) is "prevention," so everything that prevents something is ʿāṣim (a protector) of it.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 102:

Allah's words, ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared﴾. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: There was enmity and fighting between the Aws and the Khazraj in the Jahiliyyah (the Age of Ignorance, the pre-Islamic period) until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ migrated to Medina, and he reconciled between them. After that, two men from among them boasted: Tha'labah ibn Ghanm from the Aws and As'ad ibn Zurarah from the Khazraj. The Awsi said: "From us is Khuzaymah ibn Thabit, the one with two testimonies (Dhu al-Shahadatayn); from us is Hanzalah, the one washed by the angels (Ghasil al-Mala'ikah); from us is 'Asim ibn Thabit ibn Aflah, the protector of the hornets (Hami al-Dabr); and from us is Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, for whose death the Throne of the Most Merciful trembled (ihtazza), and with whose judgment Allah was pleased concerning Banu Qurayzah."

The Khazraji said: "From us are four who perfected the Qur'an in its judgments: Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Mu'adh ibn Jabal, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Abu Zayd. And from us is Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, the orator and chief of the Ansar." The conversation between them continued, and they became angry and recited poetry and boasted. The Aws and the Khazraj came, and with them were weapons. The Prophet ﷺ came to them, and Allah the Exalted revealed this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared﴾ [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 151.]].

'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas said: "It means that He is obeyed and not disobeyed." Mujahid said: "It means that you strive in the way of Allah with the striving due to Him, that the blame of any blamer does not deter you concerning Allah, and that you stand firm for Allah in justice, even against yourselves, your fathers and your sons." And it is narrated from Anas that he said: "No servant fears Allah as He should be feared until he guards his tongue."

The people of tafsir said: When this verse was revealed, it was difficult for them, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is able to do this?" So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ (al-Taghabun 16), and this verse was abrogated (naskh). Muqatil said: "In Surah Al 'Imran there is nothing abrogated except this." [[See al-Tabari: 7/68-69, where he mentions both opinions without preferring either. Shaykh Mahmud Shakir related from al-Nahhas that he preferred the view that there is no abrogation, so refer to it.]].

﴿And do not die except as Muslims﴾, i.e., believers. It was said: sincere, entrusting your affairs to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Al-Fudayl said: "Those who think well of Allah."

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, Abu Bakr al-'Abdusi informed us, Abu Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdun ibn Khalid ibn Yazid informed us, Sulayman ibn Sayf informed us, Wahb ibn Jarir informed us, Shu'bah informed us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O people, fear Allah as He should be feared. If a single drop of al-Zaqqum were dripped onto the earth, it would ruin the livelihood of the people of the world. So how about one for whom it is the food, and who has no other food?" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Sifat Jahannam, chapter on what has come concerning the drink of the people of the Fire: 7/307, and he said: "Hasan sahih." Also by Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd, chapter on the description of the Fire, no. (4325), 2/1446; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/294, and he authenticated it according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim); Ibn Hibban in Mawarid al-Zam'an, al-Haythami, p. 649; Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/301, 338; and the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/246. Al-Suyuti also attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tayalisi, al-Tabarani and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th wa al-Nushur. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/284. See also Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/389. Al-Albani authenticated it in his notes on al-Mishkat: 3/1582.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 103 (part 1 of 3):

The Exalted and Majestic One said: ﴿And hold fast, all together, to the rope of Allah﴾. Al-habl (the rope) is the means by which one reaches the desired goal. Faith is called a rope (habl) because it is a means by which one reaches the removal of fear.

The scholars differed over its meaning here. Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning is "hold fast to the religion of Allah." Ibn Mas'ud said: it is the community (al-jama'ah). He said: "Adhere to the community, for it is the rope of Allah which He commanded you to hold. What you dislike in the community and obedience is better than what you love in division." Mujahid and 'Ata' said: it means "the covenant of Allah." Qatadah and al-Suddi said: it is the Qur'an. It is narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "This Qur'an is the rope of Allah, it is the clear light, the beneficial cure, a protection for those who hold fast to it, and salvation for those who follow it." [Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) in the Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an, chapter "What has come concerning the virtue of the Qur'an" (8/218-221), and said: "This is a strange hadith; we do not know it except through the hadith of Hamzah al-Zayyat, and its chain is unknown. There is criticism concerning the hadith of al-Harith." Ibn Abi Shaybah also narrated it in al-Musannaf (10/482). It has a supporting report from the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the trials and magnified them, and 'Ali ibn Abi Talib said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the way out of them?" He said: "The Book of Allah, in which is news of what came before you..." It was narrated by al-Tabarani, and in its chain is 'Amr ibn Waqid, who is abandoned (matruk). See Majma' al-Zawa'id (7/165). Al-Darimi narrated it from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, in the Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an, chapter "The virtue of one who recites the Qur'an" (2/431). Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (1/555) and said: "This hadith has a sound chain, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not include it, with Salih ibn 'Umar." Al-Hafiz al-Dhahabi said: "Salih is trustworthy, and Muslim narrated from him, but Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hijri is weak." Al-Tabarani also narrated it; al-Haythami said (7/164): "In its chain is Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hijri, who is abandoned." Ibn Abi Shaybah (10/482-483) and 'Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf (2/375) narrated it via the route of Ibn 'Uyaynah from Ibrahim al-Hijri. It is also cited in Kanz al-'Ummal from the narration of Ibn Abi Shaybah, and Ibn Kathir also attributed it to Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam. (Tafsir Ibn Kathir 4/582). Ibn Hajar also attributed it to al-Bazzar and Ishaq, through the route of al-Harith. Al-Bazzar said: "We do not know it except through 'Ali, and we do not know anyone narrated it from him except al-Harith." See al-Kafi al-Shafi by Ibn Hajar, p. 29. Al-Hafiz Ibn Kathir, after citing the narration of al-Tirmidhi, said: "Hamzah al-Zayyat did not alone narrate it; rather Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from al-Harith, thus clearing Hamzah of responsibility..." The best that can be said of this hadith is that it is a statement of the Commander of the Faithful 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), and some have erred in attributing it to the Prophet. It is a good, sound statement. It has also been narrated with a supporting report from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud from the Prophet (ﷺ), and then he cited the hadith of Abu 'Ubayd from him. See Fada'il al-Qur'an appended to the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir (4/582).]] Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "with the rope of Allah" means "with the command of Allah and His obedience." ﴿And do not be divided﴾ as the Jews and Christians became divided. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Exalted, is pleased with three things for you, and He is displeased with three things for you. He is pleased that you worship Him and associate nothing with Him, that you all hold fast to the rope of Allah together, and that you give sincere advice to the one whom Allah has placed in charge of your affairs. And He is displeased with: 'It is said and it is said' (qil wa qal), the squandering of wealth, and excessive questioning." [Muslim narrated it in the Book of Judgments, chapter "The prohibition of excessive questions without need..." no. 1715, 3/1340. Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of al-Mughirah that he (ﷺ) used to forbid "qil wa qal," excessive questioning, and the squandering of wealth. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah (1/202-203).]]

The Exalted said: ﴿And remember the favor of Allah upon you, when you were enemies and He joined your hearts together﴾. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar and others among the people of reports (akhbar) said: al-Aws and al-Khazraj were two brothers, sons of the same father and mother. Enmity arose between them over a slain man, and that enmity and war between them lasted one hundred and twenty years, until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, extinguished it through Islam and joined them together through His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). The cause of their coming together was that Suwayd ibn al-Samit, brother of Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, who was a nobleman whom his people called "the Perfect" (al-Kamil) because of his strength and lineage, came to Mecca for the pilgrimage or the lesser pilgrimage (umrah). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had been sent and commanded to call to the faith. When Suwayd heard of him, he approached him, and called him to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to Islam. Suwayd said to him: "Perhaps what you have is like what I have." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "And what is it that you have?" He said: "The Luqman's collection," meaning his wisdom. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Present it to me." So he presented it, and he said: "This is indeed a good saying, but what I have is better than this: a Qur'an which Allah revealed to me as light and guidance." Then he (ﷺ) recited the Qur'an to him and called him to Islam. He did not turn away from it and said: "This is indeed a good saying." Then he returned to Medina, and not long after, al-Khazraj killed him before the day of Bu'ath. His people would say: "He was killed while he was a Muslim."

Then Abu al-Haysar Anas ibn Rafi' came, and with him a group (fi'ah) from Banu al-Ashhal, among them Iyas ibn Mu'adh, seeking an alliance from Quraysh against a people from al-Khazraj. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard of them, he came to them and sat with them and said: "Is there for you something better than what you came for?" They said: "And what is that?" He said: "I am the Messenger of Allah. He sent me to the servants to call them to not associate anything with Allah. He revealed the Book to me." Then he mentioned Islam to them and recited the Qur'an to them. Iyas ibn Mu'adh, who was a young lad, said: "O people, by Allah, this is better than what you came for." Abu al-Haysar took a handful of gravel from the valley (al-Batha') and struck Iyas's face with it and said: "Leave us alone from you, for by my life, we came for other than this." Iyas fell silent, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) rose from them, and they returned to Medina. The battle of Bu'ath took place between al-Aws and al-Khazraj. Then Iyas ibn Mu'adh did not remain long before he died.

When Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, wished to manifest His religion and exalt His Prophet, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out during the season in which he met the group of the Ansar, presenting himself to the tribes of the Arabs as he used to do in every season. At al-'Aqabah he met a company (rahṭ) of al-Khazraj whom Allah wished good for. They were six men: As'ad ibn Zurarah, 'Awf ibn al-Harith, who is Ibn 'Afra', Rafi' ibn Malik al-'Ajlani, Qutbah ibn 'Amir ibn Hadidah, 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir ibn Nabi, and Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "Who are you?" They said: "A group of al-Khazraj." He said: "Are you of the allies of the Jews?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Will you not sit so that I may speak with you?" They said: "Yes," and they sat with him. He called them to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, presented Islam to them, and recited the Qur'an to them.

They said: Among what Allah did for them in Islam was that Jews were with them in their lands, and the Jews were people of the Book and knowledge, while they were people of idols and polytheism. Whenever some matter arose between them, the Jews would say: "A prophet is now about to be sent, whose time has drawn near. We will follow him and kill you alongside him, as 'Ad and Iram were destroyed." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke to those men and called them to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, some of them said to others: "O people, you know by Allah that he is the Prophet whom the Jews have threatened you with, so let them not outrun you to him." They responded to him, believed him, and embraced Islam. They said: "We have left our people, and there is no people with such enmity and evil between them as there is between them. Perhaps Allah will unite them through you. We will go to them and call them to your cause. If Allah unites them upon you, there will be no man more mighty than you."

Then they departed from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), returning to their lands, having believed in him (ﷺ). When they reached Medina, they mentioned the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the people and called them to Islam, until it spread among them, and there was no house among the houses of the Ansar except that the mention of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in it. When the following year came, there came to the pilgrimage from the Ansar twelve men: As'ad ibn Zurarah, 'Awf and Mu'adh, the two sons of 'Afra', Rafi' ibn Malik ibn al-'Ajlan, Dhakwan ibn 'Abd al-Qays, 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, Yazid ibn Tha'labah, 'Abbas ibn 'Ubadah, 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir, and Qutbah ibn 'Amir. These were of al-Khazraj. And Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan and 'Uwaymir ibn Sa'idah were from al-Aws. They met him at al-'Aqabah, which is the First 'Aqabah, and they pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with the pledge of the women: that they would not associate anything with Allah, nor steal, nor commit adultery, up to the end of the verse. "If you fulfil it, then for you is Paradise. And if you commit any of those things and are punished for it in this world, then it is an expiation for it. And if it is concealed from you, then your affair is with Allah: if He wills, He will punish you, and if He wills, He will forgive you." He said: "That was before the war was made obligatory upon them."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on surah 3, verse 103 (part 2 of 3):

He said: When the people had returned, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr ibn Hashim ibn 'Abd Manaf with them, and commanded him to teach them the Qur'an, instruct them in Islam, and give them understanding of the religion. Mus'ab was called "the Reciter" (al-Muqri') in Medina. He lodged at the house of As'ad ibn Zurarah. Then As'ad ibn Zurarah went out with Mus'ab and entered with him an orchard belonging to the Banu Zafar. They both sat in the orchard, and men who had embraced Islam gathered around them.

Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said to Usayd ibn Hudayr: "Go to those two men who have come to our dwelling in order to make our weak ones foolish. Rebuke them. As'ad ibn Zurarah is my maternal cousin, and were it not for that, I would have dealt with him for you." Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Usayd ibn Hudayr were the chiefs of their people, from the Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, and both were polytheists. So Usayd ibn Hudayr took his spear and came toward Mus'ab and As'ad, who were sitting in the orchard. When As'ad ibn Zurarah saw him, he said to Mus'ab: "This is the chief of his people, and he has come to you. Be sincere with Allah concerning him." Mus'ab said: "If he sits, I will speak with him." So he (Usayd) stood over them, hostile, and said: "What has brought you to us, that you make our weak ones foolish? Withdraw, if you have any need for yourselves." Mus'ab said to him: "Will you sit and listen? If you approve of a matter, accept it, and if you dislike it, we will refrain from what you dislike." He said: "You have been fair." Then he planted his spear and sat with them. Mus'ab spoke to him about Islam and recited the Qur'an to him. They said: "By Allah, we recognized Islam in his face before he spoke it, in its radiance and its gentleness." Then he said: "How excellent and beautiful is this speech! What do you do when you wish to enter this religion?" They said to him: "You bathe, purify your garments, then testify to the truth [then pray two rak'ahs]." [[Addition from manuscript "A".]] So he rose, bathed, purified his garments, and testified to the truth [[ then ]] he stood and performed two rak'ahs. Then he said to them: "Behind me is a man, and if he follows you, no one of his people will remain behind him. I will send him to you now: Sa'd ibn Mu'adh." Then he took his spear and went back to Sa'd and his people, who were sitting in their assembly place. When Sa'd ibn Mu'adh saw him approaching, he said: "I swear by Allah, Usayd has come to you with a face other than the one with which he left you." When he stood over the assembly, Sa'd said to him: "What have you done?" He said: "I spoke with the two men. By Allah, I saw no harm in them, and I forbade them, and they said, 'Do what you like.'" He added: "I have been told that the Banu Harithah went out to As'ad ibn Zurarah to kill him, because they knew he was your maternal cousin, in order to humiliate you." So Sa'd stood [angry] [[In A: "mubghadan," which is an error.]], hastening toward what had been mentioned to him about the Banu Harithah, took the spear and said: "By Allah, I do not think you have accomplished anything." But when he saw that they both were at ease, he realized that Usayd had only intended to hear from them. So he stood over them, hostile, and then said to As'ad ibn Zurarah: "Were it not for the kinship between me and you, you would not have made this request of me. You come to us in our home with what we dislike." As'ad had said to Mus'ab: "By Allah, he is the chief of his people. If he follows you, not one of them will oppose you." Mus'ab said to Sa'd: "Will you sit and listen? If you approve of a matter and desire it, accept it, and if you dislike it, we will withdraw from you what you dislike." Sa'd said: "You have been fair." Then he planted the spear and sat. Mus'ab presented Islam to him and recited the Qur'an to him. They said: "By Allah, we recognized Islam in his face before he spoke it, in its radiance and its gentleness." Then he said to them: "What do you do when you embrace Islam and enter this religion?" They said: "You bathe and purify your garments, then testify to the truth, then [pray] [[In A: "bow" (tarka').]] two rak'ahs." So he rose, bathed, purified his garments, testified to the truth, and performed two rak'ahs. Then he took his spear and went purposefully to the assembly of his people, and Usayd ibn Hudayr was with him. When his people saw him approaching, they said: "We swear by Allah, Sa'd has returned to you with a face other than the one with which he left you." When he stood over them, he said: "O Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, how do you regard my standing among you?" They said: "You are our master and the most judicious of us in opinion, and the most blessed in our affairs." He said: "Then the speech of your men and your women is forbidden to me until you believe in Allah and His Messenger." He said: "No man or woman remained in the house of the Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal who did not become a Muslim, man or woman." As'ad ibn Zurarah and Mus'ab returned to the house of As'ad ibn Zurarah, and he remained there, calling the people to Islam, until there was no house among the houses of the Ansar (Helpers) without Muslim men and Muslim women in it, except the house of the Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd, Khatmah, Wa'il, and Waqif. The reason was that Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat the poet was among them, and they listened to him and obeyed him, so he held them back from Islam until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) emigrated to Medina, and Badr, Uhud, and the Trench had passed.

They said: Then Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr returned to Mecca, and there went out with him seventy men of the Muslim Ansar, accompanying the pilgrims of their people who were polytheists, until they arrived at Mecca. They arranged with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a meeting at the 'Aqabah during the middle days of the Days of Tashriq (the days after the Eid sacrifice). This is the Second Pledge of al-'Aqabah.

Ka'b ibn Malik said, and he had witnessed it: When we had finished the pilgrimage, and the night came that we had arranged with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and with us was 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn Haram, Abu Jabir (we had informed him of our affair, and we used to conceal it from those of our people who were polytheists among us), we spoke to him and said: "O Abu Jabir, you are a master among our masters and a nobleman among our nobles, and we wish for you that you not be firewood for the Fire tomorrow." We invited him to Islam, and he embraced it, and we informed him of the appointment with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he witnessed the 'Aqabah with us, and he was a naqib (representative). We spent that night with our people in our lodgings, until a third of the night had passed, and we went out for the appointment with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), stealing away secretly like sandgrouse, until we gathered in the ravine at the 'Aqabah. We were seventy men, and with us were two women of our women: Nusaybah bint Ka'b, Umm 'Umarah, one of the women of the Banu al-Najjar, and Asma' bint 'Amr ibn 'Adi, Umm Mani', one of the women of the Banu Salamah. We gathered in the ravine waiting for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), until he came to us, and with him was his paternal uncle al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, who was at that time upon the religion of his people, but he wished to be present for the affair of his nephew and to secure it for him. When we had sat down, the first to speak was al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib. He said: "O assembly of the Khazraj," for the Arabs used to call this tribe of the Ansar "al-Khazraj" and "al-Aws" (both parties), "Muhammad (ﷺ) is one of us, as you know. We have protected him from our people, from those who think as we do, and he is in honor among his people and in protection in his land. He has refused except to join you and to go to you. So if you think that you will be faithful to him in what you have invited him to, and will protect him against those who oppose him, then you are responsible for that which you have undertaken. But if you think that you will hand him over and abandon him after he goes out to you, then leave him now, for he is in honor and protection."

He said: We said: "We have heard what you have said. So speak, O Messenger of Allah, and take for yourself and for your Lord whatever you wish."

He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke, recited the Qur'an, called to Allah, and encouraged toward Islam. Then he said: "I pledge to you that you protect me from what you protect your own selves and your women and your children from." He said: Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur took his hand and said: "By Him who sent you with the truth as a prophet, we will protect you from what we protect our waist-wrappers. So pledge to us, O Messenger of Allah. We are men of war and men of arms, which we have inherited from our forefathers, generation after generation." 

He said: [Then he interjected] [[In A: "fa'arada," "fa'arad."]] the speech, while al-Bara' was speaking to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan, who said: "O Messenger of Allah, between us and the people there are cords, meaning covenants, and we will sever them. Would it be that if we do this, and then Allah makes you triumphant, you would return to your people and leave us?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) smiled, then said: "Blood for blood, and destruction for destruction. You are of me and I am of you. I will fight whom you fight, and make peace with whom you make peace."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Bring out to me twelve chiefs (nuqaba') from among you, sureties over their people for what is in them, as the disciples (hawariyyun) were sureties for Jesus, son of Mary." So they brought out twelve chiefs: nine from the Khazraj and three from the Aws.

'Asim ibn 'Amr ibn Qatadah said: When the people gathered for the pledge to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), al-'Abbas ibn 'Ubadah ibn Nadlah al-Ansari said: "O assembly of the Khazraj, do you know what you are pledging to this man? You are pledging yourselves to war against the red and the black (i.e., all people). So if you think that when your wealth is destroyed and your nobles are killed you will abandon him, then from now on, by Allah, if you do so, it is disgrace in this world and the next. But if you think that you will be faithful to him in what you have invited him to, even at the cost of the ruin of wealth and the killing of nobles, then take him, for by Allah, he is the best of this world and the next."

They said: "We take him at the cost of the ruin of wealth and the killing of nobles. What will we have for that, O Messenger of Allah, if we are faithful?" He said: "Paradise." They said: "Extend your hand." He extended his hand, and they pledged to him. The first to strike upon his hand was al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, then the people followed one after another.

When we had pledged to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Satan shouted from the top of the 'Aqabah with the most piercing voice I have ever heard: "O people of the Jabajib, do you want Mudhammam (the Prophet) and the Sabi' (those who have turned away from their religion), who have gathered to fight you?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "This is the enemy of Allah, this is the Azabb of the 'Aqabah. Listen, O enemy of Allah! By Allah, I will attend to you!" Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Disperse to your lodgings."

Al-'Abbas ibn 'Ubadah ibn Nadlah said: "By Him who sent you with the truth, if you wish, we will fall tomorrow upon the people of Mina with our swords." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We have not been commanded to that. Rather, return to your lodgings."

He said: "So we returned to our beds and lay down on them until morning. When morning came, the chiefs of Quraysh came to us at our homes and said, 'O assembly of Khazraj, we have been told that you came to our companion here to take him out from among us and pledge allegiance to him for war against us. By God, there is no tribe of the Arabs more hateful to us than that war should break out between us and them, [from you]." [The word "from you" is missing in manuscript (A).]

He said: "Then those polytheists of our people who were there rose up, swearing to them by God that none of this had happened and that they had no knowledge of it, and they spoke the truth, for they did not know. Some of us looked at others. The people stood up, and among them was al-Harith ibn Hisham ibn al-Mughira [al-Makhzumi]. [The name al-Makhzumi is missing in manuscript (A).] He was wearing a pair of new sandals. He said: I said a word to him, as if I wanted to make the people share in it regarding what they had said: 'O Jabir, can you not get, being one of our lords, a pair of sandals like the sandals of this young man from Quraysh?'" [Then] he said: "al-Harith heard it, took off his sandals from his feet, threw them at me, and said, 'By God, you will certainly wear them!'"

He said: Abu Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Enough! By God, you have shamed the young man. Return his sandals to him." He said: "I will not return them. An omen, by God, is good. By God, if the omen comes true, [I will certainly take him captive]." [In manuscript (A): "I will certainly seize him" (لأستغلبنه).]

He said: Then the Ansar returned to Madinah, having strengthened the covenant. When they reached it, they openly declared Islam there. This reached Quraysh, and they harmed the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to his companions: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, has made for you brothers and a home in which you will be safe." Then he commanded them to emigrate to Madinah and to join their brothers among the Ansar.

The first to emigrate to Madinah was Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad al-Makhzumi, then Amir ibn Rabi'ah, then Abdullah ibn Jahsh. Then the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ followed one another in groups to Madinah. Allah gathered the people of Madinah, both its Aws and its Khazraj, under Islam, and by His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ He reconciled their hearts. [This story was related by Ibn Ishaq in al-Maghazi, 1/265–266, from the Sirah of Ibn Hisham with al-Rawd al-Unuf; and from him al-Tabari related it in his Tafsir, 7/78–79.]

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And remember the favor of Allah upon you﴾, O assembly of the Ansar, ﴿when you were enemies﴾ before Islam, ﴿and He brought your hearts together﴾ through Islam, ﴿so you became﴾, that is, you became, ﴿by His favor﴾, by His mercy and by His religion, Islam, ﴿brothers﴾ in religion and in mutual loyalty among you. ﴿And you were﴾, O assembly of Aws and Khazraj, ﴿on the brink of a pit of the Fire﴾, that is, on the edge of a pit like the brink of a well. Its meaning is: you were on the edge of a pit of the Fire, with nothing between you and falling into it except that you would die in your disbelief. ﴿Then He saved you from it﴾, Allah did, ﴿from it﴾ through faith. ﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His signs, that you may be guided﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 104:**

﴿Let there be among you a community﴾: meaning, "Be a community." The *min* (مِنْ) here is a *silah* (a grammatically redundant particle, lit. "connector") and is not partitive (*li-l-tab'id*, "indicating a part of a whole"). This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So avoid the abomination of the idols﴾ [al-Hajj: 30]. He did not mean avoiding *some* of the idols; He meant avoid the idols. The *lam* in His saying ﴿let there be﴾ is the *lam al-amr* (the imperative *lam*, which expresses a command). ﴿They call to good﴾: to Islam. ﴿And enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. And those are the successful﴾.

We were informed by Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir, who said: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us, who said: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us [in A: Isa ibn Muhammad], who said: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj related to us, who said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abi Shaybah related to us, who said: Waki' informed us, from Sufyan, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Sa'id (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he is unable, then with his tongue; if he is unable, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith."[[Related by Muslim in the Book of Faith, chapter on the explanation that forbidding evil is part of faith, no. (78): 1/69.]]

We were informed by Abu Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl al-Kharqi, who said: Abu al-Hasan al-Tayasfuni informed us, who said: Abd Allah ibn Umar al-Jawhari informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Kushmihani informed us, who said: Ali ibn Hujr informed us, who said: Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us, who said: Amr ibn Abi Amr related to us, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Ashhali, from Hudhayfah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand my soul is, you will surely enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, or else Allah will soon send upon you a punishment from Him, then you will supplicate Him and your supplication will not be answered."[[Related by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Trials, chapter on what has come concerning enjoining good and forbidding evil: 6/391, and he said: "This is a hasan (good) hadith." Also Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/388, and the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/345. Al-Haythami said: "Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat and al-Bazzar from Abu Hurayrah, and in its chain is Hibban ibn Ali, who is matruk (abandoned in narration); Ibn Ma'in declared him trustworthy in one narration and weak in another." Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/266.]]

We were informed by Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, who said: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmish al-Ziyadi informed us, who said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us, who said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Darawardi informed us, who said: Abu al-Nu'man informed us, who said: Abd al-Aziz ibn Muslim al-Qasmali informed us, who said: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, who said: I heard Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) say: "O people, you recite this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, take care of yourselves; those who have strayed cannot harm you once you are guided﴾, but I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'When people see an evil and do not change it, Allah the Exalted will soon encompass them with His punishment.'"[[Related by Abu Dawud in the Book of Trials, chapter on enjoining and forbidding: 6/187, and al-Mundhiri attributed it to al-Nasa'i. Also related by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Trials, chapter on the descent of punishment when they do not change evil: 6/388-389, and in the Book of Tafsir, Surah al-Ma'idah: 8/422-423, and he said: "A hasan sahih (good and authentic) hadith." Also Ibn Majah in the Book of Trials, chapter on enjoining good and forbidding evil, no. (4005): 2/1327; Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/7; Ibn Hibban, p. (455), in Mawarid al-Zam'an; the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/344; and Abu Bakr al-Marwazi in Musnad Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, no. (86-88), pp. 130-131. The hafiz Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir (2/110): "This hadith has been narrated by the authors of the four Sunan and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and others, through many routes from a large group, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, in a connected, raised form (marfu'), and some narrated it from them as halted (mawquf) upon al-Siddiq. Al-Daraqutni and others preferred its being raised." See also: al-Albani, Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Sahihah: 4/88-89.]]

We were informed by Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi, who said: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, who said: Amr ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath informed us, who said: My father related to us, who said: Al-A'mash related to me, who said: Al-Sha'bi related to me that he heard al-Nu'man ibn Bashir (may Allah be pleased with him) say: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of the one who compromises concerning the limits of Allah the Exalted, and of the one who falls into them, is like a people who drew lots over a ship: some of them ended up in its lower part and some in its upper part. Those in the lower part would pass by water over those in the upper part, and they were harmed by it. So one of them took an axe and began to hack at the bottom of the ship. They came to him and said, 'What is wrong with you?' He said, 'You have been harmed by me, and I must have water.' So if they seize his hands, they will save him and save themselves; but if they leave him, they will destroy him and destroy themselves."[[Related by al-Bukhari in the Book of Testimonies, chapter on lots in dubious matters: 5/292, with this wording; and the author (al-Baghawi) related it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/342 with closely similar wording.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 105:**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And do not be like those who became divided and differed after the clear proofs had come to them﴾. Most of the commentators (mufassirun, those who write tafsir, or Qur'anic exegesis) said: They are the Jews and the Christians. Some of them said: They are the innovators (al-mubtadi'a) from this Ummah. Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: They are the Harurites (al-Harutiyya, an early Kharijite group) in Syria.

ʿAbd Allah ibn Shaddad said: Abu Umamah stopped, and I was with him, at the heads of the Harurites in Syria, and he said: "They are the dogs of the Fire. They were believers, then they disbelieved after their faith." Then he recited: ﴿And do not be like those who became divided and differed after the clear proofs had come to them﴾, up to His saying: ﴿Did you disbelieve after your faith?﴾

Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Salihi informed us, Abu al-Hasan ibn Bishran informed us, Ismaʿil ibn Muhammad al-Saffar informed us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Maʿmar informed us, from ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever wishes to be in the very center of Paradise, then he must adhere to the community (al-jama'a), for Satan is with the lone one, and he is farther from two."

[This is a portion of a long hadith in ʿUmar's sermon at al-Jabiya. It was recorded by al-Tirmidhi in Kitab al-Fitan, chapter "What has come concerning adherence to the community," 6/383–386, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith from this route. Ibn al-Mubarak narrated it from Muhammad ibn Suqa, and this hadith has been narrated through more than one route from ʿUmar, from the Prophet ﷺ." It was also recorded by Ibn Abi ʿAsim in al-Sunna, nos. (86–88), 1/42; by al-Lalika'i in Sharh Usul I'tiqad Ahl al-Sunna wa'l-Jama'a, 1/106–107; by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak, 1/114, who declared it sahih according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him and mentioned two supporting narrations for it; and by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad, 1/18, from ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Albani authenticated it in his commentary on Ibn Abi ʿAsim's al-Sunna.]

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And those will have a great punishment﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 3, verse 106:**

﴿On the day when some faces will turn white and some faces will turn black.﴾ ﴿On the day﴾ is in the accusative as an adverb of time (*zarf*), meaning "during the day," and the adverb's accusative case is by analogy to the object (*tashbih bil-maf'ul*). The meaning is: the faces of the believers will turn white and the faces of the disbelievers will turn black. It is also said: the faces of the sincere (*mukhlisin*) will turn white and the faces of the hypocrites (*munafiqun*) will turn black.

It is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he recited this verse and said: "The faces of the People of the Sunnah will turn white, and the faces of the People of Innovation will turn black."

Al-Kalbi related from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, for every people will be raised what they used to worship, and every people will go after what they used to worship. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We shall turn him to what he has turned to﴾ [al-Nisa': 115]. When they reach it, they will be grieved, and their faces will turn black from grief. The People of the Qibla (*ahl al-qibla*), the Jews and the Christians will remain, not recognizing anything of what was raised for them. Then Allah will come to them, and whoever used to prostrate to Him in the world, obedient and believing, will prostrate to Him. The People of the Book and the hypocrites will remain unable to prostrate. Then they will be permitted, and they will lift their heads, while the faces of the believers will be as white as snow. When the hypocrites and the People of the Book look at the faces of the believers, they will be grieved with a severe grief, and their faces will turn black. They will say: 'Our Lord, why are our faces blackened? By Allah, we were not polytheists!' Then Allah will say to the angels: 'Look how they have lied against themselves' [al-An'am: 24]."

The scholars of meanings (*ahl al-ma'ani*) said: The whitening of the faces is their radiance, their gladness, and their joy at their deeds and at Allah's reward. Their blackening is their sorrow, their dejection, and their gloom at their deeds and at Allah's punishment. This is indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For those who did good is the best reward and more. Neither darkness nor humiliation will cover their faces﴾ [Yunus: 26]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who earned evil deeds, the recompense of an evil deed is its like, and humiliation will cover them﴾ [Yunus: 27] [66b]. And He said: "Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord. And faces that Day will be dismal" (al-Qiyamah: 22–24). And He said: "Faces that Day will be bright, laughing, rejoicing. And faces that Day will have upon them dust, overcast with darkness" (Abasa: 38–41).

﴿As for those whose faces turned black, [it will be said]: "Did you disbelieve after your belief?"﴾ Its meaning: it will be said to them, "Did you disbelieve after your belief?" ﴿So taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve.﴾

If it is asked: How does He say "Did you disbelieve after your belief," when they were not believers? It is related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that he meant by it the belief on the Day of the Covenant, when He said to them: "Am I not your Lord?" They said: "Yes." So it means: "Did you disbelieve after your belief on the Day of the Covenant?" Al-Hasan said: They are the hypocrites, who spoke the belief with their tongues and denied it in their hearts.

It is related from Ikrimah that they are the People of the Book, who believed in their prophets and in Muhammad ﷺ before he was sent, and when he was sent, they disbelieved in him.

Some people said: They are from the people of our Qibla. Abu Umamah said: They are the Khawarij. Qatadah said: They are the People of Innovations (*ahl al-bida'*).

Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi informed us: Abu al-Hasan al-Tayasfuni informed us: Abdullah ibn Umar al-Jawhari informed us: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Kushmihani informed us: Ali ibn Hujr informed us: Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us, from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Hasten to good deeds before trials like pieces of the dark night, when a man becomes a believer in the morning and an unbeliever by evening, or a believer by evening and an unbeliever in the morning, selling his religion for a trifle of worldly goods."

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 107–109:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And as for those whose faces turn white﴾, these are the people of obedience, ﴿then in the mercy of Allah﴾, the Garden of Allah.

﴿They will abide therein eternally.﴾

﴿These are the verses of Allah; We recite them to you in truth. And Allah does not desire injustice for the worlds.﴾

﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 107–109:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And as for those whose faces turn white﴾, these are the people of obedience, ﴿then in the mercy of Allah﴾, the Garden of Allah.

﴿They will abide therein eternally.﴾

﴿These are the verses of Allah; We recite them to you in truth. And Allah does not desire injustice for the worlds.﴾

﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 107–109:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And as for those whose faces turn white﴾, these are the people of obedience, ﴿then in the mercy of Allah﴾, the Garden of Allah.

﴿They will abide therein eternally.﴾

﴿These are the verses of Allah; We recite them to you in truth. And Allah does not desire injustice for the worlds.﴾

﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned.﴾

﴿You are the best nation ever brought forth for mankind﴾. ʿIkrimah and Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Ibn Masʿud, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Muʿadh ibn Jabal, and Salim, the freed slave of Abu Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with them. The reason was that Malik ibn al-Sayf and Wahb ibn Yahuda [[In B: "Yahud".]], the two Jews, said to them: "We are better than you, and our religion is better than what you call us to." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, regarding ﴿You are the best nation ever brought forth for mankind﴾: "They are those who emigrated with the Prophet ﷺ to Madinah." Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak: "They are the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ specifically, the transmitters and callers whom Allah commanded the Muslims to obey."

It is also related from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab that he said: "You are the best nation ever brought forth for mankind," meaning: it applies to our first generation and does not apply to our last generation.

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Muliḥi informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Shurayh informed us, saying: Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi informed us, saying: ʿAli ibn al-Jaʿd informed us, saying: Shuʿbah informed us, from Abu Hamzah, who said: I heard Zahdam ibn Mudarrib ibn ʿImran ibn Husayn, may Allah be pleased with him, narrating from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The best of you are my generation, then those who follow them, then those who follow them." ʿImran said: "I do not know whether the Prophet ﷺ mentioned after his generation two or three [generations]. And he said: 'Indeed, after you there will be a people who betray and are not trusted, who bear witness though they are not asked to bear witness, who make vows and do not fulfill them, and among whom corpulence will appear.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter "The virtues of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ": 7/3, and in al-Shahadat, chapter "He does not bear witness to an unjust testimony." Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter "The virtue of the Companions," no. (2535): 4/1964–1965. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/67.]]

And by this same chain, from ʿAli ibn al-Jaʿd: Shuʿbah and Abu Muʿawiyah informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Dhakwan, from Abu Saʿid, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Do not revile my Companions. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if any one of you spent gold equal to Mount Uhud, it would not reach a mudd of one of them, nor half of it." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter "The Prophet's ﷺ saying: 'If I were to take a close friend...'": 7/21. Muslim in Fada'il al-Sahabah, chapter "The prohibition of reviling the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them," no. (2540): 4/1967. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah 14/69.]]

Others said: "They are all the believers of this Ummah."

His saying ﴿You were﴾ means: "You are," like His saying: ﴿And remember when you were few﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 86], and He said in another place: "And remember when you were few" [al-Anfal: 26]. It was also said: its meaning is: "You were the best nation with Allah in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz)." Some people said: His saying ﴿for mankind﴾ — "min" is the complement of His saying "best nation," meaning: you are the best of mankind for mankind.

Abu Hurayrah said its meaning is: "You were the best of people, bringing them in chains and then admitting them to Islam." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, as a mawquf report, in the Tafsir of Al ʿImran, chapter "You are the best nation ever brought forth for mankind": 8/224, and with similar meaning as a marfuʿ report in al-Jihad, chapter "Prisoners in chains": 6/145.]]

Qatadah said: "They are the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ. No prophet before him was commanded to fight, so they fight the disbelievers and bring them into their religion, and so they are the best nation for mankind."

It was also said that "for mankind" is the complement of His saying "brought forth": meaning, Allah has not brought forth for mankind a nation better than the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ.

Abu Saʿid al-Shurayhi informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, saying: Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hafiz informed us, saying: Abu ʿAli al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Hubaysh al-Muqri informed us, saying: ʿAli ibn Zanjawayh informed us, saying: Salamah ibn Shabib informed us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Bahz ibn Hakim, from his father, from his grandfather, that he heard the Prophet ﷺ say, concerning His saying ﴿You are the best nation ever brought forth for mankind﴾: "Indeed you will complete seventy nations, you are the best of them and the most honored of them before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Tafsir, Surah Al ʿImran: 8/352, and he said: "This is a hasan hadith, and more than one narrator has related this hadith from Bahz ibn Hakim similar to this, but they did not mention in it: 'You are the best nation ever brought forth for mankind.'" Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd, chapter "The description of the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ," no. (4288): 2/1433. al-Darimi in al-Raqaʾiq, chapter "On the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: 'You are the last of the nations'": 2/313. al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 4/84, and he said: "This hadith has a sound chain, but they did not record it," and Saʿid ibn Iyas al-Jurayri has followed him in this in a narration from Hakim ibn Muʿawiyah, and added to the text. al-Tabari in al-Tafsir: 2/25, 7/104, and Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/447, 5/5. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath 8/325: "It is a hasan sahih hadith." See the commentary of Shaykh Mahmud Shakir on al-Tabari: 2/25–26 and 7/104.]]

ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Muliḥi informed us, saying: Abu Maʿshar Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-FirakI informed us, saying: Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn Zakariyya ibn Yahya informed us, saying: Abu al-Salt informed us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd informed us, saying: ʿAli ibn Zayd informed us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Behold, this Ummah will be followed by seventy nations, it is the best of them and the most honored of them before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd, chapter "The description of the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ," no. (4288): 2/1433, and Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/447 from Muʿawiyah ibn Haydah, 5/5. al-Haythami said: "Ahmad narrated it and its narrators are trustworthy." Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid: 10/397.]]

Abu Saʿid al-Shurayhi informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, saying: Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl informed us, saying: Abu Khalifah al-Fadl ibn al-Hubab informed us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman, that is Ibn al-Mubarak, said: Hammad ibn Yahya al-Abahh informed us, saying: Thabit al-Bunani informed us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The likeness of my Ummah is the likeness of rain: one does not know whether its beginning is better or its end." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Adab, chapter "Haddathana Qutaybah": 8/170, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this direction." Ahmad in al-Musnad: 3/130–143 from Anas, and 4/319 from ʿAmmar. Abu al-Shaykh al-Asbahani narrated it in al-Amthal p. 223. Ibn al-Rabiʿ al-Shaybani said in Tamyiz al-Tayyib min al-Khabith p. 168: "The saying of al-Nawawi in his fatawa that it is weak is refuted." Al-Tabarani and al-Bazzar narrated it from ʿAmmar. al-Haythami said in al-Majmaʿ 10/68: "The narrators of al-Bazzar are the narrators of the sahih except al-Hasan ibn Qazaʿah and ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman al-Aghar, and both are trustworthy." See also Fayd al-Qadir: 5/517.]]

Abu Saʿid al-Shurayhi informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad al-Makhladi informed us, saying: Abu Nuʿaym ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAdi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿIsa al-Tinnisi informed us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Abi Salamah informed us, saying: Sadaqah ibn ʿAbd Allah informed us, from Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAqil, from al-Zuhri, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Indeed Paradise was forbidden to all the prophets until I enter it, and it was forbidden to all the nations until my Ummah enters it." [[Ibn Kathir said in al-Tafsir 1/397: "Al-Daraqutni narrated it in al-Afrad from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAqil, from al-Zuhri, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab... Then al-Daraqutni said: Ibn ʿAqil alone narrated it from al-Zuhri and no one else narrated it from him; Zuhayr ibn Muhammad alone narrated it from Ibn ʿAqil, and ʿAmr ibn Abi Salamah alone narrated it from Zuhayr. Abu Ahmad ibn ʿAdi al-Hafiz also narrated it... and al-Tha'labi narrated it." I say: Sadaqah ibn ʿAbd Allah is weak (Taqrib), and ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad was used as a proof by Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil and Ishaq, while Abu Hatim and others said he is weak in hadith (al-Mughni of al-Dhahabi).]]

Abu Saʿid al-Shurayhi said: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, saying: Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Abu al-Qasim ʿUmar ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Hatim al-Tirmidhi informed us, saying: My maternal grandfather Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Marzuq informed us, saying: ʿAffan ibn Muslim informed us, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Muslim informed us, saying: Abu Sinan, that is Dirar ibn Murrah, informed us, from Muharib ibn Dithar, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty rows; eighty of them are from this Ummah." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Jannah, chapter "What has come about how many rows the people of Paradise have": 7/254, and he said: "This is a hasan hadith." Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd, chapter "The description of the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ," no. (4290): 2/1434. al-Darimi in al-Raqaʾiq, chapter "On the rows of the people of Paradise": 2/337. Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/453 from Ibn Masʿud, and 5/347 from Buraydah. al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak: 1/82. Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi 7/254 attributes it to al-Bayhaqi in al-Baʿth wa al-Nushur and to Ibn Hibban.]]

His saying the Exalted: ﴿You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and you believe in Allah. And if the People of the Book had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient﴾. That is: the disbelievers.

The Almighty's saying: ﴿They will not harm you, except for a little hurt﴾. Muqatil said: The heads of the Jews set out against those among them who had believed, Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions, and they harmed them. So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿They will not harm you, except for a little hurt﴾. That is: they will not harm you, O believers, these Jews, except with a hurt of the tongue: threats and slander.
