Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 114–117:

Allah's words: ﴿They believe in Allah and the Last Day, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and hasten to do good deeds. And they are among the righteous.﴾

﴿And whatever good they do, they will not be denied its reward.﴾ Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Hafs read "yuknafarūhu" (with the yā') in both places, as a report about the upright community. The others read it with the tā' in both places, in accordance with His words ﴿You are the best community﴾. Abu 'Amr accepted both readings. The meaning of the verse: whatever good you do, you will not be deprived of its reward; rather, it will be appreciated for you and you will be recompensed for it. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of the God-fearing﴾, meaning, of the believers.

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth and their children will not avail them at all against Allah.﴾ That is: their wealth will not ransom them, nor their children help them, against any of the punishment of Allah. He mentioned these two specifically because a person sometimes defends himself by ransoming with wealth, and sometimes by seeking help from his children.

﴿Those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.﴾ He made them companions of the Fire because they are its people; they will not leave it nor be separated from it, like the companion of a man who does not part from him.

﴿The example of what they spend in this worldly life is like a wind containing a freezing cold...﴾ It was said: He meant the expenditures of Abu Sufyan and his companions at Badr and Uhud, in hostility toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Muqatil said: it is the expenditure of the Jews on their scholars. Mujahid said: it refers to all the expenditures and charities of the disbelievers [in this world]. It was also said: He meant the spending of the hypocrite (murā'ī) who does not seek thereby the Face of Allah, Exalted. ﴿Like a wind containing a freezing cold﴾. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father: that it is the scorching simoom which kills. It was said: "fīhā ṣirr" means a sound. Most of the exegetes said: it contains intense cold. ﴿Which strikes the tilth of a people﴾, the crops of a people, ﴿who have wronged themselves﴾ through disbelief, disobedience, and withholding the right of Allah, Exalted, ﴿and destroys it﴾.

So the meaning of the verse: the example of the disbelievers' expenditures, in their vanishing at the time they are needed, is like a crop struck by a cold wind that destroys it, or by a fire that burns it, so that its owners gain nothing from it. ﴿And Allah did not wrong them﴾ by that, ﴿but they wronged themselves﴾ through disbelief and disobedience.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 118–119:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as bitanah (inner circle, confidants) those other than your own﴾ to the end of the verse. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Some men among the Muslims used to associate closely with the Jews because of the kinship, friendship, alliance, neighbourhood and fosterage between them. So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed this verse, forbidding them from taking them as intimate confidants, out of fear of the trial (fitnah) that would befall them.

Mujahid said: It was revealed concerning a people among the believers who used to show friendship to the hypocrites, so Allah, may He be exalted, forbade them from doing so [[See Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi (153); Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/141; Sirah of Ibn Hisham: 2/207.]] and said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as bitanah those other than your own﴾, meaning: as allies and intimate friends from outside your religious community. The bitanah of a man is his inner circle, by analogy with the lining of a garment (bitanat al-thawb), which lies against the body, because they are privy to his affairs and become aware of what others are not aware of.

Then He explained the reason for the prohibition on taking them as confidants, saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿They do not spare you any ruin (khabal)﴾, meaning: they do not fall short and do not hold back their effort in what brings you evil and corruption. Al-khabal means evil and corruption. The word "khabalan" is in the accusative as the second object (maf'ul thani), because the verb ya'lu (يَأْلُو), meaning "to fall short of, to spare", takes two objects [[In manuscript A: "because al-alw is transitive to two objects."]]. It was also said that it is in the accusative by the removal of the preposition, meaning "with ruin", as one says "I struck him with beating" (awja'tuhu darban). ﴿They love what distresses you﴾, meaning: they wish for what is hard for you of harm, evil and destruction. Al-'anat is hardship. ﴿Hatred has already appeared﴾, meaning: enmity has become evident, ﴿from their mouths﴾ through insults and slander against the Muslims. It was also said: through disclosing the secrets of the believers to the polytheists. ﴿And what their chests conceal﴾ of enmity and rage ﴿is greater﴾, meaning: greater in magnitude. ﴿We have made the signs clear to you, if you use reason.﴾

﴿Here you are﴾: ha is an alert particle (tanbih), and antum is a pronoun for the addressed males. ﴿Those﴾ (ula'i) is a noun for those pointed to, meaning: you, O believers. ﴿You love them﴾, meaning: you love these Jews whom I have forbidden you to take as confidants, because of the ties between you of kinship, fosterage and marriage. ﴿But they do not love you﴾, because of the difference of religion between you. Muqatil said: They are the hypocrites. The believers love them because of the faith they showed outwardly, while they do not know what is in their hearts. ﴿And you believe in the Book, all of it﴾, meaning: in all the books, while they do not believe in your Book. ﴿When they meet you, they say, "We believe"; but when they are alone﴾ together with one another ﴿they bite their fingertips at you out of rage﴾, meaning: the tips of the fingers, singular unumulah, with the m vowelled with either damma or fatha, out of rage at seeing the unity of the believers and the harmony of their word. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 118–119:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as bitanah (inner circle, confidants) those other than your own﴾ to the end of the verse. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Some men among the Muslims used to associate closely with the Jews because of the kinship, friendship, alliance, neighbourhood and fosterage between them. So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed this verse, forbidding them from taking them as intimate confidants, out of fear of the trial (fitnah) that would befall them.

Mujahid said: It was revealed concerning a people among the believers who used to show friendship to the hypocrites, so Allah, may He be exalted, forbade them from doing so [[See Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi (153); Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/141; Sirah of Ibn Hisham: 2/207.]] and said: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take as bitanah those other than your own﴾, meaning: as allies and intimate friends from outside your religious community. The bitanah of a man is his inner circle, by analogy with the lining of a garment (bitanat al-thawb), which lies against the body, because they are privy to his affairs and become aware of what others are not aware of.

Then He explained the reason for the prohibition on taking them as confidants, saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿They do not spare you any ruin (khabal)﴾, meaning: they do not fall short and do not hold back their effort in what brings you evil and corruption. Al-khabal means evil and corruption. The word "khabalan" is in the accusative as the second object (maf'ul thani), because the verb ya'lu (يَأْلُو), meaning "to fall short of, to spare", takes two objects [[In manuscript A: "because al-alw is transitive to two objects."]]. It was also said that it is in the accusative by the removal of the preposition, meaning "with ruin", as one says "I struck him with beating" (awja'tuhu darban). ﴿They love what distresses you﴾, meaning: they wish for what is hard for you of harm, evil and destruction. Al-'anat is hardship. ﴿Hatred has already appeared﴾, meaning: enmity has become evident, ﴿from their mouths﴾ through insults and slander against the Muslims. It was also said: through disclosing the secrets of the believers to the polytheists. ﴿And what their chests conceal﴾ of enmity and rage ﴿is greater﴾, meaning: greater in magnitude. ﴿We have made the signs clear to you, if you use reason.﴾

Biting the fingertips is an expression for intense rage, and this is a figurative idiom (majaz al-amthal), even if there is no actual biting. ﴿Say: "Die in your rage!"﴾, meaning: remain in your rage until death. ﴿Indeed Allah knows what is in the breasts﴾, meaning: of good and evil in the hearts.

**Al-Baghawi's Commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 3, Verses 120–121**

His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿If good touches you﴾, meaning: if it reaches you, O believers, through your victory over your enemy, booty that you obtain from them, people's rush to enter your religion, and abundance in your livelihoods, ﴿it distresses them﴾, meaning: it grieves them. ﴿But if an evil touches you﴾, meaning a misfortune: through the failure of a detachment of yours, the injury of one of your enemies to you, disagreement arising among you, drought, or a calamity that befalls you, ﴿they rejoice at it. But if you are patient﴾ under their harm ﴿and conscious of God﴾, meaning you fear your Lord, ﴿their scheming will not harm you at all﴾, meaning it will not diminish you in any way.

Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and the people of Basra recited ﴿lā yadurrukum﴾ with a kasra on the dad and a light (unstressed) ra, from ḍāra, yaḍīru, ḍayran. This is a jussive (jazm) in answer to the conditional (jawab al-jaza'). The rest of the readers recited it with a damma on the dad and a shadda on the ra, from ḍarra, yaḍurru, ḍarran, like radda, yaruddu, raddan. There are two views regarding its vowelling. The first: he intended the jussive, and its original form is yaḍrurukum; the ra was assimilated into the ra (idgham, assimilation of identical consonants), the damma of the first ra was transferred to the dad, and the second was given a damma for harmony (ittiba'). The second: lā is in the sense of laysa (not), and a fa' is understood before it, its estimated form being: "And if you are patient and conscious of God, then their scheming does not harm you at all." Then: ﴿Indeed, God is encompassing of what they do﴾, meaning knowing.

His statement, Exalted is He: ﴿And [remember] when you set out from your family in the morning to station the believers at their positions for battle﴾. Al-Hasan said: this is the Day of Badr. Muqatil said: the Day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab). The rest of the exegetes said: it is the Day of Uhud, because what follows, up to nearly the end of the surah, concerns the battle of Uhud.

Mujahid, al-Kalbi and al-Waqidi said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) set out from the house of 'Aisha (may God be pleased with her), walked on foot to Uhud, and began arranging his companions for battle, as an arrow is straightened [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur by al-Suyuti: 2/302.]].

Muhammad ibn Ishaq and al-Suddi, on the authority of their men, said: the polytheists alighted at Uhud on Wednesday. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) heard of their arrival, he consulted his companions and summoned 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, whom he had never summoned before that, and consulted him. 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and most of the Ansar said: "O Messenger of God, remain in Medina and do not go out to them. By God, we have never gone out from it to an enemy without them inflicting harm upon us, and they have never entered it against us without our inflicting harm upon them. So how much more so when you are among us. Leave them, O Messenger of God; if they stay, they will have stayed in the worst of places; if they enter, the men will fight them at close quarters, and the women and children will pelt them with stones from above; and if they return, they will return defeated." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was pleased with this opinion.

But some of his companions said: "O Messenger of God, go out with us to these dogs (al-aklub). Let them not think that we were cowardly before them and weak." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I saw in my dream cows being slaughtered, and I interpreted them as good. I saw nicks in the edge of my sword, and I interpreted them as a defeat. And I saw that I put my hand into a sturdy coat of mail, and I interpreted it as Medina. So if you see fit, remain in Medina." He was fond of their entering upon him in Medina and fighting in its alleys [[An addition from manuscript "b".]]. Some men [[In ms. b: "a man".]] among the Muslims, those who had missed the Day of Badr and whom God had honoured with martyrdom on the Day of Uhud, said: "Go out with us to our enemies." They kept pressing the Messenger of God (ﷺ), out of their desire to meet the people, until the Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered, put on his armour. When they saw him wearing his weapons, they regretted it and said: "We have done wrong; we advised the Messenger of God (ﷺ) while revelation was coming to him." They stood up, apologized to him, and said: "Do what you see fit." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "It is not fitting for a prophet to put on his armour and then take it off until he fights" [[The Prophetic Biography of Ibn Hisham: 2/126 onward, with al-Rawd al-Unuf; the Musnad of Imam Ahmad: 3/351; al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim: 2/128–129, which he declared authentic and al-Dhahabi agreed with.]].

The polytheists had been encamped at Uhud on Wednesday and Thursday. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) set out on Friday, after leading his companions in the Friday prayer. A man from the Ansar died on that day, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) prayed over him, then went out to them. He arrived at the mountain pass of Uhud on Saturday, the middle of Shawwal, in the third year after the Hijra. What happened in the battle of Uhud then happened. That is His statement: ﴿And [remember] when you set out from your family﴾, meaning: and remember when you set out from your family ﴿to station the believers﴾, meaning: to settle the believers ﴿at their positions for battle﴾, meaning: places and stations for fighting. It is said: bawwa'tu al-qawm means I settled the people, and tabawwa'u means they settled themselves. God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿And We had settled the Children of Israel in a true abode﴾ [Yunus: 93], and He said: ﴿that you two settle your people in Egypt in houses﴾ [Yunus: 87]. It is also said: it means he takes a camp. ﴿And God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 122:

﴿When two groups among you were about to lose heart, and Allah was their protector.﴾ That is: they were about to become cowardly, weaken, and withdraw. The two groups were Banu Salamah from the Khazraj and Banu Harithah from the Aws. Both were the two wings of the army. This was because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to Uhud with a thousand men, and it is said: with nine hundred and fifty men. When they reached al-Shawt [[A place name between Medina and Uhud. (Mu'jam al-Buldan).]], Abdullah ibn Ubayy withdrew with a third of the people and turned back with three hundred men, saying: "Why should we kill ourselves and our children?" Abu Jabir al-Sulami followed them and said: "I implore you by Allah, regarding your Prophet and yourselves." Abdullah ibn Ubayy said: "If we knew there would be fighting, we would have followed you." Banu Salamah and Banu Harithah were about to turn back with Abdullah ibn Ubayy, but Allah preserved them and they did not turn back. Then Allah reminded them of the magnitude of His blessing [[See: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2/128.]], and the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿When two groups among you were about to lose heart, and Allah was their protector.﴾ That is, His helper and guardian.

﴿And upon Allah let the believers put their trust.﴾ Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) related to us, and Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us from Ibn Uyaynah, from Amr, from Jabir, who said: This verse was revealed about us: ﴿When two groups among you were about to lose heart, and Allah was their protector.﴾ They were Banu Salamah and Banu Harithah, and I would not like it if it had not been revealed, since Allah says: ﴿and Allah was their protector﴾ [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter "When two groups among you were about to lose heart..." 7/357.]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 123–124:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah had already given you victory at Badr﴾ Badr is a place between Makkah and Madinah, and it is the name of a location. Most scholars hold this view. It was also said that Badr is the name of a well there. And it was said: Badr was a well belonging to a man called Badr. This was reported by al-Sha'bi, but others rejected it.

In this verse, Allah, may He be exalted, mentions His favour upon them by granting them victory on the day of Badr. ﴿And you were humble﴾ is the plural of dhalil (humble, weak), and by it He means the small number of their men. They were three hundred and thirteen men, and Allah gave them victory despite their small number. ﴿So fear Allah that you may be grateful.﴾

﴿When you said to the believers, "Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you﴾ The scholars differed regarding this verse. Qatadah said: This was on the day of Badr. Allah, may He be exalted, reinforced them with a thousand angels, as He said: "When you sought help of your Lord, and He answered you, 'I will reinforce you with a thousand of the angels, following one another'" [al-Anfal: 9]. Then they became three thousand, and then they became five thousand, as is mentioned here: ﴿with three thousand angels sent down.﴾

Then they became three thousand, and then they became five thousand, as is mentioned here: ﴿with three thousand angels sent down.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 3, verse 125:**

﴿Yes, if you are patient and mindful of God, and they come upon you in this very moment, your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels, marked out.﴾ So they were patient on the Day of Badr, and they were mindful of God, so God reinforced them with five thousand, as He had promised. Al-Hasan said: These five thousand are a support (ridf) for the believers until the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: The angels did not fight in battle except on the Day of Badr. On other occasions they witness the fighting but do not fight; they are only a number and a reinforcement (madad).

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: On the Day of Uhud, the people withdrew from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Sa'd ibn Malik remained shooting arrows, and a young man was handing him arrows. Whenever his arrows ran out, the young man brought him more and scattered them before him, and [the Prophet] said: "Shoot, Abu Ishaq," twice. When the battle ended, he was asked about that man, but he was not recognised.

'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd Allah informed us: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd informed us, from his father, from his grandfather, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the Day of Uhud,[[In A: "Badr." See Fath al-Bari: 7/349.]] and with him were two men fighting on his behalf, wearing white garments, fighting most fiercely; I had never seen them before or since."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Maghazi, chapter: "When two groups among you were about to lose heart" (7/358), and in al-Libas, chapter on white garments; and Muslim in al-Fada'il, chapter on the fighting of Jibril and Mika'il on behalf of the Prophet (ﷺ) on the Day of Uhud, no. 2306 (4/1802); and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah (13/292).]]

Muslim narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, who said: Muhammad ibn Bishr and Abu Usamah informed us, from Mis'ar, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Sa'd, meaning Ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: "I saw, on the Day of Uhud, on the right and left of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), two men wearing white garments; I had never seen them before or since," meaning Jibril and Mika'il.[[Narrated by Muslim in al-Fada'il, chapter on the fighting of Jibril and Mika'il on behalf of the Prophet (ﷺ), no. 2306 (4/1802).]]

Al-Sha'bi said: News reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims on the Day of Badr that Kurz ibn Jabir al-Muharibi intended to reinforce the polytheists, and this distressed them. So Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿Is it not enough for you that your Lord reinforces you…﴾ up to His words ﴿marked out﴾. Then the news of the defeat reached Kurz, so he turned back and did not come to them, and did not reinforce them. Thus Allah did not reinforce them with the five thousand either, although they had been reinforced with a thousand.

Others said: Allah, exalted is He, promised the Muslims on the Day of Badr that, if they remained patient in obeying Him and mindful of His prohibitions, He would reinforce them again in all their wars. But they were not patient except on the Day of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), so Allah reinforced them until they besieged Qurayzah and al-Nadir. 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Awfa said: "We were besieging Qurayzah and al-Nadir[[No book of biography reports that Qurayzah and al-Nadir were besieged at the same time, as this narration implies. See: al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (2/194 and following), with al-Rawd al-Unuf; Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd (2/57 and 74).]] for as long as Allah willed, and nothing was opened to us, so we returned. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked for water for washing, and he was washing his head when Jibril, peace be upon him, came to him and said: 'You have laid down your weapons, but the angels have not laid down their burdens?' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked for a cloth, wrapped his head in it, and did not wash it. Then he called out among us, and we rose and went until we reached Qurayzah and al-Nadir.[[See: al-Musannaf of Ibn Abi Shaybah (14/424); al-Iktifa' fi Maghazi Rasul Allah of al-Kala'i (2/176).]] On that day Allah, exalted is He, reinforced us with three thousand angels, and He granted us a limited victory."

Al-Dahhak and Ikrimah said: This was on the Day of Uhud. Allah had promised them reinforcement if they were patient, but they were not patient, so they were not reinforced.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿that your Lord reinforce you﴾. Al-Imdad (reinforcement) means aiding an army with an army. It was also said: what is in the sense of strength and assistance is said as amaddahu imdadan, and what is in the sense of increase is said as maddahu madda. From this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and the sea, with seven more seas to supply it (yamudduhu)﴾ [Luqman: 27]. It was also said: al-madd is used for evil and al-imdad for good, as indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and He extends them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-Baqarah: 15], and ﴿We extend for him the extension of punishment﴾ [Maryam: 79]; and He said regarding good: ﴿I will reinforce you (mumiddukum) with a thousand angels following one another﴾, and He said: ﴿and We reinforced you with wealth and sons﴾ [al-Isra': 26].

His words, exalted is He: ﴿with three thousand angels sent down﴾ (munzalin). Ibn 'Amir read it with the doubled zay (nazzalin), for multiplicity, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Even if We had sent down the angels to them﴾ [al-An'am: 111]. The others read it with the single zay (anzalin), and the evidence is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Why were the angels not sent down upon us?﴾ [al-Furqan: 21], and His saying: ﴿and sent down hosts you did not see﴾ [al-Tawbah: 26].

Then He said: ﴿Yes﴾, We will reinforce you, ﴿if you are patient﴾ against your enemy, ﴿and mindful﴾, that is, of opposing your Prophet, ﴿and they come upon you﴾, meaning the polytheists, ﴿in this very moment﴾. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, Qatadah, al-Hasan and most of the exegetes said: "from this direction (wajhihim) of theirs." Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: "from their anger (ghadabihim) at this moment," because they only returned to war on the Day of Uhud out of anger over the Day of Badr. ﴿Your Lord will reinforce you with five thousand angels﴾: He did not intend five thousand in addition to the three thousand already mentioned; rather He meant them together with those [three thousand].[[In A: "what we mentioned."]] His words ﴿marked out﴾ mean "distinguished." Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and 'Asim read it with a kasra on the waw (musawwimin), while the others read it with a fatha (musawwamin). Whoever reads it with a kasra means that they marked their horses; whoever reads it with a fatha means themselves. Al-Taswim means making something known, from al-sawmah, which is the mark.

They differed about that mark. 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said: The angels were on piebald horses (bulq), wearing yellow turbans. 'Ali and Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them, said: They wore white turbans, letting them hang between their shoulders. (Hisham ibn 'Urwah and al-Kalbi said: yellow turbans, loosened and hanging over their shoulders.)[[Addition from A.]] Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: They had marked the forelocks and tails of the horses with wool (al-'ihn). It is also narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions on the Day of Badr: "Mark yourselves, for the angels have marked themselves with white wool on their helmets and their armour."[[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf, Kitab al-Jihad (12/261), through Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adiyy from Ibn 'Awn from 'Umayr ibn Ishaq who said…; and he also narrated it in al-Maghazi (14/358) through Abu Usamah from Ibn 'Awn from 'Umayr ibn Ishaq, as a mursal report. al-Tabari narrated it in his Tafsir (7/186). al-Waqidi said: Muhammad ibn Salih narrated to me from 'Asim ibn 'Umar from Mahmud ibn Labid… and he mentioned it. Ibn Sa'd narrated it in al-Tabaqat (2/16). See also: al-Kafi al-Shaf of Ibn Hajar, p. 31.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 126–129:

The words of His, exalted is He: (And Allah did not make it) meaning this promise and reinforcement, (except as good news for you) that is, as glad tidings, so that you may be reassured by it (and that your hearts may be at rest) and be tranquil, (through it) so that you do not lose heart because of the multitude of your enemy and the fewness of your number. (And victory is only from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise). Meaning: do not attribute victory to the angels and the soldiers; victory is from Allah, exalted is He, so seek His help and put your trust in Him, for might and judgment belong to Him.

The words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿That He may cut off a part of those who disbelieve﴾. He says: Allah indeed helped you at Badr, so that He might cut off a part, that is, so that He might destroy a group of those who disbelieve. Al-Suddi said: its meaning is that He might demolish a pillar of the pillars of polytheism by killing and capturing. Seventy of their leaders and chiefs were killed on the day of Badr, and seventy were taken captive. Whoever applies the verse to the battle of Uhud, sixteen of them were killed on that day. Victory belonged to the Muslims until they disobeyed the command of the Messenger (ﷺ), and then it turned against them. ﴿Or subdue them﴾: al-Kalbi said: defeat them. Yaman said: throw them down on their faces. Al-Suddi said: curse them. Abu 'Ubayda said: destroy them. It was said: sadden them. Al-maknub means the grieved. It was also said that its origin is "yakbidahum," meaning that grief and rage reach their livers, and the letters ta' and dal interchange, as one says "sabata ra'sahu" and "sabadahu" when he shaves it. It was also said: He subdues them with disappointment. ﴿So that they turn back frustrated﴾: they fail to attain anything of what they hoped for of gaining the upper hand over you.

The words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿You have no say in the matter﴾, to the end of the verse. The scholars differed concerning the occasion of the revelation of this verse. A group said: it was revealed concerning the people of Bi'r Ma'una, who were seventy men of the reciters. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent them to Bi'r Ma'una in Safar of the fourth year after the Hijra, four months after Uhud, to teach the people the Qur'an and knowledge. Their leader was al-Mundhir ibn 'Amr. 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl killed them, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was deeply grieved by this. He performed the qunut for a month in all the prayers, invoking curses and calamities upon a group of those tribes. Then this was revealed: ﴿You have no say in the matter﴾ [[See: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Tafsir, chapter "You have no say in the matter": 8/225–226.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Hibban ibn Musa informed us: Abd Allah, that is Ibn al-Mubarak, informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim narrated to me, from his father, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he raised his head from bowing in the last rak'a of the Dawn prayer, say: "O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so and so-and-so," after he said: "Allah hears whoever praises Him; our Lord, and to You is the praise." Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿You have no say in the matter, whether He turns to them or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾ [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Maghazi, chapter "You have no say in the matter, whether He turns to them": 7/365.]].

Another group said: it was revealed on the day of Uhud. Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us: 'Abd al-Ghafir [[In "A": 'Abd al-Ghaffar.]] ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us: Abd Allah ibn Maslama ibn Qa'nab informed us: Hammad ibn Salama informed us, from Thabit, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had his incisor broken on the day of Uhud and was wounded in the head. He began wiping the blood from it and saying: "How will a people prosper who wound the head of their prophet and break his tooth, while he calls them to Allah, mighty and majestic?" Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿You have no say in the matter﴾ [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Maghazi, chapter "You have no say in the matter, whether He turns to them": 7/365, and Muslim in Kitab al-Jihad, chapter on the battle of Uhud, no. 1791: 3/1417.]].

And from Abd Allah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of Uhud: "O Allah, curse Abu Sufyan. O Allah, curse al-Harith ibn Hisham. O Allah, curse Safwan ibn Umayya." Then this was revealed: ﴿You have no say in the matter, whether He turns to them﴾, and they embraced Islam and their Islam was good [[Narrated by al-Bukhari from Ibn Umar with the wording: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to invoke curses upon Safwan ibn Umayya, Suhayl ibn Amr and al-Harith ibn Hisham, and then this was revealed: You have no say in the matter," in Kitab al-Maghazi, chapter "You have no say in the matter": 7/365. With the wording of the author, it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Kitab al-Tafsir, Tafsir of Surah Al 'Imran: 8/355–356, and he said: this is a hasan gharib hadith, which is unusual from the hadith of Umar ibn Hamza from Salim; and similarly al-Zuhri narrated it from Salim from his father. And Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2/93.]].

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said [[See: Ibn Hisham's al-Sira al-Nabawiyya: 2/141.]]: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims saw on the day of Uhud what had been done to their companions of mutilation of ears and noses and cutting off of private parts, they said: "If Allah grants us victory over them, we will do to them what they did, and we will mutilate them with a mutilation that no one among the Arabs has ever inflicted upon anyone." Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

It was also said: the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to invoke destruction upon them, and then this verse was revealed [[See: al-Tabari: 7/198.]], because he knew that many of them would embrace Islam. So the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿You have no say in the matter﴾ mean: it is not up to you. The lam here means "ila" (to), as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 193], meaning: to faith. His words: ﴿or He turns to them﴾ (some of them said: its meaning is "until He turns to them") or: "until He turns to them." It was also said: it is a continuation of His words "that He may cut off a part," and His words "You have no say in the matter" are a parenthetical interruption between the structure of the sentence and the structure of the verse, [[In "B" the phrase reads: an interruption between the lam and the structure of the verse.]] "that He may cut off a part of those who disbelieve, or subdue them, or turn to them, or punish them, for indeed they are wrongdoers. You have no say in the matter; rather the command is Mine in all of that."

Then He said: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Then this was revealed: ﴿You have no say in the matter﴾ [[See: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Tafsir, chapter "You have no say in the matter": 8/225–226.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Hibban ibn Musa informed us: Abd Allah, that is Ibn al-Mubarak, informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim narrated to me, from his father, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he raised his head from bowing in the last rak'a of the Dawn prayer, say: "O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so and so-and-so," after he said: "Allah hears whoever praises Him; our Lord, and to You is the praise." Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿You have no say in the matter, whether He turns to them or punishes them, for indeed they are wrongdoers﴾ [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Maghazi, chapter "You have no say in the matter, whether He turns to them": 7/365.]].

Another group said: it was revealed on the day of Uhud. Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us: 'Abd al-Ghafir [[In "A": 'Abd al-Ghaffar.]] ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan informed us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj informed us: Abd Allah ibn Maslama ibn Qa'nab informed us: Hammad ibn Salama informed us, from Thabit, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had his incisor broken on the day of Uhud and was wounded in the head. He began wiping the blood from it and saying: "How will a people prosper who wound the head of their prophet and break his tooth, while he calls them to Allah, mighty and majestic?" Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿You have no say in the matter﴾ [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Maghazi, chapter "You have no say in the matter, whether He turns to them": 7/365, and Muslim in Kitab al-Jihad, chapter on the battle of Uhud, no. 1791: 3/1417.]].

And from Abd Allah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said on the day of Uhud: "O Allah, curse Abu Sufyan. O Allah, curse al-Harith ibn Hisham. O Allah, curse Safwan ibn Umayya." Then this was revealed: ﴿You have no say in the matter, whether He turns to them﴾, and they embraced Islam and their Islam was good [[Narrated by al-Bukhari from Ibn Umar with the wording: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to invoke curses upon Safwan ibn Umayya, Suhayl ibn Amr and al-Harith ibn Hisham, and then this was revealed: You have no say in the matter," in Kitab al-Maghazi, chapter "You have no say in the matter": 7/365. With the wording of the author, it was narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Kitab al-Tafsir, Tafsir of Surah Al 'Imran: 8/355–356, and he said: this is a hasan gharib hadith, which is unusual from the hadith of Umar ibn Hamza from Salim; and similarly al-Zuhri narrated it from Salim from his father. And Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2/93.]].

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said [[See: Ibn Hisham's al-Sira al-Nabawiyya: 2/141.]]: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Muslims saw on the day of Uhud what had been done to their companions of mutilation of ears and noses and cutting off of private parts, they said: "If Allah grants us victory over them, we will do to them what they did, and we will mutilate them with a mutilation that no one among the Arabs has ever inflicted upon anyone." Then Allah, exalted is He, revealed this verse.

It was also said: the Prophet (ﷺ) wished to invoke destruction upon them, and then this verse was revealed [[See: al-Tabari: 7/198.]], because he knew that many of them would embrace Islam. So the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿You have no say in the matter﴾ mean: it is not up to you. The lam here means "ila" (to), as in His words, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard a caller calling to faith﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 193], meaning: to faith. His words: ﴿or He turns to them﴾ (some of them said: its meaning is "until He turns to them") or: "until He turns to them." It was also said: it is a continuation of His words "that He may cut off a part," and His words "You have no say in the matter" are a parenthetical interruption between the structure of the sentence and the structure of the verse, [[In "B" the phrase reads: an interruption between the lam and the structure of the verse.]] "that He may cut off a part of those who disbelieve, or subdue them, or turn to them, or punish them, for indeed they are wrongdoers. You have no say in the matter; rather the command is Mine in all of that."

Then He said: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 130–132:

﴿O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied﴾. He means by it what they used to do when the term of a debt came due: an increase in the money and a delay in demanding it. ﴿And fear Allah﴾ regarding the matter of usury, so do not consume it, ﴿that you may be successful﴾.

Then He warned them, saying: ﴿And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾.

﴿And obey Allah and the Messenger that you may be shown mercy﴾ (132).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 130–132:

﴿O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied﴾. He means by it what they used to do when the term of a debt came due: an increase in the money and a delay in demanding it. ﴿And fear Allah﴾ regarding the matter of usury, so do not consume it, ﴿that you may be successful﴾.

Then He warned them, saying: ﴿And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾.

﴿And obey Allah and the Messenger that you may be shown mercy﴾ (132).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 130–132:

﴿O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied﴾. He means by it what they used to do when the term of a debt came due: an increase in the money and a delay in demanding it. ﴿And fear Allah﴾ regarding the matter of usury, so do not consume it, ﴿that you may be successful﴾.

Then He warned them, saying: ﴿And fear the Fire which has been prepared for the disbelievers﴾.

﴿And obey Allah and the Messenger that you may be shown mercy﴾ (132).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 133:

﴿And obey Allah and the Messenger, that you may be shown mercy.﴾ That is, so that you may be shown mercy.

﴿And hasten﴾ The people of Medina and Syria recited "sara'ū" (سَارِعُوا) without the waw. ﴿To forgiveness from your Lord﴾ means: hurry and race toward the deeds that necessitate forgiveness.

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "To Islam." It is also narrated from him: "To repentance," and Ikrimah said the same. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "To performing the obligatory duties." Abu al-'Aliyah said: "To migration." al-Dahhak said: "To jihad." Muqatil said: "To righteous deeds." It is narrated from Anas ibn Malik that it refers to the first takbir (opening takbir of the prayer).

﴿And a Garden﴾ means: and toward a Garden, ﴿whose width is the heavens and the earth﴾ means: its width is like the width of the heavens and the earth, as He said in surah al-Hadid: "And a Garden whose width is like the width of the heaven and the earth" [al-Hadid: 21], meaning its vastness. The mention of "width" is for emphasis, because the length of anything is usually greater than its width. It is said: "This is the description of its width, so how is its length?" al-Zuhri said: "He only described its width; as for its length, none knows it except Allah." This is an illustration, not that it is only like the heavens and the earth. The meaning is: like the width of the seven heavens and the seven earths, by your reckoning. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾ [Hud: 107], meaning by your reckoning, for otherwise they both will pass away.

It is narrated from Tariq ibn Shihab that some Jews asked 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, while his companions (may Allah be pleased with them) were with him, and they said: "Tell us about His saying: ﴿a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth﴾. Then where is the Fire?" 'Umar said: "Tell me, when the night comes, where is the day, and when the day comes, where is the night?" They said: "Indeed it is like that in the Tawrah."[[Recorded by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 7/133. Ibn Hibban recorded from Abu Hurayrah who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, tell me about a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth; then where is the Fire?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "Tell me, this night has passed, and there is nothing; where was it placed?" He said: "Allah knows best." He said: "Indeed Allah does what He wills." (Mawarid al-Zam'an, p. 428). al-Hakim recorded it in al-Mustadrak: 1/36, and declared it sound according to the conditions of the two shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim). al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id: 6/327: "al-Bazzar recorded it, and its narrators are the narrators of the sound (hadith)." See also: Tafsir al-Tabari with the commentary of Shaykh Shakir: 7/212.]] Its meaning is that it is wherever Allah wills.

If it is said: Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And in the heaven is your provision and what you are promised﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 22], and by "what we were promised" He meant Paradise. If Paradise is in the heaven, how can its width be the heavens and the earth? It is said: the gate of Paradise is in the heaven, and its width is the heavens and the earth, as He has informed. Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked about Paradise: "Is it in the heaven or in the earth?" He said: "And what earth and heaven could contain Paradise?" It was said: "Then where is it?" He said: "Above the seven heavens, beneath the Throne." Qatadah said: "They used to hold that Paradise is above the seven heavens, and that Hell is beneath the seven earths," ﴿prepared for the righteous﴾.

﴿Those who spend in ease and in hardship﴾, that is, in prosperity and in adversity. The first of the qualities that make them deserving of Paradise that is mentioned is generosity (al-sakha'). A hadith has come concerning this:

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi related to us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi related to us, Abu 'Amr al-Furati related to us, Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Isma'il al-'Anbari related to us, Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Hazim al-Baghawi in Mecca related to us, Abu Salih ibn Ayyub al-Hashimi related to us, Ibrahim ibn Sa'd related to us, Sa'id ibn Muhammad related to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The generous person is near to Allah, near to Paradise, near to people, and far from the Fire. The miser is far from Allah, far from Paradise, far from people, and near to the Fire. And an ignorant generous person is more beloved to Allah than a miserly worshipper." [[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi in al-Birr wa al-Silah, chapter on what has come concerning generosity: 6/95-96, and he said: "This is a strange hadith which we do not know except from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Muhammad from Yahya ibn Sa'id from al-A'raj from Abu Hurayrah. Sa'id ibn Muhammad was contradicted in narrating this hadith from Yahya ibn Sa'id; it is only narrated from Yahya ibn Sa'id from 'A'ishah as a mursal report." Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id: "al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat, and in its chain is Sa'id ibn Muhammad al-Warraq, who is weak." Al-Majma': 3/127. See also: Fayd al-Qadir by al-Munawi: 4/139.]].

﴿And those who restrain their anger﴾, that is, those who swallow their anger when their souls are filled with it. Al-kazm (restraint) means holding back something when it is full, and kazm al-ghayz (restraining anger) means that a person is filled with anger but returns it into his inner self and does not show it. From this is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿When the hearts rise up to the throats, choking with grief﴾ (Ghafir: 18). Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi related to us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi related to us, Abu 'Amr al-Furati related to us, Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Isfara'ini related to us, Abu 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad Zakariyya al-'Allani related to us, Rawh ibn 'Abd al-Mu'min related to us, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri related to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub related to us, who said: Abu Marhum narrated to me from Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas al-Juhani, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever restrains anger while he is able to act upon it, Allah will call him on the Day of Resurrection before all creatures until He lets him choose from whichever of the wide-eyed maidens (hur) he wishes." [[Recorded by Abu Dawud in al-Adab, chapter on one who restrains anger: 7/164. He said, al-Mundhiri: "Sahl ibn Mu'adh ibn Anas al-Juhani is weak, and the one who narrated this hadith from him is Abu Marhum 'Abd al-Rahim ibn Maymun al-Laythi, their client, from Egypt, and his hadith is not to be used as evidence." It was also recorded by al-Tirmidhi in al-Birr wa al-Silah, chapter on restraining anger: 6/166, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith," and he also recorded it in al-Qiyamah. Ibn Majah recorded it in al-Zuhd, chapter on forbearance, no. (4186): 2/1400, and Ahmad in al-Musnad: 3/438. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/317 to 'Abd ibn Humayd and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.]].

﴿And those who pardon people﴾. Al-Kalbi said: [they pardon] the bad manners of their slaves. Zayd ibn Aslam and Muqatil said: [they pardon] those who wronged them and harmed them.

﴿And Allah loves the good-doers﴾ [[In the printed edition there is this addition: "From al-Thawri: Ihsan is that you do good to the one who does evil, for doing good to the one who does good is mere trade." It is not found in the two manuscript copies.]].

The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 135:

The Almighty's statement: ﴿And those who, when they commit an immoral act or wrong themselves﴾ – to the end of the verse. Ibn Mas'ud said: The believers said, "O Messenger of Allah, the Children of Israel were more honoured by Allah than us. When one of them committed a sin, the expiation of his sin would be written on the threshold of his door: 'Cut off your nose and your ear, do such-and-such.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained silent, and then Allah revealed this verse.[[Narrated by al-Tabari, 7/219, and al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul (occasions of revelation), p. 119, with his chain from ʿAta'; al-Suyuti cites it in al-Durr al-Manthur, 2/326, attributing it to Ibn al-Mundhir from Ibn ʿAbbas.]]

ʿAta' said: It was revealed concerning Nabhan al-Tammar, whose kunya was Abu Ma'bad. A beautiful woman came to him to buy dates from him. He said to her, "These dates are not good, but there are better ones in the house." So he took her to his house, embraced her and kissed her. She said to him, "Fear Allah!" So he left her, and he regretted this. He came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, and then this verse was revealed.[[Al-Wahidi, Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 118. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar also mentioned the story in al-Isabah, 6/418–419, in his biography of Nabhan al-Tammar. He said: Muqatil ibn Sulayman mentioned in his tafsir, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas… Then he said: Likewise Abd al-Ghani ibn Sa'id al-Thaqafi transmitted it in his tafsir from Musa ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAta', from Ibn ʿAbbas, at length. Muqatil is abandoned (matruk), al-Dahhak did not hear from Ibn ʿAbbas, and Abd al-Ghani and Musa are both destroyed (halik). Al-Tha'labi, al-Mahdawi, Makki and al-Mawardi also cited this story in their tafsirs without a chain.]]

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) established brotherhood between two men, one of them from the Ansar and the other from Thaqif. The Thaqafi went out on a military expedition and appointed the Ansari as his deputy over his family. One day he bought meat for them. When the woman wanted to take it from him, he followed her inside and kissed her hand. Then he regretted it, left, put dust on his head and wandered aimlessly. When the Thaqafi returned, the Ansari did not come to greet him. He asked his wife about his condition, and she said, "May Allah not multiply brothers like him," and described the situation to him. Meanwhile the Ansari was roaming the mountains, repentant and seeking forgiveness. The Thaqafi searched for him until he found him, and brought him to Abu Bakr, hoping he would find comfort and relief with him. The Ansari said, "I am ruined," and related the story to him. Abu Bakr said, "Woe to you! Do you not know that Allah, the Exalted, becomes more jealous for the one on campaign than for the one who stays at home?" Then they went to ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), and he said the same. Then they came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said to him what they had said, and so Allah revealed this verse: ﴿And those who, when they commit an immoral act﴾.[[Asbab al-Nuzul, al-Wahidi, p. 118, without a chain; al-Kalbi is weak.]] That is: an ugly act that exceeds what Allah has permitted to him. The root of al-fuhsh (immorality) is ugliness and going beyond the limit. Jabir said: "al-Fahisha" is adultery.

﴿Or wrong themselves﴾ refers to what is less than adultery: kissing, embracing, looking and touching.

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: "Al-fahisha" is what is less than adultery, such as a kiss, a touch, or a look at what is not lawful; "or wrong themselves" means by disobedience.

It was also said: "They commit an immoral act" refers to major sins, and "wrong themselves" refers to minor sins.

It was also said: "They commit an immoral act" in deed, or "wrong themselves" in speech.

﴿They remember Allah﴾, that is, they remember Allah's threat and that Allah will call them to account. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: They remember Allah with their tongues at the time of sins.

﴿And seek forgiveness for their sins – and who forgives sins except Allah?﴾ That is: and who forgives sins except Allah?

﴿And do not persist in what they have done﴾, that is: they do not remain and do not persist in it, but they repent, turn back in penitence and seek forgiveness. The root of al-israr (persistence) is steadfastness upon something. Al-Hasan said: Persistence is when a servant commits a sin deliberately and does not repent until he repents.

Al-Suddi said: Persistence is remaining silent and abandoning seeking forgiveness.

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us; Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us; Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us; Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us; Yahya ibn Yahya informed us; ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman informed us, from ʿUthman ibn Waqid al-ʿUmari, from Abu Nusayra, who said: I met a client (mawla) of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), and I said to him: "Did you hear anything from Abu Bakr?" He said: "Yes, I heard him say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'One who seeks forgiveness does not persist, even if he returns to the sin seventy times in a day.'"[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Witr, in the chapter on seeking forgiveness, 2/150; al-Tirmidhi in al-Da'awat, chapter of various hadiths on supplications, 10/4, who said: This is a gharib hadith; we know it only from the hadith of Abu Nusayra, and its chain is not strong. Also narrated by al-Marwazi in Musnad Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, nos. 121–122, pp. 155–156; the hadith is also unknown in that the client of Abu Bakr is unidentified. Al-Tabari narrated it in his tafsir, 7/225–226. Abu Ya'la and al-Bazzar also narrated it, and al-Bazzar said: We do not know it except from the hadith of Abu Bakr through this route, and Abu Nusayra and his shaykh are not known. Ibn Hajar said: It has a witness narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Da'a' from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas; see al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 32. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir, 1/409, and said: "Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Bazzar in his Musnad narrated it from the hadith of ʿUthman ibn Waqid, whom Yahya ibn Ma'in deemed reliable; his shaykh Abu Bakr al-Muqasati, whose name is Salim ibn ʿUbayd, was deemed reliable by Imam Ahmad and Ibn Hibban. But the statement of Ali ibn al-Madini and al-Tirmidhi that the chain of this hadith is not of that level is noted. The apparent reason is the anonymity of the client of Abu Bakr. However, the anonymity of such a person is not harmful, because he is a senior Successor (tabi'i), and his attribution to Abu Bakr suffices for him.")]]

﴿And they know﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: "And they know" that it is disobedience. It was also said: "And they know" that persistence is harmful. Al-Dahhak said: "And they know" that Allah possesses the forgiveness of sins. Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: "And they know" that they have a Lord who forgives sins. It was also said: "And they know" that Allah is not overwhelmed by pardoning sins, however many they may be. It was also said: "And they know" that if they seek forgiveness, they will be forgiven.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 3, verse 136:**

﴿Those—their reward is forgiveness from their Lord, and gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein, and excellent is the reward of those who work.﴾

The reward of the obedient.

Abu al-Hasan... [see note below]

Hmm, I need to correct myself: the passage must be translated in full, so here is the complete translation.

The reward of the obedient. ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us: Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: ʿAffan ibn Muslim informed us: Abu ʿAwana informed us: ʿUthman ibn al-Mughira informed us, from ʿAli ibn Rabi'a al-Asadi, from Asma' ibn al-Hakam al-Fazari, who said: I heard ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) say: "I was a man who, whenever I heard a hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Allah benefited me from it as much as He willed. And when any of his Companions related to me, I would make him swear, and if he swore to me, I would believe him. Abu Bakr related to me, and Abu Bakr spoke the truth, that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'There is no servant who commits a sin, then performs wudu well, then stands and prays, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, except that Allah forgives him.'" And Abu ʿIsa related it from Qutayba, from Abu ʿAwana, and added: Then he recited: ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves...﴾ to the end of the verse. [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Salat, chapter on what has come concerning prayer at repentance: 2/442–444, and he said: a hasan hadith which we do not know except through this route. He also narrated it in al-Tafsir. Also narrated by Ibn Hibban in al-Tawba, p. 608 (from Mawarid al-Zam'an), and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad from Abu Bakr: 1/10; Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi in al-Musnad (p. 2); Abu Bakr al-Marwazi in Musnad Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, no. 9–10, pp. 42–43. Al-Tabari narrated it in al-Tafsir: 7/220. The author narrated it in Sharh al-Sunna: 4/151–152 and said: a hasan hadith not known except from the hadith of ʿUthman ibn al-Mughira, from whom Shu'ba, Mis'ar and others narrated. Al-Suyuti attributed it to al-Nasa'i, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman. See al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/327. Ibn Hajar said in al-Tahdhib: 1/235: "This hadith has a good chain." Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir: 1/408, after citing the narration of Imam Ahmad: "Thus it was narrated by ʿAli ibn al-Madini, al-Humaydi, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shayba, the people of the Sunna, Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, al-Bazzar and al-Daraqutni through various routes from ʿUthman ibn al-Mughira. We have mentioned its routes and a detailed discussion of it in the Musnad of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him. In sum, it is a hasan hadith." Then he cited supporting evidence for its authenticity in the Two Sahihs. See also Ibn Kathir 1/554.]]

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us: Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us: Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us: Hisham ibn ʿAbd al-Malik informed us: Hammam informed us, from Ishaq, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Talha, who said: There was a judge in Medina called ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi ʿAmra, and I heard him say: I heard Abu Hurayra say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "A servant committed a sin and said: 'O Lord, I have committed a sin, so forgive it for me.' His Lord, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'My servant knows that he has a Lord who forgives sins and takes account for them. I have forgiven My servant, so let him do what he wills.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Tawhid, chapter on the saying of Allah Most High "They wish to change the words of Allah": 13/466; Muslim in al-Tawba, chapter on accepting repentance from sins even if repeated, no. 2758: 4/2112; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 5/72.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 137–138:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed there have passed before you [similar] ways (sunan)﴾. ʿAṭāʾ said: "Laws (sharāʾiʿ)." Al-Kalbi said: "For every nation there passed a way (sunnah) and a path (minhaj); if they follow it, Allah is pleased with them." Mujahid said: "There have passed before you sunan, by destruction, upon those who denied before you." It was also said: "Sunan" means "umam" (nations), and the sunnah means the nation. The poet said:

"The people have not witnessed a virtue like your virtue,
nor have they seen anyone like you in the bygone sunan."

It was also said that the meaning is: "ahl al-sunan" (people of the ways). The sunnah is the followed course of conduct in good and evil. It is said: "So-and-so established a good sunnah or an evil sunnah," when he does a deed that is imitated, whether good or evil.

The meaning of the verse: There have passed and gone before from Me ways concerning those who were before you of the past disbelieving nations, through My granting them respite and My gradual leading them on, until the Book reaches its term concerning them, the appointed time I set for their destruction, and through the alternation (idālah) of My prophets over them.

﴿So travel through the earth and observe how was the end of the deniers﴾, i.e., the final outcome of those who denied. This refers to the battle of Uhud. Allah, mighty and majestic, says: "I grant them respite and lead them on until My appointed time arrives, which I have set for the support of the Prophet ﷺ and his allies and the destruction of his enemies."

﴿This﴾, i.e., this Qur'an, ﴿is a clarification (bayan) for mankind﴾ in general, ﴿and guidance﴾ from misguidance, ﴿and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾ in particular.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 3, verses 139–140:**

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Do not weaken and do not grieve﴾. This is an exhortation to the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) to engage in jihad, in addition to what had befallen them of killing and wounding on the Day of Uhud. Allah the Exalted says: "Do not weaken," meaning: do not become feeble and do not shrink back from fighting your enemies because of what has befallen you of killing and wounding. On that day, five of the Muhajirun were killed, among them Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Mus'ab ibn Umayr, and seventy men of the Ansar were killed.

﴿And do not grieve﴾, for ﴿you will be the uppermost﴾, meaning the final outcome will be yours, with victory and triumph, ﴿if you are believers﴾. It means: since you are believers, that is, because you are believers. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: When the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were routed in the mountain pass (al-Shi'b), Khalid ibn al-Walid came with the cavalry of the polytheists, wanting to climb the mountain above them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, let them not gain height over us. O Allah, we have no strength except through You." A group of Muslim archers rose up, climbed the mountain, and shot at the cavalry of the polytheists until they routed them. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and you are the uppermost﴾. Al-Kalbi said: This verse was revealed after the Day of Uhud, when the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered his Companions to pursue the enemy despite the wounds they had suffered, and this was hard on the Muslims, so Allah revealed this verse. Its evidence is His saying: ﴿And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy﴾ [al-Nisa': 104].

﴿If a wound touches you﴾. Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read *qurhun* (قُرْحٌ) with a *damma* on the *qaf* wherever it occurs, while the others read it with a *fatha* (*qarhun*, قَرْحٌ). Both are dialectal forms with the same meaning, like *al-juhd* and *al-jahd*. Al-Farra' said: *al-qarh* with a *fatha* means the wound itself, and with a *damma* it means the pain of the wound. This is an address to the Muslims, who withdrew from Uhud in sorrow and grief. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿If a wound touches you﴾ at Uhud, ﴿then a wound has touched the others like it﴾ at Badr, ﴿and these days We alternate among the people﴾, so there is a day for them and a day against them. The Muslims prevailed over the polytheists on the Day of Badr, killing seventy of them and taking seventy captive, and the polytheists prevailed over the Muslims on the Day of Uhud, wounding seventy of them and killing seventy-odd.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Amr ibn Khalid informed us: Zuhayr informed us: Abu Ishaq informed us, saying: I heard al-Bara' ibn Azib say: On the Day of Uhud, the Prophet (ﷺ) placed over the infantry (*rujjala*), who were fifty men, Abd Allah ibn Jubayr, and said: "If you see us snatched by birds, do not leave your place until I send for you. And if you see us defeat the enemy and trample them, do not leave until I send for you." They routed them. He said: "By Allah, I saw the women running, their anklets showing and their shins exposed, lifting their garments." The companions of Abd Allah ibn Jubayr said: "The spoils! O people, the spoils! Your companions have prevailed, so what are you waiting for?" Abd Allah ibn Jubayr said: "Have you forgotten what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to you?" They said: "By Allah, we will go to the people and surely take a share of the spoils." When they reached them, their faces were turned, and they came back in flight. That is the meaning of His saying: "when the Messenger was calling them from behind them" [Al 'Imran: 153]. Only twelve men remained with the Prophet (ﷺ), and the enemy struck seventy of us.

The Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions had taken from the polytheists on the Day of Badr one hundred and forty: seventy captives and seventy slain. Abu Sufyan then said: "Is Muhammad among the people?" three times. The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade them to answer him. Then he said: "Is the son of Abu Quhafah among the people?" three times. Then he said: "Is the son of al-Khattab among the people?" three times. Then he returned to his companions and said: "As for these, they have been killed." Umar could not contain himself and said: "You lie, by Allah, O enemy of Allah! Those whom you counted are all alive, and there remains for you what will grieve you." He said: "A day for a day of Badr, and war is in turns (*sijal*). You will find among the people mutilation which I did not order, but it does not displease me." Then he began to chant in rajaz: "Exalted is Hubal!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Will you not answer him?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what should we say?" He said: "Say: Allah is most high and most majestic." He said: "We have al-Uzza, and you have no al-Uzza." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Will you not answer him?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what should we say?" He said: "Say: Allah is our Protector, and you have no protector."

It is narrated with this meaning from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and in his narration Abu Sufyan said: "A day for a day, and the days alternate, and war is in turns." Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Our slain are not equal to yours: our slain are in Paradise and your slain are in the Fire."

Al-Zajjaj said: Victory (*al-dawlah*) belongs to the Muslims over the unbelievers, by His saying: ﴿And indeed Our soldiers, they are the victorious﴾. On the Day of Uhud, victory went to the unbelievers over the Muslims because they disobeyed the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And that Allah may know those who believe﴾, meaning: this alternation occurred so that Allah might see those who believe, distinguishing the believer from the hypocrite. ﴿And take from among you martyrs﴾, honouring certain people with martyrdom. ﴿And Allah does not love the wrongdoers﴾.

﴿And that Allah may purify those who believe﴾, meaning: He may cleanse them of sins, ﴿and destroy the disbelievers﴾, meaning: He may annihilate and ruin them. The meaning is: if they kill you, that is a purification for you, and if you kill them, that is their destruction and eradication.

﴿Or do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those of you who strive (jahadu) and made evident the patient?﴾ (142)

﴿Or do you think﴾: "Do you think?" ﴿that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet known﴾ [meaning: and Allah has not known] [[Addition from (B).]] ﴿those of you who strove, and [has not known] the patient﴾.

﴿And you had certainly wished for death before you met it. Then you have seen it while you were looking on﴾ (143). The reason for this was that a group of Muslims wished for a day like the Day of Badr, so that they might fight and be martyred. Allah then showed them the Day of Uhud. His words ﴿you wished for death﴾ mean: the cause of death, which is jihad, before you met it. ﴿Then you have seen it﴾ means: its causes.

If it is asked: what is the meaning of His words ﴿while you were looking on﴾ after His words ﴿you have seen it﴾? It is said: He mentioned it for emphasis. It is also said: sight (ru'yah) may mean knowledge, so He said ﴿while you were looking on﴾ to make clear that the intended meaning of sight is looking (nazar). It is also said: ﴿while you were looking on﴾ means: while you were looking at Muhammad ﷺ.

The words of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And Muhammad is not but a messenger; messengers have passed on before him. So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?﴾ (144)

The scholars of military expeditions (ashab al-maghazi) [[See: Sirat Ibn Hisham 2/127 and what follows, with al-Rawd al-Unuf; Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd 2/36 and what follows.]] said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out until he camped at the mountain pass (al-shi'b) of Uhud with seven hundred men. He placed Abdullah ibn Jubayr, who was the brother of Khawwat ibn Jubayr, over the archers, who numbered fifty men, and said: "Stand at the foot of the mountain and shoot arrows at them to protect us, so that they do not come at us from behind. Whether we win or lose, do not leave your position until I send for you, for we will not cease to be victorious as long as you remain in your place." Then the Quraysh came, with Khalid ibn al-Walid on their right wing and Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl on their left, and with them were the women beating tambourines and reciting verses. They fought until the battle became fierce. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a sword and said: "Who will take this sword with its right and strike the enemy with it until he is overcome?" Abu Dujanah Simak ibn Kharashah [[In (A): Harb. See: Usd al-Ghaba 2/451.]] al-Ansari took it. When he took it, he tied on a red turban and began to strut. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This is a gait that Allah the Exalted dislikes, except in this place." He split the heads of the polytheists with it. The Prophet ﷺ and his companions attacked the polytheists and defeated them.

It has been transmitted from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: "By Allah, I saw the women running up, their anklets showing and their shins bare, lifting their garments. The companions of Abdullah ibn Jubayr said: 'The spoils! By Allah, we will go to the people and take a share of the spoils!' When they reached them, their faces were turned away."

Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam said: "I saw Hind and her companions fleeing, climbing up the mountain, their ankles exposed, and their attendants were not holding anything back from them." When the archers saw the enemy had retreated and saw their companions plundering the spoils, they came forward wanting plunder.

When Khalid ibn al-Walid saw the few archers and the Muslims busy with the spoils, and saw their rear was unguarded, he called out to his cavalry among the polytheists, then charged at the companions of the Prophet ﷺ from behind. They defeated them and killed them. Abdullah ibn Qami'ah struck the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with a stone, breaking his nose and his incisor (rubā'iyah) and wounding his face, so that he was weighed down. His companions scattered from him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose toward a rock to climb it, but he had put on two coats of mail and could not manage, so Talhah sat beneath him and he rose until he stood upon it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Talhah has made it obligatory [for himself]" [[That is, he did a deed that made Paradise obligatory for him.]]. Hind and the women with her came and mutilated the slain of the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, cutting off ears and noses, until Hind made necklaces from them and gave them to Wahshi. She ripped open the liver of Hamzah and chewed it, but could not swallow it, so she spat it out. Abdullah ibn Qami'ah came intending to kill the Prophet ﷺ, but Mus'ab ibn Umayr, who was the bearer of the banner of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, defended the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Ibn Qami'ah killed him, believing that he had killed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He returned to the polytheists and said: "I have killed Muhammad." A crier cried out: "Verily Muhammad has been killed." It is said that this crier was Iblis. The people then fled, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began calling out to the people: "To me, servants of Allah! ﴿To me, servants of Allah!﴾" [[Addition from (B).]] Thirty men gathered to him and protected him until they drove the polytheists away from him. Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas shot until the string of his bow snapped, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ handed him his quiver and said to him: "Shoot! May my father and mother be your ransom!" Abu Talhah was a skilled archer with a powerful draw; that day he broke two or three bows. A man would pass by carrying a quiver of arrows and say: "Empty it out for Abu Talhah." Whenever he shot, the Prophet ﷺ would raise himself to look at where his arrow landed. The hand of Talhah ibn Ubaydullah was struck and became paralyzed when he shielded the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with it. The eye of Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man was struck that day when it fell onto his cheek; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put it back in its place, and it became better than it had been.

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ withdrew, Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi caught up with him, saying: "I will not be saved if you are saved!" The people said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall one of us not turn against him?" He ﷺ said: "Leave him." When he came close to him, Ubayy had previously met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "I have a mare that I feed a farq of grain every day, and I will kill you on her." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Rather, I will kill you, if Allah wills." When he came close, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a spear from al-Harith ibn al-Simmah, then faced him and thrust it into his neck, scratching him slightly. He fell from his horse, bellowing like a bull, and saying: "Muhammad has killed me!" His companions took hold of him and said: "There is no harm for you." He said: "Yes indeed! If this blow had been dealt to Rabi'ah and Mudar, it would have killed them all. Did he not say to me, 'I will kill you'? If he had spat on me after that statement, he would have killed me." He did not survive more than a day before he died at a place called Sarif.

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Amr ibn Ali informed us: Abu Asim informed us, from Ibn Juraj, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The wrath of Allah intensified against the one who killed a prophet [70/b], and the wrath of Allah intensified against the one who drew blood from the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Maghazi, chapter "What the Prophet ﷺ suffered of wounds on the day of Uhud": 7/372.]]

They said: The rumour spread among the people that Muhammad had been killed. Some of the Muslims said: "If only we had a messenger to Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, who could obtain safe-conduct for us from Abu Sufyan." Some of the companions sat down and cast down their arms. Some people from among the hypocrites said: "If Muhammad has been killed, then return to your former religion." Anas ibn al-Nadr, the paternal uncle of Anas ibn Malik, said: "O people, if Muhammad has been killed, the Lord of Muhammad has not been killed. What good is life after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Fight for what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fought for, and die for what he died for." Then he said: "O Allah, I apologize to You for what these people say," meaning the Muslims, "and I disown what these have brought," meaning the hypocrites. Then he drew his sword, fought until he was killed.

Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the rock, calling the people. The first to recognize the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was Ka'b ibn Malik, who said: "I recognized his eyes beneath the helmet, shining. I called out at the top of my voice: 'O assembly of Muslims, rejoice! This is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!' He signalled to me to be silent. A group of his companions gathered to him.
