He returned to the polytheists and said: "I have killed Muhammad." A crier cried out: "Verily Muhammad has been killed." It is said that this crier was Iblis. The people then fled, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began calling out to the people: "To me, servants of Allah! ﴿To me, servants of Allah!﴾" [[Addition from (B).]] Thirty men gathered to him and protected him until they drove the polytheists away from him. Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas shot until the string of his bow snapped, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ handed him his quiver and said to him: "Shoot! May my father and mother be your ransom!" Abu Talhah was a skilled archer with a powerful draw; that day he broke two or three bows. A man would pass by carrying a quiver of arrows and say: "Empty it out for Abu Talhah." Whenever he shot, the Prophet ﷺ would raise himself to look at where his arrow landed. The hand of Talhah ibn Ubaydullah was struck and became paralyzed when he shielded the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with it. The eye of Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man was struck that day when it fell onto his cheek; the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put it back in its place, and it became better than it had been.

When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ withdrew, Ubayy ibn Khalaf al-Jumahi caught up with him, saying: "I will not be saved if you are saved!" The people said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall one of us not turn against him?" He ﷺ said: "Leave him." When he came close to him, Ubayy had previously met the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "I have a mare that I feed a farq of grain every day, and I will kill you on her." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Rather, I will kill you, if Allah wills." When he came close, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took a spear from al-Harith ibn al-Simmah, then faced him and thrust it into his neck, scratching him slightly. He fell from his horse, bellowing like a bull, and saying: "Muhammad has killed me!" His companions took hold of him and said: "There is no harm for you." He said: "Yes indeed! If this blow had been dealt to Rabi'ah and Mudar, it would have killed them all. Did he not say to me, 'I will kill you'? If he had spat on me after that statement, he would have killed me." He did not survive more than a day before he died at a place called Sarif.

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Amr ibn Ali informed us: Abu Asim informed us, from Ibn Juraj, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "The wrath of Allah intensified against the one who killed a prophet [70/b], and the wrath of Allah intensified against the one who drew blood from the face of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Maghazi, chapter "What the Prophet ﷺ suffered of wounds on the day of Uhud": 7/372.]]

They said: The rumour spread among the people that Muhammad had been killed. Some of the Muslims said: "If only we had a messenger to Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, who could obtain safe-conduct for us from Abu Sufyan." Some of the companions sat down and cast down their arms. Some people from among the hypocrites said: "If Muhammad has been killed, then return to your former religion." Anas ibn al-Nadr, the paternal uncle of Anas ibn Malik, said: "O people, if Muhammad has been killed, the Lord of Muhammad has not been killed. What good is life after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ? Fight for what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fought for, and die for what he died for." Then he said: "O Allah, I apologize to You for what these people say," meaning the Muslims, "and I disown what these have brought," meaning the hypocrites. Then he drew his sword, fought until he was killed.

Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to the rock, calling the people. The first to recognize the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was Ka'b ibn Malik, who said: "I recognized his eyes beneath the helmet, shining. I called out at the top of my voice: 'O assembly of Muslims, rejoice! This is the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!' He signalled to me to be silent. A group of his companions gathered to him. The Prophet ﷺ rebuked them for fleeing. They said: 'O Prophet of Allah, we ransom you with our fathers and mothers! News reached us that you had been killed, so our hearts were terrified and we turned and fled.' Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse [[Narrated by Ibn Ishaq in his Sirah through the route of Ja'far ibn Abd Allah ibn Aslam, mawla of Umar ibn al-Khattab, from a man of the Ansar from the Banu Salamah. See Sirat Ibn Hisham 2/127–132; also see al-Iktifa' of al-Kala'i 2/90 and what follows; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi p. 158; al-Kafi al-Shaf of Ibn Hajar pp. 32–33.]] ﴿And Muhammad is not but a messenger; messengers have passed on before him﴾.

Muhammad is the one who encompasses all praiseworthy qualities (al-mustaghriq li-jami' al-mahamid), because praise (hamd) is deserved only by the perfect, and tahmid (glorification with praise) surpasses hamd. Thus none deserves it except the one who holds sovereignty over perfection. Allah honoured His prophet and chosen one with two names derived from His own name, may His majesty be exalted: Muhammad and Ahmad. Concerning this Hassan ibn Thabit said:

"Did you not see that Allah sent His servant with His proof, while Allah is higher and more glorious?
And He split for him from His name, to honour him: the Lord of the Throne is Mahmud (praised), and this is Muhammad."

His words, exalted is He: ﴿So if he dies or is killed, will you turn back on your heels?﴾ means: will you return to your former religion? ﴿And whoever turns back on his heels﴾ means: will apostatize from his religion. ﴿He will not harm Allah at all﴾ by his apostasy; he only harms himself. ﴿And Allah will reward the grateful.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 3, verse 145:**

﴿It is not for any soul to die except by Allah's permission, at a decreed time.﴾ Al-Akhfash said: The lam in ﴿li-nafs﴾ (for a soul) is transposed (ma'quulah), its implied meaning being: "No soul was [such that it could] die..." (wa-ma kanat nafsun li-tamuta). ﴿Except by the permission of Allah﴾: by the decree of Allah and His destiny. It was also said: by His knowledge; and it was said: by His command. ﴿A decreed term (kitaban mu'ajjalan)﴾: that is, He has prescribed for every soul a term that no one can alter or postpone. The word ﴿kitaban﴾ is in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun, the infinitive-type noun), meaning: "He prescribed a prescription."

﴿And whoever desires the reward of this world, We will give him of it﴾: meaning, whoever desires the world by his obedience and works for it, We will give him from it what is the recompense for his deed. He wills that We give him from it what We will, according to what We have decreed for him, as He said: ﴿Whoever desires the hastening [world], We hasten for him therein what We will, for whom We wish﴾ [al-Isra: 18]. It was revealed concerning those who abandoned their position on the Day of Uhud, seeking the spoils of war. ﴿And whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter, We will give him of it﴾: that is, whoever intends the Hereafter by his action. It was said: this refers to those who remained steadfast with their commander, Abdullah ibn Jubayr, until they were killed.

﴿And We will reward the grateful﴾: that is, the believers who obey.

Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi informed us; Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Musa ibn al-Salt informed us; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us; Abu Yahya Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Yazid ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Muqri informed us; my father informed us; al-Rabi' ibn Subayh informed us, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever's intention is the pursuit of the Hereafter, Allah will place his self-sufficiency in his heart, gather his scattered affairs for him, and the world will come to him humbled. And whoever's intention is the pursuit of the world, Allah will place poverty before his eyes, scatter his affairs for him, and he will not obtain from it except what has been written for him."

[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Qiyamah, chapter no. (14): 7/165, and in it is Yazid al-Raqashi, who is weak. It has a corroborating narration with Ibn Majah from the hadith of Zayd ibn Thabit in al-Zuhd, chapter "Concern for the World," no. (4105): 2/1375; he said in al-Zawa'id: its chain is sound and its narrators are trustworthy. Also narrated by Ibn Hibban, no. (72), p. (47), from Mawarid al-Zam'an, and by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/183, at length, from Zayd ibn Thabit. The author also cited it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/331. Al-Haythami said: al-Bazzar narrated it, and in it is Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Makki, who is weak. Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10/247.]]

Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Tawbah al-Zarrad informed us; Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Idris ibn Muhammad al-Jurjani, and Abu Ahmad Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mu'allim al-Harawi, both said: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Isa al-Malini informed us; Abu al-Abbas al-Hasan ibn Sufyan al-Nasawi informed us; Hayyan ibn Musa and Abd Allah ibn Asma', son of the brother of Juwayriyah ibn Asma', informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Taymi, from Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi, from Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Actions are only by intentions, and every person will only have what he intended. So whoever's migration was to Allah and His Messenger, his migration is to Allah and His Messenger; and whoever's migration was for worldly gain he might obtain, or for a woman he might marry, his migration is to that for which he migrated."

[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in seven places in the Sahih: in Bad' al-Wahy, chapter "How the Beginning of Revelation Came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)": 1/9; and in Iman, in Itq, in Manaqib al-Ansar, in Nikah, in Iman and Nudhur, and in Hiyal. Also narrated by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on his saying (ﷺ): "Actions are only by intentions," no. (1907): 3/1515-1516.]]

The commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 146:

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿How many a prophet fought, and with him fought many devoted followers (ribbiyyun kathir)﴾. Ibn Kathir read "وَكَائِنٌ" (*wa ka'in*) with a long vowel and a hamza, on the pattern of *fa'il*. Abu Ja'far softened the hamza. The others read "وَكَأَيِّنْ" (*wa ka'ayyin*) with a hamza and a shaddah, on the pattern of *ka'ayyin*, and its meaning is "and how many." It is the *kaf* of comparison joined to the interrogative *ayy*. The tanwin has no written form in the orthography except in this word alone. Some readers pause on "وَكَأَيٍّ" (*wa ka'ayyin*) without a nun, while most pause with the nun.

His statement, "قَاتَلَ" (*qatala*, "fought"): Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and the people of Basra read it with a *damma* on the *qaf*, as "قُتِلَ" (*qutila*, "were killed"). The others read "قَاتَلَ" (*qatala*). Whoever reads "قَاتَلَ" (*qatala*) does so because of His statement, ﴿so they did not weaken﴾. It would be impossible to describe them as not weakening after they had been killed. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "We have not heard that a prophet was killed in battle." Also, "قَاتَلَ" (*qatala*) is more general.

Abu 'Ubayd said: When God praises those who fought, those who were killed are included in it. When He praises those who killed, no one other than them is included. So "قَاتَلَ" (*qatala*) is more general.

As for whoever reads "قُتِلَ" (*qutila*), it has three aspects:

First: the killing refers to the Prophet alone. The sentence is then complete at His statement "قُتِلَ" (*qutila*). In the verse there is an implied element, meaning: "and with him were many devoted followers," as one says, "So-and-so was killed, and with him was a large army," meaning "and with him."

The second aspect: the killing reached the Prophet and those with him from among the ribbiyyun. The intended meaning is some of those with him. The Arabs say, "We killed the Banu so-and-so," though only some of them were killed. His statement, ﴿so they did not weaken﴾, refers to those who remained.

The third aspect: the killing befell the ribbiyyun only.

His statement, ﴿ribbiyyun kathir﴾: Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: "Large groups." Ibn Mas'ud said: "The ribbiyyun are thousands." Al-Kalbi said: "A ribbiyyah is ten thousand." Al-Dahhak said: "A ribbiyyah is a thousand." Al-Hasan said: "Jurists and scholars." It is also said: they are the followers, while the rabbaniyyun are the rulers, and the ribbiyyun are the subjects. It is also said: it is derived from *rabb* (Lord), and they are those who worship the Lord.

﴿so they did not weaken﴾, meaning: they did not lose courage ﴿for what befell them in the way of God, nor did they weaken﴾ in the struggle because of the pain of wounds [[In manuscript "A": (al-jarh, "the wound")]] and the killing of their companions.

﴿nor did they submit﴾: Muqatil said: "Nor did they surrender, nor did they yield to their enemy." Al-Suddi said: "Wa ma dhallu" [71a]. 'Ata' said: "Nor did they humble themselves in supplication." Abu al-'Aliyah said: "Nor did they lose courage, but they were patient in obedience to their Lord, in obedience to their Prophet, and in struggle against their enemy." ﴿And God loves the patient﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 147–148:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And their words were not⁠﴾ is in the accusative as the predicate of kāna (was), and the subject is in "an qālū" (that they said). Its meaning: "And their words were not, at the time of the killing of their prophet," ﴿except that they said: "Our Lord, forgive us our sins"﴾, that is, the minor sins, ﴿"and our excesses in our affair"﴾, that is, the major sins, ﴿"and make firm our feet"﴾ so that they do not slip, ﴿"and help us against the disbelieving people."﴾ It is as if He says: "Why did you not do this and say such things, O companions of Muhammad?"

﴿So Allah gave them the reward of the world﴾, which is victory and spoils, ﴿and the good reward of the Hereafter﴾, which is the recompense and Paradise. ﴿And Allah loves the good-doers.﴾

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, if you obey those who disbelieve﴾ means: the Jews and the Christians. Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: it means the hypocrites, in their saying to the believers at the time of defeat: "Return to your brothers and enter into their religion."

﴿They will return you on your heels﴾ meaning, they will bring you back to your first state of associating partners with Allah, ﴿and you will turn back as losers﴾, meaning, defrauded.

Then He said: ﴿Rather, Allah is your Protector﴾, your Helper and the Guardian of your religion, ﴿and He is the best of helpers.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 149–152:

﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾. This was because Abu Sufyan and the polytheists, when they set off on the day of Uhud, heading toward Makkah, went on until they reached part of the way and then regretted it and said: "We did a wrong thing. We killed them until only the fugitives among them remained, and then we left them. Return and destroy them completely." But when they resolved upon that, Allah cast terror into their hearts, until they turned back from what they had intended.

Sanulqi (we shall cast): i.e., We shall throw into the hearts of those who disbelieved terror (al-ru'b), fear. Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read ﴿al-ru'ub﴾ with a damma on the ayn, while the others read it with a sukun on it. ﴿Because they associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority﴾: no proof or evidence. ﴿And their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers﴾: the abode of the disbelievers.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you﴾. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions returned to Madinah from Uhud, having suffered what they had suffered, some of his companions said: "From where has this afflicted us, when Allah promised us victory?" So Allah the Exalted revealed:

﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you﴾ with victory and triumph. This is because victory and triumph belonged to the Muslims at the beginning. ﴿When you were killing them by His permission﴾. This is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed Uhud behind his back, faced Madinah, and placed 'Aynayn (a mountain on his left) and stationed archers upon it, appointing over them 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr, and said to them: "Protect our rear. If you see us gaining the spoils, do not join us; and if you see us being killed, do not come to our aid." The polytheists advanced and began fighting, and the archers began shooting the polytheists' horses with arrows while the Muslims struck them with swords, until they turned and fled. This is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿When you were killing them by His permission﴾, i.e., you were killing them with a devastating slaughter by the decree of Allah.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-hass is annihilation by killing.

﴿Until when you lost heart﴾: i.e., if you became cowardly. It was also said: its meaning is "so when you lost heart." ﴿And disputed about the matter and disobeyed﴾. The waw in ﴿and disputed﴾ is extra; meaning: until when you lost heart, you disputed. It was also said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it, its sense being: until when you disputed about the matter and disobeyed, you lost heart. The meaning of tanazu' is disagreement.

Their disagreement was that when the polytheists were routed, the archers differed. Some of them said: "The people have been defeated, so what is the point of our staying here?" and they turned to the spoils. Others said: "Do not transgress the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr remained steadfast with a small group of fewer than ten.

When Khalid ibn al-Walid and 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl saw this, they charged at the archers and killed 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr and his companions, then turned upon the Muslims. The wind shifted, becoming dabur (the wind opposite to the saba) after it had been sabā [[al-Dabur: the wind that blows opposite the sabā; and al-Sabā: a wind that blows from the rising of the Pleiades.]], the Muslims' ranks were broken and they became mixed up, and they began killing one another without a battle-cry, striking each other without realizing it because of the confusion. Iblis cried out that Muhammad had been killed, and that was the cause of the Muslims' defeat.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And disobeyed﴾, i.e., the Messenger (ﷺ), and opposed his command. ﴿After He had shown you﴾ Allah ﴿what you love﴾, O assembly of Muslims, of victory and spoils. ﴿Among you are those who desire this world﴾, i.e., those who abandoned their post and turned to plunder. ﴿And among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾, i.e., those who remained steadfast with 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr until they were killed. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "I did not perceive that any of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) desired this world until the day of Uhud, when this verse was revealed." ﴿Then He turned you away from them﴾, i.e., He repelled you from them by defeat, ﴿to test you﴾, to try you. It was also said: so that He might send affliction upon you. ﴿And He had certainly pardoned you﴾, i.e., He did not destroy you after the disobedience and opposition. ﴿And Allah is full of bounty toward the believers.﴾

Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read ﴿al-ru'ub﴾ with a damma on the ayn, while the others read it with a sukun on it. ﴿Because they associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority﴾: no proof or evidence. ﴿And their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers﴾: the abode of the disbelievers.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you﴾. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions returned to Madinah from Uhud, having suffered what they had suffered, some of his companions said: "From where has this afflicted us, when Allah promised us victory?" So Allah the Exalted revealed:

﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you﴾ with victory and triumph. This is because victory and triumph belonged to the Muslims at the beginning. ﴿When you were killing them by His permission﴾. This is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed Uhud behind his back, faced Madinah, and placed 'Aynayn (a mountain on his left) and stationed archers upon it, appointing over them 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr, and said to them: "Protect our rear. If you see us gaining the spoils, do not join us; and if you see us being killed, do not come to our aid." The polytheists advanced and began fighting, and the archers began shooting the polytheists' horses with arrows while the Muslims struck them with swords, until they turned and fled. This is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿When you were killing them by His permission﴾, i.e., you were killing them with a devastating slaughter by the decree of Allah.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-hass is annihilation by killing.

﴿Until when you lost heart﴾: i.e., if you became cowardly. It was also said: its meaning is "so when you lost heart." ﴿And disputed about the matter and disobeyed﴾. The waw in ﴿and disputed﴾ is extra; meaning: until when you lost heart, you disputed. It was also said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it, its sense being: until when you disputed about the matter and disobeyed, you lost heart. The meaning of tanazu' is disagreement.

Their disagreement was that when the polytheists were routed, the archers differed. Some of them said: "The people have been defeated, so what is the point of our staying here?" and they turned to the spoils. Others said: "Do not transgress the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr remained steadfast with a small group of fewer than ten.

When Khalid ibn al-Walid and 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl saw this, they charged at the archers and killed 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr and his companions, then turned upon the Muslims. The wind shifted, becoming dabur (the wind opposite to the saba) after it had been sabā [[al-Dabur: the wind that blows opposite the sabā; and al-Sabā: a wind that blows from the rising of the Pleiades.]], the Muslims' ranks were broken and they became mixed up, and they began killing one another without a battle-cry, striking each other without realizing it because of the confusion. Iblis cried out that Muhammad had been killed, and that was the cause of the Muslims' defeat.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And disobeyed﴾, i.e., the Messenger (ﷺ), and opposed his command. ﴿After He had shown you﴾ Allah ﴿what you love﴾, O assembly of Muslims, of victory and spoils. ﴿Among you are those who desire this world﴾, i.e., those who abandoned their post and turned to plunder. ﴿And among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾, i.e., those who remained steadfast with 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr until they were killed. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "I did not perceive that any of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) desired this world until the day of Uhud, when this verse was revealed." ﴿Then He turned you away from them﴾, i.e., He repelled you from them by defeat, ﴿to test you﴾, to try you. It was also said: so that He might send affliction upon you. ﴿And He had certainly pardoned you﴾, i.e., He did not destroy you after the disobedience and opposition. ﴿And Allah is full of bounty toward the believers.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 149–152:

﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾. This was because Abu Sufyan and the polytheists, when they set off on the day of Uhud, heading toward Makkah, went on until they reached part of the way and then regretted it and said: "We did a wrong thing. We killed them until only the fugitives among them remained, and then we left them. Return and destroy them completely." But when they resolved upon that, Allah cast terror into their hearts, until they turned back from what they had intended.

Sanulqi (we shall cast): i.e., We shall throw into the hearts of those who disbelieved terror (al-ru'b), fear. Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read ﴿al-ru'ub﴾ with a damma on the ayn, while the others read it with a sukun on it. ﴿Because they associated with Allah that for which He had sent down no authority﴾: no proof or evidence. ﴿And their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers﴾: the abode of the disbelievers.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you﴾. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions returned to Madinah from Uhud, having suffered what they had suffered, some of his companions said: "From where has this afflicted us, when Allah promised us victory?" So Allah the Exalted revealed:

﴿And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you﴾ with victory and triumph. This is because victory and triumph belonged to the Muslims at the beginning. ﴿When you were killing them by His permission﴾. This is because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed Uhud behind his back, faced Madinah, and placed 'Aynayn (a mountain on his left) and stationed archers upon it, appointing over them 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr, and said to them: "Protect our rear. If you see us gaining the spoils, do not join us; and if you see us being killed, do not come to our aid." The polytheists advanced and began fighting, and the archers began shooting the polytheists' horses with arrows while the Muslims struck them with swords, until they turned and fled. This is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿When you were killing them by His permission﴾, i.e., you were killing them with a devastating slaughter by the decree of Allah.

Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-hass is annihilation by killing.

﴿Until when you lost heart﴾: i.e., if you became cowardly. It was also said: its meaning is "so when you lost heart." ﴿And disputed about the matter and disobeyed﴾. The waw in ﴿and disputed﴾ is extra; meaning: until when you lost heart, you disputed. It was also said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it, its sense being: until when you disputed about the matter and disobeyed, you lost heart. The meaning of tanazu' is disagreement.

Their disagreement was that when the polytheists were routed, the archers differed. Some of them said: "The people have been defeated, so what is the point of our staying here?" and they turned to the spoils. Others said: "Do not transgress the command of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr remained steadfast with a small group of fewer than ten.

When Khalid ibn al-Walid and 'Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl saw this, they charged at the archers and killed 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr and his companions, then turned upon the Muslims. The wind shifted, becoming dabur (the wind opposite to the saba) after it had been sabā [[al-Dabur: the wind that blows opposite the sabā; and al-Sabā: a wind that blows from the rising of the Pleiades.]], the Muslims' ranks were broken and they became mixed up, and they began killing one another without a battle-cry, striking each other without realizing it because of the confusion. Iblis cried out that Muhammad had been killed, and that was the cause of the Muslims' defeat.

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And disobeyed﴾, i.e., the Messenger (ﷺ), and opposed his command. ﴿After He had shown you﴾ Allah ﴿what you love﴾, O assembly of Muslims, of victory and spoils. ﴿Among you are those who desire this world﴾, i.e., those who abandoned their post and turned to plunder. ﴿And among you are those who desire the Hereafter﴾, i.e., those who remained steadfast with 'Abdullah ibn Jubayr until they were killed. 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said: "I did not perceive that any of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) desired this world until the day of Uhud, when this verse was revealed." ﴿Then He turned you away from them﴾, i.e., He repelled you from them by defeat, ﴿to test you﴾, to try you. It was also said: so that He might send affliction upon you. ﴿And He had certainly pardoned you﴾, i.e., He did not destroy you after the disobedience and opposition. ﴿And Allah is full of bounty toward the believers.﴾

﴿Idh tus'idūn﴾ means: Allah had already pardoned you when you were fleeing, going off [in the direction of the flat ground]. Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, al-Hasan and Qatada recited ﴿tasʿadūn﴾ with a fatha on the ta' and on the 'ayn. The well-known reading is with a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the 'ayn.

Al-ʾisʿad (going off across level ground) and al-ṣuʿūd (climbing up mountains and elevated places). Abu Hatim said: one says "asʿadta" when you continue straight ahead in the direction you are facing, and "saʿidta" when you climb up a mountain or something else. Al-Mubarrad said: "asʿada" means to go far away in departing. Both readings are correct, for on that day some of the defeated were "muṣʿid" (going off across level ground) and some were "ṣāʿid" (climbing). Al-Mufaddal said: ṣaʿida, aṣʿada and ṣaʿʿada have the same meaning.

﴿Wa lā talwūna ʿalā aḥad﴾ means: you did not turn aside, nor did you stay for anyone, and some of you did not turn toward others. ﴿Wa al-rasūl yadʿūkum fī ukhrākum﴾ means: in your rear, and from behind you, the Messenger was calling you toward the servants of Allah: "I am the Messenger of Allah; whoever turns back will have Paradise." [[Recorded by al-Tabari in his History: 2/519–520; see also al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya: 4/23.]] ﴿Fa-athābakum﴾ means: He rewarded you. He treated the recompense (ithāba) as a punishment ('iqāb), though its original use is for good deeds, because He placed it in the position of reward, as in His saying, ﴿fa-bashshirhum bi-ʿadhābin alīm﴾ ("give them the good news of a painful punishment"), where He made the "good news" apply to punishment. Its meaning is: He put in place of the reward you were hoping for [[.]] ﴿Ghaman bi-ghamm﴾. It has been said: the bāʾ means "upon", i.e., grief upon grief. It has also been said: grief joined to grief. The first grief was what escaped them of victory and spoils, and the second grief was what befell them of killing and defeat.

It has been said: the first grief was what befell them of killing and wounds, and the second grief was what they heard, that Muhammad (ﷺ) had been killed, and this made them forget the first grief.

It has also been said: the first grief was Khalid ibn al-Walid's appearance above them with the cavalry of the polytheists, and the second grief was when Abu Sufyan came up over them. That was because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out that day calling the people, until he reached the companions of the rock (Ashab al-Sakhra). When they saw him, a man placed an arrow in his bow and wanted to shoot him, but [the Prophet] said, "I am the Messenger of Allah." They rejoiced at finding the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) rejoiced when he saw that among his companions there were those who could hold their ground. Then they began to recall the victory and what they had missed of it, and to mention their companions who had been killed. Abu Sufyan and his companions came until they stopped at the entrance of the mountain pass (Shiʿb). When the Muslims looked at them, this troubled them, and they thought that [the enemy] would come down upon them and kill them, so this made them forget what had befallen them. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "They must not be allowed to get above us. O Allah, if You let this band be killed, You will not be worshipped on earth." Then he urged his companions, and they pelted them with stones until they brought them down.

It has also been said: they grieved the Messenger by disobeying his command, so Allah rewarded them with that grief, the grief of killing and defeat.

His saying, ﴿li-kaylā taḥzanū ʿalā mā fātakum﴾ means: so that you would not grieve over what escaped you of victory and spoils, ﴿wa lā mā aṣābakum﴾, meaning: nor over what befell you of killing and defeat. ﴿Wa Allāhu khabīrun bi-mā taʿmalūn﴾ means: and Allah is All-Aware of what you do.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 154:

﴿Then He sent down upon you﴾, O company of Muslims, ﴿after the distress, security, a slumber﴾. It means: security. The words amn (security) and amanah (security) have one meaning. It is also said that amn occurs when the cause of fear has been removed, while amanah occurs when the cause of fear remains, and the cause of fear was still present here. ﴿A slumber﴾ is a substitute (badal) for amanah. ﴿It overcame a group of you﴾. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read "taghsha" with the feminine ta', referring it back to amanah. The others read "yaghsha" with the masculine ya', referring it back to al-nu'as (slumber).

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "On that day He gave them security by a slumber that covered them, for only one who feels secure falls asleep, while the one who is afraid does not sleep."

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman informed us, saying: Husayn ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Shaybān informed us, from Qatadah, who said: Anas informed us that Abu Talhah said: "Slumber overcame us while we were in our battle lines on the day of Uhud." He said: "My sword kept falling from my hand, so I would pick it up, and it would fall, and I would pick it up again."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tafsir, the chapter on His saying, "Security, a slumber" (8/228), and in the Book of Maghazi (military expeditions). The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah (13/392).]]

And Thabit said, from Anas, from Abu Talhah, who said: "I raised my head on the day of Uhud, and I saw no one among the people but that he was swaying beneath his helmet from slumber."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Tafsir, Surah Al 'Imran (8/358), and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Al-Hakim authenticated it according to the conditions of Muslim (2/297), and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. Ibn Hajar (in Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi) attributed it to al-Nasa'i.]]

And Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr said, from his father al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam: "I saw myself with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when the fighting grew fierce against us, and Allah sent sleep upon us. By Allah, I was hearing the words of Mu'attib ibn Qushayr while slumber was covering me; I heard them only as in a dream. He was saying: 'If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here.'"[[Narrated by Ibn Ishaq in the Maghazi, and by al-Bazzar in his Musnad, al-Tabari, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nu'aym, and al-Bayhaqi, all through the chain of Ibn Ishaq. See al-Kafi al-Shafi, p. 33.]] Concerning this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It overcame a group of you﴾, meaning the believers. ﴿And another group, whose own selves had made them anxious﴾, meaning the hypocrites. It is said: Allah intended by this to distinguish the hypocrites from the believers. He caused slumber to fall upon the believers until they felt secure, and He did not cause it to fall upon the hypocrites, so they remained in fear, and their own selves had made them anxious, that is, their selves had driven them to worry. It is said: "amr muhimm" (a grave matter).

﴿They think about Allah other than the truth﴾, that is, that He would not help Muhammad. It is also said: they thought that Muhammad (ﷺ) had been killed. ﴿The thought of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance)﴾, that is, like the thought of the people of ignorance and polytheism. ﴿They say, "Is there anything for us in the affair?"﴾ The wording is a question, but its meaning is a denial. ﴿Any thing in the affair﴾, meaning victory. ﴿Say: "Indeed the affair is entirely for Allah."﴾ The people of Basra read "kulluhu" (all of it) with a raised lam, as a subject (mubtada'), with its predicate in "lillah" (for Allah). The others read it with a fatha (nasb), as an apposition (badal). It is also said it is an adjective (na't).

﴿They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you. They say, "If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here."﴾ This is because some of the hypocrites said to others: "If we had sense, we would not have gone out with Muhammad to fight the people of Makkah, and our leaders would not have been killed." It is also said: "If we had been upon the truth, we would not have been killed here."

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: ﴿They think about Allah other than the truth﴾, the thought of the Jahiliyyah, meaning denial of the qadar (divine decree), and this is their saying: ﴿If we had any say in the matter, we would not have been killed here.﴾

﴿Say: "Even if you had been in your houses, those destined to be killed would have gone out to their places of death."﴾ "Kutiba" means decreed. ﴿Upon them the killing, to their resting places﴾ means their places of falling. ﴿And that Allah might test﴾ means that Allah might examine ﴿what is in your breasts, and that He might purify﴾, meaning bring out and make apparent ﴿what is in your hearts. And Allah is Knowing of what is in the breasts﴾, that is, of what is in the hearts of good and evil.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 155:

﴿Indeed, those of you who turned away﴾, i.e., fled in defeat, ﴿of you﴾, O company of Muslims, ﴿on the day the two hosts met﴾, the host of the Muslims and the host of the polytheists, on the day of Uhud. Most of the Muslims had fled, and there remained with the Prophet (ﷺ) only thirteen men: six from the Muhajirun, namely Abu Bakr, Umar, Ali, Talhah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with them.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿It was only Satan who caused them to slip﴾, i.e., he sought their slip, as one says, "I hastened so-and-so" when you sought his haste. It was said: he drove them to the slip, which is the sin. It was also said: "azalla" and "istazalla" have one meaning. ﴿Because of some of what they had earned﴾, i.e., because of the evil consequences of their sins. Some of them said: by their abandonment of the position. Al-Hasan said: "what they had earned" is their acceptance from Satan of what he whispered to them of the defeat. ﴿And Allah has certainly pardoned them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing﴾.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 3, verses 156–159:**

﴿O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: the hypocrites, 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions, ﴿and who say of their brothers﴾ in hypocrisy and disbelief. It was said: (their brothers) in lineage. ﴿When they travel through the earth﴾, that is, they journey through it for trade or other purposes, ﴿or are raiders﴾, that is, warriors, the plural of *ghazin* (ghāzin), ﴿and they die or are killed﴾, ﴿[saying]: "Had they remained with us, they would not have died or been killed," so that Allah may make that﴾, meaning their saying and their assumption, ﴿a regret﴾, a grief ﴿in their hearts. And Allah gives life and causes death, and Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾. Ibn Kathir, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *ya'malūna* (يَعْمَلُونَ) with the *yā'* (i.e., "they do"), while the others read it with the *tā'* (i.e., "you do").

﴿And if you are killed in the way of Allah or die﴾. Nafi', Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *mittum* (مِتُّمْ) with a *kasrah* on the *mīm*, while the others read it with a *ḍammah*. Whoever reads it with a *ḍammah* takes it from *māta yamūtu* (مَاتَ يَمُوتُ), as in your saying *min qāla yaqūlu, qultu* (مِنْ قَالَ يَقُولُ قُلْتُ) with a *ḍammah* on the *qāf*. Whoever reads it with a *kasrah* takes it from *māta yamātu* (مَاتَ يَمَاتُ), as in your saying *min khāfa yakhāfu, khiftu* (مِنْ خَافَ يَخَافُ خِفْتُ). ﴿Surely forgiveness from Allah﴾ in the outcome, ﴿and mercy are better than what they gather﴾ of the spoils. The common reading is *taǧma'ūna* (تَجْمَعُونَ) with a *tā'*, in accordance with His saying ﴿And if you are killed﴾. Ḥafs, from 'Āṣim, read *yaǧma'ūna* (يَجْمَعُونَ) with a *yā'*, meaning: "better than what people gather."

﴿And if you die or are killed, surely to Allah you will be gathered﴾ in the outcome.

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So by mercy from Allah﴾, that is, *fa-bi-raḥmatin min Allāh* (فَبِرَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ), and *mā* (مَا) is a *ṣilah* (an extra particle), as in His saying ﴿so for their breaking [of the covenant]﴾ (*fa-bimā naqḍihim*).

﴿You were gentle with them﴾, that is, your character was easy toward them and you bore much, and you did not hasten against them over what they did on the day of Uhud. ﴿Had you been harsh﴾, meaning: rough, bad-tempered, of little forbearance, ﴿hard of heart﴾. al-Kalbi said: harsh in speech and hard of heart in action. ﴿They would have dispersed from around you﴾, that is, they would have fled and scattered from you. It is said: *faḍaḍtuhum fa-infaḍḍū* (فَضَضْتُهُمْ فَانْفَضُّوا), meaning: I scattered them, so they scattered. ﴿So pardon them﴾, overlook what they did on the day of Uhud. ﴿And ask forgiveness for them﴾, until I intercede for them. ﴿And consult them in the matter﴾, that is: draw out their opinions and know what they have, from the Arabic saying: *shurtu al-dābbata wa-shawwartuhā* (شُرْتُ الدَّابَّةَ وَشَوَّرْتُهَا) when I draw out its running, and *shurtu al-‘asala wa-ashartuhu* (شُرْتُ الْعَسَلَ وَأَشَرْتُهُ) when I take it from its place and extract it.

Scholars differed about the reason for which Allah commanded His Prophet ﷺ to consult (them), despite his perfect intellect, the soundness of his judgment, the revelation descending upon him, and the obligation upon creation to obey him in what they love and dislike.

Some said: it is specific in meaning, that is: consult them concerning matters on which you have no command from Allah, the Exalted. al-Kalbi said: that is, discuss with them the meeting of the enemy and the stratagems of war during the raid.

Muqatil and Qatadah said: Allah, the Exalted, commanded consulting them in order to win their hearts, for that is more inclining of them toward him and more removing of their resentments, since the chiefs of the Arabs, when they were not consulted in a matter, were burdened by that.

al-Hasan said: Allah, the Exalted, knew that He had no need of their consultation, but He wanted those after him to follow his example (*an yastanna bihi man ba‘dahu*).

Abu Tahir al-Mutahhar ibn 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah al-Fariski informed us: Abu Dharr Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn 'Ali al-Salihani informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Hayyan informed us: 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas al-Muqani'i informed us: Ahmad ibn Ma-han informed us: my father informed me: Talhah ibn Zayd informed us, from 'Uqayl, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "I have not seen anyone who consulted men more than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi from Abu Hurayrah, in the chapter on jihad, "What has come concerning consultation": 5/373–374. He said: "It is related from Abu Hurayrah: I have not seen anyone..." The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 13/188, and in its chain is Talhah ibn Zayd al-Qurashi, Abu Miskin or Abu Muhammad al-Raqqi, originally from Damascus; he is abandoned (matruk). Ahmad, 'Ali and Abu Dawud said: he used to fabricate hadith. See al-Taqrib: 1/378. Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shafi, p. 33: al-Shafi'i narrated it (2/177 in the arrangement of the Musnad) from Ibn 'Uyaynah, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Hurayrah, and it is disconnected (munqati'), and it is an abridgment of the long hadith on the story of al-Hudaybiyah and the conquest. Ibn Hibban narrated it from the transmission of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from 'Umar, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from al-Miswar and Marwan...]]

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So when you have resolved, then rely upon Allah﴾, not upon their consultation, that is: carry out the command of Allah, trust in Him, and seek His help. ﴿Surely Allah loves those who rely (upon Him)﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 160:

﴿If Allah helps you, none can overcome you﴾: Allah aids you and protects you from your enemy. ﴿So none can overcome you﴾ like the Day of Badr. ﴿And if He forsakes you﴾: He leaves you, so He does not help you as on the day of Uhud. Al-khidhlan (forsaking) is refraining from giving support, and Islam being left to destruction. ﴿Who, then, can help you after Him?﴾ That is, after His forsaking. ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾. It was said: tawakkul (reliance upon Allah) is that you do not disobey Allah for the sake of your provision. It was also said: it is that you do not seek for yourself any helper other than Allah, nor any treasurer of your provision other than Him, nor any witness of your deeds other than Him.

Abu al-Qasim Abd al-Karim ibn Hawazin al-Qushayri informed us: Abu Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Shuja al-Bazzar in Baghdad informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Haytham al-Anbari informed us: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Awwam informed us: Wahb ibn Jarir informed us: Hisham ibn Hassan informed us, from al-Hasan, from Imran ibn Husayn (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Seventy thousand of my nation will enter Paradise without reckoning." It was asked: "O Messenger of Allah, who are they?" He said: "They are those who do not seek cauterization, nor seek incantation, nor believe in omens, and upon their Lord they rely." Thereupon Ukashah ibn Mihsan said: "O Messenger of Allah, invoke Allah that He make me one of them." He said: "You are one of them." Then another man stood and said: "O Messenger of Allah, invoke Allah that He make me one of them." He said: "Ukashah has preceded you with it." [[Recorded by Muslim in al-Iman, chapter on the evidence that groups of Muslims will enter Paradise without reckoning or punishment, no. (371): 1/198. With a similar wording, it is recorded by al-Bukhari in al-Tibb, chapter on one who has cauterized himself or had another cauterize him: 10/155. It is also recorded from Ibn Abbas in al-Riqaq. The author recorded it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/300.]]

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Tawba informed us: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Harith informed us: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kisa'i informed us: Abd Allah ibn Mahmud informed us: Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah al-Khallal informed us: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak informed me, from Hayat ibn Shurayh, who narrated to me: Bakr ibn Amr, from Abd Allah ibn Hubayra, that he heard Abu Tamim al-Jayshani say: I heard Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "If you truly relied upon Allah with the reliance due to Him, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out hungry in the morning and return full in the evening." [[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi in al-Zuhd, chapter on what has come concerning asceticism in this world: 7/8, and he said: this is a hadith hasan sahih, which we do not know except through this route.
