**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 161:**

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate (ghulul)...﴾ [the verse]. 'Ikrimah and Miqsam narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that this verse was revealed concerning a red woolen cloak (qatifah hamra') that went missing on the day of Badr. Some people said, "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took it." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud at the beginning of Kitab al-Huruf: 6/3 in the abridgment of al-Mundhiri, and by al-Tirmidhi in the tafsir of Surah Al 'Imran: 8/359, where he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith. 'Abd al-Salam ibn Harb narrated something similar from Khusayf, but some narrated this hadith from Khusayf from Miqsam... and did not mention Ibn 'Abbas." It was also narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir: 7/348-349. Al-Mundhiri said in his abridgment of Sunan Abi Dawud: "In its chain is Khusayf, who is Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Harrani, and more than one scholar has spoken about him."]]

Al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning the spoils of Uhud, when the archers left their position (al-markaz) for the booty. They said: "We fear that the Prophet (ﷺ) will say, 'Whoever takes something, it is his,' and that he will not distribute the spoils, as he did not distribute them on the day of Badr." So they left their position and fell upon the spoils. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "Did I not charge you not to leave your position until my command reaches you?" They said: "We left the rest of our brothers standing." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Rather, you thought that we would misappropriate and not distribute to you." Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse. [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul by al-Wahidi, p. 161, second edition.]]

Qatadah said: "It has been mentioned to us that it was revealed concerning a group from among his companions who misappropriated (ghallat)." [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul p. 161; Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/353.]]

It is also said: The powerful among them pressed him, asking him for a share of the booty, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾, meaning that he gives to some people and withholds from others; rather, it is incumbent upon him to distribute it among them equally. [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/351; al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/363.]]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said: "This refers to revelation. It means: It is not for a prophet to conceal anything of the revelation, out of desire, fear, or flattery."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is not for a prophet to misappropriate﴾. Ibn Kathir, the people of Basra, and 'Asim read "يَغُلَّ" (yaghull) with a fatha on the ya' and a damma on the ghayn. Its meaning is: to betray. The intended meaning is the community (ummah). It is also said that the lam in it is transferred, meaning: "The Prophet would not misappropriate." It is also said that its meaning is: it is not conceivable of him and not befitting to him. The others read "يُغَلَّ" (yughalla) with a damma on the ya' and a fatha on the ghayn, and it has two aspects. The first: that it is also from ghulul, meaning: it is not for a prophet to be betrayed, i.e., that his community betray him. The second aspect: that it is from al-ighlal, meaning: it is not for a prophet to betray, i.e., to be attributed with betrayal.

﴿And whoever misappropriates will come with what he misappropriated on the Day of Resurrection﴾. Al-Kalbi said: That thing will be made to appear to him in the Fire, and then it will be said to him: "Descend and take it." So he descends and carries it on his back. When he reaches its place, it falls into the Fire, and then he is commanded to descend to it and bring it out. And that is what is done to him.

Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us; Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Faqih informed us; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us; Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Thawr ibn Zayd al-Dili, from Abu al-Ghayth, client of Ibn Mutei', from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the year of Khaybar. We did not acquire gold or silver, only goods, clothing, and provisions." He said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then headed toward Wadi al-Qura. Rifa'ah ibn Zayd had given the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a black slave called Mid'am." He said: "We set out until, when we were at Wadi al-Qura, while Mid'am was unloading the saddle of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a stray arrow came to him, struck him, and killed him. The people said: 'Good tidings to him, Paradise!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'No! By Him in whose hand is my soul, the cloak that he took on the day of Khaybar from the spoils, which had not yet been distributed, is burning upon him with fire.' When the people heard that, a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with one or two thongs (of a sandal) and said: 'A thong of fire, or two thongs of fire.'" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Iman wa'l-Nudhur, chapter "Does the earth and the sheep enter into the oath and vow..." 11/593; and by Muslim in Kitab al-Iman, chapter on the severity of the prohibition of ghulul and that none enters Paradise except believers, no. 115: 1/108. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/116.]]

Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us; Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi informed us; Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hayyan, from Abu 'Amrah al-Ansari, from Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, who said: "A man died on the day of Khaybar, and they mentioned him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: 'Pray over your companion.' The faces of the people changed because of that. Zayd claimed that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, your companion has misappropriated in the way of Allah.'" He said: "We opened his belongings and found some beads from the beads of the Jews, worth two dirhams." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Jihad, chapter on the severity of ghulul: 4/38; al-Nasa'i in Kitab al-Jana'iz, chapter on praying over one who misappropriated: 4/64; Ibn Majah in Kitab al-Jihad, chapter on ghulul, no. 2848: 2/950; Malik in al-Muwatta': 2/458; and Ahmad: 4/114 and 5/192. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 11/117.]]

'Abd al-Wahhab ibn Muhammad al-Khatib al-Marwazi informed us; 'Abd al-Aziz ibn Ahmad al-Khallal informed us; Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm informed us; al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman informed us; al-Shafi'i informed us; Sufyan informed us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) appointed a man of the Azd called Ibn al-Lutbiyyah over the zakat. When he came back, he said: 'This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift.' So the Prophet (ﷺ) stood upon the pulpit and said: 'What is the matter with the official whom we send on one of our tasks, and he says: "This is for you, and this was given to me as a gift." Why did he not sit in the house of his mother or the house of his father, and see whether a gift would be given to him or not? By Him in whose hand is my soul, none of you takes anything from it except that he will come with it on the Day of Resurrection, carrying it on his neck: if it is a camel, it will be bellowing; if it is a cow, it will be lowing; if it is a sheep, it will be bleating.'" Then he raised his hands until we saw the whiteness of his armpits, and then said: "O Allah, have I conveyed?" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Kitab al-Hibah, chapter on one who does not accept a gift for a reason: 5/220, and in the chapters on Friday, on tricks, on zakat, and on oaths and vows; and by Muslim in Kitab al-Imarah, chapter on the prohibition of gifts to officials, no. 1832: 4/1463-1464. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 5/496-497.]]

Qays ibn Abi Hazim narrated from Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to Yemen and said: 'Do not take anything without my permission, for that is ghulul. And whoever misappropriates will come with what he misappropriated on the Day of Resurrection.'" [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in Kitab al-Ahkam, chapter on what has come concerning the gifts of rulers: 4/564, and said: "The hadith of Mu'adh is gharib; we do not know it except through this route, from the hadith of Abu Usamah from Dawud al-Awdi. Dawud ibn Yazid al-Awdi is weak (Taqrib: 1/235)."]]

It was narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "If you find a man who has misappropriated, burn his belongings and beat him." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Jihad, chapter on the punishment of the one who misappropriates: 4/39-40; and al-Tirmidhi in Kitab al-Hudud, chapter on what has come concerning the one who misappropriates and what is done to him: 5/29, and said: "This is a gharib hadith; we do not know it except through this route. I asked Muhammad about this hadith, and he said: 'It is only narrated by Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Za'idah, who is Abu Waqid al-Laythi, and he is munkar al-hadith.' Muhammad said: 'It has been narrated in more than one hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning the one who misappropriates, and in it he did not order that his belongings be burned.'" It was also narrated by al-Darimi in Kitab al-Siyar, chapter on the punishment of the one who misappropriates: 2/231, with the wording: "Whoever you find has misappropriated, beat him and burn his belongings." Al-Hakim authenticated it in al-Mustadrak: 2/128, and al-Dhahabi agreed, saying: "Sahih." It was also narrated by Sa'id ibn Mansur in al-Sunan: 2/269. Al-Mundhiri said in Tahdhib al-Sunan: 4/40: "Salih ibn Muhammad ibn Za'idah has been criticized by more than one of the imams, and it has been said that he narrated it alone." Al-Bukhari said: "Most of our companions argue with this regarding ghulul, and this is false, nothing." Al-Daraqutni said: "They rejected this hadith from Salih ibn Muhammad. He said: 'This hadith has no follower, and there is no basis for this hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). What is preserved is that Salim ordered that, and Abu Dawud authenticated its being a statement of a companion (mawquf).'"]]

It was narrated from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, may Allah be pleased with him: "That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), Abu Bakr, and 'Umar burned the belongings of the one who misappropriated and beat him." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in Kitab al-Jihad, chapter on the punishment of the one who misappropriates: 4/41. He said: "'Ali ibn Bahr added from al-Walid, but I did not hear it from him: 'And they withheld his share.'" Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The defect of this hadith is that it is from the narration of Zuhayr ibn Muhammad from 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, and this Zuhayr is weak." Al-Bayhaqi said: "This Zuhayr is said to be unknown, and he is not the Meccan one. It has also been narrated as mursal." It was narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/131, and he said: "A gharib sahih hadith, but they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi said the same. Al-Shawkani said: "It was also narrated by al-Hakim and al-Bayhaqi, and in its chain is Zuhayr ibn Muhammad, who is al-Khurasani, resident of Mecca. Al-Bayhaqi said: 'It is said he is someone else, and that he is unknown. Abu Dawud also narrated it through another route from Zuhayr as mawquf.' In al-Fath, it says: 'This is the preferred view.'" See: Nayl al-Awtar: 9/226.]]

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever misappropriates will come with what he misappropriated on the Day of Resurrection; then every soul will be paid in full what it earned, and they will not be wronged﴾.

Al-Baghawi, Ma'alim al-Tanzil (Commentary on surah 3, verses 162–163):

﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah﴾ and abandons embezzlement (ghulul), ﴿like one who has drawn upon himself anger from Allah﴾ by committing it, ﴿and his refuge is Hell, and what an evil destination﴾.

﴿They are of varying degrees with Allah﴾: meaning, they are of different ranks (darajat) with Allah. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: meaning, those who follow the pleasure of Allah and those who have drawn upon themselves anger from Allah are of differing stations with Allah. For those who follow the pleasure of Allah is the great reward, and for those who have drawn upon themselves anger from Allah is the painful punishment.

﴿And Allah is All-Seeing of what they do﴾.

Al-Baghawi, Ma'alim al-Tanzil (Commentary on surah 3, verses 162–163):

﴿Is one who follows the pleasure of Allah﴾ and abandons embezzlement (ghulul), ﴿like one who has drawn upon himself anger from Allah﴾ by committing it, ﴿and his refuge is Hell, and what an evil destination﴾.

﴿They are of varying degrees with Allah﴾: meaning, they are of different ranks (darajat) with Allah. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: meaning, those who follow the pleasure of Allah and those who have drawn upon themselves anger from Allah are of differing stations with Allah. For those who follow the pleasure of Allah is the great reward, and for those who have drawn upon themselves anger from Allah is the painful punishment.

﴿And Allah is All-Seeing of what they do﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 164–165:

﴿Indeed, Allah conferred a favour upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves﴾. It has been said: by this He meant the Arabs, because there is no tribe of the Arabs but that the Prophet has a lineage among them, except Banu Ta'laba. The evidence for this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered (ummiyyin) a Messenger from among them﴾. Others said: by this He meant all the believers. The meaning of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿from among themselves﴾ is: through faith and compassion, not through lineage. The evidence for this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾ ﴿who recites to them His verses, purifies them, and teaches them the Book and wisdom﴾. Indeed, they had been, ﴿before﴾, that is, before his being sent, ﴿in clear error﴾.

﴿Why, when﴾, that is, when ﴿a calamity struck you﴾ at Uhud, ﴿although you had inflicted twice as much﴾ at Badr. That is because the polytheists killed seventy of the Muslims on the day of Uhud, and the Muslims had killed seventy of them at Badr and taken seventy captive. ﴿You said: "From where is this?"﴾, that is: from where is this killing and defeat for us, when we are Muslims and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is among us? ﴿Say: "It is from yourselves"﴾. Ubaydah al-Salmani narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Indeed Allah has disliked what your people did in taking ransom from the captives. He has commanded you to offer them a choice between being brought forward to have their necks struck, or taking ransom on condition that an equal number of them will be killed." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned that to the people, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are our clans and our brothers. No, rather we will take their ransom and gain strength thereby against our enemy, and an equal number of us will be martyred." So seventy of them were killed at Uhud, equal to the number of the captives of the people of Badr. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "It is from yourselves"﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 7/367, and Ibn Hibban in abridged form in Mawarid al-Zam'an, p. 411. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir and said: "Thus it was narrated by al-Nasa'i and al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Hafari, from Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'ida. Abu Usama narrated from Hisham something similar, and it is narrated from Ibn Sirin, from Ubayda, from the Prophet ﷺ." See Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/426; Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 5/188.]], that is: by your taking the ransom and your choosing to be killed. ﴿Indeed Allah is over all things competent﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 164–165:

﴿Indeed, Allah conferred a favour upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from among themselves﴾. It has been said: by this He meant the Arabs, because there is no tribe of the Arabs but that the Prophet has a lineage among them, except Banu Ta'laba. The evidence for this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who sent among the unlettered (ummiyyin) a Messenger from among them﴾. Others said: by this He meant all the believers. The meaning of His saying, exalted is He, ﴿from among themselves﴾ is: through faith and compassion, not through lineage. The evidence for this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves﴾ ﴿who recites to them His verses, purifies them, and teaches them the Book and wisdom﴾. Indeed, they had been, ﴿before﴾, that is, before his being sent, ﴿in clear error﴾.

﴿Why, when﴾, that is, when ﴿a calamity struck you﴾ at Uhud, ﴿although you had inflicted twice as much﴾ at Badr. That is because the polytheists killed seventy of the Muslims on the day of Uhud, and the Muslims had killed seventy of them at Badr and taken seventy captive. ﴿You said: "From where is this?"﴾, that is: from where is this killing and defeat for us, when we are Muslims and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is among us? ﴿Say: "It is from yourselves"﴾. Ubaydah al-Salmani narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "Indeed Allah has disliked what your people did in taking ransom from the captives. He has commanded you to offer them a choice between being brought forward to have their necks struck, or taking ransom on condition that an equal number of them will be killed." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned that to the people, and they said: "O Messenger of Allah, they are our clans and our brothers. No, rather we will take their ransom and gain strength thereby against our enemy, and an equal number of us will be martyred." So seventy of them were killed at Uhud, equal to the number of the captives of the people of Badr. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "It is from yourselves"﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 7/367, and Ibn Hibban in abridged form in Mawarid al-Zam'an, p. 411. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir and said: "Thus it was narrated by al-Nasa'i and al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Hafari, from Yahya ibn Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'ida. Abu Usama narrated from Hisham something similar, and it is narrated from Ibn Sirin, from Ubayda, from the Prophet ﷺ." See Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/426; Tuhfat al-Ahwadhi: 5/188.]], that is: by your taking the ransom and your choosing to be killed. ﴿Indeed Allah is over all things competent﴾.

﴿And what befell you on the day the two armies met﴾ at Uhud, of killing, wounding and defeat, ﴿was by the permission of Allah﴾, i.e., by His decree and His predestination. ﴿And that He might make known the believers﴾, i.e., that He might distinguish them. It was also said: that He might see them.

﴿And that He might make known those who turned hypocrite, and it was said to them: "Come, fight in the way of Allah"﴾, i.e., for the sake of the religion of Allah and obedience to Him, ﴿or repel [the enemy]﴾ from your families and your sanctuaries. Al-Suddi said: i.e., increase the numbers of the Muslims and stand guard, for if you do not fight, that will be a repelling and a suppression of the enemy. ﴿They said: "If we knew there would be fighting, we would surely follow you."﴾ These were ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions, who withdrew from Uhud, and they were three hundred. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith﴾, i.e., nearer to disbelief on that day ﴿than to faith﴾ [(i.e., nearer to faith)] [[Addition from (B).]], ﴿saying with their mouths what is not in their hearts; and Allah knows best what they conceal.﴾

﴿Those who said of their brethren﴾ in lineage, not in religion, and they were the martyrs of Uhud, ﴿while they themselves sat back﴾, i.e., these speakers sat back from jihad, ﴿"If they had obeyed us﴾ and turned away from Muhammad (ﷺ) and stayed in their houses, ﴿they would not have been killed."﴾ Say, O Muhammad: ﴿"Then avert from yourselves death, if you are truthful."﴾ [i.e.,] ﴿avert﴾ means repel. Caution does not avail against decree.

The Exalted said: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead﴾ — to the end of the verse. It was said: it was revealed concerning the martyrs of Badr [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari 7/390; al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti 2/372.]], and they were fourteen men: eight from the Ansar and six from the Muhajirun.

Others said: it was revealed concerning the martyrs of Uhud, and they were seventy men: four from the Muhajirun, namely Hamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, Musʿab ibn ʿUmayr, ʿUthman ibn Shammas and ʿAbd Allah ibn Jahsh, and the rest were from the Ansar [[Al-Suyuti attributed it to Saʿid ibn Mansur, and it is in his Sunan in the Book of Jihad, chapter on the collection of martyrdom: 2/319; and to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim. Al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/371; and see Asbab al-Nuzul p. 163.]].

Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Salihi informed us; Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us; Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us; Muhammad ibn Hammad informed us; Abu Muʿawiyah informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, who said: We asked ʿAbd Allah (that is, Ibn Masʿud), may Allah be pleased with both of them, about this verse: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ — to the end of the verse. He said: "Indeed, we also asked about that, and he said: 'Their souls are like green birds'" — and it is related: "in the bellies of green birds, which have lamps suspended from the Throne, roaming in Paradise wherever they wish, then returning to the lamps suspended from the Throne. While they are thus, your Lord looks down on them with a look and says: 'Ask Me whatever you wish.' They said: 'O Lord, how can we ask You, when we roam in Paradise wherever we wish?' When they saw that they would not be left alone until they asked for something, they said: 'We ask You to return our souls to our bodies, that we may be killed for Your sake a second time.' When He saw that they asked only for this, they were left alone."" [[Related by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the explanation that the souls of the martyrs are in Paradise... no. 1887, 3/1502. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/364.]]

Abu Saʿid al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Thaʿlabi informed us; ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhan informed us; Jaʿwayh informed us; Salih ibn Muhammad informed us; Sulayman ibn ʿAmr informed us, from Ismaʿil ibn Umayyah, from ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When your brothers were struck on the day of Uhud, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed their souls in the bellies of green birds, which come to the rivers of Paradise and eat of its fruits, and roam in Paradise wherever they wish, and return to lamps of gold beneath the Throne. When they saw the goodness of their resting place, their food and their drink, and saw the honour Allah had prepared for them, they said: 'Would that our people knew what we are in of bliss, and what Allah has done for us, so that they would desire jihad and not slacken from it.' Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I will inform them about you and convey to your brothers.' So they rejoiced and were glad. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead﴾ to His saying ﴿He does not waste the reward of the believers.﴾" [[Related by Abu Dawud in al-Jihad, chapter on the virtue of martyrdom: 3/373–374. Al-Mundhiri said: al-Daraqutni mentioned that ʿAbd Allah ibn Idris alone narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others, and he narrated it from Ibn Ishaq without mentioning Saʿid ibn Jubayr. Also related by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/88, 297, and he declared it sound according to the condition of Muslim; and Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/266 from Ibn ʿAbbas. And al-Tabari in al-Tafsir: 7/285; see what Shaykh Ahmad Shakir wrote about the hadith in the same place. Ibn Hajar in al-Kafi al-Shafi p. 34 attributed it to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Yaʿla and al-Bazzar, all from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas, and more complete than it. The origin of the hadith is in Muslim from the hadith of Ibn Masʿud mentioned earlier. Al-Suyuti also attributed it to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il. See: al-Durr al-Manthur 2/371. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 1/428, and Shaykh Ahmad Shakir declared it sound in his commentary on the abridgment of Sunan Abi Dawud: 3/374.]]

I heard ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi say: I heard al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Qutaybi [[In "A": "al-Laythi".]] say: I heard Muhammad [[In "A": "Ahmad".]] ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf say: I heard Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil al-Bakri say: I heard Yahya ibn Habib ibn ʿArabi say: I heard Musa ibn Ibrahim say: I heard Talhah ibn Khirash say: I heard Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, may Allah be pleased with both of them, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met me and said to me: "O Jabir, why do I see you dejected?" I said: O Messenger of Allah, my father was martyred and left behind dependants and debt. He said: "Shall I not give you good news of what Allah met your father with?" I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Allah, the Exalted, has never spoken to anyone except from behind a veil. But He gave your father life, and spoke to him face to face. He said: 'O My servant, wish of Me and I will give you.' He said: 'O Lord, return me to life that I may be killed for You a second time.' The Lord, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'It has already preceded from Me that they will not return.' Then this was revealed concerning them: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead﴾" [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir, Surat Al ʿImran: 8/360–361, and said: this is a good, strange hadith from this route, and we do not know it except from the hadith of Musa ibn Ibrahim. And Ibn Majah in the Introduction, chapter on what the Jahmiyyah denied, no. 190: 1/68; and in al-Jihad also; and Ibn Abi ʿAsim in al-Sunnah: 1/267. Al-Hakim declared it sound in al-Mustadrak: 3/203, and al-Dhahabi criticised him, saying: Fayd ibn Wathiq is a liar. Al-Suyuti added its attribution to al-Tabarani, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il (al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/371). Al-Wahidi related it with his chain in Asbab al-Nuzul p. 162. Al-Albani said in Takhrij al-Sunnah: its chain is good, its narrators are truthful, with some weakness in Musa ibn Ibrahim ibn Kathir.]]

Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi informed us; Abu al-Hasan al-Tayasfuni informed us; ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar al-Jawhari informed us; Ahmad ibn ʿAli al-Kushmihani informed us; ʿAli ibn Hujr informed us; Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us; Humayd informed us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No servant dies for whom there is good with Allah, who would wish to return to the world and have the world and all in it, except the martyr, because of what he sees of the excellence of martyrdom; so he wishes to return to the world and be killed a second time." [[Related by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the virtue of martyrdom in the way of Allah, no. 1877: 3/1498; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/368.]]

Some people said: this verse was revealed concerning the martyrs of Bi'r Ma'unah [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari 7/392; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi p. 163.]]. The reason for that, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from his father Ishaq ibn Yasar, from al-Mughirah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, and ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Hazm, and from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, and others among the people of knowledge, was: Abu Bara' ʿAmir ibn Malik ibn Ja'far, the lance-player, who was the chief of Banu ʿAmir ibn Sa'sa'ah, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina and presented him a gift. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused to accept it and said: "I do not accept the gift of a polytheist. Will you embrace Islam, if you want me to accept your gift?" Then he presented Islam to him, informed him of what is in it for him and what Allah has prepared for the believers, and recited the Qur'an to him, but he did not embrace Islam. He did not keep away either, and said: "O Muhammad, what you call to is good and beautiful. If you were to send men from your companions to the people of Najd to call them to your affair, I hope they would respond to you."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I fear for them from the people of Najd."

Abu Bara' said: "I will be their protector, so send them, and they will call the people to your affair."

So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr, brother of Banu Sa'idah, with seventy men from the best of the Muslims, among them al-Harith ibn al-Simmah, Haram ibn Milhan, ʿUrwah ibn Asma' ibn al-Salt al-Sulami, Nafi' ibn Yazid ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i, and ʿAmir ibn Fuhayrah, client of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. That was in Safar of the fourth year after the Hijrah (migration to Medina), four months after Uhud. They set out until they halted at Bi'r Ma'unah, a land between the land of Banu ʿAmir and the lava-field of Banu Sulaym. When they had halted there, some of them said to others: "Which of you will convey the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the people of this water?" Haram ibn Milhan said: "I will." So he went out with the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl, who was over that water. When Haram ibn Milhan came to them, ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl did not look at the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Haram ibn Milhan said: "O people of Bi'r Ma'unah, I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah to you. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger." So they believed in Allah and His Messenger. Then a man from the rear of the tent came out with a spear and struck him in the side, until it came out through the other side. He said: "Allahu Akbar! I have triumphed by the Lord of the Ka'bah!"

Then ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl called upon the Banu ʿĀmir against the Muslims, but they refused to answer his call, saying: "We will not betray Abu Bara', for he has made a pact and given protection to them." Then he called upon tribes of the Banu Sulaym — ʿUṣayya, Ri'l and Dhakwan — and they answered him. They set out and overtook the people, surrounding them in their camp. When the Muslims saw them, they took up their swords and fought them until they were all killed, except Kaʿb ibn Zayd, for they left him with a little life in him. He was taken up from among the slain and was thought dead, and he lived until he was killed on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq).

There was also in the grazing herd of the people ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamrī and a man from the Ansar, of the Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf. They were not alerted to the fate of their companions except by the birds circling over the encampment. They said: "By God, these birds have a matter (to tell)!" So they came to look, and there were the people in their blood, and the horsemen who had struck them were standing by. The Ansari said to ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamrī: "What do you think?" He said: "I think we should join the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and inform him." The Ansari said: "God is greater! But I will not turn my self away from a place where al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr was killed." Then he fought the people until he was killed. They took ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamrī captive, and when he informed them that he was from Mudar, ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl released him, cut his forelock, and freed him on account of a slave which he claimed was owed by his mother.

ʿAmr ibn Umayya came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and told him the news. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "This is the work of Abu Bara'. I was averse to this and apprehensive of it." News of this reached Abu Bara', and the betrayal by ʿĀmir of his protection, and what befell the Messenger of God (ﷺ) because of it and his protection, grieved him greatly.

Among those who were killed was ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra. Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, that ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl used to say: "Who was the man among them whom I saw raised between the sky and the earth after he was killed, until I saw the sky beneath him?" They said: "He was ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra." Then after that, Rabi'a ibn Abi Bara' charged at ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl and stabbed him on his horse, killing him. [See: al-Sira al-Nabawiyya of Ibn Hisham with al-Rawd al-Unuf: 2/174–176.]

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi, who said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, ʿAbd al-A'la ibn Hammad informed us, Yazid ibn Zurayʿ informed us, Sa'id informed us, from Qatada, from Anas ibn Malik: "That Ri'l, Dhakwan, ʿUṣayya and Banu Lihyan asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for reinforcements against an enemy of theirs, so he sent them seventy men from the Ansar. We used to call them the Qurra' (reciters) in their time; they would gather firewood by day and pray by night. Until they reached Bi'r Ma'una, they killed them and betrayed them. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he performed qunut for a month, supplicating in the dawn prayer against some Arab tribes: against Ri'l, Dhakwan, ʿUṣayya and Banu Lihyan."

Anas (may God be pleased with him) said: "We recited a Qur'an concerning them, then that was abrogated [after we had recited it] for a time. And God, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of God as dead⦆ — the verse."

It was also said: when the relatives of the martyrs experienced any blessing, they would grieve over the martyrs and say: "We are in blessing while our fathers, our sons and our brothers are in the graves." So God, the Exalted, revealed, to comfort them and to inform them about the state of their slain: ﴿And do not think﴾, that is, do not suppose, ﴿those who were killed in the way of God﴾ — Ibn ʿĀmir read "quttilū" with doubling, and the others without doubling — ﴿dead﴾, like the dead of those who were not killed in the way of God. ﴿Rather, they are alive with their Lord﴾. It was said: alive in religion; it was said: in remembrance; it was said: because they are provided for and eat and enjoy themselves as the living do; it was said: because their spirits bow and prostrate each night beneath the Throne until the Day of Resurrection; and it was said: because the martyr does not decay in the grave and the earth does not consume him.

ʿUbayda ibn ʿUmayr said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) returned from Uhud, he passed by Mus'ab ibn ʿUmayr, who was slain, and he stopped over him and supplicated for him. Then he recited: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God⦆. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I testify that these are martyrs before God on the Day of Resurrection. Come to them, visit them, and greet them, for by Him in whose hand is my soul, no one will greet them until the Day of Resurrection except that they will return the greeting." [Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/248, who said: "This is a sound hadith according to the criteria of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi criticized him, saying: "So he said, and I consider it fabricated; Qutn was not narrated by al-Bukhari, and ʿAbd al-A'la was not recorded by them both." Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah. Al-Haythami said: "In its chain is ʿAbd al-A'la ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Farwa, who is abandoned (matruk)." Majma' al-Zawa'id: 6/123.]

﴿They are provided for﴾ — from the fruits of Paradise and its gifts.

﴿And what befell you on the day the two armies met﴾ at Uhud, of killing, wounding and defeat, ﴿was by the permission of Allah﴾, i.e., by His decree and His predestination. ﴿And that He might make known the believers﴾, i.e., that He might distinguish them. It was also said: that He might see them.

﴿And that He might make known those who turned hypocrite, and it was said to them: "Come, fight in the way of Allah"﴾, i.e., for the sake of the religion of Allah and obedience to Him, ﴿or repel [the enemy]﴾ from your families and your sanctuaries. Al-Suddi said: i.e., increase the numbers of the Muslims and stand guard, for if you do not fight, that will be a repelling and a suppression of the enemy. ﴿They said: "If we knew there would be fighting, we would surely follow you."﴾ These were ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions, who withdrew from Uhud, and they were three hundred. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith﴾, i.e., nearer to disbelief on that day ﴿than to faith﴾ [(i.e., nearer to faith)] [[Addition from (B).]], ﴿saying with their mouths what is not in their hearts; and Allah knows best what they conceal.﴾

﴿Those who said of their brethren﴾ in lineage, not in religion, and they were the martyrs of Uhud, ﴿while they themselves sat back﴾, i.e., these speakers sat back from jihad, ﴿"If they had obeyed us﴾ and turned away from Muhammad (ﷺ) and stayed in their houses, ﴿they would not have been killed."﴾ Say, O Muhammad: ﴿"Then avert from yourselves death, if you are truthful."﴾ [i.e.,] ﴿avert﴾ means repel. Caution does not avail against decree.

The Exalted said: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead﴾ — to the end of the verse. It was said: it was revealed concerning the martyrs of Badr [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari 7/390; al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti 2/372.]], and they were fourteen men: eight from the Ansar and six from the Muhajirun.

Others said: it was revealed concerning the martyrs of Uhud, and they were seventy men: four from the Muhajirun, namely Hamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, Musʿab ibn ʿUmayr, ʿUthman ibn Shammas and ʿAbd Allah ibn Jahsh, and the rest were from the Ansar [[Al-Suyuti attributed it to Saʿid ibn Mansur, and it is in his Sunan in the Book of Jihad, chapter on the collection of martyrdom: 2/319; and to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim. Al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/371; and see Asbab al-Nuzul p. 163.]].

Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Salihi informed us; Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us; Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us; Muhammad ibn Hammad informed us; Abu Muʿawiyah informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, who said: We asked ʿAbd Allah (that is, Ibn Masʿud), may Allah be pleased with both of them, about this verse: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ — to the end of the verse. He said: "Indeed, we also asked about that, and he said: 'Their souls are like green birds'" — and it is related: "in the bellies of green birds, which have lamps suspended from the Throne, roaming in Paradise wherever they wish, then returning to the lamps suspended from the Throne. While they are thus, your Lord looks down on them with a look and says: 'Ask Me whatever you wish.' They said: 'O Lord, how can we ask You, when we roam in Paradise wherever we wish?' When they saw that they would not be left alone until they asked for something, they said: 'We ask You to return our souls to our bodies, that we may be killed for Your sake a second time.' When He saw that they asked only for this, they were left alone."" [[Related by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the explanation that the souls of the martyrs are in Paradise... no. 1887, 3/1502. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/364.]]

Abu Saʿid al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Thaʿlabi informed us; ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhan informed us; Jaʿwayh informed us; Salih ibn Muhammad informed us; Sulayman ibn ʿAmr informed us, from Ismaʿil ibn Umayyah, from ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When your brothers were struck on the day of Uhud, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed their souls in the bellies of green birds, which come to the rivers of Paradise and eat of its fruits, and roam in Paradise wherever they wish, and return to lamps of gold beneath the Throne. When they saw the goodness of their resting place, their food and their drink, and saw the honour Allah had prepared for them, they said: 'Would that our people knew what we are in of bliss, and what Allah has done for us, so that they would desire jihad and not slacken from it.' Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I will inform them about you and convey to your brothers.' So they rejoiced and were glad. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead﴾ to His saying ﴿He does not waste the reward of the believers.﴾" [[Related by Abu Dawud in al-Jihad, chapter on the virtue of martyrdom: 3/373–374. Al-Mundhiri said: al-Daraqutni mentioned that ʿAbd Allah ibn Idris alone narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others, and he narrated it from Ibn Ishaq without mentioning Saʿid ibn Jubayr. Also related by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/88, 297, and he declared it sound according to the condition of Muslim; and Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/266 from Ibn ʿAbbas. And al-Tabari in al-Tafsir: 7/285; see what Shaykh Ahmad Shakir wrote about the hadith in the same place. Ibn Hajar in al-Kafi al-Shafi p. 34 attributed it to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Yaʿla and al-Bazzar, all from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas, and more complete than it. The origin of the hadith is in Muslim from the hadith of Ibn Masʿud mentioned earlier. Al-Suyuti also attributed it to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il. See: al-Durr al-Manthur 2/371. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 1/428, and Shaykh Ahmad Shakir declared it sound in his commentary on the abridgment of Sunan Abi Dawud: 3/374.]]

I heard ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi say: I heard al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Qutaybi [[In "A": "al-Laythi".]] say: I heard Muhammad [[In "A": "Ahmad".]] ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf say: I heard Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil al-Bakri say: I heard Yahya ibn Habib ibn ʿArabi say: I heard Musa ibn Ibrahim say: I heard Talhah ibn Khirash say: I heard Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, may Allah be pleased with both of them, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met me and said to me: "O Jabir, why do I see you dejected?" I said: O Messenger of Allah, my father was martyred and left behind dependants and debt. He said: "Shall I not give you good news of what Allah met your father with?" I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Allah, the Exalted, has never spoken to anyone except from behind a veil. But He gave your father life, and spoke to him face to face. He said: 'O My servant, wish of Me and I will give you.' He said: 'O Lord, return me to life that I may be killed for You a second time.' The Lord, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'It has already preceded from Me that they will not return.' Then this was revealed concerning them: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead﴾" [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir, Surat Al ʿImran: 8/360–361, and said: this is a good, strange hadith from this route, and we do not know it except from the hadith of Musa ibn Ibrahim. And Ibn Majah in the Introduction, chapter on what the Jahmiyyah denied, no. 190: 1/68; and in al-Jihad also; and Ibn Abi ʿAsim in al-Sunnah: 1/267. Al-Hakim declared it sound in al-Mustadrak: 3/203, and al-Dhahabi criticised him, saying: Fayd ibn Wathiq is a liar. Al-Suyuti added its attribution to al-Tabarani, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il (al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/371). Al-Wahidi related it with his chain in Asbab al-Nuzul p. 162. Al-Albani said in Takhrij al-Sunnah: its chain is good, its narrators are truthful, with some weakness in Musa ibn Ibrahim ibn Kathir.]]

Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi informed us; Abu al-Hasan al-Tayasfuni informed us; ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar al-Jawhari informed us; Ahmad ibn ʿAli al-Kushmihani informed us; ʿAli ibn Hujr informed us; Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us; Humayd informed us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No servant dies for whom there is good with Allah, who would wish to return to the world and have the world and all in it, except the martyr, because of what he sees of the excellence of martyrdom; so he wishes to return to the world and be killed a second time." [[Related by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the virtue of martyrdom in the way of Allah, no. 1877: 3/1498; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/368.]]

Some people said: this verse was revealed concerning the martyrs of Bi'r Ma'unah [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari 7/392; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi p. 163.]]. The reason for that, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from his father Ishaq ibn Yasar, from al-Mughirah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, and ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Hazm, and from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, and others among the people of knowledge, was: Abu Bara' ʿAmir ibn Malik ibn Ja'far, the lance-player, who was the chief of Banu ʿAmir ibn Sa'sa'ah, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina and presented him a gift. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused to accept it and said: "I do not accept the gift of a polytheist. Will you embrace Islam, if you want me to accept your gift?" Then he presented Islam to him, informed him of what is in it for him and what Allah has prepared for the believers, and recited the Qur'an to him, but he did not embrace Islam. He did not keep away either, and said: "O Muhammad, what you call to is good and beautiful. If you were to send men from your companions to the people of Najd to call them to your affair, I hope they would respond to you."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I fear for them from the people of Najd."

Abu Bara' said: "I will be their protector, so send them, and they will call the people to your affair."

So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr, brother of Banu Sa'idah, with seventy men from the best of the Muslims, among them al-Harith ibn al-Simmah, Haram ibn Milhan, ʿUrwah ibn Asma' ibn al-Salt al-Sulami, Nafi' ibn Yazid ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i, and ʿAmir ibn Fuhayrah, client of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. That was in Safar of the fourth year after the Hijrah (migration to Medina), four months after Uhud. They set out until they halted at Bi'r Ma'unah, a land between the land of Banu ʿAmir and the lava-field of Banu Sulaym. When they had halted there, some of them said to others: "Which of you will convey the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the people of this water?" Haram ibn Milhan said: "I will." So he went out with the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl, who was over that water. When Haram ibn Milhan came to them, ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl did not look at the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Haram ibn Milhan said: "O people of Bi'r Ma'unah, I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah to you. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger." So they believed in Allah and His Messenger. Then a man from the rear of the tent came out with a spear and struck him in the side, until it came out through the other side. He said: "Allahu Akbar! I have triumphed by the Lord of the Ka'bah!"

Then ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl called upon the Banu ʿĀmir against the Muslims, but they refused to answer his call, saying: "We will not betray Abu Bara', for he has made a pact and given protection to them." Then he called upon tribes of the Banu Sulaym — ʿUṣayya, Ri'l and Dhakwan — and they answered him. They set out and overtook the people, surrounding them in their camp. When the Muslims saw them, they took up their swords and fought them until they were all killed, except Kaʿb ibn Zayd, for they left him with a little life in him. He was taken up from among the slain and was thought dead, and he lived until he was killed on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq).

There was also in the grazing herd of the people ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamrī and a man from the Ansar, of the Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf. They were not alerted to the fate of their companions except by the birds circling over the encampment. They said: "By God, these birds have a matter (to tell)!" So they came to look, and there were the people in their blood, and the horsemen who had struck them were standing by. The Ansari said to ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamrī: "What do you think?" He said: "I think we should join the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and inform him." The Ansari said: "God is greater! But I will not turn my self away from a place where al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr was killed." Then he fought the people until he was killed. They took ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamrī captive, and when he informed them that he was from Mudar, ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl released him, cut his forelock, and freed him on account of a slave which he claimed was owed by his mother.

ʿAmr ibn Umayya came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and told him the news. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "This is the work of Abu Bara'. I was averse to this and apprehensive of it." News of this reached Abu Bara', and the betrayal by ʿĀmir of his protection, and what befell the Messenger of God (ﷺ) because of it and his protection, grieved him greatly.

Among those who were killed was ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra. Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, that ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl used to say: "Who was the man among them whom I saw raised between the sky and the earth after he was killed, until I saw the sky beneath him?" They said: "He was ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra." Then after that, Rabi'a ibn Abi Bara' charged at ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl and stabbed him on his horse, killing him. [See: al-Sira al-Nabawiyya of Ibn Hisham with al-Rawd al-Unuf: 2/174–176.]

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi, who said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, ʿAbd al-A'la ibn Hammad informed us, Yazid ibn Zurayʿ informed us, Sa'id informed us, from Qatada, from Anas ibn Malik: "That Ri'l, Dhakwan, ʿUṣayya and Banu Lihyan asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for reinforcements against an enemy of theirs, so he sent them seventy men from the Ansar. We used to call them the Qurra' (reciters) in their time; they would gather firewood by day and pray by night. Until they reached Bi'r Ma'una, they killed them and betrayed them. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he performed qunut for a month, supplicating in the dawn prayer against some Arab tribes: against Ri'l, Dhakwan, ʿUṣayya and Banu Lihyan."

Anas (may God be pleased with him) said: "We recited a Qur'an concerning them, then that was abrogated [after we had recited it] for a time. And God, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of God as dead⦆ — the verse."

It was also said: when the relatives of the martyrs experienced any blessing, they would grieve over the martyrs and say: "We are in blessing while our fathers, our sons and our brothers are in the graves." So God, the Exalted, revealed, to comfort them and to inform them about the state of their slain: ﴿And do not think﴾, that is, do not suppose, ﴿those who were killed in the way of God﴾ — Ibn ʿĀmir read "quttilū" with doubling, and the others without doubling — ﴿dead﴾, like the dead of those who were not killed in the way of God. ﴿Rather, they are alive with their Lord﴾. It was said: alive in religion; it was said: in remembrance; it was said: because they are provided for and eat and enjoy themselves as the living do; it was said: because their spirits bow and prostrate each night beneath the Throne until the Day of Resurrection; and it was said: because the martyr does not decay in the grave and the earth does not consume him.

ʿUbayda ibn ʿUmayr said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) returned from Uhud, he passed by Mus'ab ibn ʿUmayr, who was slain, and he stopped over him and supplicated for him. Then he recited: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God⦆. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I testify that these are martyrs before God on the Day of Resurrection. Come to them, visit them, and greet them, for by Him in whose hand is my soul, no one will greet them until the Day of Resurrection except that they will return the greeting." [Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/248, who said: "This is a sound hadith according to the criteria of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi criticized him, saying: "So he said, and I consider it fabricated; Qutn was not narrated by al-Bukhari, and ʿAbd al-A'la was not recorded by them both." Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah. Al-Haythami said: "In its chain is ʿAbd al-A'la ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Farwa, who is abandoned (matruk)." Majma' al-Zawa'id: 6/123.]

﴿They are provided for﴾ — from the fruits of Paradise and its gifts.

﴿And what befell you on the day the two armies met﴾ at Uhud, of killing, wounding and defeat, ﴿was by the permission of Allah﴾, i.e., by His decree and His predestination. ﴿And that He might make known the believers﴾, i.e., that He might distinguish them. It was also said: that He might see them.

﴿And that He might make known those who turned hypocrite, and it was said to them: "Come, fight in the way of Allah"﴾, i.e., for the sake of the religion of Allah and obedience to Him, ﴿or repel [the enemy]﴾ from your families and your sanctuaries. Al-Suddi said: i.e., increase the numbers of the Muslims and stand guard, for if you do not fight, that will be a repelling and a suppression of the enemy. ﴿They said: "If we knew there would be fighting, we would surely follow you."﴾ These were ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions, who withdrew from Uhud, and they were three hundred. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith﴾, i.e., nearer to disbelief on that day ﴿than to faith﴾ [(i.e., nearer to faith)] [[Addition from (B).]], ﴿saying with their mouths what is not in their hearts; and Allah knows best what they conceal.﴾

﴿Those who said of their brethren﴾ in lineage, not in religion, and they were the martyrs of Uhud, ﴿while they themselves sat back﴾, i.e., these speakers sat back from jihad, ﴿"If they had obeyed us﴾ and turned away from Muhammad (ﷺ) and stayed in their houses, ﴿they would not have been killed."﴾ Say, O Muhammad: ﴿"Then avert from yourselves death, if you are truthful."﴾ [i.e.,] ﴿avert﴾ means repel. Caution does not avail against decree.

The Exalted said: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead﴾ — to the end of the verse. It was said: it was revealed concerning the martyrs of Badr [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari 7/390; al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti 2/372.]], and they were fourteen men: eight from the Ansar and six from the Muhajirun.

Others said: it was revealed concerning the martyrs of Uhud, and they were seventy men: four from the Muhajirun, namely Hamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, Musʿab ibn ʿUmayr, ʿUthman ibn Shammas and ʿAbd Allah ibn Jahsh, and the rest were from the Ansar [[Al-Suyuti attributed it to Saʿid ibn Mansur, and it is in his Sunan in the Book of Jihad, chapter on the collection of martyrdom: 2/319; and to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim. Al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/371; and see Asbab al-Nuzul p. 163.]].

Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Salihi informed us; Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us; Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us; Muhammad ibn Hammad informed us; Abu Muʿawiyah informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, who said: We asked ʿAbd Allah (that is, Ibn Masʿud), may Allah be pleased with both of them, about this verse: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ — to the end of the verse. He said: "Indeed, we also asked about that, and he said: 'Their souls are like green birds'" — and it is related: "in the bellies of green birds, which have lamps suspended from the Throne, roaming in Paradise wherever they wish, then returning to the lamps suspended from the Throne. While they are thus, your Lord looks down on them with a look and says: 'Ask Me whatever you wish.' They said: 'O Lord, how can we ask You, when we roam in Paradise wherever we wish?' When they saw that they would not be left alone until they asked for something, they said: 'We ask You to return our souls to our bodies, that we may be killed for Your sake a second time.' When He saw that they asked only for this, they were left alone."" [[Related by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the explanation that the souls of the martyrs are in Paradise... no. 1887, 3/1502. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/364.]]

Abu Saʿid al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Thaʿlabi informed us; ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhan informed us; Jaʿwayh informed us; Salih ibn Muhammad informed us; Sulayman ibn ʿAmr informed us, from Ismaʿil ibn Umayyah, from ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When your brothers were struck on the day of Uhud, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed their souls in the bellies of green birds, which come to the rivers of Paradise and eat of its fruits, and roam in Paradise wherever they wish, and return to lamps of gold beneath the Throne. When they saw the goodness of their resting place, their food and their drink, and saw the honour Allah had prepared for them, they said: 'Would that our people knew what we are in of bliss, and what Allah has done for us, so that they would desire jihad and not slacken from it.' Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'I will inform them about you and convey to your brothers.' So they rejoiced and were glad. Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead﴾ to His saying ﴿He does not waste the reward of the believers.﴾" [[Related by Abu Dawud in al-Jihad, chapter on the virtue of martyrdom: 3/373–374. Al-Mundhiri said: al-Daraqutni mentioned that ʿAbd Allah ibn Idris alone narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others, and he narrated it from Ibn Ishaq without mentioning Saʿid ibn Jubayr. Also related by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/88, 297, and he declared it sound according to the condition of Muslim; and Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/266 from Ibn ʿAbbas. And al-Tabari in al-Tafsir: 7/285; see what Shaykh Ahmad Shakir wrote about the hadith in the same place. Ibn Hajar in al-Kafi al-Shafi p. 34 attributed it to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Yaʿla and al-Bazzar, all from the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas, and more complete than it. The origin of the hadith is in Muslim from the hadith of Ibn Masʿud mentioned earlier. Al-Suyuti also attributed it to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il. See: al-Durr al-Manthur 2/371. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 1/428, and Shaykh Ahmad Shakir declared it sound in his commentary on the abridgment of Sunan Abi Dawud: 3/374.]]

I heard ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi say: I heard al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Qutaybi [[In "A": "al-Laythi".]] say: I heard Muhammad [[In "A": "Ahmad".]] ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf say: I heard Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil al-Bakri say: I heard Yahya ibn Habib ibn ʿArabi say: I heard Musa ibn Ibrahim say: I heard Talhah ibn Khirash say: I heard Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, may Allah be pleased with both of them, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met me and said to me: "O Jabir, why do I see you dejected?" I said: O Messenger of Allah, my father was martyred and left behind dependants and debt. He said: "Shall I not give you good news of what Allah met your father with?" I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "Allah, the Exalted, has never spoken to anyone except from behind a veil. But He gave your father life, and spoke to him face to face. He said: 'O My servant, wish of Me and I will give you.' He said: 'O Lord, return me to life that I may be killed for You a second time.' The Lord, Blessed and Exalted, said: 'It has already preceded from Me that they will not return.' Then this was revealed concerning them: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead﴾" [[Related by al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir, Surat Al ʿImran: 8/360–361, and said: this is a good, strange hadith from this route, and we do not know it except from the hadith of Musa ibn Ibrahim. And Ibn Majah in the Introduction, chapter on what the Jahmiyyah denied, no. 190: 1/68; and in al-Jihad also; and Ibn Abi ʿAsim in al-Sunnah: 1/267. Al-Hakim declared it sound in al-Mustadrak: 3/203, and al-Dhahabi criticised him, saying: Fayd ibn Wathiq is a liar. Al-Suyuti added its attribution to al-Tabarani, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il (al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/371). Al-Wahidi related it with his chain in Asbab al-Nuzul p. 162. Al-Albani said in Takhrij al-Sunnah: its chain is good, its narrators are truthful, with some weakness in Musa ibn Ibrahim ibn Kathir.]]

Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi informed us; Abu al-Hasan al-Tayasfuni informed us; ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar al-Jawhari informed us; Ahmad ibn ʿAli al-Kushmihani informed us; ʿAli ibn Hujr informed us; Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us; Humayd informed us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No servant dies for whom there is good with Allah, who would wish to return to the world and have the world and all in it, except the martyr, because of what he sees of the excellence of martyrdom; so he wishes to return to the world and be killed a second time." [[Related by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the virtue of martyrdom in the way of Allah, no. 1877: 3/1498; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/368.]]

Some people said: this verse was revealed concerning the martyrs of Bi'r Ma'unah [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari 7/392; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi p. 163.]]. The reason for that, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from his father Ishaq ibn Yasar, from al-Mughirah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, and ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Hazm, and from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, and others among the people of knowledge, was: Abu Bara' ʿAmir ibn Malik ibn Ja'far, the lance-player, who was the chief of Banu ʿAmir ibn Sa'sa'ah, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina and presented him a gift. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused to accept it and said: "I do not accept the gift of a polytheist. Will you embrace Islam, if you want me to accept your gift?" Then he presented Islam to him, informed him of what is in it for him and what Allah has prepared for the believers, and recited the Qur'an to him, but he did not embrace Islam. He did not keep away either, and said: "O Muhammad, what you call to is good and beautiful. If you were to send men from your companions to the people of Najd to call them to your affair, I hope they would respond to you."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I fear for them from the people of Najd."

Abu Bara' said: "I will be their protector, so send them, and they will call the people to your affair."

So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr, brother of Banu Sa'idah, with seventy men from the best of the Muslims, among them al-Harith ibn al-Simmah, Haram ibn Milhan, ʿUrwah ibn Asma' ibn al-Salt al-Sulami, Nafi' ibn Yazid ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i, and ʿAmir ibn Fuhayrah, client of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. That was in Safar of the fourth year after the Hijrah (migration to Medina), four months after Uhud. They set out until they halted at Bi'r Ma'unah, a land between the land of Banu ʿAmir and the lava-field of Banu Sulaym. When they had halted there, some of them said to others: "Which of you will convey the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the people of this water?" Haram ibn Milhan said: "I will." So he went out with the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl, who was over that water. When Haram ibn Milhan came to them, ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl did not look at the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Haram ibn Milhan said: "O people of Bi'r Ma'unah, I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah to you. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger." So they believed in Allah and His Messenger. Then a man from the rear of the tent came out with a spear and struck him in the side, until it came out through the other side. He said: "Allahu Akbar! I have triumphed by the Lord of the Ka'bah!"

Then ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl called upon the Banu ʿĀmir against the Muslims, but they refused to answer his call, saying: "We will not betray Abu Bara', for he has made a pact and given protection to them." Then he called upon tribes of the Banu Sulaym — ʿUṣayya, Ri'l and Dhakwan — and they answered him. They set out and overtook the people, surrounding them in their camp. When the Muslims saw them, they took up their swords and fought them until they were all killed, except Kaʿb ibn Zayd, for they left him with a little life in him. He was taken up from among the slain and was thought dead, and he lived until he was killed on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq).

There was also in the grazing herd of the people ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamrī and a man from the Ansar, of the Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf. They were not alerted to the fate of their companions except by the birds circling over the encampment. They said: "By God, these birds have a matter (to tell)!" So they came to look, and there were the people in their blood, and the horsemen who had struck them were standing by. The Ansari said to ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamrī: "What do you think?" He said: "I think we should join the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and inform him." The Ansari said: "God is greater! But I will not turn my self away from a place where al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr was killed." Then he fought the people until he was killed. They took ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamrī captive, and when he informed them that he was from Mudar, ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl released him, cut his forelock, and freed him on account of a slave which he claimed was owed by his mother.

ʿAmr ibn Umayya came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and told him the news. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "This is the work of Abu Bara'. I was averse to this and apprehensive of it." News of this reached Abu Bara', and the betrayal by ʿĀmir of his protection, and what befell the Messenger of God (ﷺ) because of it and his protection, grieved him greatly.

Among those who were killed was ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra. Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, that ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl used to say: "Who was the man among them whom I saw raised between the sky and the earth after he was killed, until I saw the sky beneath him?" They said: "He was ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra." Then after that, Rabi'a ibn Abi Bara' charged at ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl and stabbed him on his horse, killing him. [See: al-Sira al-Nabawiyya of Ibn Hisham with al-Rawd al-Unuf: 2/174–176.]

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi, who said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, ʿAbd al-A'la ibn Hammad informed us, Yazid ibn Zurayʿ informed us, Sa'id informed us, from Qatada, from Anas ibn Malik: "That Ri'l, Dhakwan, ʿUṣayya and Banu Lihyan asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for reinforcements against an enemy of theirs, so he sent them seventy men from the Ansar. We used to call them the Qurra' (reciters) in their time; they would gather firewood by day and pray by night. Until they reached Bi'r Ma'una, they killed them and betrayed them. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he performed qunut for a month, supplicating in the dawn prayer against some Arab tribes: against Ri'l, Dhakwan, ʿUṣayya and Banu Lihyan."

Anas (may God be pleased with him) said: "We recited a Qur'an concerning them, then that was abrogated [after we had recited it] for a time. And God, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of God as dead⦆ — the verse."

It was also said: when the relatives of the martyrs experienced any blessing, they would grieve over the martyrs and say: "We are in blessing while our fathers, our sons and our brothers are in the graves." So God, the Exalted, revealed, to comfort them and to inform them about the state of their slain: ﴿And do not think﴾, that is, do not suppose, ﴿those who were killed in the way of God﴾ — Ibn ʿĀmir read "quttilū" with doubling, and the others without doubling — ﴿dead﴾, like the dead of those who were not killed in the way of God. ﴿Rather, they are alive with their Lord﴾. It was said: alive in religion; it was said: in remembrance; it was said: because they are provided for and eat and enjoy themselves as the living do; it was said: because their spirits bow and prostrate each night beneath the Throne until the Day of Resurrection; and it was said: because the martyr does not decay in the grave and the earth does not consume him.

ʿUbayda ibn ʿUmayr said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) returned from Uhud, he passed by Mus'ab ibn ʿUmayr, who was slain, and he stopped over him and supplicated for him. Then he recited: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God⦆. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I testify that these are martyrs before God on the Day of Resurrection. Come to them, visit them, and greet them, for by Him in whose hand is my soul, no one will greet them until the Day of Resurrection except that they will return the greeting." [Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/248, who said: "This is a sound hadith according to the criteria of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi criticized him, saying: "So he said, and I consider it fabricated; Qutn was not narrated by al-Bukhari, and ʿAbd al-A'la was not recorded by them both." Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah. Al-Haythami said: "In its chain is ʿAbd al-A'la ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Farwa, who is abandoned (matruk)." Majma' al-Zawa'id: 6/123.]

﴿They are provided for﴾ — from the fruits of Paradise and its gifts.

﴿And what befell you on the day the two armies met﴾ at Uhud, of killing, wounding and defeat, ﴿was by the permission of Allah﴾, i.e., by His decree and His predestination. ﴿And that He might make known the believers﴾, i.e., that He might distinguish them. It was also said: that He might see them.

﴿And that He might make known those who turned hypocrite, and it was said to them: "Come, fight in the way of Allah"﴾, i.e., for the sake of the religion of Allah and obedience to Him, ﴿or repel [the enemy]﴾ from your families and your sanctuaries. Al-Suddi said: i.e., increase the numbers of the Muslims and stand guard, for if you do not fight, that will be a repelling and a suppression of the enemy. ﴿They said: "If we knew there would be fighting, we would surely follow you."﴾ These were ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy and his companions, who withdrew from Uhud, and they were three hundred. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They were nearer to disbelief that day than to faith﴾, i.e., nearer to disbelief on that day ﴿than to faith﴾ [(i.e., nearer to faith)] [[Addition from (B).]], ﴿saying with their mouths what is not in their hearts; and Allah knows best what they conceal.﴾

﴿Those who said of their brethren﴾ in lineage, not in religion, and they were the martyrs of Uhud, ﴿while they themselves sat back﴾, i.e., these speakers sat back from jihad, ﴿"If they had obeyed us﴾ and turned away from Muhammad (ﷺ) and stayed in their houses, ﴿they would not have been killed."﴾ Say, O Muhammad: ﴿"Then avert from yourselves death, if you are truthful."﴾ [i.e.,] ﴿avert﴾ means repel. Caution does not avail against decree.

The Exalted said: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead﴾ — to the end of the verse. It was said: it was revealed concerning the martyrs of Badr [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari 7/390; al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti 2/372.]], and they were fourteen men: eight from the Ansar and six from the Muhajirun.

Others said: it was revealed concerning the martyrs of Uhud, and they were seventy men: four from the Muhajirun, namely Hamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib, Musʿab ibn ʿUmayr, ʿUthman ibn Shammas and ʿAbd Allah ibn Jahsh, and the rest were from the Ansar [[Al-Suyuti attributed it to Saʿid ibn Mansur, and it is in his Sunan in the Book of Jihad, chapter on the collection of martyrdom: 2/319; and to ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim. Al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/371; and see Asbab al-Nuzul p. 163.]].

Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Salihi informed us; Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us; Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us; Muhammad ibn Hammad informed us; Abu Muʿawiyah informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, who said: We asked ʿAbd Allah (that is, Ibn Masʿud), may Allah be pleased with both of them, about this verse: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of Allah as dead; rather they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ — to the end of the verse. He said: "Indeed, we also asked about that, and he said: 'Their souls are like green birds'" — and it is related: "in the bellies of green birds, which have lamps suspended from the Throne, roaming in Paradise wherever they wish, then returning to the lamps suspended from the Throne. While they are thus, your Lord looks down on them with a look and says: 'Ask Me whatever you wish.' They said: 'O Lord, how can we ask You, when we roam in Paradise wherever we wish?' When they saw that they would not be left alone until they asked for something, they said: 'We ask You to return our souls to our bodies, that we may be killed for Your sake a second time.' When He saw that they asked only for this, they were left alone."" [[Related by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the explanation that the souls of the martyrs are in Paradise... no. 1887, 3/1502. And the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/364.]]

Abu Saʿid al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Thaʿlabi informed us; ʿAbd Allah ibn Hamid informed us; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Shadhan informed us; Jaʿwayh informed us; Salih ibn Muhammad informed us; Sulayman ibn ʿAmr informed us, from Ismaʿil ibn Umayyah, from ʿAta' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When your brothers were struck on the day of Uhud, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed their souls in the bellies of green birds, which come to the rivers of Paradise and eat of its fruits, and roam in Paradise wherever they wish, and return to lamps of gold beneath the Throne. When they saw the goodness of their resting place, their food and their drink, and saw the honour Allah had prepared for them, they said: 'Would that our people knew what we are in of bliss, and what Allah has done for us, so that they would desire jihad and not slacken from it.' Al-Mundhiri said: al-Daraqutni mentioned that ʿAbd Allah ibn Idris alone narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others, and he narrated it from Ibn Ishaq without mentioning Saʿid ibn Jubayr. See: al-Durr al-Manthur 2/371. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 1/428, and Shaykh Ahmad Shakir declared it sound in his commentary on the abridgment of Sunan Abi Dawud: 3/374.]]

I heard ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi say: I heard al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Qutaybi [[In "A": "al-Laythi".]] say: I heard Muhammad [[In "A": "Ahmad".]] ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf say: I heard Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil al-Bakri say: I heard Yahya ibn Habib ibn ʿArabi say: I heard Musa ibn Ibrahim say: I heard Talhah ibn Khirash say: I heard Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, may Allah be pleased with both of them, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met me and said to me: "O Jabir, why do I see you dejected?"
