Al-Suyuti added its attribution to al-Tabarani, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il (al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/371). Al-Wahidi related it with his chain in Asbab al-Nuzul p. 162. Al-Albani said in Takhrij al-Sunnah: its chain is good, its narrators are truthful, with some weakness in Musa ibn Ibrahim ibn Kathir.]]

Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn al-Fadl al-Kharaqi informed us; Abu al-Hasan al-Tayasfuni informed us; ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar al-Jawhari informed us; Ahmad ibn ʿAli al-Kushmihani informed us; ʿAli ibn Hujr informed us; Isma'il ibn Ja'far informed us; Humayd informed us, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with them, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No servant dies for whom there is good with Allah, who would wish to return to the world and have the world and all in it, except the martyr, because of what he sees of the excellence of martyrdom; so he wishes to return to the world and be killed a second time." [[Related by Muslim in al-Imarah, chapter on the virtue of martyrdom in the way of Allah, no. 1877: 3/1498; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/368.]]

Some people said: this verse was revealed concerning the martyrs of Bi'r Ma'unah [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari 7/392; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi p. 163.]]. The reason for that, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from his father Ishaq ibn Yasar, from al-Mughirah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, and ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn Hazm, and from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, and others among the people of knowledge, was: Abu Bara' ʿAmir ibn Malik ibn Ja'far, the lance-player, who was the chief of Banu ʿAmir ibn Sa'sa'ah, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Medina and presented him a gift. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) refused to accept it and said: "I do not accept the gift of a polytheist. Will you embrace Islam, if you want me to accept your gift?" Then he presented Islam to him, informed him of what is in it for him and what Allah has prepared for the believers, and recited the Qur'an to him, but he did not embrace Islam. He did not keep away either, and said: "O Muhammad, what you call to is good and beautiful. If you were to send men from your companions to the people of Najd to call them to your affair, I hope they would respond to you."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I fear for them from the people of Najd."

Abu Bara' said: "I will be their protector, so send them, and they will call the people to your affair."

So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr, brother of Banu Sa'idah, with seventy men from the best of the Muslims, among them al-Harith ibn al-Simmah, Haram ibn Milhan, ʿUrwah ibn Asma' ibn al-Salt al-Sulami, Nafi' ibn Yazid ibn Warqa' al-Khuza'i, and ʿAmir ibn Fuhayrah, client of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him. That was in Safar of the fourth year after the Hijrah (migration to Medina), four months after Uhud. They set out until they halted at Bi'r Ma'unah, a land between the land of Banu ʿAmir and the lava-field of Banu Sulaym. When they had halted there, some of them said to others: "Which of you will convey the message of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to the people of this water?" Haram ibn Milhan said: "I will." So he went out with the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl, who was over that water. When Haram ibn Milhan came to them, ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl did not look at the letter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Haram ibn Milhan said: "O people of Bi'r Ma'unah, I am the messenger of the Messenger of Allah to you. I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger." So they believed in Allah and His Messenger. Then a man from the rear of the tent came out with a spear and struck him in the side, until it came out through the other side. He said: "Allahu Akbar! I have triumphed by the Lord of the Ka'bah!"

Then ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl called upon the Banu ʿĀmir against the Muslims, but they refused to answer his call, saying: "We will not betray Abu Bara', for he has made a pact and given protection to them." Then he called upon tribes of the Banu Sulaym — ʿUṣayya, Ri'l and Dhakwan — and they answered him. They set out and overtook the people, surrounding them in their camp. When the Muslims saw them, they took up their swords and fought them until they were all killed, except Kaʿb ibn Zayd, for they left him with a little life in him. He was taken up from among the slain and was thought dead, and he lived until he was killed on the day of the Trench (al-Khandaq).

There was also in the grazing herd of the people ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamrī and a man from the Ansar, of the Banu ʿAmr ibn ʿAwf. They were not alerted to the fate of their companions except by the birds circling over the encampment. They said: "By God, these birds have a matter (to tell)!" So they came to look, and there were the people in their blood, and the horsemen who had struck them were standing by. The Ansari said to ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamrī: "What do you think?" He said: "I think we should join the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and inform him." The Ansari said: "God is greater! But I will not turn my self away from a place where al-Mundhir ibn ʿAmr was killed." Then he fought the people until he was killed. They took ʿAmr ibn Umayya al-Ḍamrī captive, and when he informed them that he was from Mudar, ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl released him, cut his forelock, and freed him on account of a slave which he claimed was owed by his mother.

ʿAmr ibn Umayya came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and told him the news. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "This is the work of Abu Bara'. I was averse to this and apprehensive of it." News of this reached Abu Bara', and the betrayal by ʿĀmir of his protection, and what befell the Messenger of God (ﷺ) because of it and his protection, grieved him greatly.

Among those who were killed was ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra. Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, that ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl used to say: "Who was the man among them whom I saw raised between the sky and the earth after he was killed, until I saw the sky beneath him?" They said: "He was ʿĀmir ibn Fuhayra." Then after that, Rabi'a ibn Abi Bara' charged at ʿĀmir ibn al-Ṭufayl and stabbed him on his horse, killing him. [See: al-Sira al-Nabawiyya of Ibn Hisham with al-Rawd al-Unuf: 2/174–176.]

We were informed by ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi, who said: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, ʿAbd al-A'la ibn Hammad informed us, Yazid ibn Zurayʿ informed us, Sa'id informed us, from Qatada, from Anas ibn Malik: "That Ri'l, Dhakwan, ʿUṣayya and Banu Lihyan asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for reinforcements against an enemy of theirs, so he sent them seventy men from the Ansar. We used to call them the Qurra' (reciters) in their time; they would gather firewood by day and pray by night. Until they reached Bi'r Ma'una, they killed them and betrayed them. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he performed qunut for a month, supplicating in the dawn prayer against some Arab tribes: against Ri'l, Dhakwan, ʿUṣayya and Banu Lihyan."

Anas (may God be pleased with him) said: "We recited a Qur'an concerning them, then that was abrogated [after we had recited it] for a time. And God, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And do not think of those who were killed in the way of God as dead⦆ — the verse."

It was also said: when the relatives of the martyrs experienced any blessing, they would grieve over the martyrs and say: "We are in blessing while our fathers, our sons and our brothers are in the graves." So God, the Exalted, revealed, to comfort them and to inform them about the state of their slain: ﴿And do not think﴾, that is, do not suppose, ﴿those who were killed in the way of God﴾ — Ibn ʿĀmir read "quttilū" with doubling, and the others without doubling — ﴿dead﴾, like the dead of those who were not killed in the way of God. ﴿Rather, they are alive with their Lord﴾. It was said: alive in religion; it was said: in remembrance; it was said: because they are provided for and eat and enjoy themselves as the living do; it was said: because their spirits bow and prostrate each night beneath the Throne until the Day of Resurrection; and it was said: because the martyr does not decay in the grave and the earth does not consume him.

ʿUbayda ibn ʿUmayr said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) returned from Uhud, he passed by Mus'ab ibn ʿUmayr, who was slain, and he stopped over him and supplicated for him. Then he recited: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with God⦆. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "I testify that these are martyrs before God on the Day of Resurrection. Come to them, visit them, and greet them, for by Him in whose hand is my soul, no one will greet them until the Day of Resurrection except that they will return the greeting." [Narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/248, who said: "This is a sound hadith according to the criteria of the two Shaykhs, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi criticized him, saying: "So he said, and I consider it fabricated; Qutn was not narrated by al-Bukhari, and ʿAbd al-A'la was not recorded by them both." Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah. Al-Haythami said: "In its chain is ʿAbd al-A'la ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Farwa, who is abandoned (matruk)." Majma' al-Zawa'id: 6/123.]

﴿They are provided for﴾ — from the fruits of Paradise and its gifts.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 170:

﴿Rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾: [that is, of] His provision and His reward. ﴿And they rejoice﴾ and are glad ﴿for those who have not yet joined them from behind them﴾

[That is,] of their brothers who were left behind alive in the world, upon the paths of faith and jihad. [The martyrs] know that if they are martyred and join them, and attain the same honour that they have attained, then they rejoice on that account. ﴿That no fear will be on them, nor will they grieve.﴾

﴿They rejoice in a blessing from Allah and bounty, and that Allah﴾, meaning: and [they rejoice] that Allah [does not waste]. Al-Kisa'i (d. 189 AH) read the alif of ﴿وَأَنَّ﴾ with a kasra, *inna*, on the basis of *isti'naf* (resumption of a new sentence, a fresh clause not governed by what precedes it).

﴿does not waste the reward of the believers﴾. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi related to us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has guaranteed for the one who strives in His way, whom nothing takes out of his house except striving in His way and belief in His word, that He will admit him to Paradise, or return him to the dwelling from which he went out, with the reward and spoils he has gained." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in *al-Khums*, chapter on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ), "Spoils have been made lawful for you," 6/220, and in *al-Tawhid*, chapter on "And Our word has already preceded for Our servants the messengers," 13/441. And Muslim in *al-Imara*, chapter on the virtue of jihad and going out in the way of Allah, no. (1876), 3/1496.]]

And he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one is wounded in the way of Allah — and Allah knows best who is wounded in His way — except that he will come on the Day of Resurrection with his wound gushing blood: its colour is the colour of blood and its scent is the scent of musk." [[Narrated by Muslim in *al-Imara*, in the place mentioned above, and by al-Bukhari in *al-Wudu'*, chapter on what befalls of impurities..., 1/344, and in *al-Jihad*, chapter on whoever is wounded in the way of Allah, 6/20; and the author in *Sharh al-Sunna*, 10/365.]]

Al-Imam Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Darabjirdi informed us: Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' informed us: Sa'id related to us: Muhammad ibn Ajlan told me, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The martyr feels no more pain from being killed than one of you feels from a pinch." [[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in *al-Jihad*, chapter on what the martyr feels of pain, 6/36; Ibn Majah in *al-Jihad*, chapter on the virtue of martyrdom in the way of Allah, no. (2802), 2/937; al-Darimi in *al-Jihad*, chapter on the virtue of the martyr, 2/205; and Ahmad in *al-Musnad*, 2/297; and the author in *Sharh al-Sunna*, 10/365. Its isnad is good.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them﴾, the verse. The occasion was that Abu Sufyan and his companions, when they turned back from Uhud and reached al-Rawha', regretted their turning back and blamed one another, saying: "You have not killed Muhammad, nor have you taken the young women captive! You killed them until only the remnant was left, and you left them? Return and finish them off!" This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he wished to instil fear in the enemy and to show them strength in himself and his companions. He summoned his companions to go out in pursuit of Abu Sufyan, and a group of them responded, despite the injuries and wounds that had struck them on the day of Uhud. The caller of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out: "Let no one go out with us except those who were present with us yesterday." Jabir ibn Abdullah spoke to him, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, my father had left me in charge of seven sisters of mine, and he said to me: 'My son, it is not fitting for me or for you to leave these women without a man among them, and I am not one to prefer you over myself in jihad with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So stay behind with your sisters.' So I stayed behind with them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him permission, and he went out with him.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out only to instil fear in the enemy and to let them know that he had gone out in pursuit of them, so that they would think him strong, and that what had befallen them had not weakened them, so that they would turn back.

So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out, with Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talha, al-Zubayr, Sa'd, Sa'id, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman, and Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah, with seventy men, may Allah be pleased with them all, until they reached Hamra' al-Asad, which is eight miles from Medina. [[See: *Sirat Ibn Hisham*, 2/143–144; *Tafsir al-Tabari*, 7/400–401.]]

It is related from A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said to Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr: "O son of my sister, by Allah, your father and your grandfather — meaning Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr — are among those of whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them﴾." [[A sound hadith, narrated by al-Hakim, who declared it sound according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim, and al-Dhahabi agreed: 2/298. It is in the two Sahihs with a difference in the address to Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, narrated by al-Bukhari in *al-Maghazi*, chapter "Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger," 7/373, and by Muslim.]]

Then there passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) Ma'bad al-Khuza'i at Hamra' al-Asad. The Khuza'a, both its Muslims and its disbelievers, were a trusted repository of sincere counsel for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Tihama; they were his allies and kept nothing from him that happened there. Ma'bad was then a polytheist, and he said: "O Muhammad, by Allah, what has befallen you among your companions has grieved us, and we wished that Allah had spared you from them." Then he went out from the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until he met Abu Sufyan and those with him at al-Rawha', who had resolved to return to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "We have struck the greatest part of his companions and their leaders; we will attack what remains of them and finish them off." When Abu Sufyan saw Ma'bad, he said: "What is behind you, O Ma'bad?" He said: "Muhammad has gone out with his companions, seeking you, with a host the like of which I have never seen. They are burning with rage against you, and those who had stayed behind from him on your day have joined him, and they regret what they did. There is among them a wrath against you the like of which I have never seen." He said: "Woe to you, what are you saying?" He said: "By Allah, I do not think you will move until you see the forelocks of the horses." He said: "By Allah, we have resolved to attack them again, to wipe out what remains of them." He said: "By Allah, I forbid you from that. By Allah, what I have seen has moved me to say verses about it:

*The mounts were almost crushed by the clamour,*
*when the earth flowed with the dark-grey, galloping hosts.*

[The text then cites further verses.] These verses turned Abu Sufyan and those with him back.

A caravan of Abd al-Qays passed by him and he said: "Where are you heading?" They said: "We are heading to Medina." He said: "And why?" They said: "We want provisions." [[The phrase in the printed edition is distorted as: "(wa-lam yaqulu nurid al-mira)" and the correction is from *Tafsir al-Tabari*.]] He said: "Will you convey a message from me to Muhammad, and I will load your camels with raisins for you at 'Ukaz tomorrow, when you meet us?" They said: "Yes." He said: "When you come to him, tell him that we have resolved to march against him and his companions to wipe out what remains of them." Abu Sufyan returned to Mecca. The caravan passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while they were at Hamra' al-Asad, and they informed him of what Abu Sufyan had said. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions said: "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to Medina after three days. [[See: *Sirat Ibn Hisham*, 2/144; *Tafsir al-Tabari*, 7/406–409.]] This is the view of most of the commentators.

Mujahid and Ikrima said: This verse was revealed concerning the lesser Battle of Badr. This was because, on the day of Uhud, when Abu Sufyan wanted to turn back, he said: "O Muhammad, our appointment between us is the season of the lesser Badr next year, if you wish." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That is between us and you, if Allah wills." When the following year came, Abu Sufyan went out with the people of Mecca until he halted at Majanna, on the side of Marr al-Zahran. Then Allah cast terror into his heart, and he resolved to turn back. He met Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud al-Ashja'i, who had come to perform *'umra*, and Abu Sufyan said to him: "O Nu'aym, I had arranged with Muhammad and his companions that we would meet at the season of the lesser Badr, but this is a year of drought, and only a year in which we graze on the trees and drink milk will set us right. It has occurred to me not to go out to it, and I dislike that Muhammad goes out while I do not. That would embolden them, and it is more beloved to me that the breaking of the promise should come from their side rather than from mine. So go to Medina, discourage them, and inform them that I have a great host with which they have no power against us. For you, I will give you ten camels, which I will place in the hands of Suhayl ibn Amr, who will guarantee them." He said: Suhayl came, and Nu'aym said to him: "O Abu Yazid, will you guarantee these she-camels for me, while I go to Muhammad and discourage him?" He said: "Yes." So Nu'aym set out until he came to Medina and found the people preparing for the appointment of Abu Sufyan. He said: "Where are you heading?" They said: "Abu Sufyan promised us the season of the lesser Badr, that we would fight there." He said: "What an evil opinion you have! They came to you in your homes and dwellings, and only the fugitive escaped from you. Do you want to go out when they have gathered against you at the season? By Allah, not one of you will escape." The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked going out. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, I will go out even if I am alone." As for the coward, he turned back; as for the brave, he prepared himself for battle, and said: "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."

So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out with his companions until they arrived at the lesser Badr. They began to meet the polytheists and ask them about Quraysh, and the polytheists would say: "They have gathered against you, intending to terrify the Muslims." The believers would say: "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs," until they reached Badr, which had been the site of a market for them in the Jahiliyya, where they would gather each year for eight days. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained at Badr waiting for Abu Sufyan, but Abu Sufyan had turned back from Majanna to Mecca. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions met no one from the polytheists. They came to the market, and they had merchandise and provisions with them; they sold and gained two dirhams for every dirham, and returned to Medina safe and carrying spoils. [[See *Tafsir al-Tabari*, 7/411–412, where he preferred the first view, which is the view of most commentators: 7/412–413.]]

That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger﴾, that is, they answered. The position of ﴿alladhina﴾ is in the genitive, as a description of ﴿the believers﴾, its implied sense being: "Indeed Allah does not waste the reward of the believers who responded to Allah and the Messenger, ﴿after the wound had afflicted them﴾," that is, (the wounds had struck them). [[In manuscript B: (the injury had struck them).]] The sentence ends here, and then a new beginning: ﴿For those among them who did good﴾ by obeying the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and answering his call to the raid, ﴿and were mindful of Allah﴾ by avoiding disobedience to him, ﴿there is a great reward.﴾

﴿They rejoice in a blessing from Allah and bounty, and that Allah﴾, meaning: and [they rejoice] that Allah [does not waste]. Al-Kisa'i (d. 189 AH) read the alif of ﴿وَأَنَّ﴾ with a kasra, *inna*, on the basis of *isti'naf* (resumption of a new sentence, a fresh clause not governed by what precedes it).

﴿does not waste the reward of the believers﴾. Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us: Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Hashimi related to us: Abu Mus'ab informed us, from Malik, from Abu al-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has guaranteed for the one who strives in His way, whom nothing takes out of his house except striving in His way and belief in His word, that He will admit him to Paradise, or return him to the dwelling from which he went out, with the reward and spoils he has gained." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in *al-Khums*, chapter on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ), "Spoils have been made lawful for you," 6/220, and in *al-Tawhid*, chapter on "And Our word has already preceded for Our servants the messengers," 13/441. And Muslim in *al-Imara*, chapter on the virtue of jihad and going out in the way of Allah, no. (1876), 3/1496.]]

And he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, no one is wounded in the way of Allah — and Allah knows best who is wounded in His way — except that he will come on the Day of Resurrection with his wound gushing blood: its colour is the colour of blood and its scent is the scent of musk." [[Narrated by Muslim in *al-Imara*, in the place mentioned above, and by al-Bukhari in *al-Wudu'*, chapter on what befalls of impurities..., 1/344, and in *al-Jihad*, chapter on whoever is wounded in the way of Allah, 6/20; and the author in *Sharh al-Sunna*, 10/365.]]

Al-Imam Abu Ali al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us: Abu Tahir Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Mahmash al-Ziyadi informed us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn al-Husayn al-Qattan informed us: Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Darabjirdi informed us: Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Muqri' informed us: Sa'id related to us: Muhammad ibn Ajlan told me, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The martyr feels no more pain from being killed than one of you feels from a pinch." [[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in *al-Jihad*, chapter on what the martyr feels of pain, 6/36; Ibn Majah in *al-Jihad*, chapter on the virtue of martyrdom in the way of Allah, no. (2802), 2/937; al-Darimi in *al-Jihad*, chapter on the virtue of the martyr, 2/205; and Ahmad in *al-Musnad*, 2/297; and the author in *Sharh al-Sunna*, 10/365. Its isnad is good.]]

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them﴾, the verse. The occasion was that Abu Sufyan and his companions, when they turned back from Uhud and reached al-Rawha', regretted their turning back and blamed one another, saying: "You have not killed Muhammad, nor have you taken the young women captive! You killed them until only the remnant was left, and you left them? Return and finish them off!" This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he wished to instil fear in the enemy and to show them strength in himself and his companions. He summoned his companions to go out in pursuit of Abu Sufyan, and a group of them responded, despite the injuries and wounds that had struck them on the day of Uhud. The caller of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out: "Let no one go out with us except those who were present with us yesterday." Jabir ibn Abdullah spoke to him, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, my father had left me in charge of seven sisters of mine, and he said to me: 'My son, it is not fitting for me or for you to leave these women without a man among them, and I am not one to prefer you over myself in jihad with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So stay behind with your sisters.' So I stayed behind with them." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave him permission, and he went out with him.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out only to instil fear in the enemy and to let them know that he had gone out in pursuit of them, so that they would think him strong, and that what had befallen them had not weakened them, so that they would turn back.

So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out, with Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, Ali, Talha, al-Zubayr, Sa'd, Sa'id, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman, and Abu Ubayda ibn al-Jarrah, with seventy men, may Allah be pleased with them all, until they reached Hamra' al-Asad, which is eight miles from Medina. [[See: *Sirat Ibn Hisham*, 2/143–144; *Tafsir al-Tabari*, 7/400–401.]]

It is related from A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said to Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr: "O son of my sister, by Allah, your father and your grandfather — meaning Abu Bakr and al-Zubayr — are among those of whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the wound had afflicted them﴾." [[A sound hadith, narrated by al-Hakim, who declared it sound according to the conditions of al-Bukhari and Muslim, and al-Dhahabi agreed: 2/298. It is in the two Sahihs with a difference in the address to Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, narrated by al-Bukhari in *al-Maghazi*, chapter "Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger," 7/373, and by Muslim.]]

Then there passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) Ma'bad al-Khuza'i at Hamra' al-Asad. The Khuza'a, both its Muslims and its disbelievers, were a trusted repository of sincere counsel for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Tihama; they were his allies and kept nothing from him that happened there. Ma'bad was then a polytheist, and he said: "O Muhammad, by Allah, what has befallen you among your companions has grieved us, and we wished that Allah had spared you from them." Then he went out from the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) until he met Abu Sufyan and those with him at al-Rawha', who had resolved to return to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "We have struck the greatest part of his companions and their leaders; we will attack what remains of them and finish them off." When Abu Sufyan saw Ma'bad, he said: "What is behind you, O Ma'bad?" He said: "Muhammad has gone out with his companions, seeking you, with a host the like of which I have never seen. They are burning with rage against you, and those who had stayed behind from him on your day have joined him, and they regret what they did. There is among them a wrath against you the like of which I have never seen." He said: "Woe to you, what are you saying?" He said: "By Allah, I do not think you will move until you see the forelocks of the horses." He said: "By Allah, we have resolved to attack them again, to wipe out what remains of them." He said: "By Allah, I forbid you from that. By Allah, what I have seen has moved me to say verses about it:

*The mounts were almost crushed by the clamour,*
*when the earth flowed with the dark-grey, galloping hosts.*

[The text then cites further verses.] These verses turned Abu Sufyan and those with him back.

A caravan of Abd al-Qays passed by him and he said: "Where are you heading?" They said: "We are heading to Medina." He said: "And why?" They said: "We want provisions." [[The phrase in the printed edition is distorted as: "(wa-lam yaqulu nurid al-mira)" and the correction is from *Tafsir al-Tabari*.]] He said: "Will you convey a message from me to Muhammad, and I will load your camels with raisins for you at 'Ukaz tomorrow, when you meet us?" They said: "Yes." He said: "When you come to him, tell him that we have resolved to march against him and his companions to wipe out what remains of them." Abu Sufyan returned to Mecca. The caravan passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while they were at Hamra' al-Asad, and they informed him of what Abu Sufyan had said. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions said: "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to Medina after three days. [[See: *Sirat Ibn Hisham*, 2/144; *Tafsir al-Tabari*, 7/406–409.]] This is the view of most of the commentators.

Mujahid and Ikrima said: This verse was revealed concerning the lesser Battle of Badr. This was because, on the day of Uhud, when Abu Sufyan wanted to turn back, he said: "O Muhammad, our appointment between us is the season of the lesser Badr next year, if you wish." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That is between us and you, if Allah wills." When the following year came, Abu Sufyan went out with the people of Mecca until he halted at Majanna, on the side of Marr al-Zahran. Then Allah cast terror into his heart, and he resolved to turn back. He met Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud al-Ashja'i, who had come to perform *'umra*, and Abu Sufyan said to him: "O Nu'aym, I had arranged with Muhammad and his companions that we would meet at the season of the lesser Badr, but this is a year of drought, and only a year in which we graze on the trees and drink milk will set us right. It has occurred to me not to go out to it, and I dislike that Muhammad goes out while I do not. That would embolden them, and it is more beloved to me that the breaking of the promise should come from their side rather than from mine. So go to Medina, discourage them, and inform them that I have a great host with which they have no power against us. For you, I will give you ten camels, which I will place in the hands of Suhayl ibn Amr, who will guarantee them." He said: Suhayl came, and Nu'aym said to him: "O Abu Yazid, will you guarantee these she-camels for me, while I go to Muhammad and discourage him?" He said: "Yes." So Nu'aym set out until he came to Medina and found the people preparing for the appointment of Abu Sufyan. He said: "Where are you heading?" They said: "Abu Sufyan promised us the season of the lesser Badr, that we would fight there." He said: "What an evil opinion you have! They came to you in your homes and dwellings, and only the fugitive escaped from you. Do you want to go out when they have gathered against you at the season? By Allah, not one of you will escape." The companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked going out. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is Muhammad's soul, I will go out even if I am alone." As for the coward, he turned back; as for the brave, he prepared himself for battle, and said: "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs."

So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out with his companions until they arrived at the lesser Badr. They began to meet the polytheists and ask them about Quraysh, and the polytheists would say: "They have gathered against you, intending to terrify the Muslims." The believers would say: "Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs," until they reached Badr, which had been the site of a market for them in the Jahiliyya, where they would gather each year for eight days. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained at Badr waiting for Abu Sufyan, but Abu Sufyan had turned back from Majanna to Mecca. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions met no one from the polytheists. They came to the market, and they had merchandise and provisions with them; they sold and gained two dirhams for every dirham, and returned to Medina safe and carrying spoils. [[See *Tafsir al-Tabari*, 7/411–412, where he preferred the first view, which is the view of most commentators: 7/412–413.]]

That is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger﴾, that is, they answered. The position of ﴿alladhina﴾ is in the genitive, as a description of ﴿the believers﴾, its implied sense being: "Indeed Allah does not waste the reward of the believers who responded to Allah and the Messenger, ﴿after the wound had afflicted them﴾," that is, (the wounds had struck them). [[In manuscript B: (the injury had struck them).]] The sentence ends here, and then a new beginning: ﴿For those among them who did good﴾ by obeying the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and answering his call to the raid, ﴿and were mindful of Allah﴾ by avoiding disobedience to him, ﴿there is a great reward.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 173–174:**

﴿Those to whom the people said﴾. The grammatical position (*mahall*) of ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ in the genitive case is also governed by the first ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ (*alladhina*). By "the people" (*al-nas*) is meant Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud, according to Mujahid and Ikrimah. This is an instance of the *'amm* (general term) being used to mean the *khass* (specific), like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Or do they envy the people?﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ) alone. Muhammad ibn Ishaq and a group said: by "the people" he meant the riders of 'Abd al-Qays. ﴿Indeed, the people have gathered against you﴾, meaning Abu Sufyan and his companions. ﴿So fear them﴾, meaning be afraid of them and beware of them, for you have no power against them. ﴿But it increased them in faith﴾, meaning in confirmation, certainty and strength. ﴿And they said, "Allah is sufficient for us"﴾, meaning Allah is our sufficiency. ﴿And He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾, meaning the one to whom affairs are entrusted; *fa'il* here has the sense of *maf'ul*.

Abdul-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi related to us: Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi related to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) related to us: Ahmad ibn Yunus related to us: Abu Bakr related to us, from Abu Husayn, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs﴾ was said by Abraham when he was thrown into the fire, and Muhammad (ﷺ) said it when they said: ﴿Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them,﴾ and it increased them in faith, and they said, ﴿Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.﴾ [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir, chapter of Surat Al 'Imran, "Those to whom the people said, 'Indeed, the people have gathered against you'": 8/229.]]

﴿So they returned﴾, meaning they went back, ﴿with favour from Allah﴾, meaning with well-being, as they did not meet an enemy, ﴿and bounty﴾, meaning trade and profit, which is what they gained in the market. ﴿No harm touched them﴾, meaning no injury or displeasing thing afflicted them. ﴿And they pursued the pleasure of Allah﴾, meaning in obedience to Allah and obedience to His Messenger. This is because they said, "Would this be considered a military expedition?" So Allah gave them the reward of a military expedition and was pleased with them. ﴿And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 175–178:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens you of his allies﴾. That is: that one who said to you, ﴿Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them﴾ is from the action of Satan, who cast it into their mouths so that they would terrify you and make you cowardly toward them. ﴿He frightens his allies﴾, meaning: he frightens you through his allies. Thus it is also in the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, meaning: he frightens the believers through the disbelievers. Al-Suddi said: he magnifies his allies in their hearts so that they fear them. This is indicated by the recitation of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "He frightens you of his allies." ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me﴾ in abandoning My command, ﴿if you are believers﴾, meaning those who affirm My promise, for I am the guarantor for you of victory and triumph.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And let them not grieve you﴾. Nafi' read "yuhzinka" with a damma on the yā' and a kasra on the zāy, and so throughout the Qur'an except His saying ﴿The Great Terror will not grieve them﴾; Abu Ja'far read the opposite. They are two dialects: ḥazina yaḥzanu and aḥzana yuḥzinu, except that the more prevalent dialect is ḥazina yaḥzanu. ﴿Those who race to disbelief﴾. Al-Dahhak said: they are the disbelievers of Quraysh. Others said: they are the hypocrites who race to disbelief by supporting the disbelievers.

﴿Indeed, they will not harm Allah at all﴾ by their racing to disbelief. ﴿Allah intends not to give them a share in the Hereafter﴾, meaning a portion of the reward of the Hereafter. Therefore He forsook them until they raced to disbelief. ﴿And for them is a great punishment.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who have exchanged﴾ (istabdalu), i.e., substituted, ﴿disbelief for faith will not harm Allah at all﴾, and they only harm themselves. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment.﴾

﴿And let not those who disbelieve think﴾. Hamzah read this and the following with a tā' in both; the others read with a yā'. Whoever reads with a yā', "fa-alladhina" is in the nominative position as the subject, and its implied sense is: ﴿and let not the disbelievers think that Our granting them respite is good for them﴾. Whoever reads with a tā', meaning: "and do not think, O Muhammad, that those who disbelieve..." — it is in the accusative as a substitute for "alladhina". ﴿That what We grant them respite is good for their souls.﴾ Al-imla' is granting respite and delay. It is said: "I lived long and was praised, and I enjoyed a while" (tamallaytu hinan), and from it is His saying: ﴿And leave me alone for a long time﴾ [Maryam: 46], meaning: a long while. Then He began, saying: ﴿Indeed, We grant them respite﴾, We give them time, ﴿so that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾

Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning the polytheists of Makkah. ʿAta' said: concerning Qurayzah and al-Nadir.

Al-Qaffal ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Allah informed us: Abu Mansur Ahmad ibn al-Fadl al-Baronjirdi informed us: Abu Ahmad Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdan al-Sayrafi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yunus informed us: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi informed us: Shu'bah informed us, from ʿAli ibn Zayd, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked, "Who among the people is best?" He said: "One whose life is long and whose deeds are good." It was said: "Then who among the people is worst?" He said: "One whose life is long and whose deeds are evil."

[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Zuhd, chapter on what has come about the long life of the believer: 6/622, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith. And al-Darimi in al-Raqa'iq, chapter "Which of the believers is best?": 2/308. And al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 1/339, and he authenticated it according to the condition of Muslim, and he also narrated from Jabir: "Shall I inform you of the best of you and the worst of you?" They said: "Yes." He said: "The best of you are those with the longest lives and the best deeds." He said: this is a sahih hadith according to the condition of the two Shaykhs, and it has a sahih supporting narration according to the condition of Muslim, then he mentioned the hadith of Abu Bakrah. Also narrated by Imam Ahmad: 4/188, 190; 5/40, 43, 44, and in other places. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/287, 288. And al-Tayalisi in al-Musnad p. (116).]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 175–178:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿It is only Satan who frightens you of his allies﴾. That is: that one who said to you, ﴿Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them﴾ is from the action of Satan, who cast it into their mouths so that they would terrify you and make you cowardly toward them. ﴿He frightens his allies﴾, meaning: he frightens you through his allies. Thus it is also in the recitation of Ubayy ibn Ka'b, meaning: he frightens the believers through the disbelievers. Al-Suddi said: he magnifies his allies in their hearts so that they fear them. This is indicated by the recitation of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "He frightens you of his allies." ﴿So do not fear them, but fear Me﴾ in abandoning My command, ﴿if you are believers﴾, meaning those who affirm My promise, for I am the guarantor for you of victory and triumph.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿And let them not grieve you﴾. Nafi' read "yuhzinka" with a damma on the yā' and a kasra on the zāy, and so throughout the Qur'an except His saying ﴿The Great Terror will not grieve them﴾; Abu Ja'far read the opposite. They are two dialects: ḥazina yaḥzanu and aḥzana yuḥzinu, except that the more prevalent dialect is ḥazina yaḥzanu. ﴿Those who race to disbelief﴾. Al-Dahhak said: they are the disbelievers of Quraysh. Others said: they are the hypocrites who race to disbelief by supporting the disbelievers.

﴿Indeed, they will not harm Allah at all﴾ by their racing to disbelief. ﴿Allah intends not to give them a share in the Hereafter﴾, meaning a portion of the reward of the Hereafter. Therefore He forsook them until they raced to disbelief. ﴿And for them is a great punishment.﴾

﴿Indeed, those who have exchanged﴾ (istabdalu), i.e., substituted, ﴿disbelief for faith will not harm Allah at all﴾, and they only harm themselves. ﴿And for them is a painful punishment.﴾

﴿And let not those who disbelieve think﴾. Hamzah read this and the following with a tā' in both; the others read with a yā'. Whoever reads with a yā', "fa-alladhina" is in the nominative position as the subject, and its implied sense is: ﴿and let not the disbelievers think that Our granting them respite is good for them﴾. Whoever reads with a tā', meaning: "and do not think, O Muhammad, that those who disbelieve..." — it is in the accusative as a substitute for "alladhina". ﴿That what We grant them respite is good for their souls.﴾ Al-imla' is granting respite and delay. It is said: "I lived long and was praised, and I enjoyed a while" (tamallaytu hinan), and from it is His saying: ﴿And leave me alone for a long time﴾ [Maryam: 46], meaning: a long while. Then He began, saying: ﴿Indeed, We grant them respite﴾, We give them time, ﴿so that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾

Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning the polytheists of Makkah. ʿAta' said: concerning Qurayzah and al-Nadir.

Al-Qaffal ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAbd Allah informed us: Abu Mansur Ahmad ibn al-Fadl al-Baronjirdi informed us: Abu Ahmad Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Hamdan al-Sayrafi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yunus informed us: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi informed us: Shu'bah informed us, from ʿAli ibn Zayd, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakrah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked, "Who among the people is best?" He said: "One whose life is long and whose deeds are good." It was said: "Then who among the people is worst?" He said: "One whose life is long and whose deeds are evil."

[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Zuhd, chapter on what has come about the long life of the believer: 6/622, and he said: this is a hasan sahih hadith. And al-Darimi in al-Raqa'iq, chapter "Which of the believers is best?": 2/308. And al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 1/339, and he authenticated it according to the condition of Muslim, and he also narrated from Jabir: "Shall I inform you of the best of you and the worst of you?" They said: "Yes." He said: "The best of you are those with the longest lives and the best deeds." He said: this is a sahih hadith according to the condition of the two Shaykhs, and it has a sahih supporting narration according to the condition of Muslim, then he mentioned the hadith of Abu Bakrah. Also narrated by Imam Ahmad: 4/188, 190; 5/40, 43, 44, and in other places. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/287, 288. And al-Tayalisi in al-Musnad p. (116).]

**Al-Baghawi's commentary (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 3, verse 179:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in the state you are in until He distinguishes the wicked from the good.﴾ Scholars differed regarding it. Al-Kalbi said: The Quraysh said, "O Muhammad, you claim that whoever opposes you is in the Fire and Allah is angry with him, and that whoever follows you in your religion is in Paradise and Allah is pleased with him. So inform us about who believes in you and who does not believe in you." Then Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Suddi said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "My community was shown to me in their forms in clay, just as Adam was shown them, and I was informed of who will believe in me and who will disbelieve in me." This reached the hypocrites, who said mockingly: "Muhammad claims that he knows who will believe in him and who will disbelieve among those who have not yet been created, while we are with him and he does not know us." This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he stood on the pulpit, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "What is wrong with people who cast doubt on my knowledge? Do not ask me about anything between you and the Hour except that I will inform you of it." Then 'Abdullah ibn Hudhafah al-Sahmi stood up and said: "Who is my father, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Hudhafah." Then 'Umar stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are content with Allah as Lord, with Islam as religion, with the Qur'an as leader, and with you as Prophet. So pardon us; may Allah pardon you." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Will you then desist?" Then he came down from the pulpit, and Allah revealed this verse. [[Al-Wahidi mentioned it without a chain of narration from al-Suddi up to his saying: "This reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he stood..." See *Asbab al-Nuzul*, p. 165. Imam Ahmad also narrated in the *Musnad* (3/162) from Anas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out when the sun had passed its zenith, prayed the noon prayer, and when he had finished the greeting he stood on the pulpit... without mentioning that the revelation of the verse came after that. Ibn 'Abd al-Barr narrated it with his chain from Anas in *Usd al-Ghabah* (3/212). See also Ibn Hajar's *al-Isabah* (4/57).]]

They differed regarding the ruling (*hukm*) of the verse and its arrangement (*nazm*). Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, al-Dahhak, Muqatil, al-Kalbi and most of the exegetes said: the address is to the disbelievers and hypocrites, meaning ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in what you are in﴾ — O assembly of disbelievers and hypocrites — of disbelief and hypocrisy ﴿until He distinguishes the wicked from the good﴾.

Others said: the address is to the believers, about whom He gave the report. Its meaning is: Allah would not leave you, O assembly of believers, in the state you are in of the mixing of the believer with the hypocrite. So the discourse shifted from the third person (report) to the second person (address).

﴿Until He distinguishes﴾ (*yamiz*): Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Ya'qub read it with a *damma* on the *ya'* and a *shaddah*, and likewise the one in al-Anfal. The rest read it with the light form. It is said: *maza al-shay'a yamizuhu mayzan* and *mayyazahu tamyizan* when one separates it, so that it is separated. The light form is intransitive in itself. Abu Mu'adh said: when you separate between two things you say *miztu mayzan*; when there are many things you say *mayyaztuha tamyizan*. Likewise, when you make one thing into two you say *faraqtu* with the light form, from which comes *farq al-sha'r* (the parting of the hair). If you make it into many things you say *farraqtuhu tafriqan*. The meaning of the verse is: until He distinguishes the hypocrite from the sincere one. Allah distinguished the believers from the hypocrites on the day of Uhud, when they showed hypocrisy and lagged behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Qatadah said: until He distinguishes the disbeliever from the believer through emigration (*hijrah*) and struggle (*jihad*).

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Allah would not leave the believers in what you are in﴾ — in the loins of men and the wombs of women — O assembly of hypocrites and polytheists — until He separates between you and those in your loins and the wombs of your women who are believers. It was also said: ﴿until He distinguishes the wicked﴾, who is the sinner, ﴿from the good﴾, who is the believer. That is: until He removes burdens from the believer through what afflicts him of calamity, trial and misfortune.

﴿Nor would Allah disclose to you the unseen﴾, because none knows the unseen except Him, ﴿but Allah chooses from His messengers whom He wills﴾, so He informs him of some of the knowledge of the unseen. Its parallel is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He is the Knower of the unseen, and He does not reveal His unseen to anyone except a messenger whom He has approved﴾ (Surah al-Jinn, verses 26–27).

Al-Suddi said: its meaning is: Allah would not disclose the unseen to Muhammad (ﷺ), but Allah chose him. ﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers. And if you believe and fear Allah, you will have a great reward.﴾

﴿And let not those who are stingy with what Allah has given them of His bounty suppose that it is good for them﴾. That is: let not the miserly suppose that their miserliness is good for them. ﴿Rather, it is bad for them﴾, meaning the miserliness. ﴿They will have the things they were stingy with hung around their necks on the Day of Resurrection﴾, that is, they will be made to carry what they withheld. The meaning is that the wealth they refused to give in zakat (obligatory almsgiving) will become a serpent, coiled around their necks on the Day of Resurrection, striking at them from its head to its feet. This is the view of Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Wa'il, al-Sha'bi and al-Suddi.

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi, who said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah al-Madini informed us, Hashim ibn al-Qasim informed us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar informed us, from his father, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever Allah has given wealth, but he does not pay its zakat, his wealth will be displayed to him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald, venomous serpent with two black spots over its eyes. It will be coiled around his neck, then it will seize him by his two jaws, that is, his cheeks, and say: 'I am your wealth, I am your treasure.'" Then he recited: ﴿And let not those who are stingy suppose...﴾ to the end of the verse.

We were informed by 'Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi, who said: Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, 'Amr ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath informed us, my father informed us, al-A'mash informed us, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I came to him, meaning the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, or by Him besides whom there is no god, or as he swore: there is no man who has camels, cattle or sheep, and does not pay their due, except that they will be brought to him on the Day of Resurrection, at their largest and fattest. They will trample him with their hooves and gore him with their horns. Whenever the last of them passes, the first of them will be returned to him, until judgment is passed between the people."

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: The meaning of the verse is that on the Day of Resurrection a collar of fire will be placed around their necks. Mujahid said: On the Day of Resurrection they will be required to bring what they withheld of their wealth in this world.

'Atiyya narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that this verse was revealed concerning the rabbis (ahbar, scholars) of the Jews who concealed the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) and his prophethood. By miserliness, he meant concealing knowledge, as He said in Surah al-Nisa': ﴿Those who are miserly and enjoin miserliness upon people, and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾ [al-Nisa': 37].

The meaning of His words ﴿they will have the things they were stingy with hung around their necks on the Day of Resurrection﴾ is that they will bear its burden and its sin, as in His saying: ﴿And they will bear their burdens upon their backs﴾ [al-An'am: 31].

﴿And to Allah belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth﴾. That is, He is the Everlasting who remains after the annihilation of His creation and the passing away of their possessions, when they die and He inherits them. Compare His saying: ﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is upon it﴾ [Maryam: 40]. ﴿And Allah is All-Aware of what you do﴾. The people of Basra and Makka read ya'malun (with the letter ya', "they do"), while the others read ta'malun (with the letter ta', "you do").

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 181:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich."﴾ Al-Hasan and Mujahid said: When the verse ﴿Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan?﴾ was revealed, the Jews said: "Indeed, Allah is poor and asks loans from us, while we are rich." Al-Hasan also mentioned that the one who made this statement was Huyayy ibn Akhtab [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 7 / 444; al-Durr al-Manthur: 2 / 397.]].

Ikrimah, al-Suddi, Muqatil and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: The Prophet (ﷺ) wrote, along with Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him), to the Jews of Banu Qaynuqa', inviting them to Islam, to establishing the prayer and giving the zakat, and to loaning Allah a goodly loan. One day Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) entered their house of study and found many Jews gathered around a man among them called Finhas ibn 'Azura', who was one of their scholars, and with him was another rabbi called Ashya'. Abu Bakr said to Finhas: "Fear Allah and embrace Islam, for by Allah, you know that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah; he has come to you with the truth from Allah, and you find it written in your Torah. So believe and affirm, and loan Allah a goodly loan; it will admit you to Paradise and multiply the reward for you."

Finhas said: "O Abu Bakr, you claim that our Lord asks loans of our wealth, and none asks a loan except the poor from the rich? If what you say is true, then Allah is indeed poor and we are rich. He forbids you from usury and gives us, and if He were rich He would not have given us usury."

Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) became angry and struck Finhas's face a severe blow, saying: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, were it not for the covenant between us and you, I would strike off your neck, O enemy of Allah!" Finhas went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Muhammad, look at what your companion did to me!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him): "What led you to do what you did?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, the enemy of Allah said a monstrous thing: he claimed that Allah is poor and that they are rich. So I became angry for the sake of Allah and struck his face." Finhas denied this, so Allah, may He be exalted, revealed, as a refutation of Finhas and a confirmation of Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him): ﴿Indeed, Allah has heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor, and we are rich."﴾ [[Narrated by Ibn Ishaq in al-Sirah: 2 / 207-208, al-Halabi edition, and Ibn Jarir al-Tabari in al-Tafsir: 7 / 441-444, and Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim; see: al-Durr al-Manthur: 2 / 396; Asbab al-Nuzul of al-Wahidi, p. (166).]] 75/a

﴿We will record what they have said﴾ of falsehood and fabrication against Allah, ﴿and their killing of the prophets without right, and We will say: "Taste the punishment of the burning."﴾ [[Omitted from (b).]] Muqatil said: "We will preserve it against them." Al-Waqidi said: "We will command the recording angels to write it down," like His saying: ﴿And indeed We are its recorders﴾. Hamzah read "sa-yuktabu" with a damma on the ya', and "wa-qatlahum" with a raf' on the lam, and "wa-yaqulu" with a ya'. ﴿Taste the punishment of the burning﴾: that is, the Fire, and it bears the meaning of "the burning one," just as it is said: "for them is a painful punishment," meaning "painful."

﴿That is for what your hands have sent forth, and that Allah is not ever unjust to the servants﴾, so that He would punish without any sin.

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those who said, "Indeed Allah has taken a covenant from us"﴾ to the end of the verse. Al-Kalbi said: It was revealed concerning Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, Malik ibn al-Sayf, Wahb ibn Yahudha, Zayd ibn al-Tabut [[In manuscript A: (al-Baqir).]], Finhas ibn 'Azura', and Huyayy ibn Akhtab. They came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, you claim that Allah the Exalted has sent you to us as a messenger and has sent down the Book to you, and that Allah the Exalted has taken a covenant from us in the Torah: ﴿that we should not believe a messenger﴾ who claims he has come from Allah, ﴿until he brings us an offering which the fire consumes﴾. If you bring us that, we will believe you." He said: Then Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Those who said﴾ [[See: Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 167; Tafsir al-Qurtubi, 4/295.]], meaning: Allah heard the saying of those who said it. The place of ﴿alladhina﴾ (those who) is in the genitive case, as a repetition of the first ﴿alladhina﴾. ﴿Indeed Allah has taken a covenant from us﴾ means: He commanded us and enjoined us in His books that we should not believe in a messenger, meaning we should not accept as true a messenger who claims he has come from Allah, ﴿until he brings us an offering which the fire consumes﴾, so that this would be a proof of his truthfulness. The qurban (offering) is everything by which the servant draws near to Allah the Exalted, such as a sacrifice, charity, or good deed; it is on the pattern fu'lan, from qurba (nearness). Offerings and spoils of war were not lawful for the Children of Israel. When they offered an offering or took spoils, a white fire would come down from the sky, having no smoke, and having a roaring and crackling sound, and it would consume that offering and that spoil. That would be a sign of acceptance. If it was not accepted, it would remain in its state.

Al-Suddi said: Allah the Exalted commanded the Children of Israel: "Whoever comes to you claiming he is a messenger of Allah, do not believe him until he brings you an offering which the fire consumes, until there comes to you the Messiah and Muhammad. When they come to you, believe in them both, for they will come without an offering." Allah the Exalted said, establishing the proof against them: ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿Indeed there have come to you﴾, O assembly of Jews, ﴿messengers before me with clear proofs and with what you have spoken of﴾, the offering, ﴿so why did you kill them﴾, meaning Zakariyya, Yahya, and the rest of the prophets whom they killed. He intended by this their forefathers, and addressed them thus because they were content with the deeds of their forefathers. ﴿If you are truthful﴾, meaning: your denial of them while knowing of your truthfulness, like the killing of their fathers of the prophets, despite their bringing offerings and miracles. Then He said, consoling His Prophet ﷺ:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 184–185:

﴿If they deny you, then messengers before you were also denied, who came with the clear proofs and the scriptures and the illuminating Book.﴾ Ibn 'Amir recited "wa-bi-l-zubur" (and with the scriptures). That is, with the written books; the word *al-zubur* means the written [books]. Its singular is *zabur*, like *rasul* and *rusul* (messenger and messengers). ﴿And the illuminating Book﴾: the clear, shining one.

His saying, mighty and majestic is He: ﴿Every soul﴾ that has been given a soul ﴿shall taste death﴾. In a hadith: "When God Most High created Adam, the earth complained to its Lord about what had been taken from it. So He promised it that He would return into it what had been taken from it, and so no one is there but he will be buried in the dust from which he was created." [[Not established with this wording. What appears, and God knows best, is that it is not a hadith. Al-Khazin mentioned it in his tafsir without indicating that it is a hadith. See al-Matalib al-'Aliyah 3/333–334, where something close to it is narrated.]] ﴿And you will only be paid your rewards﴾ in full, meaning you will be recompensed for your deeds ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾: if good, then good; if evil, then evil. ﴿So whoever is drawn away﴾ from ﴿the Fire and is admitted to the Garden has indeed succeeded﴾: [meaning] he has attained salvation and been safe from fear. ﴿And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion﴾: that is, a benefit and a pleasure, like the axe, the cooking pot and the bowl, which then pass away and do not remain.

Al-Hasan said: "Like the greenness of plants and the play of girls; it has no lasting outcome."

Qatadah said: "It is a fleeting enjoyment, about to vanish with its people. So take from this enjoyment by obeying God as much as you are able." And *al-ghurur* means falsehood.

Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us; Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us; Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us; Ibn Harun informed us; Muhammad ibn 'Amr informed us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "God Most High says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." And recite, if you wish: "No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for their eyes, as a reward for what they used to do" [al-Sajdah: 17]. Indeed, in the Garden there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it. Recite, if you wish: "And extended shade" [al-Waqi'ah: 30]. And a place the size of a whip in the Garden is better than the world and all that is in it. Recite, if you wish: ﴿Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and is admitted to the Garden has indeed succeeded. And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the tafsir of Surat al-Waqi'ah: 9/179–180, who said it is hasan sahih; and Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2/438 from Abu Hurairah. Part of it was narrated by al-Bukhari in the tafsir, chapter "No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for their eyes" 9:8/515, and in Bad' al-Khalq; and Muslim in al-Jannah wa-Sifat Na'imiha, no. (2824): 4/2174. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/208–209.]]
