So He promised it that He would return into it what had been taken from it, and so no one is there but he will be buried in the dust from which he was created." [[Not established with this wording. What appears, and God knows best, is that it is not a hadith. Al-Khazin mentioned it in his tafsir without indicating that it is a hadith. See al-Matalib al-'Aliyah 3/333–334, where something close to it is narrated.]] ﴿And you will only be paid your rewards﴾ in full, meaning you will be recompensed for your deeds ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾: if good, then good; if evil, then evil. ﴿So whoever is drawn away﴾ from ﴿the Fire and is admitted to the Garden has indeed succeeded﴾: [meaning] he has attained salvation and been safe from fear. ﴿And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion﴾: that is, a benefit and a pleasure, like the axe, the cooking pot and the bowl, which then pass away and do not remain.

Al-Hasan said: "Like the greenness of plants and the play of girls; it has no lasting outcome."

Qatadah said: "It is a fleeting enjoyment, about to vanish with its people. So take from this enjoyment by obeying God as much as you are able." And *al-ghurur* means falsehood.

Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us; Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Hiri informed us; Hajib ibn Ahmad al-Tusi informed us; Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us; Ibn Harun informed us; Muhammad ibn 'Amr informed us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "God Most High says: I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived." And recite, if you wish: "No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for their eyes, as a reward for what they used to do" [al-Sajdah: 17]. Indeed, in the Garden there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it. Recite, if you wish: "And extended shade" [al-Waqi'ah: 30]. And a place the size of a whip in the Garden is better than the world and all that is in it. Recite, if you wish: ﴿Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and is admitted to the Garden has indeed succeeded. And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the tafsir of Surat al-Waqi'ah: 9/179–180, who said it is hasan sahih; and Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2/438 from Abu Hurairah. Part of it was narrated by al-Bukhari in the tafsir, chapter "No soul knows what is hidden for them of comfort for their eyes" 9:8/515, and in Bad' al-Khalq; and Muslim in al-Jannah wa-Sifat Na'imiha, no. (2824): 4/2174. The author also narrated it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 15/208–209.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 186:**

﴿You will surely be tested in your possessions and in your selves﴾ — the verse (al-ayah). ʿIkrimah, Muqatil, al-Kalbi and Ibn Jurayj said: the verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr and Finhas ibn ʿAzuraʾ. The reason was that the Prophet (ﷺ) sent Abu Bakr to Finhas ibn ʿAzuraʾ, the chief of Banu Qaynuqaʿ, to ask him for a loan (li-yastamiddahu), and he wrote a letter to him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him: "Do not act presumptuously (la tuftatanna) against me in anything until you return." Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, came, wearing his sword across his body, and gave him the letter. When he read it, he said: "Your Lord has become in need that we should lend Him [money]." Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, resolved to strike him with the sword, then recalled the words of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Do not act presumptuously against me in anything until you return," and he refrained. Then this verse was revealed.[[Al-Tabari: 7/455. Al-Suyuti, in Lubab al-Nuqul p. 126, attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn al-Mundhir, and said: "its chain is good." See also Fath al-Bari: 8/231.]]

Al-Zuhri said: it was revealed concerning Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf, for he used to satirize the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), revile the Muslims, incite the polytheists against the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions in his poetry, and compose amorous verses about the women of the Muslims. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Who will deal with Ibn al-Ashraf for he has harmed Allah and His Messenger?"

Muhammad ibn Maslama al-Ansari said: "I will deal with him for you, O Messenger of Allah; I will kill him." He said: "Do so, if you are able."

Muhammad ibn Maslama returned and remained three days without eating or drinking except what sustained his soul. This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he summoned him and said: "Why have you abandoned food and drink?" He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I said a statement, and I do not know whether I can fulfil it or not." He said: "You are only obliged to make the effort."

He said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have no choice but to say [something]." He said: "Say whatever you wish, for you are free of responsibility in that." So there gathered to kill him Muhammad ibn Maslama, Silkan ibn Salama, Abu Na'ila, who was Kaʿb's foster brother, ʿAbbad ibn Bishr, al-Harith ibn Aws, and Abu ʿAbs ibn Jabr. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) walked with them to Baqiʿ al-Gharqad, then sent them off and said: "Set out in the name of Allah. O Allah, help them." Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned, and that was on a moonlit night.

They came until they reached his fortress. They sent Abu Na'ila ahead, and he came to him and talked with him for a while, and they recited poetry to each other, for Abu Na'ila used to compose poetry. Then he said: "Woe to you, O Ibn al-Ashraf! I have come to you with a need I want to mention to you, so keep it secret from me." He said: "I will." He said: "The arrival of this man in our land has been a calamity. The Arabs have turned against us and shot at us from one bow, the roads have been cut off from us, our dependants have been lost, and our souls have been exhausted." Kaʿb said: "I am Ibn al-Ashraf! By Allah, I had already told you, O son of Salama, that the matter would come to this." Abu Na'ila said: [the next part of the narration follows] "Indeed, I have companions with me. We want you to sell us your food, and we will pledge to you and provide you with security, and you should be generous in this." He said: "Will you pledge your sons to me?" He said: "We are ashamed that our sons would be reproached, saying: 'This is a pledge for a wasq [a measure of food], and this is a pledge for two wasqs.'" He said: "Pledge your women to me." They said: "How can we pledge our women to you when you are the most handsome of the Arabs, and we do not trust you, and what woman could resist you because of your beauty? But we will pledge to you the ḥalaqa, meaning the weapons, and you know our need for weapons." He said: "Yes." Abu Na'ila wanted that he would not object to the weapons when he saw them, so he promised to come to him. Abu Na'ila returned to his companions and informed them of his news.

They came until they reached his fortress at night, and Abu Na'ila called out to him. He had only recently married, so he leapt up from his cloak. His wife said: "I hear a voice from which blood seems to drip. You are a man of war, and the man of war does not go out at an hour like this. Speak to them from above the fortress." He said: "It is only my brother Muhammad ibn Maslama and my foster brother Abu Na'ila. If this group found me sleeping, they would not wake me. Indeed, the noble man, when he is called to a thrust at night, answers." So he came down to them and talked with them for a while. Then they said: "O Ibn al-Ashraf, would you like us to walk together to the valley of al-ʿAjuz, and talk there for the rest of our night?" He said: "If you wish." So they went out walking together. Abu Na'ila had said to his companions: "I will grab his hair and smell it; when you see me having a firm grip on his head, then take him and strike him." Then he put his hand into the hair at the side of his head, then smelled his hand and said: "I have never seen a scent like tonight's, the scent of a bride!" He said: "It is the perfume of the mother of so-and-so," meaning his wife. Then he walked for a while, then did the same again until he was reassured. Then he walked for a while and did it again, then he took hold of both sides of his head until he had a firm grip, and said: "Strike the enemy of Allah!" Their swords struck him in different directions, but they did not avail anything. Muhammad ibn Maslama said: "I remembered a dagger on my sword, so I took it, and the enemy of Allah had let out a cry, such that no fortress around us remained without a fire being lit upon it." He said: "I placed it on his chest, then I pressed down on him until I reached his pubic area, and the enemy of Allah fell." Al-Harith ibn Aws had been injured on the head by one of our swords. We went out, and our companion al-Harith had been slow to follow us, and blood had drained from him. We waited for him for a while, then he came to us following our tracks. We carried him and brought him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the end of the night, and he was standing praying. We greeted him, and he came out to us, and we informed him of the killing of Kaʿb and brought his head to him. He spat on the wound of our companion.

We returned to our families, and in the morning the Jews were afraid of our encounter with the enemy of Allah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whichever men of the Jews you overcome, kill them." Then Muhayyisa ibn Masʿud leapt upon a man among the Jewish merchants who used to deal with them and trade with them, and killed him. Huwayyisa ibn Masʿud had not yet become a Muslim at that time, and he was older than Muhayyisa. When [Muhayyisa] killed him, Huwayyisa began to strike him and say: "O enemy of Allah, you killed him! By Allah, there is much fat in your belly from his wealth!" Muhayyisa said: "By Allah, if the one who ordered me to kill you had ordered me to kill him, I would have struck your neck." He said: "If Muhammad had ordered you to kill me, would you have killed me?" He said: "Yes." He said: "By Allah, a religion that has brought you to this is indeed astonishing!" Then Huwayyisa became a Muslim.[[Ibn Ishaq related the story in full in al-Sirah: 2/123–126, and al-Bukhari abridged it in al-Maghazi, chapter on the killing of Kaʿb: 7/337. See also Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/456–458. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Lubab p. 146 to ʿAbd al-Razzaq, and Ibn Hajar likewise in Fath al-Bari: 8/231.]]

Allah the Exalted revealed concerning the matter of Kaʿb: ﴿You will surely be tested﴾ — you will certainly be informed. The lam is for emphasis and contains the meaning of an oath, and the nun is for the emphasis of the oath. ﴿in your possessions﴾ — by calamities, afflictions and losses; ﴿and your selves﴾ — by illnesses. It was said: by the misfortunes of relatives and kin. ʿAta' said: these are the emigrants whose wealth and property the polytheists seized, and whom they tortured. Al-Hasan said: it is what was obligated upon them in their possessions and their selves of rights, such as prayer, fasting, pilgrimage, jihad and zakat. ﴿And you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you﴾ — meaning the Jews and the Christians, ﴿and from those who associate partners﴾ — meaning the polytheists of the Arabs, ﴿much harm.﴾ ﴿And if you are patient﴾ — under their harm, ﴿and fear Allah﴾ — ﴿indeed, that is of the steadfast matters﴾ — of the rightful and best of matters. ʿAta' said: it is of the reality of faith.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 187:

﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture: "You must make it clear to the people and not conceal it."﴾ Ibn Kathir, the people of Basra and Abu Bakr read it with the ya' (yukattimūnahu, "they shall not conceal it" in the third person) in both places, on account of His saying, ﴿So they cast it behind their backs﴾. The others read it with the ta' (tubayyinunnahu, "you shall make it clear," in the second person) in the first place, on the assumption of an implied "saying" (al-qawl, "the saying" that is understood and omitted). ﴿So they cast it behind their backs﴾ means: they threw it away, neglected it, and abandoned acting upon it. ﴿And sold it for a small price﴾ means: the foods (al-ma'akil, "the bribes and gains from food") and bribes (al-rushā, "bribes"). ﴿Evil is what they bought﴾. Qatadah said: "This is a covenant which Allah, exalted is He, took from the people of knowledge: whoever knows something should teach it. Beware of concealing knowledge, for it is destruction."

Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Were it not for what Allah took from the People of the Book, I would not have narrated anything to you," and then he recited this verse, ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture﴾ to the end of the verse.

Abu al-Fadl Ziyad ibn Muhammad al-Hanafi narrated to us: Abu Mu'adh al-Shah ibn Abd al-Rahman informed us: Abu Bakr Umar ibn Sahl ibn Isma'il al-Dinawari informed us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa al-Birti informed us: Abu Hudhayfah Musa ibn Mas'ud informed us: Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated to us from Simak ibn Harb, from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is asked about knowledge that he possesses and conceals it, will be bridled on the Day of Resurrection with a bridle of fire."

[[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-'Ilm, chapter on the disapproval of withholding knowledge: 5/251; and al-Tirmidhi in al-'Ilm, chapter on what has come concerning the concealment of knowledge: 7/407-408, and he said: "Hasan hadith." Al-Mundhiri quoted al-Tirmidhi's grading of it, then said: It has been related from Abu Hurairah through several routes, some of which have objections. The route by which Abu Dawud narrated it is a good route, for he related it from al-Tabudhaki, whom al-Bukhari and Muslim both relied upon as evidence; it is from Hammad ibn Salamah, whom Muslim relied upon and al-Bukhari cited as corroboration; it is from Ali ibn al-Hakam, Abu al-Hakam al-Bunani, of whom Imam Ahmad said: "There is nothing wrong with him"; it is from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, and the two Imams agreed upon relying on it. It is also related by Ibn Majah in the Muqaddimah, chapter on whoever is asked about his knowledge and conceals it, with the wording: "No man memorizes knowledge and conceals it except that he will be brought on the Day of Resurrection bridled with a bridle of fire," no. 261: 1/96. Also by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 1/101, who graded it sound according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs; by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 1/161, 2/263 and other places; by Ibn Abd al-Barr in Jami' Bayan al-'Ilm, p. 22; and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/301.]]

Al-Hasan ibn Imarah said: "I came to al-Zuhri after he had given up narrating hadith, and found him at his door. I said: 'If you see fit, would you narrate to me?' He said: 'Do you not know that I have given up narrating hadith?' I said: 'Either you narrate to me, or I narrate to you.' He said: 'Narrate to me.' So I said: 'al-Hakam ibn Utaybah narrated to me from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, who said: I heard Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, say: "Allah did not take a covenant from the ignorant to learn until He took a covenant from the people of knowledge to teach."'" He said: "Then he narrated to me forty hadiths."

[[Narrated by al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah: Abd al-Wahhab al-Khaffaf informed us: al-Hasan ibn Imarah informed us: al-Hakam ibn Utaybah narrated to me from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, who said: I heard Ali... and he mentioned it. Al-Hasan is abandoned (matruk). Al-Tha'labi narrated it through al-Harith's route, and Ibn Abd al-Barr mentioned it in al-'Ilm, saying: "It is related from Ali." The author of al-Firdaws also mentioned it from Ali. See: al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 35.]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 188:**

His saying: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought﴾ and the rest of the verse. Ásim, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿لَا تَحْسَبَنَّ (lā taḥsabanna)﴾ with a *tā'* (second-person form), meaning: "Do not think, O Muhammad, that those who rejoice..." The others read it with a *yā'* (third-person form), *lā yaḥsabanna*, meaning: "Let not those who rejoice think that their rejoicing will save them from the punishment." ﴿فَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّهُمْ (fa-lā yaḥsabannahum)﴾: Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read it with a *yā'* and a *ḍammah* on the *bā'*, as a report about those who rejoice, meaning: "let them not think themselves [safe]" (*fa-lā yaḥsabunna anfusahum*). The others read it with a *tā'* and a *fatḥah* on the *bā'*, meaning: "So do not think them [safe], O Muhammad." He repeated his saying ﴿so do not think them﴾ for emphasis. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought and love to be praised for what they did not do are in a place of safety from the punishment﴾, without the repetition.

They differed concerning who this verse was revealed about. Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam informed us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us: Zayd ibn Aslam narrated to me, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri [76a] that some men among the hypocrites in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would stay behind from him when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out to fight, and they rejoiced in their staying behind, in opposition to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned, they made excuses to him and swore oaths, and they loved to be praised for what they had not done. So this was revealed: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought﴾ and the rest of the verse.[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Tafsir Surat Al 'Imran, chapter "Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have brought," 8/233, and by Muslim in the Book of the Attributes of the Hypocrites and their Rulings, no. (2777), 4/2142.]]

Abd al-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us: Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us: Ibrahim ibn Musa informed us: Hisham informed us, that Ibn Jurayj informed them: Ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me that Alqamah ibn Waqqas informed him that Marwan said to his doorkeeper: "Go, O Rafi', to Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and say to him: 'If every person who rejoices in what he has been given and loves to be praised for what he did not do is punished, we will all be punished.'" Ibn Abbas said: "What is it to you with this? The Prophet (ﷺ) only called the Jews and asked them about something, and they concealed it from him and informed him of something else. They showed him that they had sought praise from him for what they had told him about what he had asked them, and they rejoiced in what they had done by concealing it." Then Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, recited: ﴿And when Allah took the covenant of those who were given the Scripture﴾ up to His saying: ﴿who rejoice in what they have brought and love to be praised for what they did not do.﴾[[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the same place and by Muslim in the same place, no. (2778).]]

Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning Finhas, Ashya' and others from among the rabbis, who rejoiced in misleading people and in people ascribing knowledge to them, while they were not people of knowledge.[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/466.]] Mujahid said: They are the Jews, who rejoiced at people's admiration for them when they altered the Book, and at their praise of them for it.[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/469.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They are the Jews, who rejoiced in what Allah had given the family of Abraham, while they were innocent of that.[[Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/469.]]

Qatadah and Muqatil said: The Jews of Khaybar came to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "We know you and we believe you, and we are upon your opinion, and we are a support for you." But that was not in their hearts. When they went out, the Muslims said to them: "What did you do?" They said: "We recognized him and we believed him." The Muslims said to them: "You did well, so do this." So they praised them and prayed for them, and Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.[[Al-Tabari: 7/471. Al-Tabari preferred that it refers to the People of the Book whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said He had taken a covenant from, to make clear to the people the matter of Muhammad (ﷺ), and that they would not conceal it. See pp. 471–472 of his work.]] And He said: ﴿who rejoice in what they have brought﴾. Al-Farra' said: "*bi-mā ataw*" means "what they did," as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿You have certainly come with a thing unprecedented﴾ [Maryam: 27], meaning "you did." ﴿And love to be praised for what they did not do﴾; ﴿so do not think them in a place of safety﴾, meaning "in a place of deliverance" ﴿from the punishment. And for them is a painful punishment.﴾

﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth.﴾ He turns them as He wills. ﴿And Allah is over all things competent.﴾

﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.﴾ Our teacher, the Imam Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, informed us: Abu Nu'aym Abd al-Malik ibn al-Husayn al-Isfara'ini informed us: Abu 'Awana Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Hafiz informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar informed us: Ibn Fudayl informed us, from Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), that he slept beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He saw him wake up, then he used the siwak (tooth-stick), then performed wudu', while reciting: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth…﴾ until he finished the surah. Then he stood and prayed two rak'ahs, prolonging the standing, the bowing and the prostration in them. Then he withdrew and slept until he snored. Then he did this three times, six rak'ahs in all, each time using the siwak, then performing wudu', then reciting these verses. Then he performed the witr with three rak'ahs. Then the muezzin came to him, and he went out to the prayer saying: "O Allah, place light in my sight, light in my hearing, light in my tongue, make light behind me and light before me, make light above me and light below me. O Allah, give me light." [Related by al-Bukhari in the Book of Supplications, chapter on the supplication upon waking at night: 11/116, in similar wording; and by Muslim in the Book of Prayer of Travellers, chapter on supplication in the night prayer and its standing, no. (763): 1/530, and the wording is his.]

And Kurayb related it from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), and added: "O Allah, place light in my heart, light in my sight, light in my hearing, light on my right, and light on my left." [Related by Muslim in the same place: 1/529.]

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿for those of understanding﴾ means: those who possess intellects. Then He described them, saying:

﴿And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth.﴾ He turns them as He wills. ﴿And Allah is over all things competent.﴾

﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.﴾ Our teacher, the Imam Abu 'Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi, informed us: Abu Nu'aym Abd al-Malik ibn al-Husayn al-Isfara'ini informed us: Abu 'Awana Ya'qub ibn Ishaq al-Hafiz informed us: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Jabbar informed us: Ibn Fudayl informed us, from Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Abbas, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), that he slept beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He saw him wake up, then he used the siwak (tooth-stick), then performed wudu', while reciting: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth…﴾ until he finished the surah. Then he stood and prayed two rak'ahs, prolonging the standing, the bowing and the prostration in them. Then he withdrew and slept until he snored. Then he did this three times, six rak'ahs in all, each time using the siwak, then performing wudu', then reciting these verses. Then he performed the witr with three rak'ahs. Then the muezzin came to him, and he went out to the prayer saying: "O Allah, place light in my sight, light in my hearing, light in my tongue, make light behind me and light before me, make light above me and light below me. O Allah, give me light." [Related by al-Bukhari in the Book of Supplications, chapter on the supplication upon waking at night: 11/116, in similar wording; and by Muslim in the Book of Prayer of Travellers, chapter on supplication in the night prayer and its standing, no. (763): 1/530, and the wording is his.]

And Kurayb related it from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), and added: "O Allah, place light in my heart, light in my sight, light in my hearing, light on my right, and light on my left." [Related by Muslim in the same place: 1/529.]

His statement, the Exalted: ﴿for those of understanding﴾ means: those who possess intellects. Then He described them, saying:

﴿Those who remember God, standing, sitting, and on their sides﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talib, Ibn Abbas, al-Nakha'i and Qatada (may God be pleased with them) said: this refers to prayer. One prays standing; if one cannot, then sitting; if one cannot, then lying on one's side.

Abu Uthman Sa'id ibn Isma'il al-Dabbi informed us: Abu Muhammad Abd al-Jabbar ibn Muhammad al-Jarrahi informed us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mahbubi informed us: Abu Isa Muhammad ibn Isa al-Tirmidhi informed us: Hannad informed us: Waki' related to us from Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from Husayn al-Mu'allim, from Abdullah ibn Buraydah, from Imran ibn Husayn, who said: I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the prayer of the sick person, and he said: "Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; if you cannot, then on your side." [Related by al-Bukhari in Taqsir al-Salat, chapter "If one cannot sit, he prays lying on his side": 2/587, and by the author (al-Baghawi) in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/109.]

The rest of the exegetes said: it means constant remembrance of God in all circumstances, because a person is rarely free of one of these three states. A parallel is in Surat al-Nisa: "So when you have finished the prayer, remember God standing, sitting, and on your sides" (al-Nisa 4:103).

﴿And they reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ and on what He originated in them, so that this would guide them to God's power and they would know that they have a Creator who is capable, governing, and wise. Ibn Awn said: reflection removes heedlessness and produces fear of God in the heart, just as water produces plants in the crops. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verses 193–195:

﴿Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller﴾: meaning Muhammad (ﷺ). This was said by Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and by most people. Al-Qurazi said: it means the Qur'an, because not everyone meets the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿Calling to faith﴾: that is, calling to faith, ﴿"Believe in your Lord," so we believed. Our Lord, forgive us our sins, remove from us our misdeeds, and cause us to die with the righteous﴾: that is, among the company of the righteous.

﴿Our Lord, and grant us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾: that is, through the tongues of Your messengers. ﴿And do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You do not fail in the promise﴾: ﴿do not disgrace us﴾ means do not punish us, do not destroy us, do not expose us, and do not humiliate us.

If it is asked: what is the meaning of their saying, ﴿Our Lord, and grant us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾, when they knew that Allah does not fail in the promise? It is said: its wording is a supplication, but its meaning is a statement, that is: "So that You will give us what You promised us through Your messengers." Its implied sense is: ﴿forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds﴾ and ﴿do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection﴾, so that You give us what You promised us through Your messengers of grace and mercy. It is also said: the meaning is, "Our Lord, make us among those who deserve Your reward, and give them what You promised them through the tongues of Your messengers," because they were not certain of their deserving that honour, so they asked Him to make them deserving of it. It is also said: they only asked Him to hasten what He promised them of victory over the enemies. They said: "We know that You do not fail, but we have no patience with Your forbearance, so hasten their humiliation and give us victory over them."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So their Lord answered them: "Indeed, I will not allow to be lost﴾, that is, I will not nullify, ﴿the work of any worker among you﴾, O believers, ﴿whether male or female﴾. Mujahid said: Umm Salamah said, "O Messenger of Allah, I hear Allah mention men in migration and not mention women." So Allah revealed this verse. ﴿Some of you are from others﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Tafsir, Tafsir of Surat al-Nisa: 8/377, and authenticated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/300 on the condition of al-Bukhari; and al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 7/486–487. Al-Suyuti also attributed it to Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, 'Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Tabarani, also from Umm Salamah. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/412, and Lubab al-Nuqul p. (150), in the margin of al-Jalalayn.]] Al-Kalbi said: in religion, support and allegiance. It is also said: all of you are from Adam and Eve. Al-Dahhak said: your men are like your women and your women are like your men in obedience, as He said: "The believing men and the believing women are allies of one another" [al-Tawbah: 71].

﴿So those who emigrated and were expelled from their homes and were harmed in My cause﴾: that is, in My obedience and My religion. They are the emigrants whom the polytheists drove out of Makkah. ﴿And fought and were killed﴾. Ibn 'Amir and Ibn Kathir read "wa-quttilu" with emphasis (tashdid). Al-Hasan said: it means that they were cut to pieces in the battle. The others read it without emphasis. Most of the reciters read ﴿wa-qatalu wa-qutilu﴾, meaning that they fought the enemy and then they were killed. Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read ﴿wa-qutilu wa-qatalu﴾. This has two possible senses. The first: its meaning is that those of them who remained fought, and the meaning of His saying ﴿wa-qutilu﴾ is that some of them were killed; the Arabs say, "We killed the sons of so-and-so," when only some of them were killed. The second: ﴿wa-qutilu﴾ means they were killed after having fought. ﴿Surely I will remove from them their misdeeds and surely I will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward from Allah﴾. It is in the accusative as an absolute (qat') phrase, as said by al-Kisa'i. Al-Mubarrad said: it is a verbal noun (masdar), meaning, "I will surely reward them with a reward." ﴿And with Allah is the best of rewards.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 196–198:

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Let not the going to and fro of those who disbelieve through the lands deceive you﴾. It was revealed concerning the polytheists, because they were in ease and comfortable living, trading and enjoying themselves. Some of the believers said: "The enemies of Allah, the Exalted, are in such good state, as we see, while we are in hardship?" So Allah, the Exalted, sent down this verse: ﴿Let not the going to and fro of those who disbelieve through the lands deceive you﴾. Their striking through the earth (ḍarb, travel) and their moving about in the lands for trade and various kinds of gain is addressed to the Prophet (ﷺ), and what is meant is others than him.

﴿A little enjoyment﴾, that is: it is a little enjoyment, a meager provision, a passing pleasure and a fleeting delight. ﴿Then their refuge is Hell, and what an evil resting-place﴾, meaning their destination. ﴿Hell, and wretched is the bed﴾, that is, the bedding.

﴿But those who fear their Lord, for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, as a welcome (nuzul) from Allah﴾: a reward and a recompense. ﴿From Allah﴾ is in the accusative as an explanation (tafsir). It was also said: He made that a welcome. ﴿And what is with Allah is better for the righteous (al-abrar)﴾, than the provision of this world.

Abdul-Wahid al-Mulayhi informed us, that Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, that Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, that Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, that Abdul-Aziz ibn Abdullah informed us, that Sulayman ibn Bilal informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Ubayd ibn Hunayn, that he heard Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) say: Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "I came and behold, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was in an upper chamber, and he was lying on a mat with nothing between him and it, and under his head was a leather cushion stuffed with palm fiber, and at his feet was a bundle of senna leaves, and at his head were hanging water-skins. I saw the mark of the mat on his side, so I wept. He said: 'What makes you weep?' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Chosroes and Caesar are in what they are in, while you are the Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'Are you not content that they should have the world and we have the Hereafter?'" [[A portion of a hadith recorded by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir, Tafsir of Surah al-Tahrim, chapter: "You seek the pleasure of your wives" 8/657.]]?

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 199:

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah﴾ [and so on]. Ibn ʿAbbas, Jabir, Anas and Qatadah said: it was revealed concerning al-Najashi, king of Abyssinia, whose name was Ashamah, which in Arabic means ʿAtiyyah. This was because when he died, Jibril (peace be upon him) informed the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) of his death on the very day he died. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Go out and pray over your brother who has died in a land other than yours, al-Najashi." He went out to al-Baqiʿ, and the land of Abyssinia was unveiled for him, so he saw the bier of al-Najashi and prayed over him, making four takbirs, and asked forgiveness for him. The hypocrites said: "Look at this one praying over a Abyssinian Christian infidel whom he has never seen and who is not of his religion." So Allah, Exalted is He, revealed this verse.

[Ibn Hajar said: al-Tha'labi mentioned it as the statement of Ibn ʿAbbas and Qatadah, and al-Wahidi mentioned it without an isnad. al-Tabari and Ibn ʿAdi narrated it in the biography of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, whose name is Salma and who is weak, from Qatadah, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, from Jabir, without the phrase "and he looked toward the land of Abyssinia." al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat from the narration of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father. See al-Kafi al-Shafi, p. 37. And from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed over al-Najashi and made four takbirs over him, narrated by al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, and the narrators of al-Tabarani are the narrators of the Sahih. See Majma' al-Zawa'id: 3/38–39, 9/419. Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 1/440. The Prophet's (ﷺ) prayer over al-Najashi is established in the two Sahihs. See al-Bukhari: 2/116 and Muslim: 2/656–657.]

ʿAta' said: it was revealed concerning forty men from the people of Najran, [from the Banu Harith ibn Kaʿb], thirty-two from Abyssinia and eight from the Romans, who were upon the religion of ʿIsa (peace be upon him), and they believed in the Prophet (ﷺ). Ibn Jurayj said: it was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his companions. [See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 3/148.]

Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning all the believers among the People of the Scripture. [See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 7/498–499, al-Durr al-Manthur: 2/388, and Ibn Kathir: 1/440.] ﴿And indeed, among the People of the Scripture are those who believe in Allah﴾ ﴿and in what has been revealed to you﴾, meaning: the Qur'an; ﴿and in what has been revealed to them﴾, meaning: the Torah and the Gospel; ﴿humbly submitting to Allah﴾, meaning: submissive and humble before Allah; ﴿they do not exchange the signs of Allah for a small price﴾, meaning: they do not distort their books nor conceal the description of Muhammad (ﷺ) for the sake of leadership and worldly gain, as others among the leaders of the Jews did; ﴿those will have their reward with their Lord. Indeed, Allah is swift in account.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 3, verse 200:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, endure and outlast [your enemies] and remain stationed [at the frontiers]﴾. Al-Hasan said: "Endure in your religion and do not abandon it, whether in hardship or in ease." Qatadah said: "Endure in obedience to Allah."

Al-Dahhak and Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: "In the matter of Allah's command."

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "In fulfilling the obligations of Allah, may He be exalted." Zayd ibn Aslam said: "In jihad." Al-Kalbi said: "In trials." And "outlast" means: the disbelievers. "Remain stationed" means: the polytheists. Abu 'Ubaydah said: that is, persist and be steadfast. Ribat (ربط) means to tie or bind fast. The original sense of ribat is that these people tie their horses and those people tie their horses. Then the term was applied to everyone who remains stationed at a frontier post to defend those behind him, even if he has no mount.

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Mulayhi informed us, from Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abd Allah ibn Munir, who heard Abu al-Nadr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A day of ribat in the way of Allah is better than the world and what is in it. The place of one of your whips in Paradise is better than the world and what is in it. And a journey that a servant makes in the way of Allah in the morning or the evening is better than the world and what is in it." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Jihad, chapter on the virtue of a day of ribat in the way of Allah, 6/85. Ibn Kathir cited many hadiths on this meaning in his tafsir of the verse: 1/445-448.]]

Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Yusuf al-Juwayni informed us, from Abu Muhammad Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Shurayk al-Shafi'i, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim Abu Bakr al-Jurbadhi, from Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la, from Ibn Wahb, who informed me: Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh, from Abd al-Karim ibn al-Harith, from Abu 'Ubaydah ibn 'Uqbah, from Shurahbil ibn al-Simt, from Salman al-Khayr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever performs ribat for one day and night in the way of Allah, he will have the reward of fasting a month continuously. And whoever dies while performing ribat, the like of that reward will continue for him, his provision will be continued for him, and he will be safe from the tempter." [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Leadership, chapter on the virtue of ribat in the way of Allah, no. (1913): 3/1520, with the wording "ribat of a day and a night." The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/352. Al-Fattan is reported with a damma or a fatha on the fa': with a damma it is the plural of fatin, the one who leads people astray from the truth and tempts them; with a fatha it is Satan, because he tempts people away from religion; and fattan is a form of intensive emphasis in temptation. See al-Nihayah: 3/410.]]

Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Rahman said: "In the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) there was no military campaign in which ribat was performed; rather, it means waiting for one prayer after another prayer." The evidence for this interpretation is what Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Sarakhsi informed us, from Zahir ibn Ahmad al-Faqih, from Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi, from Abu Mus'ab, from Malik, from al-Ala' ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of what Allah erases sins by and raises ranks by? Perfecting the ablution in difficult conditions, walking much to the mosques, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer. That is ribat, that is ribat." [[Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Purification, chapter on the virtue of perfecting ablution in difficult conditions, no. (251): 1/219. The author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/320.]]

﴿And fear Allah that you may prosper﴾. Some men of eloquence said: "Endure in ease, endure in adversity and hardship, remain stationed in the house of the enemies, and fear the God of the earth and the heavens, that you may prosper in the everlasting abode."
